title: Transatlantic Comparison of ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Guidelines: Insights From the United States and Europe.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Narrative comparison of two guidelines; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not state which recommendations differ, and the guidelines compared have since been revised.
appraisal.one_line: Review comparing the 2012 ESC and 2013 ACCF/AHA STEMI guidelines and their differences in recommendations and interpretation of evidence.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It documents transatlantic discordance on a common decision, which is a source of research questions.

title: Safety and Efficacy of New-Generation Drug-Eluting Stents in Women at High Risk for Atherothrombosis: From the Women in Innovation and Drug-Eluting Stents Collaborative Patient-Level Pooled Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Patient-level pooled analysis of 26 randomized trials; 10,449 women, of whom 5333 (51%) were at high ATR.
appraisal.main_limitation: Stent-generation comparison across trials is non-randomised within the pooled dataset and subject to residual confounding.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level pooled analysis of 26 randomised trials in women, comparing new- and early-generation DES by atherothrombotic risk.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with women not at high ATR, those at high ATR had significantly higher risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (15.8% versus 10.6%; adjusted hazard ratio: 1.53; 95% confidence interval: 1.34-1.75; P=0.006). In high-ATR risk women, the use of new-generation DES was associated with significantly lower risk of 3-year major adverse cardiovascular events (adjusted hazard ratio: 0.69; 95% confidence interval: 0.52-0.92) compared with early-generation DES.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides sex-specific IPD evidence on stent choice in an under-represented, high-risk group.

title: SCAI Expert consensus statement: Evaluation, management, and special considerations of cardio-oncology patients in the cardiac catheterization laboratory (endorsed by the cardiological society of india, and sociedad Latino Americana de Cardiologıa intervencionista).
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

appraisal.design_and_n: Expert consensus statement; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Recommendations rest on limited published evidence and operator experience.
appraisal.one_line: SCAI expert consensus statement on managing cancer patients in the cardiac catheterisation laboratory.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides society guidance for a growing population excluded from most interventional trials.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Cangrelor in Women Versus Men During Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Insights From the Cangrelor versus Standard Therapy to Achieve Optimal Management of Platelet Inhibition (CHAMPION PHOENIX) Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a randomised trial of 11,145 patients, of whom 3051 (28%) were female.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis with non-significant interaction tests for the primary and stent thrombosis end points.
appraisal.one_line: Sex-specific analysis of cangrelor versus clopidogrel during PCI from a randomised trial.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Cangrelor reduced the odds of the primary end point by 35% in women (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 0.65; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.48-0.89) and by 14% in men (OR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.70-1.05; P interaction=0.23) compared with clopidogrel.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It supports consistent benefit of intravenous P2Y12 inhibition in women undergoing PCI, with a signal of more moderate bleeding.

title: Scaffold Thrombosis After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention With ABSORB Bioresorbable Vascular Scaffold: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis; 10,510 patients (8,351 with a BVS and 2,159 with DES).
appraisal.main_limitation: Short follow-up and a mix of observational and randomised studies.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of studies of the Absorb bioresorbable scaffold reporting a higher risk of MI and definite/probable scaffold thrombosis than DES.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Meta-analysis demonstrated that patients who received a BVS were at a higher risk of MI (OR: 2.06, 95% CI: 1.31 to 3.22, p = 0.002) and definite/probable ST (OR: 2.06, 95% CI: 1.07 to 3.98, p = 0.03) compared with patients who received DES.
appraisal.why_it_matters: An early safety signal that contributed to the withdrawal of this scaffold from clinical use.

title: Effect of Chronic Kidney Disease in Women Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention With Drug-Eluting Stents: A Patient-Level Pooled Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Patient-level pooled analysis of 26 randomized trials; 4,217 women with creatinine available, of whom 603 (14%) had a CrCl <45 ml/min.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc pooled analysis; women with missing baseline creatinine were excluded.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level pooled analysis of 26 randomised trials in women assessing the effect of CKD on outcomes after DES and by stent generation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Following multivariable adjustment, CrCl <45 ml/min was independently associated with a higher risk of MACE (adjusted hazard ratio: 1.56; 95% confidence interval: 1.23 to 1.98) and all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio: 2.67; 95% confidence interval: 1.85 to 3.85).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Quantifies the prognostic weight of CKD in women after PCI and finds no interaction with stent generation.

title: Causes of Death Following PCI Versus CABG in Complex CAD: 5-Year Follow-Up of SYNTAX.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Follow-up analysis of a randomised trial with blinded event adjudication; 97 deaths after CABG and 123 deaths after PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Cause-of-death analyses are secondary and the predictor model is exploratory.
appraisal.one_line: Cause-specific mortality at 5 years after PCI versus CABG in complex coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The cumulative incidence rates of all-cause death were not significantly different between CABG and PCI (11.4% vs. 13.9%, respectively; p = 0.10), whereas there were significant differences in terms of cardiovascular (5.8% vs. 9.6%, respectively; p = 0.008) and cardiac death (5.3% vs. 9.0%, respectively; p = 0.003).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It identifies myocardial infarction related death as the main difference between strategies, which informs the PCI versus CABG decision and post-PCI prevention.

title: Immediate Versus Delayed Invasive Intervention for Non-STEMI Patients: The RIDDLE-NSTEMI Study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 323 NSTEMI patients randomized to an immediate-intervention group (<2 h after randomization, n = 162) and a delayed-intervention group (2 to 72 h, n = 161).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trial in which the difference was mainly attributable to new MI in the pre-catheterisation period.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of immediate versus delayed angiography in NSTEMI showing fewer deaths or new MI with immediate intervention.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 30 days, the primary endpoint was achieved less frequently in patients undergoing immediate intervention (4.3% vs. 13%, hazard ratio: 0.32, 95% confidence interval: 0.13 to 0.74; p = 0.008). At 1 year, this difference persisted (6.8% in the immediate-intervention group vs. 18.8% in delayed-intervention group; hazard ratio: 0.34, 95% confidence interval: 0.17 to 0.67; p = 0.002).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses the timing of the invasive strategy in NSTEMI, a common decision on which guidelines were uncertain.

title: Outcomes From Selective Use of Thrombectomy in Patients Undergoing Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: An Analysis of the British Cardiovascular Intervention Society/National Institute for Cardiovascular Outcomes Research (BCIS-NICOR) Registry, 2006-2013.

appraisal.design_and_n: National registry cohort; 98,176 patients treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), between January 1, 2006, and December 31, 2013.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational design with propensity matching; selection of thrombectomy by physician judgement may leave residual confounding.
appraisal.one_line: Large UK registry analysis finding no mortality association with selective thrombectomy in primary PCI, and higher 1-year mortality with mechanical thrombectomy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: No significant mortality difference was seen, in adjusted analyses, between the overall thrombectomy group and the no thrombectomy group, at 30 days or 1 year (at 30 days, PSM average treatment effect [ATE] coefficient 0.0028, 95% confidence interval: -0.0048 to 0.0104; p = 0.47). The complex (mechanical) thrombectomy group demonstrated a significantly higher mortality than the no thrombectomy group at 1-year follow-up (PSM ATE coefficient 0.0434, 95% confidence interval: 0.0081 to 0.0786; p = 0.017).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Real-world data consistent with randomised trials that routine thrombectomy does not lower mortality.

title: Benefits and Risks of Extended Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Everolimus-Eluting Stents.

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc subset of a randomised trial; the DAPT study enrolled 25,682 subjects (11,308 EES-treated), and 9,961 (4,703 with EES) were randomized to 18 months of continued thienopyridine or placebo.
appraisal.main_limitation: Stent type was not randomized and the EES subset analysis was post hoc.
appraisal.one_line: Post hoc analysis of the DAPT study in everolimus-eluting stent patients showing fewer stent thromboses and MIs but more bleeding and death with extended thienopyridine.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Among EES-treated patients, continued thienopyridine reduced stent thrombosis (0.3% vs. 0.7%, hazard ratio [HR]: 0.38, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.15 to 0.97; p = 0.04) and MI (2.1% vs. 3.2%, HR: 0.63, 95% CI: 0.44 to 0.91; p = 0.01) versus placebo but did not reduce a composite of death, MI, and stroke (4.3% vs. 4.5%, HR: 0.89, 95% CI: 0.67 to 1.18; p = 0.42), and increased moderate/severe bleeding (2.5% vs. 1.3%, HR: 1.79, 95% CI: 1.15 to 2.80; p = 0.01), and death (2.2% vs. 1.1%, HR: 1.80, 95% CI: 1.11 to 2.92; p = 0.02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the benefit-risk balance of prolonged DAPT with contemporary stents.

title: Invasive versus conservative strategy in patients aged 80 years or older with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction or unstable angina pectoris (After Eighty study): an open-label randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label randomised controlled multicentre trial in 16 hospitals, 229 patients assigned to the invasive group and 228 to the conservative group.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, a median follow-up of 1·53 years, and no difference in all-cause death.
appraisal.one_line: Open-label randomised trial in patients aged 80 years or older with NSTEMI or unstable angina comparing an invasive with a conservative strategy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 93 (40·6%) of 229 patients assigned to the invasive group and 140 (61·4%) of 228 patients assigned to the conservative group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·53 [95% CI 0·41-0·69], p=0·0001). HR for death from any cause was 0·89 (0·62-1·28; p=0·5340).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It addresses an older population that is under-represented in trials and informs the choice of an invasive strategy for NSTEMI in very elderly patients.

title: 1-year outcomes with the Absorb bioresorbable scaffold in patients with coronary artery disease: a patient-level, pooled meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Patient-level pooled meta-analysis of four randomised trials, 3389 patients (2164 Absorb BVS, 1225 CoCr-EES).
appraisal.main_limitation: Follow-up of 1 year only, industry funded, and the pooled trials were designed with surrogate or noninferiority primary outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level pooled meta-analysis of four randomised trials comparing the Absorb scaffold with a cobalt-chromium everolimus-eluting stent at 1 year.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The summary treatment effect for the 1-year relative rates of the patient-oriented composite endpoint did not differ significantly different between BVS and CoCr-EES (relative risk [RR] 1·09 [0·89-1·34], p=0·38). Target vessel-related myocardial infarction was increased with BVS compared with CoCr-EES (RR 1·45 [95% CI 1·02-2·07], p=0·04).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It brings pooled hard-event data on early scaffold safety, including a higher target vessel-related myocardial infarction rate.

title: Six Versus 12 Months of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Implantation of Biodegradable Polymer Sirolimus-Eluting Stent: Randomized Substudy of the I-LOVE-IT 2 Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised noninferiority substudy of the I-LOVE-IT 2 trial; 1829 patients randomized to either 6-month (n=909) or 12-month DAPT (n=920).
appraisal.main_limitation: Event rates were low and the substudy is limited to one stent platform in a Chinese population.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised noninferiority substudy of 6 versus 12 months of DAPT after a biodegradable polymer sirolimus-eluting stent.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 12-month target lesion failure in 6-month DAPT group was comparable with the 12-month DAPT group (6.8% versus 5.9%; difference and 95% confidence interval, 0.87% [-1.37% to 3.11%], P for noninferiority=0.0065).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds randomised evidence to the shortened DAPT strategies after contemporary DES.

title: Left Main Stenting in Comparison With Surgical Revascularization: 10-Year Outcomes of the (Left Main Coronary Artery Stenting) LE MANS Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised multicentre trial; 105 patients with unprotected left main coronary artery stenosis randomly assigned to PCI with stenting (n = 52) or CABG (n = 53).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample, so the trial was underpowered for clinical outcomes, and it enrolled only low to medium SYNTAX complexity.
appraisal.one_line: Ten-year follow-up of a small randomised trial of left main stenting versus CABG found no significant difference in mortality or MACCE.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The mortality (21.6% vs. 30.2%; p = 0.41) and MACCE (51.1% vs. 64.4%; p = 0.28) were statistically not different between groups. The probability of very long-term survival up to 14 years was comparable between PCI and CABG (74.2% vs. 67.5%; p = 0.34; hazard ratio: 1.45, 95% confidence interval: 0.67 to 3.13).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Long-term randomised data on left main PCI versus CABG, a decision on which guideline positions have differed.

title: Bioresorbable Coronary Scaffold Thrombosis: Multicenter Comprehensive Analysis of Clinical Presentation, Mechanisms, and Predictors.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective multicentric registry, 1,305 consecutive patients who received 1,870 BVS in 4 hospitals.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective registry with before-and-after comparison, so the implantation effect is an association.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre registry analysis of scaffold thrombosis after bioresorbable scaffold implantation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The incidence of probable and definite ScT was 1.8% at 30 days and 3.0% at 12 months. When a BVS-specific implantation strategy was implemented, 12-month ScT rates fell from 3.3% to 1.0% (hazard ratio: 0.19; 95% confidence interval: 0.05 to 0.70).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It quantifies scaffold thrombosis and suggests that implantation technique was associated with lower rates.

title: Outcomes in Patients With Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement and Left Main Stenting: The TAVR-LM Registry.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective registry; 204 patients undergoing TAVR plus LM PCI, with 128 matched pairs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective and non-randomised, with small subgroups and wide uncertainty in the unplanned-PCI comparison.
appraisal.one_line: First registry of TAVR combined with left main PCI reports mortality similar to matched TAVR-alone controls.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: One-year mortality (9.4% vs. 10.2%, p = 0.83) was similar between the TAVR plus LM PCI cohort and matched controls.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports a percutaneous strategy for TAVI candidates with left main disease and flags higher risk after unplanned PCI.

title: Is Bare-Metal Stent Implantation Still Justifiable in High Bleeding Risk Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention?: A Pre-Specified Analysis From the ZEUS Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pre-specified analysis of a randomised single-blinded trial; 828 patients fulfilling pre-defined clinical or biochemical HBR criteria.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup of a trial using a first-generation-era zotarolimus stent and a protocol-mandated short DAPT, which limits transferability to current stents.
appraisal.one_line: Pre-specified ZEUS analysis in high-bleeding-risk patients found fewer MACE with a zotarolimus-eluting stent than with a bare-metal stent.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Among HBR patients, major adverse cardiovascular events occurred in 22.6% of the E-ZES and 29% of the BMS patients (hazard ratio: 0.75; 95% confidence interval: 0.57 to 0.98; p = 0.033), driven by lower myocardial infarction (3.5% vs. 10.4%; p < 0.001) and target vessel revascularization (5.9% vs. 11.4%; p = 0.005) rates in the E-ZES arm.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on stent choice and DAPT duration in high-bleeding-risk patients.

title: Outcomes With Intravascular Ultrasound-Guided Stent Implantation: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials in the Era of Drug-Eluting Stents.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomised trials; seven trials with 3192 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooled trials were small, and the benefit was driven largely by target lesion revascularisation rather than hard endpoints.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of seven trials of routine IVUS-guided versus angiography-guided DES implantation found fewer MACE with IVUS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Routine IVUS-guided percutaneous coronary intervention was associated with a reduction in the risk of major adverse cardiac events (6.5% versus 10.3%; odds ratio, 0.60; 95% confidence interval, 0.46-0.77; P<0.0001), mainly because of reduction in the risk of ischemia-driven target lesion revascularization (4.1% versus 6.6%; odds ratio, 0.60; 95% confidence interval, 0.43-0.84; P=0.003).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports intravascular imaging guidance and preceded the larger trials that shaped later guideline recommendations.

title: Effects of Age and Sex on Clinical Outcomes After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Relative to Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Patients With Triple-Vessel Coronary Artery Disease.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre observational cohort; 5651 patients with triple-vessel disease (PCI, n=3165; CABG, n=2486).
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational, with residual confounding in revascularisation choice, and a single-country population.
appraisal.one_line: CREDO-Kyoto analysis suggests the mortality comparison of PCI with CABG in triple-vessel disease differs by age.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The excess adjusted mortality risk of PCI relative to CABG was significant in patients ≥74 years of age (hazard ratio [HR], 1.40; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.10-1.79; P=0.006).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Effect modification by age bears directly on the PCI versus CABG decision in older patients.

title: Drug-Eluting Versus Bare-Metal Stents During PCI in Patients With End-Stage Renal Disease on Dialysis.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort of 36,117 dialysis patients from the USRDS who had coronary stenting.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational data subject to confounding; the abstract gives no confidence intervals for these estimates.
appraisal.one_line: Registry analysis of drug-eluting versus bare-metal stents in dialysis patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: DES, compared with BMS, were associated with a significant 18% lower risk of death; 16% lower risk of death or MI; and 13% lower risk of death, MI, or repeat revascularization.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It addresses PCI in end-stage renal disease, a population largely excluded from stent trials.

title: Optimal Strategy for Provisional Side Branch Intervention in Coronary Bifurcation Lesions: 3-Year Outcomes of the SMART-STRATEGY Randomized Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 258 patients with a large bifurcation lesion randomized to a conservative or aggressive SB intervention strategy.
appraisal.main_limitation: Modest sample size and a benefit that emerged after 1 year through landmark analysis rather than at the primary time point.
appraisal.one_line: Three-year results of a randomised comparison of conservative versus aggressive provisional side branch intervention in bifurcation lesions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 3 years, TVF occurred in 11.7% of the conservative group versus 20.8% of the aggressive group (p = 0.049). Although no significant differences were observed in the incidence of TVF between groups at 1 year (9.4% vs. 9.2%; p = 0.97), landmark analysis between 1 and 3 years showed significantly less TVF in patients assigned to the conservative strategy (2.6% vs. 12.7%; p = 0.004).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports a conservative approach to side branch intervention in provisional stenting, a frequent technical decision.

title: Randomized Trial of Polymer-Free Sirolimus- and Probucol-Eluting Stents Versus Durable Polymer Zotarolimus-Eluting Stents: 5-Year Results of the ISAR-TEST-5 Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial with minimal exclusion criteria; 3,002 patients randomly assigned to polymer-free sirolimus- and probucol-eluting stents versus zotarolimus-eluting stents.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single comparison of two specific stent platforms, so it does not generalise to the stent class.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year results of a large all-comers randomised trial found similar outcomes for a polymer-free sirolimus- and probucol-eluting stent and a durable polymer zotarolimus-eluting stent.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 5 years, there was no difference in the incidence of the primary endpoint between sirolimus- and probucol-eluting stents and zotarolimus-eluting stents (23.8% vs. 24.2%, respectively; hazard ratio: 0.98; 95% confidence interval: 0.84 to 1.15; p = 0.80).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides long-term randomised safety data for a polymer-free stent in an all-comers population.

title: Development and Validation of a Prediction Rule for Benefit and Harm of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Beyond 1 Year After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prediction rule derived in 11,648 randomised DAPT Study patients and externally validated in 8136 patients from the PROTECT trial.
appraisal.main_limitation: Modest discrimination (c statistics of 0.70 and 0.68 in derivation, 0.64 and 0.64 in validation) and no prospective evaluation.
appraisal.one_line: Derivation and validation of a score for ischaemic and bleeding risk with DAPT continuation beyond 1 year after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Among the high score group (score ≥2, n = 5917), continued thienopyridine vs placebo was associated with reduced ischemic events (2.7% vs 5.7%; risk difference [RD], -3.0% [95% CI, -4.1% to -2.0%], P < .001) compared with the low score group (score <2, n = 5731; 1.7% vs 2.3%; RD, -0.7% [95% CI, -1.4% to 0.09%], P = .07; interaction P < .001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It offers a tool for individualising DAPT duration, a common decision.

title: Duration of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy: A Systematic Review for the 2016 ACC/AHA Guideline Focused Update on Duration of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Task Force on Clinical Practice Guidelines.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 randomized controlled trials that enrolled 33 051 patients receiving predominantly newer-generation DES, plus one RCT of 21 162 patients after MI.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract notes that evidence for increased mortality with prolonged DAPT comes from post hoc analyses and is weak.
appraisal.one_line: Systematic review with Bayesian and frequentist analyses supporting the 2016 ACC/AHA focused update on DAPT duration.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Use of DAPT for 12 months, as compared with use for 3 to 6 months, resulted in no significant differences in incidence of death (odds ratio [OR]: 1.17; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.85 to 1.63), major hemorrhage (OR: 1.65; 95% CI: 0.97 to 2.82), MI (OR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.65 to 1.18), or stent thrombosis (OR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.49 to 1.55).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It is the evidence base for the guideline position on DAPT duration after DES and after MI.

title: Duration of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy: A Systematic Review for the 2016 ACC/AHA Guideline Focused Update on Duration of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Task Force on Clinical Practice Guidelines.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 randomized controlled trials that enrolled 33 051 patients receiving predominantly newer-generation DES, plus one RCT of 21 162 patients after MI.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract notes that evidence for increased mortality with prolonged DAPT comes from post hoc analyses and is weak.
appraisal.one_line: Systematic review with Bayesian and frequentist analyses supporting the 2016 ACC/AHA focused update on DAPT duration.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Use of DAPT for 12 months, as compared with use for 3 to 6 months, resulted in no significant differences in incidence of death (odds ratio [OR]: 1.17; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.85 to 1.63), major hemorrhage (OR: 1.65; 95% CI: 0.97 to 2.82), MI (OR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.65 to 1.18), or stent thrombosis (OR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.49 to 1.55).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It is the evidence base for the guideline position on DAPT duration after DES and after MI.

title: Coronary-Artery Bypass Surgery in Patients with Ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 1212 patients with an ejection fraction of 35% or less (610 CABG plus medical therapy, 602 medical therapy alone); median follow-up 9.8 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Patients were enrolled between July 2002 and May 2007, so medical therapy and revascularisation practice predate current standards.
appraisal.one_line: Extended follow-up of a randomised trial of CABG added to medical therapy versus medical therapy alone in ischaemic cardiomyopathy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary outcome event occurred in 359 patients (58.9%) in the CABG group and in 398 patients (66.1%) in the medical-therapy group (hazard ratio with CABG vs. medical therapy, 0.84; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73 to 0.97; P=0.02 by log-rank test).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Long-term mortality benefit of surgical revascularisation in ischaemic cardiomyopathy informs the revascularisation decision in this high-risk group and the comparator for PCI studies.

title: Early Intravenous Beta-Blockers in Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Before Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised double-blind multicentre trial, 683 patients (metoprolol n = 336, placebo n = 346); CMR performed in 342 patients (54.8%).
appraisal.main_limitation: Primary end point was a surrogate (infarct size), and CMR was available in only about half of patients.
appraisal.one_line: Placebo-controlled trial of early intravenous metoprolol before primary PCI in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Infarct size (percent of left ventricle [LV]) by CMR did not differ between the metoprolol (15.3 ± 11.0%) and placebo groups (14.9 ± 11.5%; p = 0.616).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It tests early beta-blockade in a general STEMI population and found no effect on infarct size.

title: Deferred versus conventional stent implantation in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (DANAMI 3-DEFER): an open-label, randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label randomised controlled trial at 4 Danish centres, 1215 patients (612 standard PCI, 603 deferred).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design in four centres.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of deferred versus conventional stent implantation in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Events comprising the primary endpoint occurred in 109 (18%) patients who had standard PCI and in 105 (17%) patients who had deferred stent implantation (hazard ratio 0·99, 95% CI 0·76-1·29; p=0·92).
appraisal.why_it_matters: A neutral result for routine deferred stenting in primary PCI.

title: Radial Access Reduces Mortality in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes: Results From an Updated Trial Sequential Analysis of Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomised trials with trial sequential analysis; seventeen studies, encompassing data from 19,328 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Mortality signal is influenced by a single large trial and operator expertise in radial access.
appraisal.one_line: Trial sequential meta-analysis concluding radial access reduces mortality compared with femoral access in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Radial access was found to reduce mortality (relative risk [RR]: 0.73; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.60 to 0.88; p = 0.001), major adverse cardiovascular events (RR: 0.86; 95% CI: 0.77 to 0.95; p = 0.005), and major bleeding (RR: 0.60; 95% CI: 0.48 to 0.76; p < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs guideline recommendations on radial access as the default strategy in ACS.

title: Safety and Efficacy of New-Generation Drug-Eluting Stents in Women Undergoing Complex Percutaneous Coronary Artery Revascularization: From the WIN-DES Collaborative Patient-Level Pooled Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Patient-level pooled analysis of 26 randomized trials of DES in women; 10,241 women, of whom 4,629 (45%) underwent CPCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Stent generation was not randomised within the pool, so residual confounding is possible.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level pooled analysis of 26 trials in women showing higher risk after complex PCI and a uniform benefit of new-generation DES.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with non-CPCI, women who underwent CPCI had a higher 3-year risk of MACE (adjusted hazard ratio [HR]: 1.63; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.45 to 1.83; p < 0.0001). In women who underwent CPCI, use of new-generation DES was associated with significantly lower 3-year risk of MACE (adjusted HR: 0.81; 95% CI: 0.68 to 0.96).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives sex-specific evidence for stent choice in complex PCI, a group under-represented in trials.

title: Relationship Between Infarct Size and Outcomes Following Primary PCI: Patient-Level Analysis From 10 Randomized Trials.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled patient-level analysis from 10 randomized primary PCI trials, 2,632 patients; median follow-up 352 days.
appraisal.main_limitation: Follow-up of about 1 year, few events, and infarct size measured by two modalities.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled patient-level analysis of infarct size and clinical outcomes after primary PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A strong graded response was present between infarct size (per 5% increase) and subsequent mortality (Cox-adjusted hazard ratio: 1.19 [95% confidence interval: 1.18 to 1.20]; p < 0.0001) and hospitalization for heart failure (adjusted hazard ratio: 1.20 [95% confidence interval: 1.19 to 1.21]; p < 0.0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It supports infarct size as a prognostic measure and a trial endpoint in STEMI.

title: Revascularization in Patients With Multivessel Coronary Artery Disease and Severe Left Ventricular Systolic Dysfunction: Everolimus-Eluting Stents Versus Coronary Artery Bypass Graft Surgery.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry analysis of 4616 patients (1351 everolimus-eluting stent, 3265 CABG); propensity matching identified 2126 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational data with potential residual confounding and a median follow-up of 2.9 years.
appraisal.one_line: Propensity-matched registry comparison of everolimus-eluting stent PCI and CABG in multivessel disease with severe LV dysfunction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At long-term follow-up (median, 2.9 years), PCI was associated with a similar risk of death (HR, 1.01; 95% CI, 0.81-1.28; P=0.91), a higher risk of myocardial infarction (HR, 2.16; 95% CI, 1.42-3.28; P=0.0003), a lower risk of stroke (HR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.33-0.97; P=0.04), and a higher risk of repeat revascularization (HR, 2.54; 95% CI, 1.88-3.44; P<0.0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It addresses a population where randomised comparison is lacking and guidelines favour CABG.

title: Coronary bifurcation lesions treated with simple or complex stenting: 5-year survival from patient-level pooled analysis of the Nordic Bifurcation Study and the British Bifurcation Coronary Study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled patient-level analysis of two randomised trials, 913 patients; follow-up complete for 890.
appraisal.main_limitation: Mortality was not the primary endpoint of the trials, and the abstract gives no hazard ratio or confidence interval.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year mortality from a pooled patient-level analysis of two bifurcation stenting trials.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Five-year mortality was lower among patients who underwent a simple strategy rather than a complex strategy [17 patients (3.8%) vs. 31 patients (7.0%); P = 0.04].
appraisal.why_it_matters: It suggests a long-term mortality signal favouring provisional stenting in bifurcation lesions.

title: Early Stent Thrombosis and Mortality After Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Patient-Level Analysis of 2 Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Patient-level pooled analysis of the HORIZONS-AMI and EUROMAX randomised trials; 4935 patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention with stent implantation at 188 international sites.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc pooling of two trials with differing designs; early stent thrombosis events were few.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level pooled analysis of two STEMI trials associating bivalirudin with more acute stent thrombosis than heparin with or without a GPI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Early ST occurred in 100 patients (2.0%), 20 of whom (20.0%) died. Bivalirudin was associated with higher rates of early ST compared with heparin±GPI (2.5% versus 1.6%, P=0.04), because of more acute (≤24 h) ST (1.5% versus 0.2%, P<0.0001), with the risk limited to the first 4 hours after percutaneous coronary intervention.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Clarifies the mechanism of the stent thrombosis signal with bivalirudin, relevant to anticoagulant choice in primary PCI.

title: Percutaneous coronary intervention for coronary bifurcation disease: 11th consensus document from the European Bifurcation Club.
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus document; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus opinion that rests on mixed trial and observational evidence.
appraisal.one_line: European Bifurcation Club consensus recommending main vessel stenting with proximal optimisation and provisional side branch stenting.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets the reference technical approach for bifurcation PCI in Europe.

title: Biolimus-A9 polymer-free coated stent in high bleeding risk patients with acute coronary syndrome: a Leaders Free ACS sub-study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Sub-study of a randomised trial, 659 ACS patients (BA9-DCS 330, BMS 329) from 2466 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup of a larger trial, and the comparator was a bare-metal stent rather than a current-generation DES.
appraisal.one_line: Pre-specified sub-study of high bleeding risk patients with ACS receiving a polymer-free drug-coated stent or a bare-metal stent with 1-month DAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 12-month follow-up, treatment with the BA9-DCS was more effective (clinically driven target-lesion revascularization 3.9 vs. 9.0%, P = 0.009) and safer (cumulative incidence of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, or definite or probable stent thrombosis 9.3 vs. 18.5%, P = 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It informs stent choice and short DAPT in high bleeding risk patients with ACS.

title: Optimal P2Y12 Inhibitor in Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Undergoing Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Network Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Bayesian network meta-analysis of clinical trials; 37 studies with 88,402 STEMI patients and 5,077 MACE analysed.
appraisal.main_limitation: Indirect comparisons mix randomised and observational studies and may be confounded by trial era and background therapy.
appraisal.one_line: Bayesian network meta-analysis in STEMI favouring prasugrel over clopidogrel and standard ticagrelor for MACE, with both newer agents better than clopidogrel.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Outcomes at 1 month (22 studies and 60,783 patients) suggest that prasugrel was associated with: lower MACE than clopidogrel (standard dose odds ratio [OR]: 0.59, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.50 to 0.69; high-dose OR: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.51 to 0.71; upstream OR: 0.79, 95% CI: 0.66 to 0.94), and ticagrelor (standard dose OR: 0.69, 95% CI: 0.56 to 0.84; upstream OR: 0.72, 95% CI: 0.50 to 1.05).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the choice of P2Y12 inhibitor in primary PCI, where direct head-to-head randomised data were limited.

title: 6-Month Versus 12-Month Dual-Antiplatelet Therapy Following Long Everolimus-Eluting Stent Implantation: The IVUS-XPL Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial at 20 centres in Korea; 1,400 patients (mean total stent length >45 mm) randomly assigned to 6-month (n = 699) or 12-month (n = 701) DAPT.
appraisal.main_limitation: Low event rates limit power for the composite and for stent thrombosis, and the population was Korean.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of 6 versus 12 months of DAPT after long everolimus-eluting stent implantation found no increase in the composite with shorter therapy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 15 patients (2.2%) in the 6-month DAPT group and 14 patients (2.1%) in the 12-month DAPT group (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.07; p = 0.854).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports shorter DAPT even in long-stent, higher-risk lesions, where concern about thrombosis was greatest.

title: Stent Thrombosis With Drug-Eluting Stents and Bioresorbable Scaffolds: Evidence From a Network Meta-Analysis of 147 Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials; 147 trials including 126,526 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Follow-up limited to 1 year for stent thrombosis, and indirect comparisons depend on transitivity.
appraisal.one_line: Large network meta-analysis showing contemporary DES had low stent thrombosis, with the bioresorbable scaffold at higher risk than several metallic DES.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All contemporary DES were superior to BMS and PES in terms of definite or probable stent thrombosis at 1 year. CoCr-EES, PtCr-EES, and H-SES were associated with significantly lower risk than BVS. There were no significant differences regarding all-cause or cardiac mortality.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Ranks the safety of contemporary stent platforms and supports the withdrawal of early scaffolds.

title: Percutaneous Coronary Interventions for the Treatment of Stenoses in Small Coronary Arteries: A Network Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis of randomised trials: 19 trials, 5,072 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: No trial of new-generation drug-eluting stents was available, and the primary outcome was angiographic.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis of randomised trials of PCI strategies for small coronary arteries, limited to early-generation devices.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: SES significantly reduced the risk of target-lesion revascularization compared to PES (odds ratio [OR]: 0.39; 95% CI: 0.16 to 0.93), DCB (OR: 0.34; 95% CI: 0.10 to 0.97), BMS (OR: 0.21; 95% CI: 0.13 to 0.36), and BA (OR: 0.16; 95% CI: 0.09 to 0.29).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Defines the evidence gap for current-generation devices in small vessels.

title: Effect of Post-Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Bivalirudin Infusion on Acute Stent Thrombosis: Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomised trials: 5 trials including 16,294 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few trials with heterogeneous infusion regimens and rare events, giving wide intervals.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis and network meta-analysis of post-PCI bivalirudin infusion dose and acute stent thrombosis in primary PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Continuing Biv-Full gave a risk ratio of 0.90, 95% confidence interval: 0.32 to 2.54; p = 0.852 for acute stent thrombosis. After 30 days, bivalirudin decreased the risk for major bleeding compared with heparin (risk ratio: 0.29; 95% confidence interval: 0.16 to 0.53; p < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a dosing question behind the heparin versus bivalirudin debate in STEMI.

title: Long-Term Mortality After Coronary Revascularization in Nondiabetic Patients With Multivessel Disease.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data from two randomised trials pooled, 1,275 nondiabetic patients; median follow-up 61 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Only two trials were pooled and the subgroup (nondiabetic) was not the original randomisation stratum.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level meta-analysis of CABG versus PCI with drug-eluting stents in nondiabetic patients with multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The risk of death from any cause was significantly lower in the CABG group than in the PCI group (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.65; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.43 to 0.98; p = 0.039).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It informs the PCI versus CABG decision in nondiabetic multivessel disease.

title: Radial Versus Femoral Access for Coronary Interventions Across the Entire Spectrum of Patients With Coronary Artery Disease: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomised trials: Twenty-four studies enrolling 22,843 participants.
appraisal.main_limitation: Study-level pooling with variable trial quality, and the mortality signal is driven by selected trials.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of randomised trials comparing radial and femoral access for coronary intervention across clinical presentations.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Radial access was associated with a significantly lower risk for all-cause mortality (odds ratio [OR]: 0.71; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.59 to 0.87; p = 0.001, number needed to treat to benefit [NNTB] = 160), major bleeding (OR: 0.53; 95% CI: 0.42 to 0.65; p < 0.001) and major vascular complications (OR: 0.23; 95% CI: 0.16 to 0.35; p < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports radial-first access across the whole spectrum of coronary disease.

title: Short-versus long-term Dual Antiplatelet therapy after drug-eluting stent implantation in women versus men: A sex-specific patient-level pooled-analysis of six randomized trials.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled individual patient data from 6 randomized trials: 11,473 randomized patients, 3,454 (30%) women.
appraisal.main_limitation: Interaction tests are underpowered and the trials used different regimens and populations.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level pooled analysis of six DAPT-duration trials testing whether sex modifies the effect of short versus long DAPT after DES.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with long-term DAPT, short-term DAPT was associated with similar rates of MACE in both women (HR 0.88; 95% CI 0.62-1.25) and men (HR 1.25; 95% CI 0.95-1.6; P interaction = 0.08).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs sex-specific DAPT duration, a population question beyond the original trials.

title: Combined Use of Bivalirudin and Radial Access in Acute Coronary Syndromes Is Not Superior to the Use of Either One Separately: Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomised trials: Eight trials with a total of 27,491 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Indirect subgroup comparison across trials with differing access-site mix.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis testing whether bivalirudin and radial access add bleeding benefit when combined in acute coronary syndromes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Bivalirudin reduced major bleeding risk in patients with femoral access (OR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.46 to 0.6; p < 0.001) but not in patients with radial access (OR: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.45 to 1.26; p = 0.28).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Questions the added value of bivalirudin when radial access is used.

title: Very Long-Term (10 to 14 Year) Outcomes After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Versus Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting for Multivessel Coronary Artery Disease in the Bare-Metal Stent Era.

appraisal.design_and_n: Observational registry cohort: 5152 patients (PCI: n=3490 and CABG: n=1662) with multivessel disease, median follow-up 11.2 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised comparison with bare-metal stents, which limits relevance to current practice.
appraisal.one_line: Very long-term comparison of PCI and CABG for multivessel disease in the bare-metal stent era from a Kyoto registry cohort.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The cumulative 10-year incidence of all-cause death was not significantly different between PCI and CABG (32.2% versus 31.7%; log-rank P=0.93). After adjusting for confounders, the mortality risk of PCI was significantly higher than that of CABG (hazard ratio, 1.19 [95% confidence interval, 1.02-1.39]; P=0.03).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides long-term survival data on revascularisation choice, with no late divergence beyond 5 years.

title: Drug-Eluting or Bare-Metal Stents for Coronary Artery Disease.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 9013 patients with stable or unstable coronary artery disease.
appraisal.main_limitation: Primary composite excludes revascularisation, where the stent types differed.
appraisal.one_line: Large randomised comparison found no difference between contemporary drug-eluting and bare-metal stents for death or spontaneous MI, with less repeat revascularisation with drug-eluting stents.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: the rates of the primary outcome were 16.6% in the group receiving drug-eluting stents and 17.1% in the group receiving bare-metal stents (hazard ratio, 0.98; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.88 to 1.09; P=0.66).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs long-term stent choice and the hard-outcome neutrality of drug-eluting stents.

title: Prasugrel Versus Ticagrelor in Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction Treated With Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Multicenter Randomized PRAGUE-18 Study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 1230 patients assigned across 14 sites.
appraisal.main_limitation: Terminated early with broad confidence intervals; primary endpoint at 7 days.
appraisal.one_line: Head-to-head randomised comparison of prasugrel and ticagrelor in primary PCI for acute MI was stopped for futility and showed no difference at 7 days.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The occurrence of the primary end point did not differ between groups receiving prasugrel and ticagrelor (4.0% and 4.1%, respectively; odds ratio, 0.98; 95% confidence interval, 0.55-1.73; P=0.939).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a common choice of P2Y12 inhibitor in STEMI, though underpowered.

title: Effective anti-thrombotic therapy without stenting: intravascular optical coherence tomography-based management in plaque erosion (the EROSION study).

appraisal.design_and_n: Single-centre uncontrolled prospective study; 60 patients enrolled and 55 completed 1-month follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm, single-centre, with an imaging surrogate primary endpoint and short follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: Proof-of-concept study of antithrombotic therapy without stenting for ACS caused by plaque erosion identified by OCT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Forty-seven patients (47/60, 78.3%; 95% confidence interval: 65.8-87.9%) met the primary endpoint.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Signal for a stent-free strategy in a distinct ACS mechanism, supporting a randomised trial.

title: The EBC TWO Study (European Bifurcation Coronary TWO): A Randomized Comparison of Provisional T-Stenting Versus a Systematic 2 Stent Culotte Strategy in Large Caliber True Bifurcations.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial in 20 European centres; Two hundred patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample and 12-month follow-up limit power for a composite of clinical events.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of provisional T-stenting with a systematic culotte strategy in large-calibre true bifurcation lesions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point (a composite of death, myocardial infarction, and target vessel revascularization at 12 months) occurred in 7.7% of the provisional T-stent group versus 10.3% of the culotte group (hazard ratio, 1.02; 95% confidence interval, 0.78-1.34; P=0.53).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It tests the consensus view that complex bifurcations with large side branches need an upfront two-stent technique, and the simpler strategy did not differ on the composite.

title: Outcomes After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention or Bypass Surgery in Patients With Unprotected Left Main Disease.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled individual patient data analysis of two trials, 1,305 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup mortality findings are post hoc and based on small numbers.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled patient-level analysis of two trials of PCI versus CABG in unprotected left main disease, examining outcomes by anatomical complexity.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The incidence of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events at 5 years was 28.3% in the PCI group and 23.0% in the CABG group (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.23; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.01 to 1.55; p = 0.045).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Illustrates how anatomical complexity may modify the PCI versus CABG comparison.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Complex PCI.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled patient-level analysis of 6 randomised trials; 9,577 patients, 1,680 (17.5%) with complex PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis across trials not designed for the question; the complexity definition was post hoc.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled analysis of six DAPT-duration trials suggested long-term DAPT reduced MACE after complex PCI but not after non-complex PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with short-term DAPT, long-term DAPT yielded significant reductions in MACE in the complex PCI group (adjusted HR: 0.56; 95% CI: 0.35 to 0.89) versus the noncomplex PCI group (adjusted HR: 1.01; 95% CI: 0.75 to 1.35; pinteraction = 0.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests whether procedural complexity should guide DAPT duration.

title: Survival After Varying Revascularization Strategies in Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction and Multivessel Coronary Artery Disease: A Pairwise and Network Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Thirty-two studies (13 prospective and 19 retrospective) with 54,148 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Most included studies were observational, so the mortality associations are open to confounding.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis of revascularisation strategies in STEMI with multivessel disease, favouring staged multivessel PCI for mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Pairwise meta-analyses showed that staged MV-PCI was associated with lower short-term and long-term mortality compared with both IRA-only PCI and single stage MV-PCI; the abstract gives no effect estimates.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It summarises the observational evidence on timing of non-culprit revascularisation, a question later addressed by randomised trials.

title: Editor's Choice- Impact of immediate multivessel percutaneous coronary intervention versus culprit lesion intervention on 1-year outcome in patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock: Results of the randomised IABP-SHOCK II trial.
journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective analysis of a randomised trial; 451 (75%) of the total of 600 patients had multivessel coronary artery disease.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised comparison within a trial, with treatment chosen by operators.
appraisal.one_line: Post hoc analysis of IABP-SHOCK II comparing immediate multivessel PCI with culprit lesion PCI in cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 30-day (44.9% vs. 42.3%) and 12-month (54.8% vs. 52.7%) mortality rates did not significantly differ between the two groups; 12-month mortality odds ratio 0.92, 95% confidence intervals 0.69-1.21.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It bears on the strategy later tested in CULPRIT-SHOCK and shows equipoise in multivessel PCI in shock.

title: Bivalirudin or unfractionated heparin in patients with acute coronary syndromes managed invasively with and without ST elevation (MATRIX): randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised open-label trial, 7213 patients with ACS (4010 with and 3203 without ST elevation).
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis of a trial whose overall results were published previously.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified analysis by ST-elevation status found no benefit of bivalirudin over heparin on MACE or net adverse events in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In patients with ST segment elevation, major adverse cardiovascular events occurred in 118 (5.9%) assigned to bivalirudin and 129 (6.5%) assigned to heparin (rate ratio 0.90, 95% confidence interval 0.70 to 1.16; P=0.43)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs anticoagulant choice during invasive ACS management.

title: Percutaneous Intervention for Concurrent Chronic Total Occlusions in Patients With STEMI: The EXPLORE Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 304 patients with STEMI and concurrent CTO (150 CTO PCI, 154 no CTO PCI).
appraisal.main_limitation: Imaging primary endpoints; underpowered for clinical events.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of early CTO PCI after primary PCI for STEMI found no difference in LVEF or LVEDV at 4 months.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 4 months, mean LVEF did not differ between the 2 groups (44.1 ± 12.2% vs. 44.8 ± 11.9%, respectively; p = 0.60).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses non-culprit CTO treatment in STEMI.

title: Effects of Intravascular Ultrasound-Guided Versus Angiography-Guided New-Generation Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation: Meta-Analysis With Individual Patient-Level Data From 2,345 Randomized Patients.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis with individual patient data; the abstract does not state the number of patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Very few events, a wide confidence interval and inclusion of only long lesions or chronic total occlusions.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis with individual patient data of IVUS-guided versus angiography-guided new-generation DES implantation, with benefit confined to complex lesions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Major adverse cardiac events had occurred in 0.4% of the patients who underwent IVUS-guided DES implantation versus 1.2% of those who underwent angiography-guided DES implantation (hazard ratio: 0.36; 95% confidence interval: 0.13 to 0.99; p = 0.040).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Imaging guidance of PCI is a common decision, and IPD pooling allowed tests the single trials could not.

title: The Hybrid Algorithm for Treating Chronic Total Occlusions in Europe: The RECHARGE Registry.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicentre registry; 1,253 CTO-PCIs in 1,177 patients at 17 centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: In-hospital outcomes only, from operators already experienced in CTO PCI.
appraisal.one_line: RECHARGE registry validates the hybrid CTO PCI algorithm across European centres.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Overall procedure success was 86% and major in-hospital complications occurred in 2.6%.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides benchmark success and complication rates for contemporary CTO PCI.

title: Everolimus-Eluting Stents or Bypass Surgery for Left Main Coronary Artery Disease.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised noninferiority trial, 1905 patients (948 PCI, 957 CABG).
appraisal.main_limitation: Restricted to site-assessed SYNTAX score of 32 or lower; the secondary composite including revascularisation at 3 years was 23.1% with PCI and 19.1% with CABG; industry-funded.
appraisal.one_line: PCI with everolimus-eluting stents was noninferior to CABG for death, stroke or MI at 3 years in left main disease of low or intermediate anatomical complexity.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 3 years, a primary end-point event had occurred in 15.4% of the patients in the PCI group and in 14.7% of the patients in the CABG group (difference, 0.7 percentage points; upper 97.5% confidence limit, 4.0 percentage points; P=0.02 for noninferiority; hazard ratio, 1.00; 95% confidence interval, 0.79 to 1.26; P=0.98 for superiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears directly on the PCI versus CABG decision for left main disease and on guideline recommendations for it.

title: Optical coherence tomography compared with intravascular ultrasound and with angiography to guide coronary stent implantation (ILUMIEN III: OPTIMIZE PCI): a randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised three-arm trial, 450 patients randomly allocated (158 OCT, 146 IVUS, 146 angiography).
appraisal.main_limitation: Surrogate primary endpoint of stent area; not powered for clinical events.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of OCT-, IVUS- and angiography-guided stent implantation found OCT noninferior to IVUS for minimum stent area.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: OCT guidance was non-inferior to IVUS guidance (one-sided 97·5% lower CI -0·70 mm2; p=0·001), but not superior (p=0·42).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports intravascular imaging use and motivates outcome trials.

title: Percutaneous coronary angioplasty versus coronary artery bypass grafting in treatment of unprotected left main stenosis (NOBLE): a prospective, randomised, open-label, non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised open-label noninferiority trial, 1201 patients randomly assigned (598 PCI, 603 CABG).
appraisal.main_limitation: MACCE included repeat revascularisation; the device used differed from other left main trials.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial in left main disease found PCI did not meet noninferiority to CABG for MACCE at up to 5 years.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Kaplan-Meier 5 year estimates of MACCE were 29% for PCI (121 events) and 19% for CABG (81 events), HR 1·48 (95% CI 1·11-1·96), exceeding the limit for non-inferiority
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds conflicting evidence to the left main PCI versus CABG debate.

title: Timing of Coronary Invasive Strategy in Non-ST-Segment Elevation Acute Coronary Syndromes and Clinical Outcomes: An Updated Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomised trials; the abstract does not state the number of patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Heterogeneity in the definition of early and delayed timing across trials.
appraisal.one_line: Updated meta-analysis of early versus delayed invasive strategy in NSTE-ACS finding no difference in death or myocardial infarction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There was no difference in the primary endpoint of mortality (4% vs. 4.7%; random-effects odds ratio [OR]: 0.85; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.67 to 1.09; p = 0.20; I2 = 0%). Recurrent ischemia or refractory angina was lower with an early strategy (3.8% vs. 5.8%; random-effects OR: 0.54; 95% CI: 0.40 to 0.74; p < 0.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Timing of angiography in NSTE-ACS is a daily decision and guideline recommendations depend on this evidence.

title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Using Drug-Eluting Stents Versus Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting for Unprotected Left Main Coronary Artery Stenosis: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Five randomised trials; In total, 4594 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level data with short follow-up and low-surgical-risk populations.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of randomised trials of DES-PCI versus CABG for unprotected left main stenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There was no significant difference in the primary safety end point between the revascularization strategies (odds ratio [OR], 0.97; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.79-1.17; P=0.73). PCI had higher repeat revascularization (OR, 1.85; 95% CI, 1.53-2.23; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Left main revascularisation choice is contested in guidelines, so pooled estimates matter.

title: Thrombus Aspiration in ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: An Individual Patient Meta-Analysis: Thrombectomy Trialists Collaboration.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data meta-analysis of 3 trials; 19 047 patients enrolled, 18 306 in the primary analysis.
appraisal.main_limitation: High-thrombus-burden subgroup findings had interaction P values of 0.32 and 0.34.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient meta-analysis of three large trials found routine thrombus aspiration in STEMI did not improve clinical outcomes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Cardiovascular death at 30 days occurred in 221 of 9155 patients (2.4%) randomized to thrombus aspiration and 262 of 9151 (2.9%) randomized to PCI alone (hazard ratio, 0.84; 95% confidence interval, 0.70-1.01; P=0.06).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Settles routine use of thrombus aspiration in STEMI.

title: Prevention of Bleeding in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation Undergoing PCI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised three-arm trial, 2124 participants.
appraisal.main_limitation: Not powered for efficacy; broad confidence intervals for ischaemic outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial in atrial fibrillation after PCI found less clinically significant bleeding with rivaroxaban-based regimens than with a vitamin K antagonist plus DAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: hazard ratio for group 1 vs. group 3, 0.59; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.47 to 0.76; P<0.001; hazard ratio for group 2 vs. group 3, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.50 to 0.80; P<0.001
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs antithrombotic regimen choice in a common PCI population.

title: Risk Associated With Surgery Within 12 Months After Coronary Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry linkage; 4,303 DES-PCI-treated patients with surgery compared with 20,232 controls.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational with comparison to patients without ischaemic heart disease, so stent and disease effects are not separated.
appraisal.one_line: Danish registry analysis of surgical risk within 12 months after DES-PCI, suggesting risk is concentrated in the first month.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Surgery in DES-PCI-treated patients was associated with an increased risk of MI (1.6% vs. 0.2%; odds ratio [OR]: 4.82; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.25 to 7.16).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on the guideline recommendation to delay surgery for at least 6 months after DES.

title: Coronary Artery Bypass Surgery Versus Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation for Left Main or Multivessel Coronary Artery Disease: A Meta-Analysis of Individual Patient Data.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled analysis of randomised trials; median follow-up was 60 months, and follow-up was completed for 96.2% of patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: The interval is borderline and the treatment effect varied by disease type, so subgroup findings are exploratory.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled analysis comparing CABG with DES-PCI in left main or multivessel disease, with five-year outcomes favouring CABG in multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The rate of primary outcome was significantly lower with CABG than with PCI (13.0% vs. 16.0%; hazard ratio [HR]: 0.83; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.69 to 1.00; p = 0.046).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Individual-level pooling gives long-term evidence on a high-stakes choice between PCI and CABG.

title: Culprit Vessel Versus Multivessel Versus In-Hospital Staged Intervention for Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction and Multivessel Disease: Stratified Analyses in High-Risk Patient Groups and Anatomic Subsets of Nonculprit Disease.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis; the abstract does not state the number of patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Includes non-randomised data, so associations may be confounded.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis comparing culprit-only, multivessel and staged strategies in STEMI with multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with MVI, CVI-O (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.78; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.64 to 0.97; p = 0.023) and CVI-S (HR: 0.55; 95% CI: 0.36 to 0.82; p = 0.004) were associated with lower mortality.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It informs the timing of non-culprit revascularisation, a decision with little randomised evidence at the time.

title: Three, six, or twelve months of dual antiplatelet therapy after DES implantation in patients with or without acute coronary syndromes: an individual patient data pairwise and network meta-analysis of six randomized trials and 11 473 patients.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data pairwise and network meta-analysis of six trials; 11 473 randomized patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trials used aspirin plus clopidogrel and enrolled relatively low-risk ACS patients.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level pairwise and network meta-analysis of DAPT duration found the optimal duration differed by clinical presentation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In ACS patients, ≤6-month DAPT was associated with non-significantly higher 1-year rates of MI or ST compared with 1-year DAPT (Hazard Ratio (HR) 1.48, 95% Confidence interval (CI) 0.98-2.22; P = 0.059)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs DAPT duration by presentation.

title: Registry-Based Prospective, Active Surveillance of Medical-Device Safety.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective propensity-matched surveillance of the CathPCI Registry; 73,124 patients received Mynx devices.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised and limited to registry-captured vascular outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Prospective registry surveillance identified a safety signal for the Mynx vascular-closure device after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The Mynx device was associated with a significantly greater risk of any vascular complication than were alternative vascular-closure devices (absolute risk, 1.2% vs. 0.8%; relative risk, 1.59; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.42 to 1.78; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Demonstrates registry-based active device surveillance as a model for post-market safety.

title: Clinical Outcome of Double Kissing Crush Versus Provisional Stenting of Coronary Artery Bifurcation Lesions: The 5-Year Follow-Up Results From a Randomized and Multicenter DKCRUSH-II Study (Randomized Study on Double Kissing Crush Technique Versus Provisional Stenting Technique for Coronary Artery Bifurcation Lesions).

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; A total of 370 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single technique comparison with a borderline primary result and subgroup analysis by lesion complexity.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year follow-up of the DKCRUSH-II trial comparing double kissing crush with provisional stenting in bifurcation lesions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 5 years, the major adverse cardiac event rate (23.8%) in the provisional stenting group was insignificantly different to that of the double kissing group (15.7%; P=0.051). Target lesion revascularization was 16.2% versus 8.6% (P=0.027).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Long-term data on two-stent techniques in complex bifurcations inform strategy choice.

title: Complete or Culprit-Only Revascularization for Patients With Multivessel Coronary Artery Disease Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Pairwise and Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis; 10 trials with 2,285 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trials with benefit driven by urgent revascularisation rather than death or reinfarction.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis of complete versus culprit-only revascularisation in multivessel disease at PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Complete revascularization was associated with a lower risk of major adverse cardiac events (MACE) (RR: 0.57; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.42 to 0.77), due to lower risk of urgent revascularization (RR: 0.44; 95% CI: 0.30 to 0.66). All-cause mortality was similar (RR: 0.76; 95% CI: 0.52 to 1.12).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It summarises randomised evidence on timing and extent of revascularisation in multivessel disease.

title: Percutaneous coronary intervention or coronary artery bypass grafting for unprotected left main coronary artery disease.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of six randomised trials with 4,700 patients and a mean SYNTAX score of 23.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level data with DerSimonian and Laird pooling and no individual patient data to examine time-varying effects.
appraisal.one_line: Updated meta-analysis of randomised trials comparing PCI with CABG for unprotected left main disease, with outcomes by follow-up period.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At short-term follow-up, the risk of MACCE was lower with PCI (RR 0.55, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.39-0.76). At long-term follow-up, PCI was associated with a higher risk of MACCE (RR 1.19, 95% CI 1.01-1.41), due to a higher risk of revascularization (RR 1.62, 95% CI 1.34-1.94).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Summarises the early benefit and late disadvantage of PCI against CABG in left main disease, a decision on which trials have been discrepant.

title: Long-term outcomes of provisional stenting compared with a two-stent strategy for bifurcation lesions: a meta-analysis of randomised trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of eight RCTs with a total of 2778 patients, mean follow-up 3.0±1.6 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level pooling of heterogeneous bifurcation techniques with a borderline mortality signal and few events.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of randomised trials comparing provisional stenting with a two-stent strategy for bifurcation lesions at long-term follow-up.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Provisional stenting was associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality (RR=0.66; 95% CI 0.45 to 0.98; p=0.04) compared with a two-stent strategy.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides the first pooled long-term randomised comparison of bifurcation strategies, with a mortality signal that favours the simpler technique.

title: Fractional Flow Reserve-Guided Multivessel Angioplasty in Myocardial Infarction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 885 patients (295 complete revascularisation, 590 infarct artery only).
appraisal.main_limitation: Composite driven by repeat revascularisation; deaths and MI did not differ significantly.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of FFR-guided complete revascularisation in STEMI with multivessel disease found a lower composite, driven by revascularisation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: hazard ratio, 0.35; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.22 to 0.55; P<0.001
appraisal.why_it_matters: Relevant to complete revascularisation strategy in STEMI.

title: Instantaneous Wave-free Ratio versus Fractional Flow Reserve to Guide PCI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry-based randomised open-label trial, 2037 participants.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label with 12-month follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: Registry-based randomised trial found iFR noninferior to FFR for 12-month MACE.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary end-point event occurred in 68 of 1012 patients (6.7%) in the iFR group and in 61 of 1007 (6.1%) in the FFR group (difference in event rates, 0.7 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.5 to 2.8; P=0.007 for noninferiority; hazard ratio, 1.12; 95% CI, 0.79 to 1.58; P=0.53)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Concordant with a parallel trial of the same comparison, strengthening support for iFR.

title: Use of the Instantaneous Wave-free Ratio or Fractional Flow Reserve in PCI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised noninferiority trial, 2492 patients with coronary artery disease.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design with 1-year follow-up and a noninferiority margin of 3.4 percentage points.
appraisal.one_line: iFR-guided revascularisation was noninferior to FFR-guided revascularisation for 1-year major adverse cardiac events, with fewer procedural symptoms.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: the primary end point had occurred in 78 of 1148 patients (6.8%) in the iFR group and in 83 of 1182 patients (7.0%) in the FFR group (difference in risk, -0.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -2.3 to 1.8; P<0.001 for noninferiority; hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.68 to 1.33; P=0.78).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Physiology-guided PCI is a very common decision, and a noninferior adenosine-free index supports guideline use of iFR alongside FFR.

title: Fractional Flow Reserve and Cardiac Events in Coronary Artery Disease: Data From a Prospective IRIS-FFR Registry (Interventional Cardiology Research Incooperation Society Fractional Flow Reserve).

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective registry (IRIS-FFR), 5846 patients; revascularisation deferred in 6468 lesions and performed in 2165 lesions.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised lesion-level comparison with confounding by indication.
appraisal.one_line: In a large FFR registry, revascularisation was associated with fewer events than deferral at FFR 0.75 or below but not above 0.76.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: For lesions with FFR ≥0.76 the risk of major adverse cardiac events was not significantly different between deferred and revascularized lesions; for FFR 0.71-0.75, adjusted hazard ratio, 0.47; 95% confidence interval, 0.24-0.89; for FFR ≤0.70, adjusted hazard ratio 0.47; 95% confidence interval, 0.26-0.84.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on the FFR revascularisation threshold in routine practice.

title: Bioresorbable Scaffolds versus Metallic Stents in Routine PCI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Investigator-initiated randomised trial; 1845 patients (924 scaffold, 921 metallic stent); median follow-up 707 days.
appraisal.main_limitation: Preliminary report with descriptive event data after early stopping on safety grounds.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of an everolimus-eluting bioresorbable scaffold against a metallic stent in routine PCI, reported early after safety concerns.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Target-vessel failure occurred in 105 patients in the scaffold group and in 94 patients in the stent group (2-year cumulative event rates, 11.7% and 10.7%, respectively; hazard ratio, 1.12; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.85 to 1.48; P=0.43). Definite or probable device thrombosis occurred in 31 patients in the scaffold group as compared with 8 patients in the stent group (2-year cumulative event rates, 3.5% vs. 0.9%; hazard ratio, 3.87; 95% CI, 1.78 to 8.42; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: The scaffold did not differ on target-vessel failure but was associated with more device thrombosis, adding randomised evidence on the safety of this device class in routine practice.

title: Fractional Flow Reserve-Guided Complete Revascularization Improves the Prognosis in Patients With ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction and Severe Nonculprit Disease: A DANAMI 3-PRIMULTI Substudy (Primary PCI in Patients With ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction and Multivessel Disease: Treatment of Culprit Lesion Only or Complete Revascularization).

appraisal.design_and_n: Substudy of DANAMI-3-PRIMULTI, in which 627 STEMI patients were randomized to fractional flow reserve-guided complete revascularization or infarct-related PCI only.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc, unadjusted for multiplicity and underpowered for subgroup interaction testing.
