appraisal.one_line: Post hoc analysis of DANAMI-3-PRIMULTI showing that the benefit of FFR-guided complete revascularisation in STEMI varied with disease extent and stenosis severity.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In patients with 3-vessel disease, fractional flow reserve-guided complete revascularization reduced the primary end point (hazard ratio [HR], 0.33; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.17-0.64; P=0.001), with no significant effect in patients with 2-vessel disease (HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.47-1.26; P=0.29; P for interaction =0.046).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Suggests effect modification of complete revascularisation by disease burden, which is hypothesis-generating for patient selection.

title: Infarct size, left ventricular function, and prognosis in women compared to men after primary percutaneous coronary intervention in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: results from an individual patient-level pooled analysis of 10 randomized trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled patient-level data from 10 randomized primary PCI trials; 2632 patients with STEMI, 587 (22.3%) women; outcomes at 1 year.
appraisal.main_limitation: Infarct size was measured by two imaging methods in different trials, and the analysis is observational in nature within the pooled data.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level pooled analysis of 10 primary PCI trials examining whether infarct size explains the poorer outcomes of women after STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Women had a higher 1-year rate of death or HF hospitalization compared to men, and infarct size was a strong independent predictor of 1-year death or HF hospitalization (P < 0.0001), with no interaction between sex and infarct size or LVEF. The abstract does not report an effect estimate for the sex difference.
appraisal.why_it_matters: The excess risk in women was not explained by infarct size or ventricular function, which points to other mechanisms and supports questions on sex-specific care after STEMI.

title: Everolimus-Eluting Bioresorbable Scaffolds Versus Everolimus-Eluting Metallic Stents.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomised trials; seven trials, 5,583 patients (3,261 scaffold, 2,322 stent); median follow-up 2 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Aggregate trial-level data with median follow-up of only 2 years.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of seven trials comparing bioresorbable scaffolds with metallic everolimus-eluting stents at up to 3 years.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with metallic EES, risk of target lesion failure (9.6% vs. 7.2%; absolute risk difference: +2.4%; risk ratio: 1.32; 95% confidence interval: 1.10 to 1.59; number needed to harm: 41; p = 0.003; I2 = 0%) and stent thrombosis (2.4% vs. 0.7%; absolute risk difference: +1.7%; risk ratio: 3.15; 95% confidence interval: 1.87 to 5.30; number needed to harm: 60; p < 0.0001; I2 = 0%) were both significantly higher with BVS.
appraisal.why_it_matters: The pooled trials show higher target lesion failure and stent thrombosis with the scaffold, which informs device regulation and clinical use.

title: Bleeding-Related Deaths in Relation to the Duration of Dual-Antiplatelet Therapy After Coronary Stenting.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of RCTs; individual patient data for 6 RCTs and aggregate data for 12 RCTs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Attribution of death to bleeding relied on timing within 1 year of a bleeding episode, and the link between bleeding and death is observational.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis with individual patient data linking bleeding, mortality and DAPT duration after drug-eluting stent implantation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Bleeding was an independent predictor of mortality within 1 year of the bleeding episode (hazard ratio: 6.93; 95% confidence interval: 4.53 to 10.60; p < 0.0001). Shorter DAPT was associated with lower rates of bleeding-related deaths compared with prolonged DAPT (hazard ratio: 0.65; 95% confidence interval: 0.43 to 0.99; p = 0.04).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It offers a mechanistic account of why shorter DAPT has been associated with lower all-cause mortality in trials of DAPT duration.

title: Long-Term Efficacy and Safety of Everolimus-Eluting Bioresorbable Vascular Scaffolds Versus Everolimus-Eluting Metallic Stents: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of six trials with 5392 patients (mean follow-up, 25 months).
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level pooling with follow-up of about two years and a single scaffold type.
appraisal.one_line: Long-term meta-analysis of randomised trials showing worse outcomes with bioresorbable scaffolds than with everolimus-eluting metallic stents.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: BVS had a higher rate of target lesion failure (RR, 1.33; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.11-1.58). The risk of definite or probable stent/scaffold thrombosis (RR, 3.22; 95% CI, 1.89-5.49) and very late stent/scaffold thrombosis (>1 year; RR, 4.78; 95% CI, 1.66-13.8) was higher with BVS.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Quantifies late thrombosis and failure with the scaffold, informing device use and regulatory decisions.

title: Preventive Strategies for Contrast-Induced Acute Kidney Injury in Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Procedures: Evidence From a Hierarchical Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis of 124 Trials and 28 240 Patients.

appraisal.design_and_n: Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis of 124 trials (28 240 patients) comparing 10 strategies.
appraisal.main_limitation: Many small trials of variable quality, with high heterogeneity and probable publication bias for some comparisons, and a surrogate renal endpoint.
appraisal.one_line: Bayesian network meta-analysis ranking preventive strategies for contrast-induced acute kidney injury in coronary procedures.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with saline, the risk of CIAKI was reduced by using statin (odds ratio [OR], 0.42; 95% credible interval [CrI], 0.26-0.67), NAC+NaHCO3 (OR, 0.50; 95% CrI, 0.33-0.76), NAC (OR, 0.68; 95% CrI, 0.55-0.84), and NaHCO3 (OR, 0.66; 95% CrI, 0.47-0.90).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Largest network synthesis of CIAKI prevention, with a signal for statins that was robust to sensitivity analyses.

title: Geographical Difference of the Interaction of Sex With Treatment Strategy in Patients With Multivessel Disease and Left Main Disease: A Meta-Analysis From SYNTAX (Synergy Between PCI With Taxus and Cardiac Surgery), PRECOMBAT (Bypass Surgery Versus Angioplasty Using Sirolimus-Eluting Stent in Patients With Left Main Coronary Artery Disease), and BEST (Bypass Surgery and Everolimus-Eluting Stent Implantation in the Treatment of Patients With Multivessel Coronary Artery Disease) Randomized Controlled Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled patient-level analysis (n=3280) of SYNTAX, PRECOMBAT and BEST; 794 patients (24.2%) were women.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis by sex across trials that differ in era, devices and region, so geography and trial design are confounded.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level pooled analysis of three randomised trials showing heterogeneity of the sex-by-strategy interaction between Western and Asian populations in multivessel and left main disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In the Western trial (SYNTAX), female sex favored coronary artery bypass graft compared with percutaneous coronary intervention (hazard ratio(percutaneous coronary intervention) 2.213; 95% confidence interval, 1.242-3.943; P=0.007), whereas in the Asian women (PRECOMBAT and BEST), the treatment effect was neutral between both strategies.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Raises the possibility that the PCI versus CABG effect in women differs by region, relevant to transportability of trial results.

title: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Continuation Beyond 1 Year After Drug-Eluting Stents: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of four trials comprising 17 650 participants.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few trials with differing stent types and drugs, and trial-level data only.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of randomised trials of DAPT continued beyond one year after drug-eluting stents, using frequentist and Bayesian methods.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Extended DAPT did not affect all-cause mortality (odds ratio [OR], 1.11; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.79-1.5; P=0.53), was associated with a reduction in the risk of myocardial infarction (OR, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.43-0.73; P<0.001) and an increased risk of major bleeding (OR, 1.49; 95% CI, 1.06-2.11; P=0.02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Summarises the ischaemic benefit and bleeding cost of prolonged DAPT that underpins duration decisions.

title: Influence of radial versus femoral access site on coronary angiography and intervention outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 48 studies with 29,446 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Most studies had high risk of detection bias, and heterogeneity was significant for vascular complications and procedural failure.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of randomised trials comparing radial with femoral access for coronary angiography and PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There was a significant reduction of MACE with RA versus FA (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.77-0.95, I2 = 0%), driven by a reduction in death, but not MI or stroke. MB occurred less frequently with RA (RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.44-0.67, I2 = 4%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports radial access as the default route, with a mortality signal that earlier trials could not show.

title: Myocardial Damage in Patients With Deferred Stenting After STEMI: A DANAMI-3-DEFER Substudy.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Substudy of a randomized trial; 510 patients with STEMI randomized to deferred versus immediate stent implantation; primary endpoint final infarct size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Surrogate imaging endpoint, and the stent length subgroup finding came from a post hoc analysis.
appraisal.one_line: Cardiac magnetic resonance substudy of a randomised trial of deferred versus immediate stenting in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Deferred stenting did not reduce final infarct size (9% left ventricle [LV]; interquartile range [IQR]: 3% to 18% vs. 10% LV; IQR: 3% to 18%; p = 0.67). The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Routine deferred stenting did not reduce infarct size or microvascular obstruction, which does not support the strategy in primary PCI.

title: Revascularisation compared with initial medical therapy for non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndromes in the elderly: a meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Four randomised trials and three observational studies enrolling a total of 20 540 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Mixes observational and randomised data, and few randomised trials contribute to the mortality estimate.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of randomised and observational studies of routine invasive management versus initial medical therapy in older patients with NSTE-ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Analyses restricted to randomised controlled trials (RCTs) confirmed a reduction in MI (OR 0.51, CI 0.40 to 0.66), revascularisation (OR 0.27, CI 0.13 to 0.56) and a trend to reduced mortality (OR 0.84, CI 0.66 to 1.06) at the expense of major bleeding (OR 2.19, CI 1.12 to 4.28).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a population underrepresented in trials, in which the benefit of invasive management remains contested.

title: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy for 6 Versus 18 Months After Biodegradable Polymer Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised trial of 3,773 patients; intention-to-treat analysis in 3,307 patients followed for at least 6 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, wide noninferiority margin and a low event rate.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised noninferiority trial of 6 versus 18 months of DAPT after a biodegradable polymer drug-eluting stent.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: NACCE occurred in 34 patients (2.1%) receiving short-term DAPT and 24 patients (1.5%) receiving long-term DAPT (difference 0.6%, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.5 to 0.3). Noninferiority of short-term DAPT was confirmed.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds randomised evidence on shortened DAPT duration after a contemporary DES, relevant to strategy decisions.

title: 6- Versus 24-Month Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Implantation of Drug-Eluting Stents in Patients Nonresistant to Aspirin: Final Results of the ITALIC Trial (Is There a Life for DES After Discontinuation of Clopidogrel).

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised trial in which 926 were randomized to 6-month and 924 to 24-month DAPT.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, underpowered for individual components, and restricted to aspirin-sensitive patients.
appraisal.one_line: Two-year results of the ITALIC randomised trial comparing 6 with 24 months of DAPT after second-generation drug-eluting stents.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 2 years, the composite endpoint was unchanged, at 3.5% for 6 months and 3.7% for 24 months (p = 0.79). There was a trend toward higher mortality with longer DAPT (2.2% vs. 1.2%; p = 0.11).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports short DAPT after contemporary DES with no ischaemic penalty over two years.

title: Multivessel versus culprit lesion only percutaneous coronary intervention in cardiogenic shock complicating acute myocardial infarction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of 10 cohort studies including 6051 patients, 1194 (19.7%) with MV-PCI and 4857 (80.3%) with C-PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: No randomised trials and probable treatment selection bias in the contributing cohorts.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of cohort studies comparing multivessel with culprit-only PCI in cardiogenic shock after myocardial infarction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Short-term mortality was 37.5% in patients undergoing MV-PCI compared with 28.8% in C-PCI patients (risk ratio 1.26, 95% confidence interval 1.12-1.41, p=0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Pooled observational signal against immediate multivessel PCI in shock, ahead of the randomised trial in this setting.

title: 2-year outcomes with the Absorb bioresorbable scaffold for treatment of coronary artery disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis of seven randomised trials with an individual patient data substudy.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials; seven trials, 5583 patients (3261 Absorb BVS, 2299 to 2281 evaluable for individual outcomes); individual patient data from the four ABSORB trials for landmark analyses.
appraisal.main_limitation: Follow-up limited to 2 years, with industry funding and data partly drawn from presentations and registries.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of seven randomised trials, with individual patient data from four, on 2-year outcomes of the Absorb scaffold against metallic everolimus-eluting stents.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: BVS had higher 2-year relative risks of the device-oriented composite endpoint than did EES (9·4% [304 of 3217] vs 7·4% [169 of 2299]; relative risk [RR] 1·29 [95% CI 1·08-1·56], p=0·0059). The cumulative 2-year incidence of device thrombosis was higher with BVS than with EES (2·3% [73 of 3187] vs 0·7% [16 of 2281]; RR 3·35 [95% CI 1·96-5·72], p<0·0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: The scaffold was associated with more device-oriented events and device thrombosis, including between 1 and 2 years, which informed withdrawal of the device from routine use.

title: Optimal timing of an invasive strategy in patients with non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome: a meta-analysis of randomised trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomised trials, with individual patient data or standardised tabulated data; eight trials (n=5324 patients); median follow-up 180 days (IQR 180-360); PROSPERO CRD42015018988.
appraisal.main_limitation: The high-risk subgroup findings were pre-specified but tests for interaction were inconclusive, and follow-up was a median of 180 days.
appraisal.one_line: Collaborative meta-analysis of eight trials finds no overall mortality reduction with early versus delayed invasive management of NSTE-ACS but possible benefit in high-risk subgroups.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Overall, there was no significant mortality reduction in the early invasive group compared with the delayed invasive group HR 0·81, 95% CI 0·64-1·03; p=0·0879).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It addresses the timing of angiography in NSTE-ACS, a common decision on which guidelines differ, and suggests that urgency should be targeted at higher-risk patients.

title: Outcome of percutaneous coronary intervention with the Absorb bioresorbable scaffold: data from the Swedish Coronary Angiography and Angioplasty Registry (SCAAR).
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort from the Swedish Coronary Angiography and Angioplasty Registry: Absorb BRS (n=810) compared with modern DES (n=67,909), mean follow-up two years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational comparison with residual confounding, and non-compliance with DAPT guidelines was noted.
appraisal.one_line: Nationwide registry comparison of the Absorb scaffold with modern drug-eluting stents, showing higher definite stent thrombosis with the scaffold.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The Absorb BRS was associated with a higher crude incidence of definite ST at stent level: 1.5 vs. 0.6%, hazard ratio (HR) 2.38 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.34-4.23), adjusted HR 4.34 (95% CI: 2.37-7.94); p<0.001.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Confirms in unselected national practice the late thrombosis signal seen in randomised trials of the scaffold.

title: Prognostic Value of Fractional Flow Reserve Measured Immediately After Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation.

appraisal.design_and_n: Analysis of FAME 1 and FAME 2 trial patients with post-PCI FFR: Eight hundred thirty-eight vessels in 639 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised exposure within trial cohorts, with the adjusted association for target vessel revascularisation not significant and a low positive likelihood ratio.
appraisal.one_line: Post hoc analysis of FAME 1 and 2 relating post-PCI fractional flow reserve to two-year vessel outcomes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Comparing the 2-year outcome of lower and upper tertiles of post-PCI FFR significant difference was found favoring upper tertile in terms of overall vessel-oriented composite end point (9.2% versus 3.8%, respectively; hazard ratio, 1.46; 95% confidence interval, 1.02-2.08; P=0.037).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Suggests post-stent physiology has prognostic value, which could guide optimisation after PCI.

title: Perioperative acute myocardial infarction associated with non-cardiac surgery.

appraisal.design_and_n: National Inpatient Sample analysis, 9 566 277 hospitalizations for major non-cardiac surgery; propensity-matched cohort of 34 650 patients with perioperative AMI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Administrative data with in-hospital outcomes only and likely confounding by indication and immortal time.
appraisal.one_line: Large US administrative analysis linked invasive management of perioperative MI after noncardiac surgery with lower in-hospital mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Perioperative AMI occurred in 84 093 (0.88%); in the propensity-matched cohort, invasive management was associated with lower mortality than conservative management (8.9% vs. 18.1%, P < 0.001; OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.41-0.47).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Highlights an unsettled management question for perioperative MI that no trial has addressed.

title: Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection: Clinical Outcomes and Risk of Recurrence.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective single-centre cohort (Vancouver General Hospital), 327 SCAD patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-centre observational study with no randomised evidence on medical therapy.
appraisal.one_line: A large prospective SCAD cohort showed frequent long-term events, with hypertension and absence of beta-blocker use associated with recurrence.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Median long-term follow-up was 3.1 years, and overall major adverse cardiac event rate was 19.9%; recurrent SCAD occurred in 10.4% of patients; hypertension increased (hazard ratio: 2.46; p = 0.011) and beta-blocker use diminished (hazard ratio: 0.36; p = 0.004) recurrent SCAD.
appraisal.why_it_matters: SCAD management is guided by observational data only, so these findings shape secondary prevention practice.

title: Risk of Early Adverse Events After Clopidogrel Discontinuation in Patients Undergoing Short-Term Dual Antiplatelet Therapy: An Individual Participant Data Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual participant data analysis of 11,473 PCI patients from 6 randomized trials, plus an aggregate meta-analysis of 11 trials including 38,919 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few early events limit precision, and trials differed in design and stent type.
appraisal.one_line: Individual participant data analysis testing for a rebound of ischaemic events after clopidogrel discontinuation following short-term DAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: During the first 90 days following clopidogrel discontinuation, there was no significant increase in the risk of MACCE between patients randomized to short-term DAPT compared with long-term DAPT (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.18; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.71 to 1.98; p = 0.52).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses safety of DAPT de-escalation by showing no early rebound after stopping clopidogrel at 3 or 6 months.

title: Dual Antithrombotic Therapy with Dabigatran after PCI in Atrial Fibrillation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised trial; 2725 patients with atrial fibrillation who had undergone PCI; mean follow-up 14 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, with the noninferiority margin for thromboembolic events and the sample size leaving wide uncertainty for individual ischaemic events.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial showing that dual therapy with dabigatran and a P2Y12 inhibitor caused less bleeding than warfarin-based triple therapy after PCI in atrial fibrillation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The incidence of the primary end point was 15.4% in the 110-mg dual-therapy group as compared with 26.9% in the triple-therapy group (hazard ratio, 0.52; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.63; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P<0.001 for superiority) and 20.2% in the 150-mg dual-therapy group as compared with 25.7% in the corresponding triple-therapy group, which did not include elderly patients outside the United States (hazard ratio, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.88; P<0.001 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It addresses the antithrombotic regimen after PCI in a large, common population and supports removing aspirin early to reduce bleeding.

title: Bivalirudin versus Heparin Monotherapy in Myocardial Infarction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicenter, randomized, registry-based, open-label clinical trial; 6006 patients (3005 STEMI and 3001 NSTEMI).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design with 180-day follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: Registry-based randomised comparison of bivalirudin and heparin monotherapy during PCI for myocardial infarction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 180 days, a primary end-point event had occurred in 12.3% of the patients (369 of 3004) in the bivalirudin group and in 12.8% (383 of 3002) in the heparin group (hazard ratio, 0.96; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.83 to 1.10; P=0.54).
appraisal.why_it_matters: In a contemporary radial-access, potent-P2Y12 setting, bivalirudin offered no advantage over heparin alone, which simplifies anticoagulation choice in MI.

title: Ultrathin, bioresorbable polymer sirolimus-eluting stents versus thin, durable polymer everolimus-eluting stents in patients undergoing coronary revascularisation (BIOFLOW V): a randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: International randomised trial (2:1) in 90 hospitals; 1334 patients randomly assigned (884 bioresorbable polymer stent, 450 durable polymer stent).
appraisal.main_limitation: Industry-funded, with the primary non-inferiority comparison relying on Bayesian borrowing from two additional trials and follow-up limited to 12 months.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of an ultrathin-strut bioresorbable polymer sirolimus-eluting stent against a durable polymer everolimus-eluting stent.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 52 (6%) of 883 patients in the bioresorbable polymer sirolimus-eluting stent group and 41 (10%) of 427 patients in the durable polymer everolimus-eluting stent group met the 12-month primary endpoint of target lesion failure (95% CI -6·84 to -0·29, p=0·0399).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It supports the non-inferiority of a new-generation stent platform and suggests lower target lesion failure, which needs confirmation at longer follow-up.

title: PCI Versus CABG in Patients With Type 1 Diabetes and Multivessel Disease.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Nationwide registry cohort (SWEDEHEART), 683 patients who underwent CABG and 1,863 patients who underwent PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational with possible residual confounding in a group excluded from or underrepresented in trials.
appraisal.one_line: In Swedish registry data, PCI was associated with higher coronary mortality, MI and repeat revascularisation than CABG in type 1 diabetes with multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: PCI, compared with CABG, was associated with a similar risk of all-cause mortality (HR: 1.14; 95% CI: 0.99 to 1.32), but higher risks of death from coronary heart disease (HR: 1.45; 95% CI: 1.21 to 1.74), myocardial infarction (HR: 1.47; 95% CI: 1.23 to 1.78), and repeat revascularization (HR: 5.64; 95% CI: 4.67 to 6.82).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses revascularisation choice in type 1 diabetes, a population with little trial evidence.

title: Guided de-escalation of antiplatelet treatment in patients with acute coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (TROPICAL-ACS): a randomised, open-label, multicentre trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Investigator-initiated, randomised, open-label, assessor-blinded, multicentre trial at 33 sites; 2610 patients (1304 guided de-escalation, 1306 control); 1-year follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, non-inferiority margin of 30%, and the strategy combines early de-escalation with platelet function testing so the contribution of each is not separable.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of platelet function test guided de-escalation from prasugrel to clopidogrel after ACS treated with PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 95 patients (7%) in the guided de-escalation group and in 118 patients (9%) in the control group (pnon-inferiority=0·0004; hazard ratio [HR] 0·81 [95% CI 0·62-1·06], psuperiority=0·12).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It supports early de-escalation of potent P2Y12 inhibition as an alternative after ACS, a common decision on which guidelines are cautious.

title: Timing of Angiography and Outcomes in High-Risk Patients With Non-ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Managed Invasively: Insights From the TAO Trial (Treatment of Acute Coronary Syndrome With Otamixaban).

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc analysis of a randomized trial; angiography performed in 4071 patients (<12 hours, n=1648; 12-24 hours, n=1420; ≥24 hours, n=1003); 180-day outcomes.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc, non-randomised comparison of timing groups, with confounding by indication.
appraisal.one_line: Post hoc analysis of timing of angiography in high-risk NSTEMI with a GRACE score above 140.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: CAG <12 hours was associated with a lower risk of death and myocardial infarction (odds ratio, 0.71; 95% confidence interval, 0.55-0.91). Performing CAG <12 hours was also associated with a lower risk of death and myocardial infarction (odds ratio, 0.76; 95% confidence interval, 0.61-0.94; P=0.01) compared with CAG performed at 12 to 24 hours.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It bears on whether angiography within 12 hours rather than 24 hours should be pursued in high-risk NSTEMI, a question that randomised data have not settled.

title: Efficacy and Safety of the Absorb Bioresorbable Vascular Scaffold in Females and Males: Results of an Individual Patient-Level Pooled Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient-level pooled meta-analysis of the ABSORB II, ABSORB III, ABSORB Japan and ABSORB China trials: Among 3,384 randomized patients, 932 (27.5%) were female.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis with limited female numbers and a device that has since been withdrawn.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level pooled analysis of four randomised trials examining whether the effect of Absorb versus Xience differs by sex.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 2-year rates of target lesion failure with BVS versus everolimus-eluting stent in females were 8.9% versus 6.2% (study-level adjusted hazard ratio: 1.47; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.88 to 2.46) and 8.9% versus 6.4% in males (HR: 1.40; 95% CI: 1.02 to 1.92; pinteraction = 0.85).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides sex-specific randomised data in an under-represented group, finding consistent relative effects.

title: Report of an ESC-EAPCI Task Force on the evaluation and use of bioresorbable scaffolds for percutaneous coronary intervention: executive summary.
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Task Force report (executive summary); no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Executive summary only, and the recommendation reflects data on a single scaffold with published randomised results.
appraisal.one_line: ESC-EAPCI Task Force executive summary advising that bioresorbable scaffolds should not be preferred to conventional DES and setting a framework for evaluating new scaffolds.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets the European device-evaluation standard and a clinical position on scaffolds.

title: Relationship between microvascular obstruction and adverse events following primary percutaneous coronary intervention for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: an individual patient data pooled analysis from seven randomized trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled analysis using individual patient data from seven randomized primary PCI trials; n = 1688; clinical follow-up of at least 6 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational association within pooled trial data, with short follow-up and imaging timing that varied between trials.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled individual patient data analysis of microvascular obstruction on cardiac magnetic resonance and clinical outcomes after primary PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A graded response was present between the extent of MVO (per 1.0% absolute increase) and subsequent mortality [Cox adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 1.14, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.09-1.19, P < 0.0001] and hospitalization for HF (Cox adjusted HR 1.08, 95% CI 1.05-1.12, P < 0.0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It supports microvascular obstruction as a prognostic marker and a candidate surrogate for trials of reperfusion adjuncts.

title: Report of an ESC-EAPCI Task Force on the evaluation and use of bioresorbable scaffolds for percutaneous coronary intervention: executive summary.

appraisal.design_and_n: Task Force report; no sample size applies.
appraisal.main_limitation: Based on the single device with published randomised data, so recommendations on newer scaffolds rest on regulatory reasoning.
appraisal.one_line: ESC-EAPCI Task Force report on the evaluation and use of bioresorbable scaffolds in percutaneous coronary intervention.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It states that bioresorbable scaffolds should not be preferred to conventional drug-eluting stents and sets the evidence standard for new devices.

title: Impact of design of coronary stents and length of dual antiplatelet therapies on ischaemic and bleeding events: a network meta-analysis of 64 randomized controlled trials and 102 735 patients.

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials; Sixty-four studies with 150 arms and 102 735 patients; median follow-up of 20 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Indirect comparison across trials with different designs, and the stent-by-DAPT arms are not randomised factorial comparisons.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis of stent type and DAPT duration in randomised trials.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After a median follow-up of 20 months, MACE rates were similar in the different arms of interest. The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It maps ischaemic and bleeding outcomes jointly across stent platforms and DAPT durations, relevant to choices about device and therapy length.

title: Clinical outcomes of state-of-the-art percutaneous coronary revascularization in patients with de novo three vessel disease: 1-year results of the SYNTAX II study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicenter, all-comers, open-label, single arm study in 22 centres; 708 patients screened and discussed within the heart team, 454 deemed appropriate for PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised comparison with a historical cohort, so differences may reflect era and selection, and follow-up is 1 year.
appraisal.one_line: Single-arm multicentre study of a contemporary PCI strategy in three-vessel disease, compared with a predefined cohort from the earlier SYNTAX-I trial.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At one year, the SYNTAX-II strategy was superior to the equipoise-derived SYNTAX-I PCI cohort (MACCE SYNTAX-II 10.6% vs. SYNTAX-I 17.4%; HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.39-0.85, P = 0.006).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It tests whether physiology, imaging and device advances change PCI outcomes in three-vessel disease and supports a randomised comparison with contemporary bypass surgery.

title: Percutaneous coronary intervention for the left main stem and other bifurcation lesions: 12th consensus document from the European Bifurcation Club.
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus document from the 12th annual EBC meeting in 2016 in Rotterdam.
appraisal.main_limitation: Expert consensus reflecting literature review and voting rather than new trial data.
appraisal.one_line: European Bifurcation Club consensus document on left main and bifurcation PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Summarises current expert recommendations on bifurcation technique.

title: Lesion Complexity and Outcomes of Extended Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a randomized trial; enrolled n = 25,416 and randomized n = 11,554 subjects; 30 months versus 12 months of DAPT.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis of a trial of thienopyridines, with the DAPT score finding exploratory.
appraisal.one_line: Analysis of whether anatomically complex target lesions modify the effect of extended DAPT after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Reduction of MI or stent thrombosis with continued thienopyridine beyond 12 months versus placebo was similar for subjects with (2.5% vs. 4.5%; hazard ratio: 0.55; 95% confidence interval: 0.38 to 0.79; p = 0.001) and without (2.0% vs. 3.8%; hazard ratio: 0.52; 95% confidence interval: 0.39 to 0.69; p < 0.001) anatomic complexity (pinteraction = 0.81).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Lesion complexity did not modify the effect of extended DAPT, which bears on whether anatomy should guide DAPT duration.

title: PCI Strategies in Patients with Acute Myocardial Infarction and Cardiogenic Shock.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicenter randomized trial; 706 patients with multivessel disease, acute myocardial infarction and cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design with 30-day follow-up, and the culprit-only arm allowed staged revascularisation at the operator's discretion.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial finding that culprit-lesion-only PCI led to lower 30-day death or renal replacement therapy than immediate multivessel PCI in infarct-related cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 30 days, the composite primary end point of death or renal-replacement therapy had occurred in 158 of the 344 patients (45.9%) in the culprit-lesion-only PCI group and in 189 of the 341 patients (55.4%) in the multivessel PCI group (relative risk, 0.83; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.71 to 0.96; P=0.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It changes a high-mortality decision made in most patients with infarct-related cardiogenic shock and challenges routine immediate multivessel PCI.

title: International Expert Consensus on Switching Platelet P2Y12 Receptor-Inhibiting Therapies.

appraisal.design_and_n: Expert consensus document; no sample size applies.
appraisal.main_limitation: Recommendations draw on pharmacodynamic data and limited clinical outcome evidence, as the abstract notes that guidelines have not elaborated on switching.
appraisal.one_line: International expert consensus on switching between oral and intravenous P2Y12 inhibitors.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It gives guidance on a frequent clinical event, switching P2Y12 inhibitor, that guidelines have not addressed in detail.

title: Efficacy of the RADPAD Protection Drape in Reducing Operators' Radiation Exposure in the Catheterization Laboratory: A Sham-Controlled Randomized Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Double-blind trial of 766 consecutive coronary procedures randomized to RADPAD (N=255), NOPAD (N=255) or SHAMPAD (N=256).
appraisal.main_limitation: Surrogate dosimetry endpoint, not clinical outcomes in operators.
appraisal.one_line: Sham-controlled randomised trial of a radiation protection drape for operators.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: RADPAD was associated with a 20% reduction in relative operator exposure compared with NOPAD (P=0.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supplies randomised evidence on operator radiation protection in the catheterisation laboratory.

title: Three-Year Outcomes With the Absorb Bioresorbable Scaffold: Individual-Patient-Data Meta-Analysis From the ABSORB Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual-patient-data pooled meta-analysis of 4 randomized trials; 3389 patients (2164 BVS, 1225 cobalt-chromium everolimus-eluting stents).
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooling is limited to trials of one device, and follow-up ends at 3 years.
appraisal.one_line: Individual-patient-data pooled meta-analysis of four ABSORB trials reporting 3-year outcomes of the Absorb scaffold.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: BVS compared with cobalt-chromium everolimus-eluting stents resulted in higher 3-year rates of target lesion failure (11.7% versus 8.1%; risk ratio [RR], 1.38; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.10-1.73; P=0.006). Device thrombosis rates through 3 years were also higher with BVS (2.4% versus 0.6%; RR, 3.71; 95% CI, 1.70-8.11; P=0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: The patient-level data confirm higher target lesion failure and device thrombosis with the scaffold, including after the period of resorption begins.

title: Double Kissing Crush Versus Provisional Stenting for Left Main Distal Bifurcation Lesions: DKCRUSH-V Randomized Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomized trial; 482 patients from 26 centers in 5 countries (242 provisional stenting, 240 double kissing crush).
appraisal.main_limitation: Modest sample size with a 1-year endpoint, and a technique that requires specific expertise.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of planned double kissing crush and provisional stenting for true distal left main bifurcation lesions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: TLF within 1 year occurred in 26 patients (10.7%) assigned to PS, and in 12 patients (5.0%) assigned to DK crush (hazard ratio: 0.42; 95% confidence interval: 0.21 to 0.85; p = 0.02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It is the first randomised comparison of a planned two-stent technique with provisional stenting in left main bifurcations, challenging the usual default of provisional stenting.

title: 3-Year Clinical Outcomes With Everolimus-Eluting Bioresorbable Coronary Scaffolds: The ABSORB III Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized trial analysis by assigned treatment; 2,008 patients with coronary artery disease (as stated in the background) randomized to BVS versus cobalt-chromium everolimus-eluting stents.
appraisal.main_limitation: Follow-up of 3 years may be too short to show any benefit from complete bioresorption.
appraisal.one_line: Three-year outcomes of a randomised trial of the Absorb scaffold against a cobalt-chromium everolimus-eluting stent.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary composite endpoint of target lesion failure through 3 years occurred in 13.4% of BVS patients and 10.4% of EES patients (p = 0.06), and between 1 and 3 years in 7.0% versus 6.0% of patients, respectively (p = 0.39). The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: The largest scaffold trial showed higher target vessel MI and device thrombosis at 3 years, consistent with other trials and relevant to regulatory and clinical decisions.

title: Drug-eluting stents in elderly patients with coronary artery disease (SENIOR): a randomised single-blind trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised single-blind trial at 44 centres in nine countries; 1200 patients (596 DES, 604 BMS); 1-year follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Industry-funded, patients were masked but operators were not, and the trial was not powered for individual components such as stent thrombosis or bleeding.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of drug-eluting versus bare-metal stents with short DAPT in patients aged 75 years or older.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 68 (12%) patients in the DES group and 98 (16%) in the BMS group (relative risk [RR] 0·71 [95% CI 0·52-0·94]; p=0·02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It addresses a population under-represented in stent trials and supports a drug-eluting stent with short DAPT over a bare-metal stent in older patients.

title: Multisite Investigation of Outcomes With Implementation of CYP2C19 Genotype-Guided Antiplatelet Therapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

appraisal.design_and_n: Non-randomised multicentre implementation study of 1,815 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised comparison with inverse probability weighting and residual confounding.
appraisal.one_line: Pragmatic multisite study of CYP2C19 genotype-guided antiplatelet therapy after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Adjusted hazard ratio: 2.26; 95% confidence interval: 1.18 to 4.32 for loss-of-function carriers on clopidogrel versus alternative therapy.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds real-world outcome data on genotype-guided de-escalation and escalation.

title: Percutaneous coronary intervention in stable angina (ORBITA): a double-blind, randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Blinded multicentre randomised trial at five UK sites; 200 patients randomised (105 PCI, 95 placebo procedure) after medication optimisation.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample with a symptom-based primary endpoint, a single-vessel population and 6 weeks of follow-up, so it cannot address hard clinical outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Blinded, placebo-controlled randomised trial of PCI versus a placebo procedure for angina relief in stable single-vessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There was no significant difference in the primary endpoint of exercise time increment between groups (PCI minus placebo 16·6 s, 95% CI -8·9 to 42·0, p=0·200).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It is the first placebo-controlled test of PCI for stable angina and challenges the assumption that PCI relieves symptoms beyond placebo, bearing on a very common procedure.

title: Safety of six-month dual antiplatelet therapy after second-generation drug-eluting stent implantation: OPTIMA-C Randomised Clinical Trial and OCT Substudy.
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised multicentre trial of 1,368 patients, 684 per arm.
appraisal.main_limitation: Low event rate and modest sample size limit power for stent thrombosis.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised non-inferiority trial of six versus 12 months of DAPT after second-generation DES.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: MACE 1.2% versus 0.6% (risk difference 0.6%; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.4-1.6%; p=0.24), non-inferiority met against 4% margin.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Contributes to the evidence on DAPT shortening after contemporary DES.

title: Optical frequency domain imaging vs. intravascular ultrasound in percutaneous coronary intervention (OPINION trial): one-year angiographic and clinical results.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective, multicentre, randomized, active-controlled, non-inferiority study; 829 patients (414 OFDI, 415 IVUS); 12-month follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Modest size with a non-inferiority margin wide relative to the low event rate, and no angiography-guided control arm.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised non-inferiority trial of optical frequency domain imaging against intravascular ultrasound for guiding PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Target vessel failure occurred in 21 (5.2%) of 401 patients undergoing OFDI-guided PCI, and 19 (4.9%) of 390 patients undergoing IVUS-guided PCI, demonstrating non-inferiority of OFDI-guided PCI to IVUS-guided PCI (hazard ratio 1.07, upper limit of one-sided 95% confidence interval 1.80; Pnon-inferiority = 0.042).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It supports using either intravascular imaging modality to guide PCI, relevant to the growing evidence base for imaging guidance.

title: Rivaroxaban with or without aspirin in patients with stable coronary artery disease: an international, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial; 24 824 patients with stable coronary artery disease from 558 centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: Report of a coronary subpopulation from a larger trial, industry-funded, and limited to patients after a 30-day run-in.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of low-dose rivaroxaban with or without aspirin against aspirin alone in stable coronary artery disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The combination of rivaroxaban plus aspirin reduced the primary outcome more than aspirin alone (347 [4%] of 8313 vs 460 [6%] of 8261; hazard ratio [HR] 0·74, 95% CI 0·65-0·86, p<0·0001). Combined rivaroxaban plus aspirin treatment resulted in more major bleeds than treatment with aspirin alone (263 [3%] of 8313 vs 158 [2%] of 8261; HR 1·66, 95% CI 1·37-2·03, p<0·0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It tests dual-pathway inhibition in a large population of patients with coronary disease, many of whom have undergone PCI, with a trade-off between fewer vascular events and more bleeding.

title: Impact of Regionalization of ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Care on Treatment Times and Outcomes for Emergency Medical Services-Transported Patients Presenting to Hospitals With Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Mission: Lifeline Accelerator-2.

appraisal.design_and_n: Quality-improvement programme in 12 US metropolitan regions with 132 PCI-capable hospitals and 946 EMS agencies; 10 730 patients transported.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised before-and-after design without adjustment reported in the abstract.
appraisal.one_line: A regional EMS-hospital coordination programme was followed by shorter reperfusion times and lower in-hospital mortality in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The proportion with first medical contact to device time ≤90 minutes rose from 67% to 74% (P<0.002); in-hospital death fell from 4.4% to 2.3% (P=0.001), not apparent in non-participating hospitals.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Evidence for regionalised systems of care in STEMI.

title: Culprit Vessel-Only Versus Multivessel Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients With Cardiogenic Shock Complicating ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Collaborative Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of 11 nonrandomized studies and 5850 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Nonrandomised studies only, with confounding by indication.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of multivessel versus culprit-only PCI in infarct-related cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Short-term mortality OR, 1.08; 95% CI, 0.81-1.43; P=0.61 for multivessel versus culprit-only PCI.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a contested decision in cardiogenic shock before randomised trial results.

title: Clinical Outcomes Following Intravascular Imaging-Guided Versus Coronary Angiography-Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention With Stent Implantation: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis of 31 Studies and 17,882 Patients.

appraisal.design_and_n: Bayesian network meta-analysis of 31 studies encompassing 17,882 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Combines randomised trials with adjusted observational studies.
appraisal.one_line: Bayesian network meta-analysis associating intravascular imaging guidance with better PCI outcomes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause death OR: 0.74; 95% CrI: 0.58 to 0.98 for IVUS versus angiography guidance.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Compares IVUS, OCT and angiography guidance within one framework.

title: 1-Year Outcomes of Patients Undergoing Primary Angioplasty for Myocardial Infarction Treated With Prasugrel Versus Ticagrelor.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized trial; 1,230 patients with acute myocardial infarction treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention.
appraisal.main_limitation: Switching to clopidogrel was not randomised, so the finding on switching is observational and open to confounding.
appraisal.one_line: One-year follow-up of a randomised comparison of prasugrel and ticagrelor in primary PCI for myocardial infarction, including an analysis of economically motivated switching to clopidogrel.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The endpoint occurred in 6.6% of prasugrel patients and in 5.7% of ticagrelor patients (hazard ratio: 1.167; 95% confidence interval: 0.742 to 1.835; p = 0.503).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Prasugrel and ticagrelor had similar efficacy and bleeding at 1 year, and the switch analysis informs de-escalation in practice.

title: Surgical Versus Percutaneous Coronary Revascularization in Patients With Diabetes and Acute Coronary Syndromes.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Observational population-based cohort in British Columbia; n = 4,661 diabetic patients who underwent coronary revascularization between 2007 and 2014 (2,947 with ACS); median follow-up 3.3 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational comparison with residual confounding despite multivariable and propensity adjustment.
appraisal.one_line: Population-based comparison of CABG and PCI in diabetic patients with multivessel disease, including those with acute coronary syndromes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 30-days post-revascularization, for ACS patients the odds ratio for MACCE favored CABG 0.49 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.34 to 0.71), whereas among SIHD patients MACCE was not affected by revascularization strategy (odds ratio: 1.46; 95% CI: 0.71 to 3.01; pinteraction <0.01). The late hazard ratio for MACCE was 0.67 (95% CI: 0.55 to 0.81) in ACS patients and 0.55 (95% CI: 0.40 to 0.74) in SIHD patients.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It extends trial findings to patients with ACS and diabetes, who were largely excluded from earlier trials, and points to the need for a randomised comparison.

title: Outcomes of Saphenous Vein Graft Intervention With and Without Embolic Protection Device: A Comprehensive Review and Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of eight studies (n=52 893) comparing SVG intervention with EPD (n=11 506) and without EPD (n=41 387).
appraisal.main_limitation: Mainly observational data, dominated by one registry.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis finding no difference in outcomes with embolic protection devices in vein graft PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause mortality odds ratio [OR], 0.79; confidence interval [CI], 0.55-1.12; P=0.19.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Questions the class I guideline recommendation for embolic protection in vein graft intervention.

title: Benefit of Switching Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Acute Coronary Syndrome According to On-Treatment Platelet Reactivity: The TOPIC-VASP Pre-Specified Analysis of the TOPIC Randomized Study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pre-specified analysis of a randomised study including 645 patients, 305 (47%) classified as low on-treatment platelet reactivity.
appraisal.main_limitation: Substudy of a modest trial with a platelet reactivity stratification that was not the randomised factor.
appraisal.one_line: Pre-specified TOPIC substudy relating platelet reactivity to benefit of switching to aspirin and clopidogrel after ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patients defined as LTPR and randomized to unchanged DAPT were at the highest risk of primary endpoint occurrence (31%; p < 0.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Relevant to guided de-escalation of DAPT after ACS.

title: Long-term safety of bioresorbable scaffolds: insights from a network meta-analysis including 91 trials.
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis of 91 randomised controlled trials in 105,842 patients with mean follow-up of 3.7 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Network of heterogeneous trials with sparse long-term data for many devices.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis associating Absorb scaffolds with higher long-term scaffold thrombosis than metallic DES.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate; Absorb BVS was associated with higher risk of definite or probable scaffold thrombosis than metallic DES.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Consolidates randomised evidence on late safety of bioresorbable scaffolds.

title: Impact of Sex on Comparative Outcomes of Radial Versus Femoral Access in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes Undergoing Invasive Management: Data From the Randomized MATRIX-Access Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised programme analysis of 8,404 patients, 2,232 (26.6%) women.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis with limited power for interaction.
appraisal.one_line: MATRIX-Access analysis of radial versus femoral access by sex in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: No significant interaction for MACCE and NACE stratified by sex (pint = 0.15 and 0.18, respectively).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports radial access in both sexes, with relatively greater benefit in women.

title: Randomized Comparison of a CrossBoss First Versus Standard Wire Escalation Strategy for Crossing Coronary Chronic Total Occlusions: The CrossBoss First Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised trial, 246 patients randomized to the CrossBoss catheter (n = 122) or wire escalation (n = 124) at 11 U.S. centers.
appraisal.main_limitation: Procedural endpoints rather than long-term clinical outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of CrossBoss-first versus wire escalation for CTO crossing found no difference in crossing time.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Incidence of procedural major adverse cardiovascular events (3.28% vs. 4.03%; p = 1.000); crossing time p = 0.323.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Randomised evidence on initial CTO crossing strategy.

title: Randomized Comparisons of Double-Dose Clopidogrel or Adjunctive Cilostazol Versus Standard Dual Antiplatelet in Patients With High Posttreatment Platelet Reactivity: Results of the CREATIVE Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Single-center, randomized, controlled trial; 1078 patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-centre design with platelet-function-guided selection; the double-dose comparison did not reach significance.
appraisal.one_line: Single-centre randomised trial of intensified antiplatelet regimens in PCI patients with high on-clopidogrel platelet reactivity by thromboelastography.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 52 patients (14.4%) in the STANDARD group, 38 patients (10.6%) in the DOUBLE group, and 30 patients (8.5%) in the TRIPLE group (hazard ratio, 0.720; 95% confidence interval, 0.474-1.094, DOUBLE versus STANDARD; hazard ratio, 0.550; 95% confidence interval, 0.349-0.866, TRIPLE versus STANDARD).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests whether escalating therapy in high on-treatment reactivity improves outcomes, a question left open by earlier guided-therapy trials.

title: Compliance With Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy in Contemporary Coronary Revascularization Trials.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials; 5 trials included from a total of 439 references.
appraisal.main_limitation: Only a small number of trials; meta-regression is hypothesis-generating.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis showing that compliance with guideline-directed medical therapy in PCI versus CABG trials is low and differs by arm.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Overall, compliance with GDMT1 was low and decreased over time from 67% at 1 year to 53% at 5 years.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Differential medical therapy between arms may bias PCI versus CABG comparisons.

title: Anticoagulant Use Among Patients With End-Stage Renal Disease Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: An Analysis From the National Cardiovascular Data Registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: CathPCI Registry analysis of n=71 675 patients with end-stage renal disease receiving bivalirudin or UFH.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry data with confounding by indication and in-hospital outcomes only.
appraisal.one_line: Registry analysis associating bivalirudin with lower bleeding and mortality than heparin in dialysis-dependent PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In hospital bleeding (7.0% versus 9.5%; adjusted odds ratio,0.82; 95% confidence interval, 0.76-0.87) lower with bivalirudin.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides data in a population largely excluded from antithrombotic trials.

title: Coronary intervention door-to-balloon time and outcomes in ST-elevation myocardial infarction: a meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of 32 studies involving 299 320 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational studies with confounding and heterogeneous time definitions.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis associating longer door-to-balloon delay with higher mortality in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Short-term mortality pooled OR 1.52, 95% CI 1.40 to 1.65 for door-to-balloon delay above 90 min.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Characterises the non-linear time-risk relation and modification by prehospital delay.

title: Association of different antiplatelet therapies with mortality after primary percutaneous coronary intervention.

appraisal.design_and_n: BCIS national database analysis of >89 000 patients undergoing primary PCI for STEMI between 2007 and 2014.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised comparison of P2Y12 inhibitors with residual confounding.
appraisal.one_line: National registry analysis comparing prasugrel, ticagrelor and clopidogrel mortality after primary PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Prasugrel versus clopidogrel mortality at 30 days OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.78 to 0.97, P=0.014; ticagrelor versus clopidogrel at 30 days OR 1.07, 95% CI 0.95 to 1.21, P=0.237.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large real-world comparison of newer P2Y12 inhibitors in STEMI.

title: Impact of treatment delay on mortality in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) patients presenting with and without haemodynamic instability: results from the German prospective, multicentre FITT-STEMI trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Analysis of the prospective multicentre FITT-STEMI trial, n = 12 675 STEMI patients transported by emergency medical service and treated with primary PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational time-to-treatment association with possible confounding by indication.
appraisal.one_line: Contact-to-balloon delay was linked to excess mortality, most steeply in STEMI with cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In CS patients with no OHCA, every 10-min treatment delay resulted in 3.31 additional deaths in 100 PCI-treated patients, versus 0.34 in haemodynamically stable patients (P < 0.0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports prioritising speed of reperfusion in shock, relevant to shock systems of care.

title: Short-Term Versus Long-Term Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation in Elderly Patients: A Meta-Analysis of Individual Participant Data From 6 Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual participant data meta-analysis of 6 randomized trials; 5,319 elderly patients (≥65 years).
appraisal.main_limitation: Age subgroup analysis with only 12-month outcomes and trials differing in design.
appraisal.one_line: Individual participant data meta-analysis of short versus long DAPT after DES in older patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary outcome overall hazard ratio [HR]: 1.12; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.88 to 1.43; p = 0.3581; age interaction p for interaction = 0.0384.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs DAPT duration in older patients using patient-level data.

title: Comparison of Reduced-Dose Prasugrel and Standard-Dose Clopidogrel in Elderly Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes Undergoing Early Percutaneous Revascularization.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicenter, randomized, open-label, blinded end point trial; 1443 patients enrolled.
appraisal.main_limitation: Premature termination for futility limits precision on bleeding and stent thrombosis.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of reduced-dose prasugrel and clopidogrel in patients older than 74 years with ACS undergoing PCI, stopped early for futility.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 121 patients (17%) with prasugrel and 121 (16.6%) with clopidogrel (hazard ratio, 1.007; 95% confidence interval, 0.78-1.30; P=0.955).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs antiplatelet choice in older patients, a group excluded from the pivotal prasugrel trials.

title: Long-term impact of chronic total occlusion recanalisation in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised multicentre trial of 302 patients, median follow-up 3.9 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Modest sample size and few events.
appraisal.one_line: Long-term follow-up of EXPLORE finding no MACE difference with CTO-PCI after STEMI.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Randomised evidence on routine CTO recanalisation in STEMI with a concurrent CTO.

title: The efficacy of early versus delayed P2Y12 inhibition in percutaneous coronary intervention for ST-elevation myocardial infarction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of seven randomised controlled trials including 9,648 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Short follow-up and heterogeneous agents and timing.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of randomised trials of early versus delayed P2Y12 inhibition in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: MACE OR 0.73, 95% CI: 0.61-0.88, p=0.0008; major bleeding OR 0.87, 95% CI: 0.62-1.21, p=0.41 with early inhibition.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses the timing of P2Y12 loading before primary PCI.

title: Coronary Artery Bypass Surgery Improves Outcomes in Patients With Diabetes and Left Ventricular Dysfunction.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Propensity-matched observational study of patients with CAD, diabetes and LV dysfunction treated with PCI or CABG between 2004 and 2016.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational design with residual confounding and no effect estimates in the abstract.
appraisal.one_line: Propensity-matched analysis associated PCI with worse outcomes than CABG in diabetes with left ventricular dysfunction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses revascularisation choice in a population largely excluded from the defining trials.

title: Safety and Effectiveness of Second-Generation Drug-Eluting Stents in Patients With Left Main Coronary Artery Disease.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled analysis of 3 prospective registries (IRIS-DES, IRIS-MAIN, PRECOMBAT); 2,692 patients with left main disease received second-generation DES (1,254 CoCr-EES, 232 BP-BES, 616 PtCr-EES, 590 Re-ZES).
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised stent comparison with residual confounding by indication and era.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled analysis of three prospective registries comparing second-generation drug-eluting stents in left main disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The observed 3-year rates of target-vessel failure were not significantly different for the different types of DES (16.7% for the CoCr-EES, 13.2% for the BP-BES, 18.7% for the PtCr-EES, and 14.7% for the Re-ZES; p = 0.15).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Suggests broadly similar outcomes across contemporary stent platforms in left main PCI.

title: Multivessel Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction With Cardiogenic Shock.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Nationwide prospective KAMIR-NIH registry; 659 patients treated by multivessel PCI (n = 260) or IRA-only PCI (n = 399).
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational data with selection of patients for multivessel PCI despite adjustment methods.
appraisal.one_line: Registry analysis of multivessel versus infarct-related-artery-only PCI in STEMI with cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The risk of all-cause death and non-IRA repeat revascularization was significantly lower in the multivessel PCI group than in the IRA-only PCI group (21.3% vs. 31.7%; hazard ratio: 0.59; 95% confidence interval: 0.43 to 0.82; p = 0.001; and 6.7% vs. 8.2%; hazard ratio: 0.39; 95% confidence interval: 0.17 to 0.90; p = 0.028, respectively).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a decision where randomised evidence in shock is limited, and is hypothesis-generating for complete revascularisation in shock.

title: Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection: Current State of the Science: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Based largely on case series and expert opinion, so recommendations rest on limited evidence.
appraisal.one_line: American Heart Association scientific statement summarising current knowledge on spontaneous coronary artery dissection.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Reference document for a distinct cause of ACS that is managed differently from atherosclerotic MI.

title: Mortality after coronary artery bypass grafting versus percutaneous coronary intervention with stenting for coronary artery disease: a pooled analysis of individual patient data.

appraisal.design_and_n: Collaborative pooled analysis of individual patient data from 11 randomised trials involving 11 518 patients assigned to PCI (n=5753) or to CABG (n=5765).
appraisal.main_limitation: Trials used earlier-generation stents and follow-up was limited to 5 years; subgroup findings are exploratory.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data pooled analysis of 11 randomised trials comparing PCI with stents against CABG for all-cause mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 5 year all-cause mortality was 11·2% after PCI and 9·2% after CABG (hazard ratio [HR] 1·20, 95% CI 1·06-1·37; p=0·0038). 5 year all-cause mortality was significantly different between the interventions in patients with multivessel disease (11·5% after PCI vs 8·9% after CABG; HR 1·28, 95% CI 1·09-1·49; p=0·0019), including in those with diabetes (15·5% vs 10·0%; 1·48, 1·19-1·84; p=0·0004), but not in those without diabetes (8·7% vs 8·0%; 1·08, 0·86-1·36; p=0·49). 5 year all-cause mortality was similar between the interventions in patients with left main disease (10·7% after PCI vs 10·5% after CABG; 1·07, 0·87-1·33; p=0·52).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides the first mortality-powered comparison of PCI and CABG, directly informing heart team choice in multivessel and left main disease.

title: A Multidisciplinary Approach on the Perioperative Antithrombotic Management of Patients With Coronary Stents Undergoing Surgery: Surgery After Stenting 2.

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus document without a stated sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Expert recommendations rather than trial evidence.
appraisal.one_line: Multidisciplinary update on perioperative antithrombotic management after coronary stenting.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides practical risk-stratified guidance for surgery after stenting.

title: Effect of Loading Dose of Atorvastatin Prior to Planned Percutaneous Coronary Intervention on Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events in Acute Coronary Syndrome: The SECURE-PCI Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized clinical trial; 4191 patients at 53 sites in Brazil.
appraisal.main_limitation: Thirty-day follow-up only; roughly a quarter of patients did not undergo PCI.
appraisal.one_line: Placebo-controlled trial of periprocedural atorvastatin loading in ACS with planned invasive management.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 30 days, 130 patients in the atorvastatin group (6.2%) and 149 in the placebo group (7.1%) had a MACE (absolute difference, 0.85% [95% CI, -0.70% to 2.41%]; hazard ratio, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.69-1.11; P = .27).
appraisal.why_it_matters: A large adequately powered neutral trial that does not support routine statin loading before PCI.

title: Deferred vs. performed revascularization for coronary stenosis with grey-zone fractional flow reserve values: data from the IRIS-FFR registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicentre IRIS-FFR registry; 1334 native coronary stenosis in 1334 patients, deferred for 683 and performed for 651.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised comparison; treatment allocation depended on operator judgement.
appraisal.one_line: Registry comparison of deferred versus performed revascularisation for grey-zone FFR stenoses.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome, a composite of death, target-vessel myocardial infarction, and target vessel revascularization occurred in 55 (8.1%) patients in the deferred group and 55 (8.4%) in the performed group [adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 1.05, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.67-1.66; P = 0.79].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on the FFR threshold for revascularisation, where guideline thresholds are contested.

title: 6-month versus 12-month or longer dual antiplatelet therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with acute coronary syndrome (SMART-DATE): a randomised, open-label, non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, open-label, non-inferiority trial at 31 centres in South Korea; 2712 patients randomly assigned.
appraisal.main_limitation: Wide non-inferiority margin and more myocardial infarction with short DAPT.
appraisal.one_line: Non-inferiority trial of 6-month versus 12-month or longer DAPT after PCI for ACS; the authors do not conclude short DAPT is safe.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 63 patients in the 6-month DAPT group and in 56 patients in the 12-month or longer DAPT group (cumulative event rate 4·7% vs 4·2%; absolute risk difference 0·5%; upper limit of one-sided 95% CI 1·8%; pnon-inferiority=0·03 with a predefined non-inferiority margin of 2·0%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to DAPT duration after ACS, where short-course strategies are being adopted.

title: Operator volume is not associated with mortality following percutaneous coronary intervention: insights from the British Cardiovascular Intervention Society registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: Observational cohort study of the British Cardiovascular Intervention Society PCI database, 2013 to 2014; 133 970 procedures analysed.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational data limited to 30-day mortality over a short period.
appraisal.one_line: Large UK registry analysis of operator volume and 30-day mortality after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After adjustment for case-mix, the association between volume and mortality was negligible (odds ratio per 100 procedures 0.99, 95% confidence interval 0.93-1.05; P = 0.725).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs volume thresholds in PCI credentialing and service planning.

title: Delayed Coronary Obstruction After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective international registry of 18 centres, November 2005 to December 2016; 38 DCO cases from a total of 17,092 TAVR procedures.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective case collection without a denominator for timing and subject to reporting bias.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre registry description of delayed coronary obstruction after TAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 38 DCO (incidence 0.22%) cases were identified from a total of 17,092 TAVR procedures. DCO occurred more commonly after valve-in-valve procedures (0.89% vs. 0.18%; p < 0.001) and if self-expandable valves were used during the index procedure (0.36% vs. 0.11% balloon expandable; p < 0.01). The overall in-hospital death rate was 50% (n = 19).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Characterises a rare, highly lethal complication relevant to coronary access planning after TAVR.

title: Safety and efficacy of dual vs. triple antithrombotic therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation following percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis of randomised trials; 4 trials including 5317 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few trials, heterogeneous regimens, and trials underpowered for ischaemic events.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of dual versus triple antithrombotic therapy in atrial fibrillation patients after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with the TAT arm, Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) major or minor bleeding showed a reduction by 47% in the DAT arm [4.3% vs. 9.0%; hazard ratio (HR) 0.53, 95% credible interval (CrI) 0.36-0.85, I2 = 42.9%].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports de-escalation of antithrombotic therapy in a common high-bleeding-risk group.

title: Mortality Following Nonemergent, Uncomplicated Target Lesion Revascularization After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: An Individual Patient Data Pooled Analysis of 21 Randomized Trials and 32,524 Patients.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data pooled analysis of 21 randomized trials with 32,524 patients, median follow-up 37 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational analysis within trial data, with TLR as a post-randomisation event and residual confounding.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled individual patient data analysis associating non-emergent target lesion revascularisation with higher mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: TLR was an independent predictor of mortality (hazard ratio: 1.23, 95% confidence interval: 1.04 to 1.45; p = 0.02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges the view of restenosis requiring revascularisation as benign.

title: Intravascular ultrasound in the evaluation and treatment of left main coronary artery disease: a consensus statement from the European Bifurcation Club.
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus statement without a stated sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Expert consensus reviewing mostly non-randomised imaging data.
appraisal.one_line: European Bifurcation Club consensus statement on IVUS in left main disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides practical guidance on IVUS use in left main interventions.

title: Clinical impact of direct stenting and interaction with thrombus aspiration in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: Thrombectomy Trialists Collaboration.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled patient-level data from three randomized trials; unmatched population n = 17 329; propensity-matched n = 10 944.
