appraisal.main_limitation: Direct stenting was not randomised, so propensity matching leaves residual confounding.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level pooled analysis of the three largest thrombus aspiration trials examining direct stenting in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After propensity matching (n = 10 944), no significant differences were seen between DS and conventional stenting with respect to 30-day cardiovascular death [1.7% vs. 1.9%; hazard ratio 0.88, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.55-1.41; P = 0.60; Pinteraction = 0.96).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large individual-patient dataset addressing a technique choice in primary PCI.

title: Length of stay following percutaneous coronary intervention: An expert consensus document update from the society for cardiovascular angiography and interventions.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

appraisal.design_and_n: Expert consensus document without a stated sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Expert consensus relying on selected-patient studies of early discharge.
appraisal.one_line: SCAI expert consensus update on length of stay after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Updates recommendations on same-day and early discharge after PCI.

title: A randomized multicentre trial to compare revascularization with optimal medical therapy for the treatment of chronic total coronary occlusions.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective randomized, multicentre, open-label, controlled clinical trial; Three hundred and ninety-six patients were enrolled.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design with a symptom endpoint; not powered for hard outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of PCI versus optimal medical therapy for chronic total occlusion with health status as the primary endpoint.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 12 months, a greater improvement of SAQ subscales was observed with PCI as compared with OMT for angina frequency [5.23, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.75; 8.71; P = 0.003], and quality of life (6.62, 95% CI 1.78-11.46; P = 0.007).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Few randomised data exist for CTO PCI, and this supports symptomatic benefit.

title: Device-Related Thrombus After Left Atrial Appendage Closure: Incidence, Predictors, and Outcomes.

appraisal.design_and_n: Device arms of 4 prospective FDA trials (PROTECT-AF n=463; PREVAIL n=269; CAP n=566; CAP2 n=578); 1739 patients with an implant (7159 patient-years follow-up).
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational association within trial and registry cohorts; most events occurred without detected device-related thrombus.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled analysis of Watchman trials and registries on device-related thrombus and subsequent thromboembolism.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: DRT was seen in 65 patients (3.74%). The rates of SSE with and without DRT were 7.46 and 1.78 per 100 patient-years (adjusted rate ratio, 3.55; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.18-5.79; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large pooled estimate of device-related thrombus incidence and its link to stroke, relevant to post-implant antithrombotic therapy.

title: Drug-eluting stents versus bare-metal stents in saphenous vein grafts: a double-blind, randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Double-blind randomised controlled trial at 25 US Department of Veterans Affairs centres; 599 patients randomly assigned.
appraisal.main_limitation: Enrolment stopped short of the revised target sample size and almost all participants were men.
appraisal.one_line: Double-blind trial of drug-eluting versus bare-metal stents in saphenous vein graft lesions, stopped before target enrolment.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 12 months, the incidence of target vessel failure was 17% (51 of 292) in the DES group versus 19% (58 of 305) in the BMS group (adjusted hazard ratio 0·92, 95% CI 0·63-1·34, p=0·70).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Vein graft PCI remains a difficult problem and this suggests no clear advantage for DES.

title: Five-Year Outcomes with PCI Guided by Fractional Flow Reserve.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 888 patients underwent randomization (447 in the PCI group and 441 in the medical-therapy group).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label; the difference was driven by urgent revascularisation, with no difference in death.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year follow-up of FFR-guided PCI versus medical therapy in stable coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 5 years, the rate of the primary end point was lower in the PCI group than in the medical-therapy group (13.9% vs. 27.0%; hazard ratio, 0.46; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.34 to 0.63; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Long-term physiology-guided evidence that informs revascularisation choices in chronic coronary syndromes.

title: Fractional Flow Reserve and Instantaneous Wave-Free Ratio as Predictors of the Placebo-Controlled Response to Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Stable Single-Vessel Coronary Artery Disease.

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a placebo-controlled randomised trial; invasive physiology data in 196 patients (103 PCI and 93 placebo).
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc subgroup analysis in a small blinded trial.
appraisal.one_line: Analysis of ORBITA testing whether FFR or iFR predicts the placebo-controlled response to PCI in single-vessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The estimated effect of PCI on between-arm prerandomization-adjusted total exercise time was 20.7 s (95% confidence interval [CI], -4.0 to 45.5; P=0.100) with no interaction of FFR ( Pinteraction=0.318) or iFR ( Pinteraction=0.523).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests whether physiology identifies who benefits from PCI under blinded conditions.

title: Clinical use of intracoronary imaging. Part 1: guidance and optimization of coronary interventions. An expert consensus document of the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions.

appraisal.design_and_n: Expert consensus document; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus statement; several recommendations rest on limited randomised evidence.
appraisal.one_line: EAPCI expert consensus on the use of intracoronary imaging to guide and optimise PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Reference document for IVUS and OCT use in PCI guidance and stent failure.

title: Oxygen therapy in ST-elevation myocardial infarction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pre-specified analysis of a randomized trial; 2807 patients (1361 oxygen, 1446 ambient air).
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup of a trial not powered separately for STEMI.
appraisal.one_line: Pre-specified DETO2X-AMI analysis of supplemental oxygen in STEMI patients treated with PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The pre-specified primary composite endpoint occurred in 6.3% (86 of 1361) of patients allocated to oxygen compared to 7.5% (108 of 1446) allocated to ambient air [hazard ratio (HR) 0.85, 95% confidence interval (95% CI) 0.64-1.13; P = 0.27].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports abandoning routine oxygen in normoxaemic STEMI.

title: Newer-Generation Ultrathin Strut Drug-Eluting Stents Versus Older Second-Generation Thicker Strut Drug-Eluting Stents for Coronary Artery Disease.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials; 10 trials that randomly assigned 11 658 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Short follow-up and heterogeneous comparators.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of ultrathin-strut versus thicker-strut second-generation DES.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In comparison with thicker strut second-generation DES, newer-generation ultrathin strut DES were associated with a 16% reduction in target lesion failure (relative risk, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.72-0.99) driven by less myocardial infarction (relative risk, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.65-0.99).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs stent selection, although the absolute benefit is small.

title: Stroke Rates Following Surgical Versus Percutaneous Coronary Revascularization.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Collaborative individual patient-data pooled analysis of 11 randomized clinical trials; 11,518 patients randomly assigned to PCI (n = 5,753) or CABG (n = 5,765).
appraisal.main_limitation: Secondary outcome of trials not designed for stroke, with subgroup interactions that are exploratory.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data pooled analysis of 11 randomised trials comparing stroke after PCI and CABG.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 30 days, the rate of stroke was 0.4% after PCI and 1.1% after CABG (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.33; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.20 to 0.53; p < 0.001). At 5-year follow-up, stroke remained significantly lower after PCI than after CABG (2.6% vs. 3.2%; HR: 0.77; 95% CI: 0.61 to 0.97; p = 0.027).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Complements the mortality analysis and informs the benefit-risk balance between revascularisation strategies.

title: Angiographic late lumen loss revisited: impact on long-term target lesion revascularization.

appraisal.design_and_n: Patient-level meta-analysis of seven randomized controlled trials including 2426 patients and study-level meta-analysis of 40 studies including 19 199 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Surrogate endpoint analysis; limited number of trials with angiographic follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level and study-level analysis of angiographic late lumen loss as a predictor of target lesion revascularisation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In the Cox proportional hazard model, LLL >0.50 mm was independently associated with an increased incidence of TLR up to 4 years after angiographic follow-up {adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 6.62 [95% confidence interval (95% CI) 4.67-9.39], P < 0.001}.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Questions the usefulness of late lumen loss as a device endpoint.

title: Percutaneous Repair or Medical Treatment for Secondary Mitral Regurgitation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; severe secondary mitral regurgitation; intervention group 83 of 152 patients with the primary outcome and control group 78 of 152 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design; patient selection and medical therapy optimisation differ from the contemporaneous US trial.
appraisal.one_line: Open-label trial found no benefit of percutaneous mitral repair over medical therapy in severe secondary mitral regurgitation, contrasting with COAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 12 months, the rate of the primary outcome was 54.6% (83 of 152 patients) in the intervention group and 51.3% (78 of 152 patients) in the control group (odds ratio, 1.16; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73 to 1.84; P=0.53).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Together with discordant results from another trial it defines the central open question for TEER in secondary MR.

title: One-Year Outcomes after PCI Strategies in Cardiogenic Shock.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 706 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Mortality difference at 1 year was not statistically significant; open-label.
appraisal.one_line: One-year outcomes of culprit-lesion-only versus immediate multivessel PCI in AMI with cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, death had occurred in 172 of 344 patients (50.0%) in the culprit-lesion-only PCI group and in 194 of 341 patients (56.9%) in the multivessel PCI group (relative risk, 0.88; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.76 to 1.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Guides revascularisation strategy in a high-mortality setting.

title: Radial versus femoral access and bivalirudin versus unfractionated heparin in invasively managed patients with acute coronary syndrome (MATRIX): final 1-year results of a multicentre, randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Programme of three nested, randomised, multicentre, open-label, superiority trials; 8404 patients randomly assigned to radial or femoral access.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design with several nested randomisations.
appraisal.one_line: Final 1-year results of the MATRIX programme comparing radial versus femoral access and bivalirudin versus heparin in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, major adverse cardiovascular events did not differ between patients assigned to radial access compared with those assigned to femoral access (14·2% vs 15·7%; rate ratio 0·89, 95% CI 0·80-1·00; p=0·0526), but net adverse clinical events were fewer with radial than with femoral access (15·2% vs 17·2%; 0·87, 0·78-0·97; p=0·0128).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large trial data supporting radial access and informing anticoagulant choice in ACS.

title: Ticagrelor plus aspirin for 1 month, followed by ticagrelor monotherapy for 23 months vs aspirin plus clopidogrel or ticagrelor for 12 months, followed by aspirin monotherapy for 12 months after implantation of a drug-eluting stent: a multicentre, open-label, randomised superiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, open-label superiority trial at 130 sites in 18 countries; 15 968 participants randomly assigned.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design with an unconventional primary endpoint and a superiority hypothesis that was not met.
appraisal.one_line: Trial of one month of ticagrelor plus aspirin followed by ticagrelor monotherapy versus standard DAPT after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 2 years, 304 (3·81%) participants in the experimental group had died or had a non-fatal centrally adjudicated new Q-wave myocardial infarction, compared with 349 (4·37%) participants in the control group (rate ratio 0·87 [95% CI 0·75-1·01]; p=0·073]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Largest trial of P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy after short DAPT; shapes de-escalation debate.

title: Drug-coated balloons for small coronary artery disease (BASKET-SMALL 2): an open-label randomised non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre, open-label, randomised non-inferiority trial; 758 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label; modest sample size and a wide absolute non-inferiority margin.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised non-inferiority trial of drug-coated balloon versus DES for small-vessel coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After 12 months, the proportions of MACE were similar in both groups of the full-analysis population (MACE was 7·5% for the DCB group vs 7·3% for the DES group; hazard ratio [HR] 0·97 [95% CI 0·58-1·64], p=0·9180).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports DCB as an alternative to DES in small vessels.

title: Relations between implementation of new treatments and improved outcomes in patients with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction during the last 20 years: experiences from SWEDEHEART registry 1995 to 2014.

appraisal.design_and_n: Nationwide SWEDEHEART registry cohort of 205 693 NSTEMI cases between 1995 and 2014.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational temporal analysis; attribution to treatments is by statistical adjustment.
appraisal.one_line: Swedish registry analysis linking 20 years of improved NSTEMI outcomes to uptake of invasive treatment and medications.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The standardized 1-year mortality ratio compared with a control population decreased from 5.53 [95% confidence interval (CI) 5.30-5.75] to 3.03 (95% CI 2.89-3.19).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Quantifies the population-level association between guideline treatments and NSTEMI outcomes.

title: 10-Year Outcomes of Stents Versus Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting for Left Main Coronary Artery Disease.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Observational MAIN-COMPARE registry study of 2,240 patients with unprotected LMCA disease who underwent PCI (n = 1,102) or CABG (n = 1,138), median follow-up 12.0 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational design with enrolment from 2000 to 2006 and a small drug-eluting stent subgroup.
appraisal.one_line: Ten-year registry follow-up of left main PCI versus CABG suggests divergence in mortality after 5 years with drug-eluting stents.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After 5 years, drug-eluting stents were associated with higher risks of death (hazard ratio: 1.35; 95% confidence interval: 1.00 to 1.81) and the composite outcome (hazard ratio: 1.46; 95% confidence interval: 1.10 to 1.94) compared with CABG.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Long-term data on the durability of left main PCI relative to CABG.

title: Intravascular Ultrasound Versus Angiography-Guided Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation: The ULTIMATE Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized trial; 1,448 all-comer patients randomly assigned (1:1 ratio).
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-country, open-label, and modest event numbers.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of IVUS-guided versus angiography-guided DES implantation in all-comers.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 12 months follow-up, 60 TVFs (4.2%) occurred, with 21 (2.9%) in the IVUS group and 39 (5.4%) in the angiography group (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.530; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.312 to 0.901; p = 0.019).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds randomised evidence for routine imaging guidance in PCI.

title: Blinded outcomes and angina assessment of coronary bioresorbable scaffolds: 30-day and 1-year results from the ABSORB IV randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Active-controlled, blinded, multicentre, randomised trial; 2604 patients enrolled.
appraisal.main_limitation: Early follow-up only; scaffold safety concerns concern later time points.
appraisal.one_line: Blinded randomised comparison of bioresorbable scaffold and metallic everolimus-eluting stent, with angina assessment.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Target lesion failure at 1 year occurred in 98 (7·8%) patients assigned to BVS and 82 (6·4%) patients assigned to EES (difference 1·4%, upper 97·5% confidence limit 3·4; one-sided pnon-inferiority=0·0006).
appraisal.why_it_matters: A major trial on bioresorbable scaffolds with optimised implantation.

title: Stratified Medical Therapy Using Invasive Coronary Function Testing in Angina: The CorMicA Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized, controlled, blinded clinical trial; n = 76 intervention group; n = 75 blinded control group.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small, short follow-up, and symptom endpoint.
appraisal.one_line: Blinded trial of stratified therapy guided by invasive coronary function testing in angina without obstructive disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The intervention resulted in a mean improvement of 11.7 U in the Seattle Angina Questionnaire summary score at 6 months (95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.0 to 18.4; p = 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports interventional diagnostic testing in INOCA.

title: Six months versus 12 months dual antiplatelet therapy after drug-eluting stent implantation in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (DAPT-STEMI): randomised, multicentre, non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective, randomised, multicentre, non-inferiority trial; 870 randomised.
appraisal.main_limitation: Randomised after six event-free months, and the trial was small.
appraisal.one_line: Non-inferiority trial of 6 versus 12 months of DAPT after DES in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 4.8% of patients receiving SAPT versus 6.6% of patients receiving DAPT (hazard ratio 0.73, 95% confidence interval 0.41 to 1.27, P=0.26).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Short DAPT duration after STEMI is a common practical decision.

title: Transcatheter Mitral-Valve Repair in Patients with Heart Failure.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial at 78 sites in the United States and Canada; 614 patients enrolled (302 device, 312 control).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, with highly selected patients on maximal medical therapy; sharply contrasts with other trial.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial showing transcatheter mitral repair plus medical therapy reduced heart failure hospitalisation and mortality in secondary MR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The annualized rate of all hospitalizations for heart failure within 24 months was 35.8% per patient-year in the device group as compared with 67.9% per patient-year in the control group (hazard ratio, 0.53; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.40 to 0.70; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides the first randomised mortality benefit for TEER in heart failure and changes practice and guidelines.

title: Complete Versus Culprit-Only Lesion Intervention in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Observational cohort study of 37,491 NSTEMI patients; 21,857 patients (58.3%) had multivessel disease.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational design with confounding by indication, as complete revascularisation patients differed at baseline.
appraisal.one_line: Observational London cohort associating single-stage complete revascularisation in NSTEMI with lower long-term mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After multivariate Cox analysis (hazard ratio: 0.90; 95% confidence interval: 0.85 to 0.97) and the use of propensity matching (hazard ratio: 0.89; 95% confidence interval: 0.76 to 0.98) complete revascularization was associated with reduced mortality.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses complete revascularisation in NSTEMI, where randomised evidence is limited.

title: Timing of revascularization in patients with transient ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: a randomized clinical trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized clinical trial; 142 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trial with a surrogate primary endpoint.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of immediate versus delayed invasive strategy in transient ST-elevation MI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Infarct size as percentage of the left ventricular myocardial mass measured by CMR at day four was generally small and not different between the immediate and the delayed invasive group (1.3%; IQR 0.0-3.5% vs. 1.5% IQR 0.0-4.1%, P = 0.48).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses timing of angiography in an under-studied ACS presentation.

title: Long-Term Survival Following Multivessel Revascularization in Patients With Diabetes: The FREEDOM Follow-On Study.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial with extended follow-up; 943 patients contributed extended follow-up of 1,900 randomised.
appraisal.main_limitation: Follow-up covered only about half of the original cohort and was not randomised for the extension.
appraisal.one_line: Extended follow-up of FREEDOM comparing CABG with PCI-DES for diabetic multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The all-cause mortality rate was significantly higher in the PCI-DES group than in the CABG group (24.3% [159 deaths] vs. 18.3% [112 deaths]; hazard ratio: 1.36; 95% confidence interval: 1.07 to 1.74; p = 0.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Long-term survival data for revascularisation choice in diabetes.

title: Early Versus Standard Care Invasive Examination and Treatment of Patients With Non-ST-Segment Elevation Acute Coronary Syndrome.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial (VERDICT, NCT02061891); 2147 patients randomised to angiography within 12 hours or within 48 to 72 hours.
appraisal.main_limitation: The high-risk finding comes from a subgroup interaction and its confidence interval includes 1.
appraisal.one_line: Very early invasive strategy within 12 hours did not improve long-term outcomes over standard invasive care in non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome, with a signal in high-risk patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 296 (27.5%) in the very early group and 316 (29.5%) in the standard care group (hazard ratio, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.78-1.08). In patients with GRACE score >140 the hazard ratio was 0.81 (95% CI, 0.67-1.01; P value for interaction=0.023).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the timing of invasive management in NSTE-ACS and the case for early angiography in the highest-risk patients.

title: Antithrombotic Therapy in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation Treated With Oral Anticoagulation Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A North American Perspective-2018 Update.

appraisal.design_and_n: Expert consensus focused update; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus-derived recommendations from a regional expert group rather than a formal guideline process.
appraisal.one_line: North American focused update recommends non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants over vitamin K antagonists and double therapy by discharge for most patients with atrial fibrillation undergoing PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets expert guidance on antithrombotic regimens after PCI in anticoagulated patients, a common decision with ongoing evidence generation.

title: Relationship Between Operator Volume and Long-Term Outcomes After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

appraisal.design_and_n: NCDR CathPCI registry linked to Medicare claims: 723 644 PCI procedures by 8936 operators.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational; patients aged 65 years or older only, with differing case mix by operator volume.
appraisal.one_line: Medicare-linked registry analysis of operator PCI volume and outcomes, with in-hospital but not post-discharge differences.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Intermediate- and high-volume operators had a significantly lower rate of in-hospital death than low-volume operators (odds ratio, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.86-0.96 for intermediate versus low; odds ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.75-0.83 for high versus low).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs volume thresholds and quality policy for PCI operators.

title: Open-Label Randomized Trial Comparing Oral Anticoagulation With and Without Single Antiplatelet Therapy in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Stable Coronary Artery Disease Beyond 1 Year After Coronary Stent Implantation.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label noninferiority randomised trial (NCT01962545); 696 patients enrolled of 2000 planned.
appraisal.main_limitation: Premature termination left the trial underpowered and inconclusive, as the authors state.
appraisal.one_line: Open-label trial of oral anticoagulation alone versus with single antiplatelet therapy beyond 1 year after stenting in atrial fibrillation did not establish noninferiority and was terminated early.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 54 patients (15.7%) in the OAC-alone group and in 47 patients (13.6%) in the combined group (hazard ratio, 1.16; 95% CI, 0.79-1.72; P=0.20 for noninferiority, P=0.45 for superiority). Major bleeding occurred in 27 (7.8%) and 36 (10.4%) patients, respectively.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses whether antiplatelet therapy can be stopped in anticoagulated patients with stable disease after stenting, where randomised data were lacking.

title: Fractional flow reserve-guided percutaneous coronary intervention vs. medical therapy for patients with stable coronary lesions: meta-analysis of individual patient data.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and IPD meta-analysis of FAME 2 (NCT01132495), DANAMI-3-PRIMULTI (NCT01960933) and Compare-Acute (NCT01399736); 2400 subjects, 1056 to FFR-guided PCI and 1344 to medical therapy.
appraisal.main_limitation: Only three trials, with open-label design and heterogeneous populations including non-culprit lesions after acute coronary syndrome.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis of three trials found FFR-guided PCI reduced cardiac death or myocardial infarction versus medical therapy in stable coronary lesions, driven by myocardial infarction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After a median follow-up of 35 months, a reduction in the composite of cardiac death or MI was observed with FFR-guided PCI as compared with medical therapy (hazard ratio 0.72, 95% confidence interval 0.54-0.96; P = 0.02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Pools trial data on a hard composite in a common decision, though the effect is driven by myocardial infarction rather than death.

title: Effect of Low-Dose Intracoronary Alteplase During Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention on Microvascular Obstruction in Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Dose-ranging randomised trial (NCT02257294); 440 patients, placebo (n = 151), alteplase 10 mg (n = 144), alteplase 20 mg (n = 145).
appraisal.main_limitation: Primary outcome was an imaging surrogate and recruitment stopped early for futility.
appraisal.one_line: Intracoronary alteplase during primary PCI did not reduce microvascular obstruction and the trial stopped for futility.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Mean microvascular obstruction did not differ between the 20-mg alteplase and placebo groups (3.5% vs 2.3%; estimated difference, 1.16%; 95% CI, -0.08% to 2.41%; P = .32).
appraisal.why_it_matters: A negative trial that argues against adjunctive intracoronary fibrinolysis in STEMI.

title: Impact of Chronic Kidney Disease on Outcomes of Myocardial Revascularization in Patients With Diabetes.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Patient-level pooled analysis of COURAGE, BARI 2D and FREEDOM; 4,953 patients with eGFR available, 1,058 with CKD (21.4%).
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooling of trials with different designs and eras, with non-randomised comparisons across strata.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level pooled analysis of three trials associated CABG plus medical therapy with lower MACCE than PCI plus medical therapy in diabetes without CKD, but not clearly with CKD.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: CKD subjects were more likely to experience a MACCE (adjusted hazard ratio [HR]: 1.48; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.28 to 1.71; p = 0.0001). Without CKD, CABG + OMT was associated with lower MACCE than PCI + OMT (adjusted HR: 0.69; 95% CI: 0.55 to 0.86; p = 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses revascularisation choice in patients with diabetes and CKD, a population under-represented in trials.

title: The Evolving Role of the Cardiac Catheterization Laboratory in the Management of Patients With Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement; narrative review of observational and trial evidence, no pooled sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Evidence base is mainly observational case series with selection bias, as the statement notes.
appraisal.one_line: AHA scientific statement reviews coronary disease prevalence in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and the emerging use of early angiography and VA-ECMO-facilitated resuscitation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets out the position of a major society on catheterisation and mechanical support after cardiac arrest while randomised trials are pending.

title: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Duration Based on Ischemic and Bleeding Risks After Coronary Stenting.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled analysis of 8 randomised trials; 14,963 patients, 3,118 underwent complex PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis across heterogeneous trials with non-randomised stratification by risk.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled trial analysis suggests benefit of long-term DAPT after complex PCI only when high bleeding risk features are absent.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Long-term DAPT in non-HBR patients reduced ischemic events in both complex (absolute risk difference: -3.86%; 95% confidence interval: -7.71 to +0.06) and noncomplex PCI strata (absolute risk difference: -1.14%; 95% confidence interval: -2.26 to -0.02), but not among HBR patients.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs DAPT duration by weighing ischaemic and bleeding risk, a frequent decision.

title: Randomized Trial Evaluating Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for the Treatment of Chronic Total Occlusion.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label multicentre randomised noninferiority trial (NCT01078051); 834 patients randomly assigned, CTO-PCI (n=417) or no CTO-PCI (n=398), stopped before the 1284 planned.
appraisal.main_limitation: Underpowered for clinical end points because of slow recruitment, with 78 (19.6%) crossovers.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial found no difference in major adverse cardiovascular events between CTO-PCI and no CTO-PCI, but stopped early with high crossover.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary end point incidence was 22.3% versus 22.4% (hazard ratio, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.77 to 1.37; P=0.86).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds randomised data on CTO revascularisation, where prognostic benefit remains unproven.

title: Antithrombotic Therapy after Acute Coronary Syndrome or PCI in Atrial Fibrillation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: International two-by-two factorial randomised trial (AUGUSTUS, NCT02415400); 4614 patients from 33 countries.
appraisal.main_limitation: Not powered for ischaemic outcomes, and the apixaban comparison was open-label.
appraisal.one_line: Apixaban without aspirin caused less bleeding and fewer hospitalisations than vitamin K antagonist or aspirin-containing regimens in atrial fibrillation after ACS or PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was noted in 10.5% of the patients receiving apixaban, as compared with 14.7% of those receiving a vitamin K antagonist (hazard ratio, 0.69; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.58 to 0.81; P<0.001 for both noninferiority and superiority), and in 16.1% of the patients receiving aspirin, as compared with 9.0% of those receiving placebo (hazard ratio, 1.89; 95% CI, 1.59 to 2.24; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly informs the preferred antithrombotic regimen after PCI in anticoagulated patients, a common clinical problem.

title: Coronary Angiography after Cardiac Arrest without ST-Segment Elevation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised trial (COACT, NTR4973); 552 patients randomised.
appraisal.main_limitation: Delayed angiography strategy was angiography after neurological recovery, and the trial was not powered for small differences.
appraisal.one_line: Immediate coronary angiography was not better than delayed angiography for 90-day survival after resuscitated cardiac arrest without ST-segment elevation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 90 days, 176 of 273 patients (64.5%) in the immediate angiography group and 178 of 265 patients (67.2%) in the delayed angiography group were alive (odds ratio, 0.89; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.62 to 1.27; P = 0.51).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges routine immediate angiography in cardiac arrest without STEMI, a decision made in a high-mortality setting.

title: Impact of large periprocedural myocardial infarction on mortality after percutaneous coronary intervention and coronary artery bypass grafting for left main disease: an analysis from the EXCEL trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of the randomised EXCEL trial; 1858 patients treated as assigned.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc prognostic analysis of a randomised trial subject to confounding.
appraisal.one_line: Periprocedural MI in EXCEL was more common after CABG than PCI, and only large myonecrosis was associated with 3-year mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Periprocedural MI occurred in 34/935 (3.6%) of patients in the PCI group and 56/923 (6.1%) of patients in the CABG group [odds ratio 0.61, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.40-0.93; P = 0.02]. PMI was associated with all-cause death at 3 years (adjusted HR 2.28, 95% CI 1.22-4.29; P = 0.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on the definition of periprocedural MI and its prognostic threshold in left main revascularisation.

title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Older Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction and Cardiogenic Shock.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Observational analysis of 317,728 encounters with STEMI and shock, of which 111,901 (35%) were adults aged 75 years or older.
appraisal.main_limitation: In-hospital outcome only, administrative data and confounding by selection for PCI.
appraisal.one_line: National inpatient database analysis associating PCI with lower in-hospital mortality in older adults with STEMI and cardiogenic shock.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Utilizing PS matching methods, PCI was associated with a lower risk of in-hospital mortality across quintiles of propensity score (Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio: 0.48; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.45 to 0.51).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Relevant to the exclusion of older patients from invasive shock care.

title: Drug-eluting or bare-metal stents for percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review and individual patient data meta-analysis of randomised clinical trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and IPD meta-analysis of 20 randomised trials (PROSPERO CRD42017060520); 26 616 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trials were conducted over differing eras, and the comparison is not relevant to patients where DES are contraindicated.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis found new-generation DES reduced cardiac death or myocardial infarction versus bare-metal stents, with the effect arising in the first year.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The risk of the primary outcome was reduced in DES recipients compared with BMS recipients (HR 0·84, 95% CI 0·78-0·90, p<0·001). All-cause death was unaffected (HR with DES 0·96, 95% CI 0·88-1·05, p=0·358).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Settles the safety comparison of new-generation DES with bare-metal stents at scale, relevant to high bleeding risk practice.

title: Clinical use of intracoronary imaging. Part 2: acute coronary syndromes, ambiguous coronary angiography findings, and guiding interventional decision-making: an expert consensus document of the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions.

appraisal.design_and_n: Expert consensus document; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus opinion that reflects mostly observational and surrogate-based evidence.
appraisal.one_line: EAPCI consensus document sets out when intracoronary imaging should guide treatment in ACS and ambiguous lesions and how to use imaging-derived physiology.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Guides use of intravascular imaging, a rapidly expanding area of coronary intervention.

title: Defining high bleeding risk in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a consensus document from the Academic Research Consortium for High Bleeding Risk.

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus document from a 31-member consortium; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Definition derived from consensus and available evidence rather than prospective validation.
appraisal.one_line: ARC-HBR consensus document proposes a standard definition of high bleeding risk in patients undergoing PCI for trials and clinical decisions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides a common definition for trial design, regulatory review and antithrombotic decisions in high bleeding risk patients.

title: Drug-coated balloon for treatment of de-novo coronary artery lesions in patients with high bleeding risk (DEBUT): a single-blind, randomised, non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Single-blind randomised non-inferiority trial (DEBUT, NCT01781546) at five sites in Finland; 220 patients recruited, 208 assigned, drug-coated balloon (n=102) or bare metal stent (n=106).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trial in five Finnish centres with a bare-metal stent comparator rather than a contemporary drug-eluting stent.
appraisal.one_line: Drug-coated balloon PCI was associated with fewer MACE than bare-metal stents at 9 months in high bleeding risk patients in a small single-blind trial.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 9 months, major adverse cardiac events had occurred in one patient (1%) in the drug-coated balloon group and in 15 patients (14%) in the bare-metal stent group (absolute risk difference -13·2 percentage points [95% CI -6·2 to -21·1], risk ratio 0·07 [95% CI 0·01 to 0·52]; p<0·00001 for non-inferiority and p=0·00034 for superiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests a stent-free strategy in high bleeding risk patients, a population where short antiplatelet duration is desirable.

title: Magnetic Resonance Perfusion or Fractional Flow Reserve in Coronary Disease.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Unblinded multicentre randomised clinical-effectiveness trial (MR-INFORM); 918 patients randomised.
appraisal.main_limitation: Unblinded design with one-year follow-up and a noninferiority margin of 6 percentage points.
appraisal.one_line: Cardiovascular MRI-guided revascularisation was noninferior to FFR-guided revascularisation for one-year major adverse cardiac events in stable angina, with fewer revascularisations.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 15 of 421 patients (3.6%) in the cardiovascular-MRI group and 16 of 430 patients (3.7%) in the FFR group (risk difference, -0.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -2.7 to 2.4), findings that met the noninferiority threshold.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Compares non-invasive and invasive strategies for guiding revascularisation in stable coronary disease.

title: Effect of 1-Month Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Followed by Clopidogrel vs 12-Month Dual Antiplatelet Therapy on Cardiovascular and Bleeding Events in Patients Receiving PCI: The STOPDAPT-2 Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre open-label randomised trial (STOPDAPT-2) at 90 hospitals in Japan; 3045 patients randomised, 1-month DAPT (n=1523) or 12-month DAPT (n=1522).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trial in a Japanese population with a composite that combines ischaemic and bleeding events.
appraisal.one_line: One month of DAPT followed by clopidogrel monotherapy was noninferior and superior to 12 months of DAPT for a composite of cardiovascular and bleeding events after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 2.36% with 1-month DAPT and 3.70% with 12-month DAPT (absolute difference, -1.34% [95% CI, -2.57% to -0.11%]; hazard ratio [HR], 0.64 [95% CI, 0.42-0.98]), meeting criteria for noninferiority (P < .001) and for superiority (P = .04).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds to the evidence for very short DAPT after PCI, a decision made in most stented patients.

title: Effect of P2Y12 Inhibitor Monotherapy vs Dual Antiplatelet Therapy on Cardiovascular Events in Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: The SMART-CHOICE Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label noninferiority randomised trial (SMART-CHOICE) at 33 hospitals in Korea; 2993 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design and protocol adherence of 79.3% in the monotherapy group.
appraisal.one_line: P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy after 3 months of DAPT was noninferior to 12 months of DAPT for MACCE and reduced bleeding after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 12 months, major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events occurred in 42 patients in the P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy group and in 36 patients in the DAPT group (2.9% vs 2.5%; difference, 0.4% [1-sided 95% CI, -∞% to 1.3%]; P = .007 for noninferiority). The rate of bleeding was significantly lower in the P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy group than in the DAPT group (2.0% vs 3.4%; HR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.36-0.92; P = .02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy after short DAPT as a de-escalation strategy.

title: Duration of dual antiplatelet therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent: systematic review and network meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised trials; 17 studies (n=46 864).
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level pooling across heterogeneous populations and regimens, with short-term DAPT largely clopidogrel-based.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis found long-term DAPT increased major bleeding and non-cardiac death versus short-term DAPT, with similar efficacy of short and standard DAPT in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with short term DAPT, long term DAPT resulted in higher rates of major bleeding (odds ratio 1.78, 95% confidence interval 1.27 to 2.49) and non-cardiac death (1.63, 1.03 to 2.59); standard term DAPT was associated with higher rates of any bleeding (1.39, 1.01 to 1.92).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Summarises DAPT duration evidence in a general-tier journal, though newer trials were accumulating.

title: Myocardial Viability and Long-Term Outcomes in Ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial analysis (STICH, NCT00023595); 601 patients assessed for viability, with median follow-up of 10.4 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Viability substudy of a subset of the trial population with non-randomised viability assessment.
appraisal.one_line: Long-term STICH analysis found CABG plus medical therapy reduced all-cause death in ischaemic cardiomyopathy irrespective of myocardial viability.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: CABG plus medical therapy was associated with a lower incidence of death from any cause than medical therapy alone (182 deaths among 298 patients in the CABG group vs. 209 deaths among 303 patients in the medical-therapy group; adjusted hazard ratio, 0.73; 95% confidence interval, 0.60 to 0.90). No significant interaction was observed between viability and the effect of CABG (P = 0.34 for interaction).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges the use of viability testing to select patients with ischaemic cardiomyopathy for revascularisation.

title: Antithrombotic Therapy for Atrial Fibrillation with Stable Coronary Disease.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre open-label randomised trial in Japan (AFIRE, NCT02642419); 2236 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, early termination, and an exclusively Japanese population on a Japanese-specific rivaroxaban dose.
appraisal.one_line: Rivaroxaban monotherapy was noninferior for efficacy and superior for major bleeding compared with rivaroxaban plus an antiplatelet in atrial fibrillation with stable coronary disease, and the trial stopped early for mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Rivaroxaban monotherapy was noninferior to combination therapy for the primary efficacy end point, with event rates of 4.14% and 5.75% per patient-year, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.72; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.55 to 0.95; P<0.001 for noninferiority). Major bleeding rates were 1.62% and 2.76% per patient-year (hazard ratio, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.39 to 0.89; P = 0.01 for superiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports omitting antiplatelet therapy in anticoagulated patients with chronic coronary disease.

title: Complete Revascularization with Multivessel PCI for Myocardial Infarction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial (COMPLETE, NCT01740479); 2016 patients in the complete-revascularisation group and 2025 in the culprit-lesion-only group.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, and angiographic rather than physiology-guided selection of nonculprit lesions.
appraisal.one_line: Complete revascularisation with nonculprit PCI reduced cardiovascular death or myocardial infarction compared with culprit-lesion-only PCI in STEMI with multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At a median follow-up of 3 years, the first coprimary outcome had occurred in 158 of the 2016 patients (7.8%) in the complete-revascularization group as compared with 213 of the 2025 patients (10.5%) in the culprit-lesion-only PCI group (hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.60 to 0.91; P = 0.004).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Likely to change guideline recommendations on nonculprit revascularisation in STEMI, a very common decision.

title: Ticagrelor or Prasugrel in Patients with Acute Coronary Syndromes.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre open-label randomised trial (ISAR-REACT 5, NCT01944800); 4018 patients randomised.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design with unmasked treatment strategy differences, such as pretreatment, which may affect the comparison.
appraisal.one_line: Prasugrel reduced the composite of death, myocardial infarction or stroke compared with ticagrelor at one year in ACS patients undergoing planned invasive evaluation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary end-point event occurred in 184 of 2012 patients (9.3%) in the ticagrelor group and in 137 of 2006 patients (6.9%) in the prasugrel group (hazard ratio, 1.36; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.09 to 1.70; P = 0.006). Major bleeding was observed in 5.4% versus 4.8% (hazard ratio, 1.12; 95% CI, 0.83 to 1.51; P = 0.46).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly compares the two potent P2Y12 inhibitors in ACS and bears on guideline preference between them.

title: Comparison of a Complete Percutaneous Versus Surgical Approach to Aortic Valve Replacement and Revascularization in Patients at Intermediate Surgical Risk: Results From the Randomized SURTAVI Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective randomised SURTAVI trial; 332 of 1660 patients with attempted implants were assigned to revascularisation (169 TAVR plus PCI, 163 SAVR plus CABG).
appraisal.main_limitation: Revascularisation was not randomised separately and patients with SYNTAX score >22 were excluded; the subgroup is small.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified SURTAVI analysis found no difference in 2-year death or disabling stroke between TAVR plus PCI and SAVR plus CABG in intermediate-risk patients with noncomplex coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: No significant difference in the rate of the primary end point was found between TAVR and percutaneous coronary intervention and SAVR and coronary artery bypass grafting (16.0%; 95% CI, 11.1-22.9 versus 14.0%; 95% CI, 9.2-21.1; P=0.62), or between TAVR and SAVR (11.9%; 95% CI, 9.5-14.7 versus 12.3%; 95% CI, 9.8-15.4; P=0.76).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the management of CAD in TAVI candidates, a domain where evidence from randomised comparisons is sparse.

title: A Genotype-Guided Strategy for Oral P2Y12 Inhibitors in Primary PCI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, open-label, assessor-blinded trial; 2488 patients (1242 genotype-guided, 1246 standard).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design and a noninferiority margin of 2 percentage points; the bleeding result is a co-primary with a borderline P value.
appraisal.one_line: POPular Genetics found CYP2C19 genotype-guided P2Y12 inhibitor choice noninferior to ticagrelor or prasugrel after primary PCI, with less bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary combined outcome occurred in 63 patients (5.1%) in the genotype-guided group and in 73 patients (5.9%) in the standard-treatment group (absolute difference, -0.7 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -2.0 to 0.7; P<0.001 for noninferiority). The primary bleeding outcome occurred in 122 patients (9.8%) in the genotype-guided group and in 156 patients (12.5%) in the standard-treatment group (hazard ratio, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.61 to 0.98; P = 0.04).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports guided de-escalation of P2Y12 inhibitor therapy in STEMI, relevant to the guideline position on guided therapy.

title: Ticagrelor in patients with diabetes and stable coronary artery disease with a history of previous percutaneous coronary intervention (THEMIS-PCI): a phase 3, placebo-controlled, randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified subgroup of the randomised, double-blind THEMIS trial; 11 154 patients with previous PCI, median follow-up 3·3 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: A subgroup analysis of a trial that was neutral in its overall population on net benefit terms, with a manufacturer-funded design.
appraisal.one_line: THEMIS-PCI reported that ticagrelor added to aspirin reduced cardiovascular death, MI or stroke but increased TIMI major bleeding in patients with diabetes and previous PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Fewer patients receiving ticagrelor had a primary efficacy outcome event than in the placebo group (404 [7·3%] of 5558 vs 480 [8·6%] of 5596; HR 0·85 [95% CI 0·74-0·97], p=0·013). TIMI major bleeding occurred in 111 (2·0%) of 5536 patients receiving ticagrelor and 62 (1·1%) of 5564 patients receiving placebo (HR 2·03 [95% CI 1·48-2·76], p<0·0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Defines a long-term antiplatelet option for high-ischaemic-risk patients with diabetes after PCI, with an explicit bleeding cost.

title: Biodegradable polymer sirolimus-eluting stents versus durable polymer everolimus-eluting stents in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (BIOSTEMI): a single-blind, prospective, randomised superiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Investigator-initiated, single-blind randomised superiority trial; 1300 patients (649 vs 651) with Bayesian analysis.
appraisal.main_limitation: Difference driven by ischaemia-driven revascularisation, with similar cardiac death, reinfarction and stent thrombosis; manufacturer-funded and follow-up limited to 12 months.
appraisal.one_line: BIOSTEMI found lower 12-month target lesion failure with ultrathin biodegradable polymer sirolimus-eluting stents than durable polymer everolimus-eluting stents in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Target lesion failure occurred in 25 (4%) of 649 patients treated with biodegradable polymer sirolimus-eluting stents and 36 (6%) of 651 patients treated with durable polymer everolimus-eluting stents (difference -1·6 percentage points; rate ratio 0·59, 95% Bayesian credibility interval 0·37-0·94; posterior probability of superiority 0·986).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds comparative stent evidence in primary PCI, though the clinical event differences are modest.

title: Percutaneous coronary intervention versus coronary artery bypass grafting in patients with three-vessel or left main coronary artery disease: 10-year follow-up of the multicentre randomised controlled SYNTAX trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Extended follow-up of the multicentre randomised SYNTAX trial; 1800 patients (903 PCI, 897 CABG), vital status complete in 93% and 95%.
appraisal.main_limitation: First-generation paclitaxel-eluting stents were used and the subgroup interaction was a prespecified analysis not powered for mortality.
appraisal.one_line: SYNTAXES reports 10-year all-cause death after PCI or CABG for three-vessel and left main disease, with a survival difference in three-vessel disease only.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 10 years, 248 (28%) patients had died after PCI and 212 (24%) after CABG (hazard ratio 1·19 [95% CI 0·99-1·43], p=0·066). Among patients with three-vessel disease, 153 (28%) of 546 had died after PCI versus 114 (21%) of 549 after CABG (hazard ratio 1·42 [95% CI 1·11-1·81]), and among patients with left main coronary artery disease, 95 (27%) of 357 had died after PCI versus 98 (28%) of 348 after CABG (0·92 [0·69-1·22], pinteraction=0·023).
appraisal.why_it_matters: The only randomised 10-year mortality comparison of PCI and CABG, directly informing the heart-team decision and guideline classes for multivessel disease.

title: Edoxaban-based versus vitamin K antagonist-based antithrombotic regimen after successful coronary stenting in patients with atrial fibrillation (ENTRUST-AF PCI): a randomised, open-label, phase 3b trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, open-label noninferiority phase 3b trial; 1506 patients (751 edoxaban, 755 VKA).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, not powered for ischaemic events, and the comparator included aspirin for 1 to 12 months.
appraisal.one_line: ENTRUST-AF PCI showed an edoxaban-based regimen was noninferior to a VKA-based regimen for major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding after PCI in atrial fibrillation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Major or CRNM bleeding events occurred in 128 (17%) of 751 patients (annualised event rate 20·7%) with the edoxaban regimen and 152 (20%) of 755 patients (annualised event rate 25·6%) patients with the VKA regimen; hazard ratio 0·83 (95% CI 0·65-1·05; p=0·0010 for non-inferiority, margin hazard ratio 1·20; p=0·1154 for superiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds a fourth DOAC-based dual therapy trial for patients with AF undergoing PCI.

title: Effect of remote ischaemic conditioning on clinical outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction (CONDI-2/ERIC-PPCI): a single-blind randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: International single-blind randomised controlled trial; 5401 patients randomly allocated (2569 control and 2546 remote ischaemic conditioning analysed).
appraisal.main_limitation: Sham conditioning was used at UK sites only, and the analysis excluded patients after randomisation.
appraisal.one_line: CONDI-2/ERIC-PPCI found no improvement in cardiac death or heart failure hospitalisation at 12 months with remote ischaemic conditioning before primary PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The Kaplan-Meier-estimated frequencies of cardiac death or hospitalisation for heart failure were 220 (8·6%) patients in the control group and 239 (9·4%) in the remote ischaemic conditioning group (hazard ratio 1·10 [95% CI 0·91-1·32], p=0·32 for intervention versus control).
appraisal.why_it_matters: A large neutral trial that closes a long-running line of adjunctive STEMI cardioprotection research.

title: 16-year follow-up of the Danish Acute Myocardial Infarction 2 (DANAMI-2) trial: primary percutaneous coronary intervention vs. fibrinolysis in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Long-term follow-up of a randomised trial of 1572 STEMI patients at 24 referral hospitals and 5 invasive centres, with registry-based outcomes beyond 3 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Fibrinolysis-era comparator and registry-ascertained outcomes beyond 3 years; all-cause mortality did not differ.
appraisal.one_line: The 16-year DANAMI-2 follow-up found a sustained lower rate of death or reinfarction and lower cardiac mortality with primary PCI than fibrinolysis in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After 16 years, pPCI-treated patients had a sustained lower rate of composite endpoint compared to patients treated with fibrinolysis in the overall cohort [58.7% vs. 62.3%; hazard ratio (HR) 0.86, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.76-0.98]. No difference in all-cause mortality was found, but cardiac mortality was reduced by an absolute of 4.4% in favour of pPCI (18.3% vs. 22.7%; HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.63-0.98).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives the longest randomised follow-up of reperfusion strategy in STEMI.

title: Paclitaxel-coated balloon angioplasty vs. drug-eluting stenting for the treatment of coronary in-stent restenosis: a comprehensive, collaborative, individual patient data meta-analysis of 10 randomized clinical trials (DAEDALUS study).

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data meta-analysis of 10 randomised trials, 1976 patients (1033 PCB, 943 DES), registered with PROSPERO (CRD42017075007).
appraisal.main_limitation: The individual trials were small and used heterogeneous devices, so hard-outcome comparisons remain imprecise.
appraisal.one_line: DAEDALUS IPD meta-analysis found repeat stenting with DES more effective than paclitaxel-coated balloon at reducing target lesion revascularisation at 3 years in coronary in-stent restenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 3-year follow-up, PCB was associated with a significant increase in the risk of target lesion revascularization (TLR) compared with DES [hazard ratio (HR) 1.32, 95% CI 1.02-1.70, P = 0.035; number-needed-to-harm 28.5]. The primary safety endpoint of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, or target lesion thrombosis was comparable between treatments (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.58-1.09, P = 0.152).
appraisal.why_it_matters: A rigorous IPD synthesis resolving conflicting ISR trials and testing effect modification by stent type, directly relevant to DCB use.

title: Five-year outcomes following timely primary percutaneous intervention, late primary percutaneous intervention, or a pharmaco-invasive strategy in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: the FAST-MI programme.

appraisal.design_and_n: FAST-MI nationwide observational surveys, 2942 STEMI patients with reperfusion therapy: 1288 (54%) timely pPCI, 830 (28%) late pPCI and 824 (28%) intravenous fibrinolysis.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational with residual confounding and treatment-by-indication differences between strategies.
appraisal.one_line: Registry comparison of 5-year outcomes after timely pPCI, late pPCI or a pharmaco-invasive strategy in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Five-year survival was higher with a pharmaco-invasive strategy (89.8%) compared with late pPCI [79.5%; adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 1.51; 1.13-2.02] and similar to timely pPCI (88.2%, adjusted HR 1.02; 0.75-1.38).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears directly on the guideline default of pPCI when delays exceed the recommended window.

title: Clinically Significant Bleeding With Ticagrelor Versus Clopidogrel in Korean Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes Intended for Invasive Management: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised trial, 800 Korean patients (400 per arm), 12-month follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Underpowered for ischaemic efficacy, as the authors state.
appraisal.one_line: Korean RCT found more clinically significant bleeding with ticagrelor than clopidogrel in ACS patients intended for early invasive management.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 12 months, the incidence of clinically significant bleeding was significantly higher in the ticagrelor group than in the clopidogrel group (11.7% [45/400] vs 5.3% [21/400]; hazard ratio [HR], 2.26; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.34 to 3.79; P=0.002). The incidence of death from cardiovascular causes, myocardial infarction, or stroke was not significantly different between the ticagrelor group and the clopidogrel group (9.2% [36/400] vs 5.8% [23/400]; HR, 1.62; 95% CI, 0.96 to 2.74; P=0.07).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds a new signal for ethnicity-specific antiplatelet selection in East Asian ACS patients.

title: Ticagrelor with or without Aspirin in High-Risk Patients after PCI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Double-blind randomised trial; 9006 enrolled, 7119 randomised after 3 months of ticagrelor plus aspirin.
appraisal.main_limitation: Event-free selection at 3 months and an ischaemic endpoint with a noninferiority margin of 1.6 percentage points; manufacturer-funded.
appraisal.one_line: TWILIGHT found ticagrelor monotherapy after 3 months of DAPT reduced clinically relevant bleeding without more death, MI or stroke in high-risk PCI patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The incidence of the primary end point was 4.0% among patients randomly assigned to receive ticagrelor plus placebo and 7.1% among patients assigned to receive ticagrelor plus aspirin (hazard ratio, 0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.45 to 0.68; P<0.001). The incidence of death from any cause, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke was 3.9% in both groups (difference, -0.06 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.97 to 0.84; hazard ratio, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.78 to 1.25; P<0.001 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: A blinded trial of aspirin-free P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy in high-risk patients, directly shaping DAPT de-escalation recommendations.

title: Antithrombotic Therapy in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Acute Coronary Syndrome Treated Medically or With Percutaneous Coronary Intervention or Undergoing Elective Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Insights From the AUGUSTUS Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified subgroup analysis of a 2x2 factorial randomised trial; 4614 patients (1097 medically treated ACS, 1714 ACS with PCI, 1784 elective PCI).
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis in a trial not powered for ischaemic events within each stratum.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified AUGUSTUS analysis showed apixaban without aspirin gave less bleeding than VKA-based regimens across medically managed ACS, ACS with PCI and elective PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Apixaban compared with vitamin K antagonist reduced ISTH major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding in patients with ACS treated medically (hazard ratio [HR], 0.44 [95% CI, 0.28-0.68]), patients with ACS treated with PCI (HR, 0.68 [95% CI, 0.52-0.89]), and patients undergoing elective PCI (HR, 0.82 [95% CI, 0.64-1.04]; Pinteraction=0.052).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Extends the evidence for aspirin-free dual therapy with a DOAC to medically managed ACS.

title: Five-Year Outcomes after PCI or CABG for Left Main Coronary Disease.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 1905 patients with left main disease (948 PCI, 957 CABG).
appraisal.main_limitation: All-cause death was a secondary outcome and the primary comparison was not conclusive.
appraisal.one_line: EXCEL 5-year follow-up found no significant difference in death, stroke or MI between PCI and CABG for low or intermediate complexity left main disease, with higher all-cause death after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 5 years, a primary outcome event had occurred in 22.0% of the patients in the PCI group and in 19.2% of the patients in the CABG group (difference, 2.8 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.9 to 6.5; P = 0.13). Death from any cause occurred more frequently in the PCI group than in the CABG group (in 13.0% vs. 9.9%; difference, 3.1 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.2 to 6.1).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Contributes directly to the contested ESC and ACC/AHA left main revascularisation recommendations alongside NOBLE.

title: Individualizing Revascularization Strategy for Diabetic Patients With Multivessel Coronary Disease.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Heterogeneity-of-treatment-effect modelling in 1,900 FREEDOM patients with bootstrap internal validation and external registry validation.
appraisal.main_limitation: Modest discrimination (c = 0.67) and treatment interactions that were not validated against a randomised comparison.
appraisal.one_line: Risk models from FREEDOM patient-level data estimated individual benefit of CABG versus PCI in diabetes with multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 5-year MACE occurred in 346 (18.2%) patients, and 310 (16.3%) had angina at 1 year. The MACE model included 8 variables and treatment interactions with smoking status (c = 0.67). PCI was never superior to CABG, and CABG was superior to PCI for MACE in 54.5% of patients and in 100% of patients with history of smoking.
appraisal.why_it_matters: An example of HTE modelling for revascularisation choice, relevant to the heart-team decision.

title: Safety and efficacy outcomes of double vs. triple antithrombotic therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation following percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review and meta-analysis of non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulant-based randomized clinical trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 4 RCTs, 10 234 patients (DAT = 5496 vs. TAT = 4738).
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level pooling with substantial heterogeneity in bleeding (I2 = 69%) and few stent thrombosis events.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of four NOAC-based RCTs found double therapy lowered bleeding but raised stent thrombosis versus triple therapy in AF patients undergoing PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary safety endpoint (ISTH major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding) was significantly lower with DAT compared with TAT [risk ratio (RR) 0.66, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.56-0.78; P < 0.0001; I2 = 69%]. This benefit was counterbalanced by a significant increase of stent thrombosis (RR 1.59, 95% CI 1.01-2.50; P = 0.04; I2 = 0%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Summarises the efficacy-safety trade-off of dual versus triple therapy that underlies current guideline recommendations.

title: Ticagrelor Alone Versus Dual Antiplatelet Therapy From 1 Month After Drug-Eluting Coronary Stenting.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified ancillary study of the GLOBAL LEADERS randomised trial; independent adjudication of 7,585 patients from 20 sites.
appraisal.main_limitation: Substudy of a subset of sites in an open-label trial, with the parent trial missing its primary endpoint.
appraisal.one_line: GLASSY adjudication sub-study found ticagrelor monotherapy after 1 month DAPT noninferior but not superior to conventional DAPT for ischaemic events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 2-year coprimary efficacy endpoint occurred in 271 (7.14%) and in 319 (8.41%) patients in the experimental and conventional groups, respectively (rate ratio [RR]: 0.85; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.72 to 0.99), fulfilling noninferiority (p noninferiority <0.001), but not superiority (p superiority = 0.0465). The rates of BARC 3 or 5 bleeding did not differ (RR: 1.00; 95% CI: 0.75 to 1.33; p = 0.986).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the contested evidence on short DAPT followed by P2Y12 monotherapy.

title: 2019 American Heart Association Focused Update on Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support: Use of Advanced Airways, Vasopressors, and Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation During Cardiac Arrest: An Update to the American Heart Association Guidelines for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Emergency Cardiovascular Care.

appraisal.design_and_n: Guideline focused update summarising published evidence; no sample size applies.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract gives no recommendation classes or levels, so positions cannot be taken from it.
appraisal.one_line: The 2019 AHA focused update revises recommendations on advanced airways, vasopressors and extracorporeal CPR in cardiac arrest.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets the guideline position on ECPR and post-arrest care within the cardiac arrest domain.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Low-Dose Colchicine after Myocardial Infarction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, double-blind trial; 4745 patients enrolled within 30 days of MI (2366 colchicine, 2379 placebo), median follow-up 22.6 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: The effect was driven by stroke and urgent angina hospitalisation, with no clear effect on cardiovascular death or MI.
appraisal.one_line: COLCOT found low-dose colchicine reduced the composite of ischaemic cardiovascular events after recent MI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 5.5% of the patients in the colchicine group, as compared with 7.1% of those in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.77; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.61 to 0.96; P = 0.02). Pneumonia was reported as a serious adverse event in 0.9% of the patients in the colchicine group and in 0.4% of those in the placebo group (P = 0.03).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First large outcome trial of an anti-inflammatory drug started early after MI, with direct implications for post-MI secondary prevention guidelines.

title: The Evolving Landscape of Impella Use in the United States Among Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention With Mechanical Circulatory Support.

appraisal.design_and_n: Premier Healthcare Database, 48 306 patients undergoing PCI with MCS at 432 hospitals between January 2004 and December 2016; 4782 (9.9%) received Impella.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational administrative data with unmeasured confounding by indication.
appraisal.one_line: Large US hospital database analysis of Impella use trends, variation and outcomes in PCI with mechanical circulatory support.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After adjustment for the propensity score, and accounting for clustering of patients by hospitals, Impella use was associated with death: odds ratio, 1.24 (95% CI, 1.13-1.36); bleeding: odds ratio, 1.10 (95% CI, 1.00-1.21); and stroke: odds ratio, 1.34 (95% CI, 1.18-1.53).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Documents rapid uptake and wide hospital variation in Impella use despite limited randomised evidence in PCI.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Stents in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: IPD network meta-analysis of 15 RCTs, 10,979 patients, representing 87.7% of patients in the network.
appraisal.main_limitation: Network estimates between individual DES rest on few direct comparisons and indirect inference.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level network meta-analysis found DES superior to BMS in STEMI and no difference among specific DES.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with bare-metal stents (BMS), patients treated with paclitaxel-, sirolimus-, everolimus-, or biolimus-eluting stents had a significantly lower risk of the primary endpoint (adjusted hazard ratios [HRs]: 0.74 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.63 to 0.88], 0.65 [95% CI: 0.49 to 0.85], 0.70 [95% CI: 0.53 to 0.91], and 0.66 [95% CI: 0.49 to 0.88], respectively).
appraisal.why_it_matters: A synthesis of stent choice in STEMI of the kind a guideline committee would cite.

title: Timing of Staged Nonculprit Artery Revascularization in Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: COMPLETE Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified analysis of a randomised trial, 4,041 patients with STEMI and multivessel disease.
appraisal.main_limitation: Timing was investigator-chosen within a stratified randomisation, not randomised.
appraisal.one_line: COMPLETE timing analysis found the benefit of complete revascularisation in STEMI was consistent irrespective of in-hospital or post-discharge staging.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: For nonculprit-lesion PCI planned during the index hospitalization (actual time: median 1 day), CV death or MI was reduced with complete revascularization compared with culprit-lesion only PCI (HR: 0.77; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.59 to 1.00). For nonculprit lesion PCI planned to occur after hospital discharge (actual time: median 23 days), CV death or MI was also reduced with complete revascularization (HR: 0.69; 95% CI: 0.49 to 0.97; interaction p = 0.62).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses the timing of complete revascularisation after STEMI, an open practice question.

title: Long-term ticagrelor for secondary prevention in patients with prior myocardial infarction and no history of coronary stenting: insights from PEGASUS-TIMI 54.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified analysis of a randomised trial; 4199 of 21 162 patients had no prior coronary stenting.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis; benefit was shown with bleeding cost in the parent trial.
appraisal.one_line: PEGASUS-TIMI 54 analysis found similar relative benefit of long-term ticagrelor with and without prior stenting after MI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The relative risk reduction in MACE with ticagrelor (pooled doses) was similar in patients without (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.68-0.99) and with prior stenting (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.75-0.96; P for interaction = 0.76).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Extends the population eligible for prolonged P2Y12 inhibitor therapy beyond stented patients.

title: Long-Term Follow-Up of Complete Versus Lesion-Only Revascularization in STEMI and Multivessel Disease: The CvLPRIT Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Long-term follow-up of a randomised trial of complete versus infarct-artery-only revascularisation in STEMI; median follow-up 5.6 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: A small trial; landmark analysis from 12 months showed no significant difference.
appraisal.one_line: CvLPRIT long-term follow-up found the MACE benefit of complete in-hospital revascularisation was sustained to a median 5.6 years.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary MACE endpoint rate at this time point was 24.0% in the complete revascularization group but 37.7% of the infarct-related artery-only group (hazard ratio: 0.57; 95% confidence interval: 0.37 to 0.87; p = 0.0079). The composite endpoint of all-cause death/MI was 10.0% in the complete revascularization group versus 18.5% in the infarct-related artery-only group (hazard ratio: 0.47; 95% confidence interval: 0.25 to 0.89; p = 0.0175).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds long-term data for the complete revascularisation recommendation in STEMI.

title: Percutaneous coronary angioplasty versus coronary artery bypass grafting in the treatment of unprotected left main stenosis: updated 5-year outcomes from the randomised, non-inferiority NOBLE trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label randomised noninferiority trial at 36 hospitals; 1201 patients (592 per group analysed).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label with a first-generation stent in part of the cohort and manufacturer funding.
appraisal.one_line: NOBLE 5-year results found PCI inferior to CABG for MACCE in left main disease, with similar mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Kaplan-Meier 5-year estimates of MACCE were 28% (165 events) for PCI and 19% (110 events) for CABG (HR 1·58 [95% CI 1·24-2·01]); the HR exceeded the limit for non-inferiority of PCI compared to CABG. All-cause mortality was estimated in 9% after PCI versus 9% after CABG (HR 1·08 [95% CI 0·74-1·59]; p=0·68).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Together with EXCEL, the main randomised basis for the discordant left main recommendations.

title: Complete revascularization reduces cardiovascular death in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of 6 RCTs, 6528 patients (3139 complete, 3389 culprit-only), random-effects.
