appraisal.main_limitation: Follow-up of 1 to 3 years and a borderline cardiovascular death estimate across heterogeneous trial designs.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of six RCTs found complete revascularisation reduced cardiovascular death in STEMI with multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Cardiovascular death was significantly reduced in the group receiving complete revascularization (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.39-0.97, I2 = 29%). All-cause death (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.56-1.16, I2 = 27%) was not affected by the revascularization strategy.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports the guideline upgrade for complete revascularisation in STEMI with multivessel disease.

title: Association of Use of an Intravascular Microaxial Left Ventricular Assist Device vs Intra-aortic Balloon Pump With In-Hospital Mortality and Major Bleeding Among Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction Complicated by Cardiogenic Shock.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective NCDR CathPCI and Chest Pain-MI registry cohort, 28 304 patients; 1680 propensity-matched pairs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational design with confounding by indication and in-hospital outcomes only.
appraisal.one_line: Propensity-matched US registry comparison of microaxial LVAD and IABP in AMI complicated by cardiogenic shock undergoing PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Among 1680 propensity-matched pairs, there was a significantly higher risk of in-hospital death associated with use of an intravascular microaxial LVAD (45.0%) vs with an IABP (34.1% [absolute risk difference, 10.9 percentage points {95% CI, 7.6-14.2}; P < .001) and also higher risk of in-hospital major bleeding (intravascular microaxial LVAD [31.3%] vs IABP [16.0%]; absolute risk difference, 15.4 percentage points [95% CI, 12.5-18.2]; P < .001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds real-world safety signal on microaxial pump use where randomised evidence is limited.

title: Polymer-based or Polymer-free Stents in Patients at High Bleeding Risk.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised noninferiority trial; 1996 patients at high bleeding risk.
appraisal.main_limitation: Noninferiority design with 1-year follow-up only.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised noninferiority comparison of two stent types in patients at high bleeding risk given one month of DAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, the primary outcome was observed in 169 of 988 patients (17.1%) in the zotarolimus-eluting stent group and in 164 of 969 (16.9%) in the polymer-free drug-coated stent group (risk difference, 0.2 percentage points; upper boundary of the one-sided 97.5% confidence interval [CI], 3.5; noninferiority margin, 4.1; P = 0.01 for noninferiority)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs stent choice and short DAPT in a growing high-bleeding-risk population.

title: Stent-Related Adverse Events >1 Year After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data pooled study; 25,032 patients, plus 19,578 patients from 12 trials for target lesion failure.
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooled trial populations may not reflect unselected practice; comparisons across stent generations are not randomised.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled individual patient data analysis of very late stent-related events after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Between years 1 and 5, very-late MACE occurred in 9.4% of patients (including 2.9% cardiac death, 3.1% MI, and 5.1% ID-TLR)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows a continuing event rate of about 2% a year beyond one year with no plateau, framing the case for long-term outcome research.

title: Mortality after drug-eluting stents vs. coronary artery bypass grafting for left main coronary artery disease: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis; five trials, 4612 patients, weighted mean follow-up 67.1 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooled trials are not powered for mortality individually; follow-up differs across trials.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of randomised trials of PCI with drug-eluting stents versus CABG for left main disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There were no significant differences between PCI and CABG for the risk of all-cause mortality [relative risk (RR) 1.03, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.81-1.32; P = 0.779] or cardiac death (RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.79-1.34; P = 0.817)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Left main revascularisation strategy is a contested decision with guideline discordance.

title: Survival After Coronary Revascularization With Paclitaxel-Coated Balloons.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of 26 randomised trials; 4,590 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few patients and events at longer follow-up; trial heterogeneity in lesion types.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of survival after coronary revascularisation with paclitaxel-coated balloons.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At follow-up of 6 to 12 months, no significant difference in all-cause mortality was found, however, with numerically lower rates after DCB treatment (RR: 0.74; 95% CI: 0.51 to 1.08; p = 0.116)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a safety signal raised for peripheral paclitaxel devices in the coronary setting.

title: Rivaroxaban Plus Aspirin Versus Aspirin Alone in Patients With Prior Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (COMPASS-PCI).

appraisal.design_and_n: Subgroup analysis of a randomised trial; 9862 of 16 560 patients with chronic coronary syndrome had previous PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc subgroup of a trial; follow-up of 1.98 years on average.
appraisal.one_line: COMPASS substudy of dual pathway inhibition by prior PCI status in chronic coronary syndrome.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Regardless of previous PCI, DPI versus aspirin produced consistent reductions in MACE (PCI: 4.0% versus 5.5%; hazard ratio [HR], 0.74 [95% CI, 0.61-0.88]; no PCI: 4.4% versus 5.7%; HR, 0.76 [95% CI, 0.61-0.94], P-interaction=0.85)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports low-dose rivaroxaban plus aspirin in patients with prior PCI, relevant to long-term antithrombotic strategy.

title: Ten-Year Outcomes After Drug-Eluting Stents Versus Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting for Left Main Coronary Disease: Extended Follow-Up of the PRECOMBAT Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 300 patients assigned to PCI and 300 to CABG, median follow-up 11.3 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Authors state the study was underpowered and the results hypothesis-generating.
appraisal.one_line: Ten-year follow-up of a randomised trial of PCI versus CABG for unprotected left main disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 10 years, a primary outcome event occurred in 29.8% of the PCI group and in 24.7% of the CABG group (hazard ratio [HR] with PCI vs CABG, 1.25 [95% CI, 0.93-1.69])
appraisal.why_it_matters: Long-term data for left main revascularisation choice, though underpowered.

title: Initial Invasive or Conservative Strategy for Stable Coronary Disease.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 5179 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Primary outcome sensitive to the myocardial infarction definition; patients with left main disease and reduced ejection fraction were excluded.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of an initial invasive versus conservative strategy in stable coronary disease with moderate or severe ischaemia.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 6 months, the cumulative event rate was 5.3% in the invasive-strategy group and 3.4% in the conservative-strategy group (difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.8 to 3.0); at 5 years, the cumulative event rate was 16.4% and 18.2%, respectively (difference, -1.8 percentage points; 95% CI, -4.7 to 1.0). Results were similar with respect to the key secondary outcome. The incidence of the primary outcome was sensitive to the definition of myocardial infarction; a secondary analysis yielded more procedural myocardial infarctions of uncertain clinical importance. There were 145 deaths in the invasive-strategy group and 144 deaths in the conservative-strategy group (hazard ratio, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.83 to 1.32).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly informs the most common revascularisation decision in chronic coronary syndromes.

title: Management of Coronary Disease in Patients with Advanced Kidney Disease.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 777 patients with advanced chronic kidney disease and moderate or severe ischaemia.
appraisal.main_limitation: Shorter median follow-up of 2.2 years and a high-risk population with few events beyond death.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of invasive and conservative strategies in stable coronary disease with advanced kidney disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At a median follow-up of 2.2 years, a primary outcome event had occurred in 123 patients in the invasive-strategy group and in 129 patients in the conservative-strategy group (estimated 3-year event rate, 36.4% vs. 36.7%; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.01; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.79 to 1.29; P = 0.95)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Fills a population excluded from earlier revascularisation trials and shows higher stroke with the invasive strategy.

title: Ticagrelor With or Without Aspirin in High-Risk Patients With Diabetes Mellitus Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified subgroup analysis of a randomised trial; 2,620 patients with diabetes.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis not powered for ischaemic endpoints; high-risk selected population after 3 months of DAPT.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified diabetes analysis of TWILIGHT: ticagrelor monotherapy reduced clinically relevant bleeding without more ischaemic events versus ticagrelor plus aspirin.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: BARC 2, 3 or 5 bleeding was 4.5% and 6.7% with ticagrelor plus placebo versus ticagrelor plus aspirin (hazard ratio: 0.65; 95% confidence interval: 0.47 to 0.91; p = 0.012); ischemic events were 4.6% vs. 5.9% (hazard ratio: 0.77; 95% confidence interval: 0.55 to 1.09; p = 0.14).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports P2Y12 monotherapy after short DAPT in patients with diabetes, a high-risk group for de-escalation strategies.

title: Ticagrelor With or Without Aspirin After Complex PCI.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified subgroup of a randomised trial; 2,342 of 7,119 patients had complex PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis; ischaemic events were few.
appraisal.one_line: TWILIGHT complex PCI subgroup of ticagrelor monotherapy versus ticagrelor plus aspirin.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared to ticagrelor plus aspirin, ticagrelor plus placebo resulted in significantly lower rates of Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) type 2, 3, or 5 bleeding (4.2% vs. 7.7%; hazard ratio [HR]: 0.54; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.38 to 0.76)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a group at higher ischaemic risk in which aspirin withdrawal was a concern.

title: Randomized Comparison of the Polymer-Free Biolimus-Coated BioFreedom Stent With the Ultrathin Strut Biodegradable Polymer Sirolimus-Eluting Orsiro Stent in an All-Comers Population Treated With Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: The SORT OUT IX Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised noninferiority trial; 3151 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Noninferiority not met; one-year follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: Noninferiority trial of a polymer-free biolimus-coated stent versus an ultrathin biodegradable polymer sirolimus-eluting stent.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, intention-to-treat analysis showed that 79 (5.0%) patients, who were assigned the BioFreedom stent, and 59 (3.7%), who were assigned the Orsiro stent, met the primary end point (absolute risk difference 1.29% [upper limit of one-sided 95% CI 2.50%]; Pnoninferiority=0.14)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows a polymer-free stent did not match a contemporary comparator, with more target lesion revascularisation.

title: Drug-Coated Balloon Angioplasty Versus Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation in Patients With Coronary Stent Restenosis.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled patient-level analysis of randomised trials; 710 patients with BMS-ISR and 1,248 with DES-ISR.
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooled analysis of a limited number of trials; subgroup by restenosis type.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled analysis of drug-coated balloon versus drug-eluting stent for in-stent restenosis by type of restenotic stent.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In patients with BMS-ISR, no significant difference between treatments was observed in terms of primary efficacy (9.2% vs. 10.2%; hazard ratio [HR]: 0.83; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.51 to 1.37) and safety endpoints (8.7% vs. 7.5%; HR: 1.13; 95% CI: 0.65 to 1.96); results of secondary analyses were consistent. In patients with DES-ISR, the risk of the primary efficacy endpoint was higher with DCB angioplasty than with repeat DES implantation (20.3% vs. 13.4%; HR: 1.58; 95% CI: 1.16 to 2.13)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Suggests treatment choice for in-stent restenosis should depend on the type of restenotic stent.

title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Oral P2Y12 Inhibitors in Acute Coronary Syndrome: Network Meta-Analysis of 52 816 Patients From 12 Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis of randomised trials comparing prasugrel, ticagrelor and clopidogrel.
appraisal.main_limitation: Indirect comparisons across trials of differing populations and designs.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis of oral P2Y12 inhibitors in acute coronary syndrome.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In comparison with clopidogrel, ticagrelor significantly reduced cardiovascular mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.82 [95% CI, 0.72-0.92]) and all-cause mortality (HR, 0.83 [95% CI, 0.75-0.92])
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on the discordant choice between prasugrel and ticagrelor.

title: Effect of Ticagrelor Monotherapy vs Ticagrelor With Aspirin on Major Bleeding and Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome: The TICO Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised multicentre trial; 3056 patients with ACS treated with drug-eluting stents.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design in one country; limited power for ischaemic endpoints.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of ticagrelor monotherapy after 3-month DAPT versus 12-month ticagrelor-based DAPT in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 59 patients (3.9%) receiving ticagrelor monotherapy after 3-month DAPT and in 89 patients (5.9%) receiving ticagrelor-based 12-month DAPT (absolute difference, -1.98% [95% CI, -3.50% to -0.45%]; hazard ratio [HR], 0.66 [95% CI, 0.48 to 0.92]; P = .01)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds to evidence for short DAPT followed by P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy in ACS.

title: The Safety and Efficacy of Aspirin Discontinuation on a Background of a P2Y12 Inhibitor in Patients After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis; 32 145 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Aggregate trial-level data with differing P2Y12 inhibitors and populations.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of aspirin discontinuation on a P2Y12 inhibitor background after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Discontinuation of aspirin therapy 1 to 3 months after PCI significantly reduced the risk of major bleeding by 40% compared with dual antiplatelet therapy (1.97% versus 3.13%; hazard ratio [HR], 0.60 [95% CI, 0.45-0.79])
appraisal.why_it_matters: Consolidates the case for aspirin-free strategies after PCI.

title: Multicentre, randomized comparison of two-stent and provisional stenting techniques in patients with complex coronary bifurcation lesions: the DEFINITION II trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 653 patients at 49 international centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: One-year follow-up; operator-selected two-stent technique was mostly double-kissing crush.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of two-stent and provisional stenting for complex coronary bifurcation lesions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At the 1-year follow-up, TLF occurred in 37 (11.4%) and 20 (6.1%) patients in the provisional and two-stent groups, respectively [77.8%: double-kissing crush; hazard ratio (HR) 0.52, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.30-0.90; P = 0.019]
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges provisional stenting as default in complex bifurcations.

title: Randomized trials of invasive cardiovascular interventions that include a placebo control: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review; 30 trials, 4102 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Heterogeneous interventions and outcomes; mixed risk of bias.
appraisal.one_line: Systematic review of placebo-controlled randomised trials of invasive cardiovascular interventions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Ten trials (33%) demonstrated statistically significant superiority of invasive interventions over placebo controls for the respective predefined primary outcomes.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the interpretation of unblinded trials of invasive procedures.

title: Routine Revascularization Versus Initial Medical Therapy for Stable Ischemic Heart Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of 14 randomised trials; 14 877 patients, weighted mean follow-up 4.5 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Most trials enrolled patients with preserved ventricular function and excluded left main disease.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of routine revascularisation versus initial medical therapy in stable ischaemic heart disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Revascularization compared with medical therapy alone was not associated with a reduced risk of death (relative risk [RR], 0.99 [95% CI, 0.90-1.09])
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives a pooled estimate on mortality for a very common revascularisation decision.

title: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention and Drug-Eluting Stents: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis; 79 073 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Network of heterogeneous trials with indirect comparisons.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis of DAPT duration and composition after PCI with drug-eluting stents.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: extended-term DAPT was associated with a reduced risk of myocardial infarction in comparison with 12-month DAPT (absolute risk difference, -3.8 incident cases per 1000 person-years; relative risk, 0.68 [95% CI, 0.54-0.87])
appraisal.why_it_matters: Compares the full range of DAPT strategies in one framework.

title: Effect of Genotype-Guided Oral P2Y12 Inhibitor Selection vs Conventional Clopidogrel Therapy on Ischemic Outcomes After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: The TAILOR-PCI Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label randomised trial; 5302 patients undergoing PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label; primary result did not reach significance.
appraisal.one_line: Genotype-guided oral P2Y12 inhibitor selection versus clopidogrel after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 35 of 903 CYP2C19 LOF carriers (4.0%) in the genotype-guided therapy group and 54 of 946 (5.9%) in the conventional therapy group at 12 months (hazard ratio [HR], 0.66 [95% CI, 0.43-1.02]; P = .06)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests guided selection of P2Y12 inhibitor, a de-escalation and personalisation question.

title: Colchicine in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome: The Australian COPS Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 795 patients, 396 to colchicine and 399 to placebo.
appraisal.main_limitation: Underpowered for cardiovascular outcomes; mortality imbalance based on few events.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of colchicine added to standard therapy in acute coronary syndrome.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Over the 12-month follow-up, there were 24 events in the colchicine group compared with 38 events in the placebo group (P=0.09, log-rank)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Conflicts with COLCOT on early colchicine and raises a mortality signal.

title: Efficacy and safety of trimetazidine after percutaneous coronary intervention (ATPCI): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, double-blind trial; 6007 patients, 2998 to trimetazidine and 3009 to placebo.
appraisal.main_limitation: Neutral result; ongoing prescribing may continue regardless.
appraisal.one_line: Placebo-controlled trial of trimetazidine after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: incidence of primary endpoint events was not significantly different between the trimetazidine group (700 [23·3%] patients) and the placebo group (714 [23·7%]; hazard ratio 0·98 [95% CI 0·88-1·09], p=0·73)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large neutral trial on a widely used antianginal after PCI.

title: Prasugrel-based de-escalation of dual antiplatelet therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with acute coronary syndrome (HOST-REDUCE-POLYTECH-ACS): an open-label, multicentre, non-inferiority randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 2338 patients, 1170 to de-escalation and 1168 to conventional therapy.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trial in east Asian patients; many screened patients did not meet the core indication.
appraisal.one_line: Prasugrel-based de-escalation of DAPT versus conventional DAPT after PCI in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 82 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate 7·2%) in the de-escalation group and 116 patients (10·1%) in the conventional group (absolute risk difference -2·9%, pnon-inferiority<0·0001; hazard ratio 0·70 [95% CI 0·52-0·92], pequivalence=0·012)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports dose de-escalation of potent P2Y12 inhibitor in the post-ACS maintenance phase.

title: Timing of Oral P2Y12 Inhibitor Administration in Patients With Non-ST-Segment Elevation Acute Coronary Syndrome.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 1,449 patients, stopped early for futility.
appraisal.main_limitation: Stopped early; wide intervals.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison of downstream and upstream oral P2Y12 inhibitor in NSTE-ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The rate of the primary endpoint, a composite of death due to vascular causes; nonfatal myocardial infarction or nonfatal stroke; and Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 3, 4, and 5 bleeding through day 30, did not differ significantly between the downstream and upstream groups (percent absolute risk reduction: -0.46; 95% repeated confidence interval: -2.90 to 1.90)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on the timing of P2Y12 inhibitor loading in NSTE-ACS.

title: Long-Term Survival After Surgical or Percutaneous Revascularization in Patients With Diabetes and Multivessel Coronary Disease.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Linked administrative databases in Ontario, 4,519 PCI and 9,716 CABG patients; 4,301 matched pairs, median follow-up 5.5 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational with residual confounding despite matching on 23 baseline covariates.
appraisal.one_line: Large Ontario propensity-matched comparison of PCI and CABG in diabetes with multivessel coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.39; 95% CI: 1.28 to 1.51) and overall MACCEs (HR: 1.99; 95% CI: 1.86 to 2.12) were significantly higher with PCI compared with CABG.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds real-world long-term evidence to the PCI versus CABG decision in diabetes.

title: Nonculprit Lesion Severity and Outcome of Revascularization in Patients With STEMI and Multivessel Coronary Disease.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified analysis of a randomised trial; 2,479 patients with QCA stenosis >=60% and 1,372 with <60%.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis defined by quantitative angiography.
appraisal.one_line: COMPLETE trial analysis of complete revascularisation by nonculprit lesion severity in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The first coprimary outcome was reduced with complete revascularization in the 2,479 patients with QCA stenosis ≥60% (2.5%/year vs. 4.2%/year; hazard ratio [HR]: 0.61; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.47 to 0.79), but not in the 1,372 patients with QCA stenosis <60% (3.0%/year vs. 2.9%/year; HR: 1.04; 95% CI: 0.72 to 1.50; interaction p = 0.02)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs lesion selection for complete revascularisation in STEMI.

title: Revascularization in Patients With Left Main Coronary Artery Disease and Left Ventricular Dysfunction.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: IRIS-MAIN registry, 3,488 patients with LMCA disease who underwent CABG (n = 1,355) or PCI (n = 2,133).
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational with small numbers in the moderate and severe dysfunction groups.
appraisal.one_line: Registry analysis of PCI versus CABG for left main disease by severity of left ventricular dysfunction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with CABG, PCI was associated with a higher adjusted risk of primary outcomes in patients with moderate (hazard ratio [HR]: 2.23; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.17 to 4.28) or severe (HR: 2.45; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.27 to 4.73) dysfunction.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a high-risk subgroup in which randomised trials of left main revascularisation had few patients.

title: Randomized Pilot Clinical Trial of Early Coronary Angiography Versus No Early Coronary Angiography After Cardiac Arrest Without ST-Segment Elevation: The PEARL Study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised pilot trial; 99 patients, terminated prematurely.
appraisal.main_limitation: Underpowered and stopped early.
appraisal.one_line: Pilot randomised trial of early coronary angiography after cardiac arrest without ST elevation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point of efficacy and safety was not different between the 2 groups (55.1% versus 46.0%; P=0.64)
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds to equipoise on early angiography after resuscitation.

title: Implications of Alternative Definitions of Peri-Procedural Myocardial Infarction After Coronary Revascularization.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of the randomised EXCEL trial (NCT01205776); PCI n=935, CABG n=923.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc analysis with biomarker availability differing by definition (troponin in 49.5%); associations are observational within a trial.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified and Universal Definition peri-procedural MI differ in rates and prognostic weight after left main PCI versus CABG in EXCEL.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: PMIProt occurred in 34 of 935 (3.6%) patients after PCI and 56 of 923 (6.1%) after CABG (difference -2.4%; 95% CI -4.4% to -0.5%). PMIUD occurred in 37 (4.0%) and 20 (2.2%) (difference 1.8%; 95% CI 0.2% to 3.4%). PMIUD was associated with cardiovascular mortality after CABG (adjusted HR 11.94; 95% CI 4.84 to 29.47) but not after PCI (adjusted HR 1.14; 95% CI 0.35 to 3.67).
appraisal.why_it_matters: The definition of procedural MI changes which revascularisation strategy appears safer in left main disease.

title: Impact of Peri-Procedural Myocardial Infarction on Outcomes After Revascularization.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of the randomised SYNTAXES trial; 1,652 of 1,800 patients with post-procedural enzymes included.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc, observational association within a trial; 148 patients without enzyme data excluded.
appraisal.one_line: Rates and prognostic weight of peri-procedural MI depend on the definition used in the SYNTAXES trial.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: PMI rates by SYNTAX and Fourth Universal Definition were 2.7% and 3.0% in the PCI arm versus 2.4% and 2.1% in the CABG arm; SCAI or EXCEL definition rates were 5.7% (PCI) and 16.5% (CABG). The abstract does not report an effect estimate for the mortality association.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports use of stricter, ECG-supported definitions when comparing PCI and CABG outcomes.

title: Validation of high bleeding risk criteria and definition as proposed by the academic research consortium for high bleeding risk.

appraisal.design_and_n: Bern PCI Registry, 16 580 participants with complete ARC-HBR criteria.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-centre registry with most criteria adjudicated retrospectively.
appraisal.one_line: External validation of the ARC high bleeding risk criteria in a large single-centre PCI registry.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: For every 0.5 score increase a step-wise augmentation of BARC 3 or 5 bleeding rates at 1 year ranging from 1.90% among patients fulfilling no criterion, through 4.01%, 5.98%, 7.42%, 8.60%, 12.21%, 12.29%, and 17.64%.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports the ARC-HBR definition that underpins antithrombotic de-escalation trials and guideline wording.

title: Redevelopment and validation of the SYNTAX score II to individualise decision making between percutaneous and surgical revascularisation in patients with complex coronary artery disease: secondary analysis of the multicentre randomised controlled SYNTAXES trial with external cohort validation.

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of the randomised SYNTAXES trial (3-vessel or left main disease) with external cohort validation; sample size not stated in the extracted abstract.
appraisal.main_limitation: Modest discrimination on external validation, and no test of whether use of the score improves outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Re-developed SYNTAX score II 2020 predicts 10-year death and 5-year MACE and estimates individual benefit of CABG versus PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At cross-validation the C-index for 10-year all-cause death was 0.73 (95% CI 0.69-0.76) for PCI and 0.73 (0.69-0.76) for CABG; for 5-year MACE 0.65 (0.61-0.69) for PCI and 0.71 (0.67-0.75) for CABG. At external validation C-index for 5-year MACE was 0.67 (0.63-0.70) for PCI and 0.62 (0.58-0.66) for CABG.
appraisal.why_it_matters: An individualised tool for heart-team choice between PCI and CABG, derived from the longest randomised follow-up.

title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Vulnerable Coronary Atherosclerotic Plaque.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 182 patients (93 BVS, 89 GDMT alone) at 15 centres after MI; NCT02171065.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small, clinical endpoints not powered, and the bioresorbable scaffold has been withdrawn.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised PROSPECT ABSORB trial: scaffold PCI of non-flow-limiting high-burden plaques enlarged lumen and was safe, with a signal for fewer lesion-related events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Follow-up MLA was 6.9 ± 2.6 mm2 with BVS versus 3.0 ± 1.0 mm2 with GDMT alone (difference: 3.9 mm2; 95% CI 3.3 to 4.5). Target lesion failure at 24 months was 4.3% versus 4.5% (p = 0.96). Lesion-related MACE was 4.3% versus 10.7% (odds ratio 0.38; 95% CI 0.11 to 1.28).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests pre-emptive treatment of vulnerable plaque, a hypothesis-generating basis for a powered trial.

title: Intravascular Lithotripsy for Treatment of Severely Calcified Coronary Artery Disease.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Disrupt CAD III (NCT03595176), prospective single-arm multicentre study, n = 431 at 47 sites.
appraisal.main_limitation: No randomised comparator and performance goals rather than head-to-head comparison.
appraisal.one_line: Single-arm regulatory study of coronary intravascular lithotripsy in severely calcified lesions met both prespecified performance goals.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary safety endpoint of the 30-day freedom from major adverse cardiovascular events was 92.2%; the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval was 89.9%, which exceeded the PG of 84.4% (p < 0.0001). Procedural success was 92.4%; the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval was 90.2%, which exceeded the PG of 83.4% (p < 0.0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Underpins regulatory approval of coronary IVL, a main calcium modification option in complex PCI.

title: Ticagrelor alone vs. ticagrelor plus aspirin following percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with non-ST-segment elevation acute coronary syndromes: TWILIGHT-ACS.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified subgroup of the randomised TWILIGHT trial (NCT02270242); NSTE-ACS n=4614, stable n=2503, of 7119 randomised.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis, not powered for ischaemic outcomes; high-risk, adherent, event-free patients only.
appraisal.one_line: TWILIGHT-ACS: ticagrelor monotherapy after 3 months of DAPT reduced bleeding in NSTE-ACS without more ischaemic events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In NSTE-ACS, BARC 2, 3 or 5 bleeding was 3.6% vs 7.6% (HR 0.47; 95% CI 0.36-0.61; P < 0.001); in stable patients 4.8% vs 6.2% (HR 0.76; 95% CI 0.54-1.06; P = 0.11). Death, MI or stroke was 4.3% vs 4.4% (HR 0.97; 95% CI 0.74-1.28) with NSTE-ACS.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports P2Y12 monotherapy after short DAPT as a de-escalation option in NSTE-ACS.

title: Long-term efficacy and safety of drug-coated balloons versus drug-eluting stents for small coronary artery disease (BASKET-SMALL 2): 3-year follow-up of a randomised, non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, open-label, non-inferiority trial; 758 patients (DCB n=382, DES n=376); NCT01574534.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, not powered for individual components and mostly stable disease.
appraisal.one_line: BASKET-SMALL 2 at 3 years: drug-coated balloons remained comparable to drug-eluting stents in small coronary vessels.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Kaplan-Meier MACE was 15% in both groups (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.68-1.45; p=0.95). Cardiac death HR 1.29 (0.63-2.66); all-cause death HR 1.05 (0.62-1.77); major bleeding HR 0.43 (0.17-1.13).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Longer-term evidence for DCB-only strategies in small vessels.

title: Association of Ticagrelor vs Clopidogrel With Net Adverse Clinical Events in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective cohort in two US EHR databases and one South Korean database; 31 290 propensity-matched pairs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational with possible unmeasured confounding; the authors state this.
appraisal.one_line: Multi-database observational comparison found no significant NACE difference between ticagrelor and clopidogrel after PCI for ACS but more bleeding and dyspnoea with ticagrelor.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 1-year risk of NACE was 15.1% vs 14.6% (summary HR, 1.05 [95% CI, 1.00-1.10]; P = .06). Hemorrhagic events were 2.1% vs 1.6% (summary HR, 1.35 [95% CI, 1.13-1.61]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Real-world check on the guideline preference for ticagrelor over clopidogrel.

title: Ticagrelor or Prasugrel in Patients With ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Undergoing Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified subgroup of the randomised ISAR-REACT 5 trial (NCT01944800); 1653 patients with STEMI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis in an open-label trial; MI finding not adjusted for multiplicity.
appraisal.one_line: ISAR-REACT 5 STEMI subgroup: no significant difference in death, MI or stroke between ticagrelor and prasugrel, with more MI on ticagrelor.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary end point occurred in 83 patients (10.1%) with ticagrelor and 64 (7.9%) with prasugrel (hazard ratio, 1.31 [95% CI, 0.95-1.82]; P=0.10). Myocardial infarction was 5.3% vs 2.8% (hazard ratio, 1.95 [95% CI, 1.18-3.23]; P=0.010).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs choice of potent P2Y12 inhibitor in primary PCI.

title: Reduction in Revascularization With Icosapent Ethyl: Insights From REDUCE-IT Revascularization Analyses.

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc analysis of the randomised REDUCE-IT trial (NCT01492361); 8179 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Exploratory analysis of a trial whose mineral-oil comparator is debated; population is not an interventional cohort.
appraisal.one_line: REDUCE-IT revascularisation analysis: icosapent ethyl reduced first and total coronary revascularisations.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: First revascularizations were 9.2% with icosapent ethyl vs 13.3% with placebo (hazard ratio, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.58-0.76]; P<0.0001); PCI hazard ratio 0.68 [95% CI, 0.59-0.79]; CABG hazard ratio 0.61 [95% CI, 0.45-0.81].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Describes a lipid-lowering effect on revascularisation burden.

title: Influence of LDL-Cholesterol Lowering on Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients With Diabetes Mellitus Undergoing Coronary Revascularization.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled patient-level analysis of 3 randomised trials; 4,050 patients with type 2 diabetes.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post-randomisation LDL-C stratification is subject to confounding and immortal time.
appraisal.one_line: Patient-level pooled analysis suggests 1-year LDL-C level modifies the benefit of PCI versus medical therapy in diabetes, with CABG benefit across strata.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 4-year MACCE was 17.2% vs 13.3% vs 13.1% for LDL-C of at least 100, 70 to <100 and <70 mg/dl (p = 0.016). PCI versus medical therapy: MACCE hazard ratio 0.61; 95% CI 0.40 to 0.91 when 1-year LDL-C <70 mg/dl.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Links lipid control to revascularisation benefit in diabetes.

title: Association Between Adherence to Fractional Flow Reserve Treatment Thresholds and Major Adverse Cardiac Events in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective multicentre cohort in Ontario, 9106 patients with single-vessel FFR; 2693 ischaemic and 6413 nonischaemic.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational design with treatment selection bias despite inverse probability weighting.
appraisal.one_line: Population-based cohort of FFR-guided decisions found PCI was associated with lower MACE for ischaemic FFR and higher MACE for non-ischaemic FFR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In the ischemic FFR cohort, PCI was associated with a significantly lower rate and hazard of MACE at 5 years compared with no PCI (31.5% vs 39.1%; hazard ratio, 0.77 [95% CI, 0.63-0.94]). In the nonischemic cohort, 33.3% vs 24.4%; HR, 1.37 [95% CI, 1.14-1.65].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Real-world evidence on the consequence of deviating from FFR thresholds in a general-tier journal.

title: Coronary Optical Coherence Tomography and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging to Determine Underlying Causes of Myocardial Infarction With Nonobstructive Coronary Arteries in Women.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicentre observational study, 301 women enrolled at 16 sites; 170 with MINOCA, 145 with adequate OCT, 116 with CMR.
appraisal.main_limitation: Women only, no outcome follow-up reported in the abstract and no randomised treatment comparison.
appraisal.one_line: Multimodality OCT and CMR identified a probable cause in most women with MINOCA in a prospective core-laboratory study.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A cause of MINOCA was identified in 84.5% (98/116) of the women with multimodality imaging, higher than with OCT alone (P<0.001) or CMR alone (P=0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports a work-up pathway for MINOCA that could direct secondary prevention.

title: Effect of Evolocumab on Complex Coronary Disease Requiring Revascularization.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc analysis of the randomised FOURIER trial (NCT01764633); 27,564 patients, 1,724 underwent revascularisation.
appraisal.main_limitation: Exploratory, post hoc, revascularisation is a soft, investigator-driven endpoint.
appraisal.one_line: FOURIER analysis: evolocumab reduced complex coronary revascularisation, including complex PCI and CABG.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Evolocumab reduced any coronary revascularization (HR 0.78; 95% CI 0.71 to 0.86), complex PCI (HR 0.67; 95% CI 0.54 to 0.84), CABG (HR 0.76; 95% CI 0.60 to 0.96) and complex revascularization (HR 0.71; 95% CI 0.61 to 0.84).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Links LDL-C lowering to the burden of complex coronary disease treated by PCI and CABG.

title: Ticagrelor versus clopidogrel in elective percutaneous coronary intervention (ALPHEUS): a randomised, open-label, phase 3b trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, open-label, phase 3b trial; 1910 randomised (ticagrelor 956, clopidogrel 954) at 49 sites.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, biomarker-defined primary outcome rather than clinical events.
appraisal.one_line: ALPHEUS: ticagrelor was not superior to clopidogrel for periprocedural myonecrosis after high-risk elective PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 48 h, the primary outcome occurred in 334 (35%) of 941 patients on ticagrelor and 341 (36%) of 942 on clopidogrel (odds ratio 0.97, 95% CI 0.80-1.17; p=0.75). Minor bleeding at 30 days was 105 (11%) vs 71 (8%) (OR 1.54, 95% CI 1.12-2.11).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports clopidogrel as standard in elective PCI and informs the periprocedural MI debate.

title: Durable Polymer Versus Biodegradable Polymer Drug-Eluting Stents After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome: The HOST-REDUCE-POLYTECH-ACS Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, open-label, adjudicator-blinded, non-inferiority trial; 3413 patients (DP-DES 1713, BP-DES 1700); NCT02193971.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label; 12-month follow-up and driven by target lesion revascularisation.
appraisal.one_line: HOST-REDUCE-POLYTECH-ACS: durable-polymer DES was non-inferior to biodegradable-polymer DES for patient-oriented outcomes in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patient-oriented composite at 12 months was 5.2% with DP-DES and 6.4% with BP-DES (absolute risk difference, -1.2%; Pnoninferiority<0.001). Device-oriented composite was 2.6% vs 3.9% (hazard ratio, 0.67 [95% CI, 0.46-0.98]; P=0.038).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large randomised comparison of stent polymer technology in ACS.

title: Ticagrelor or Prasugrel in Patients With Non-ST-Segment Elevation Acute Coronary Syndromes.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc pooled analysis of the unstable angina and NSTEMI subgroups of the randomised ISAR-REACT 5 trial (NCT01944800); ticagrelor 1,179, prasugrel 1,186.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc nature; open-label design; authors state confirmation is needed.
appraisal.one_line: Post hoc ISAR-REACT 5 analysis in NSTE-ACS: prasugrel was associated with fewer death, MI or stroke events than ticagrelor.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 101 (8.7%) with ticagrelor and 73 (6.3%) with prasugrel (hazard ratio 1.41; 95% CI 1.04 to 1.90). Safety endpoint HR 1.09; 95% CI 0.72 to 1.65.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on the choice of potent P2Y12 inhibitor in NSTE-ACS where guidelines diverge.

title: Myocardial Infarction in the ISCHEMIA Trial: Impact of Different Definitions on Incidence, Prognosis, and Treatment Comparisons.

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of the randomised ISCHEMIA trial (NCT01471522); sample size not stated in the extracted abstract.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc analysis; prognostic associations are observational.
appraisal.one_line: ISCHEMIA: choice of MI definition changes the apparent balance of invasive versus conservative strategies.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Four-year MI rates after revascularization were 2.7% vs 1.1% (adjusted HR 2.98; 95% CI 1.87-4.73) and 8.2% vs 2.0% (adjusted HR 5.04; 95% CI 3.64-6.97) for primary and secondary definitions. Type 1 MI was 3.40% vs 6.89% (adjusted HR 0.53; 95% CI 0.41-0.69).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows that procedural MI definitions drive trial conclusions on invasive management in chronic coronary disease.

title: Short dual antiplatelet therapy followed by P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy vs. prolonged dual antiplatelet therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention with second-generation drug-eluting stents: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 5 randomised trials, 32 145 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few trials, heterogeneous populations and SAPT strategies; stent thrombosis imprecisely estimated.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of five trials: 1 to 3 months of DAPT then P2Y12 inhibitor SAPT lowered major bleeding versus 12 months of DAPT after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Major bleeding was lower with short DAPT followed by P2Y12 inhibitor SAPT (random-effects model: HR 0.63, 95% 0.45-0.86); stent thrombosis HR 1.19 (95% CI 0.86-1.65); all-cause death HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.70-1.03).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Pools trials behind guideline de-escalation recommendations.

title: Effect of Prehospital Crushed Prasugrel Tablets in Patients With ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Planned for Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: The Randomized COMPARE CRUSH Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised multicentre trial, 727 patients; NCT03296540.
appraisal.main_limitation: Surrogate primary outcome; short time to PCI.
appraisal.one_line: Prehospital crushed prasugrel did not improve TIMI 3 flow or ST resolution in STEMI despite lower platelet reactivity.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: TIMI 3 flow before pPCI occurred in 31.0% crushed vs 32.7% integral (odds ratio, 0.92 [95% CI, 0.65-1.30], P=0.64); complete ST resolution 59.9% vs 57.3% (odds ratio, 1.11 [95% CI, 0.78-1.58]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Negative trial on a common prehospital practice in STEMI.

title: Effect of long-term beta-blocker treatment following myocardial infarction among stable, optimally treated patients without heart failure in the reperfusion era: a Danish, nationwide cohort study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Nationwide registry cohort, 30 177 stable, optimally treated MI patients without heart failure, followed from 3 months to 3 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational design with confounding by indication and an excluded early period.
appraisal.one_line: Danish nationwide cohort found no difference in cardiovascular outcomes with long-term beta-blocker use after MI in stable patients without heart failure.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: BB treatment was associated with a similar risk of CV death, recurrent MI, and the composite outcome of CV events compared with no BB treatment [ARD (95% confidence intervals)] correspondingly; 0.1% (-0.3% to 0.5%), 0.2% (-0.7% to 1.2%), and 1.2% (-0.2% to 2.7%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Beta-blocker duration after MI is an open strategy question in the reperfusion era.

title: Predictive Value of the Residual SYNTAX Score in Patients With Cardiogenic Shock.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of the randomised CULPRIT-SHOCK trial; 587 patients with residual SYNTAX score available.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc and observational association; residual score is post-treatment and confounded by anatomy and haemodynamic state.
appraisal.one_line: In CULPRIT-SHOCK, residual SYNTAX score was independently associated with 30-day and 1-year mortality, and complete revascularisation was achieved in a minority.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Complete revascularisation was achieved in 75 (25.2%; 95% CI: 20.3% to 30.5%) with multivessel PCI and 27 (9.3%; 95% CI: 6.2% to 13.3%) with culprit-only PCI. Residual SYNTAX score was associated with 30-day mortality (adjusted odds ratio per 10 units: 1.49; 95% CI: 1.11 to 2.01) and 1-year mortality (adjusted odds ratio per 10 units: 1.52; 95% CI: 1.11 to 2.07).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Quantifies the prognostic cost of incomplete revascularisation in infarct-related shock, relevant to the culprit-only strategy.

title: Definitions and Clinical Trial Design Principles for Coronary Artery Chronic Total Occlusion Therapies: CTO-ARC Consensus Recommendations.

appraisal.design_and_n: Academic Research Consortium consensus document; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus rather than trial evidence.
appraisal.one_line: CTO-ARC consensus defines terminology, end points and trial design principles for chronic total occlusion PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Standardised endpoints would allow pooling of CTO PCI trials.

title: Mortality 10 Years After Percutaneous or Surgical Revascularization in Patients With Total Coronary Artery Occlusions.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Subanalysis of the randomised SYNTAXES study (NCT03417050); 460 of 1,800 patients had at least one total occlusion.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc, non-randomised comparison within a subgroup, wide confidence intervals.
appraisal.one_line: SYNTAXES: recanalisation or revascularisation of total occlusions was not associated with 10-year mortality after PCI or CABG.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 10-year all-cause mortality in the PCI arm was 29.9% vs 29.4% (adjusted HR 0.992; 95% CI 0.474 to 2.075) and in the CABG arm 28.0% vs 21.4% (adjusted HR 0.656; 95% CI 0.281 to 1.533), for unrevascularised versus revascularised occlusion.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Long-term data on whether CTO revascularisation affects survival.

title: 10-Year Follow-Up of Patients With Everolimus-Eluting Versus Bare-Metal Stents After ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial follow-up; 1,498 patients (EES 751, BMS 747); NCT04462315.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label extension; composite driven mainly by target lesion revascularisation.
appraisal.one_line: EXAMINATION-EXTEND: at 10 years, everolimus-eluting stents had fewer patient- and device-oriented events than bare-metal stents after STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patient-oriented composite was 32.4% vs 38.0% (HR 0.81; 95% CI 0.68 to 0.96; p = 0.013) and device-oriented composite 13.6% vs 18.4% (HR 0.72; 95% CI 0.55 to 0.93; p = 0.012).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Longest follow-up of DES versus BMS in primary PCI.

title: Mortality in STEMI patients without standard modifiable risk factors: a sex-disaggregated analysis of SWEDEHEART registry data.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective SWEDEHEART analysis of 62 048 patients with STEMI, 9228 without SMuRFs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational, with attenuation after adjustment for discharge pharmacotherapy suggesting a treatment gap rather than biology.
appraisal.one_line: Patients with STEMI and no standard modifiable risk factors had higher 30-day mortality, especially women, in a national registry.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: By 30 days after presentation, all-cause mortality was significantly higher in SMuRF-less patients (hazard ratio 1·47 [95% CI 1·37-1·57], p<0·0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Highlights an undertreated STEMI group in whom secondary prevention is under-prescribed.

title: Identification of vulnerable plaques and patients by intracoronary near-infrared spectroscopy and ultrasound (PROSPECT II): a prospective natural history study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicentre natural history study, 898 patients and 3629 non-culprit lesions, median follow-up 3·7 (IQR 3·0-4·4) years (NCT02171065).
appraisal.main_limitation: Natural history design with modest event numbers; no intervention tested.
appraisal.one_line: PROSPECT II found that lipid-rich, large-burden non-culprit lesions on NIRS and IVUS predicted later non-culprit MACE after MI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Highly lipidic lesions were an independent predictor of patient-level non-culprit lesion-related MACEs (adjusted odds ratio 2·27, 95% CI 1·25-4·13) and non-culprit lesion-specific MACEs (7·83, 4·12-14·89).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides the lesion-level risk basis for trials of preventive treatment of non-flow-limiting plaque.

title: Novel Supreme Drug-Eluting Stents With Early Synchronized Antiproliferative Drug Delivery to Inhibit Smooth Muscle Cell Proliferation After Drug-Eluting Stents Implantation in Coronary Artery Disease: Results of the PIONEER III Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, single-blind, 2:1 non-inferiority trial; 1629 patients (Supreme 1086, DP-EES 543); NCT03168776.
appraisal.main_limitation: 12-month follow-up of a new device; incremental comparison against a standard stent.
appraisal.one_line: Supreme DES was non-inferior to durable-polymer everolimus-eluting stents for target lesion failure at 12 months.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Target lesion failure at 12 months occurred in 57 of 1057 (5.4%) vs 27 of 532 (5.1%) (absolute risk difference, 0.32% [95% CI, -1.87 to 2.5]; Pnoninferiority=0.002).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Device approval evidence, not practice-changing.

title: Randomized Clinical Comparison of the Dual-Therapy CD34 Antibody-Covered Sirolimus-Eluting Combo Stent With the Sirolimus-Eluting Orsiro Stent in Patients Treated With Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: The SORT OUT X Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, single-blind, non-inferiority trial with registry-based follow-up; 3146 patients (DTS 1578, SES 1568); NCT03216733.
appraisal.main_limitation: 12-month follow-up; single-blind; driven by target lesion revascularisation.
appraisal.one_line: SORT OUT X: the Combo dual-therapy stent did not show non-inferiority to the Orsiro sirolimus-eluting stent for target lesion failure.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Target lesion failure at 12 months occurred in 100 (6.3%) with DTS and 58 (3.7%) with SES (absolute risk difference, 2.6% [upper limit of 1-sided 95% CI, 4.1%]; P (noninferiority)=0.76). Incidence rate ratio 1.74 [95% CI, 1.26-2.41].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large registry-based randomised comparison with a negative result for a dual-therapy stent.

title: Randomized Trial of Interleukin-6 Receptor Inhibition in Patients With Acute ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial at 3 centres; 101 tocilizumab and 98 placebo; NCT03004703.
appraisal.main_limitation: Imaging surrogate primary endpoint in a small trial.
appraisal.one_line: ASSAIL-MI: tocilizumab increased myocardial salvage in acute STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The myocardial salvage index was larger with tocilizumab (adjusted between-group difference 5.6 [95% confidence interval: 0.2 to 11.3] percentage points, p = 0.04). Final infarct size was 7.2% vs 9.1% of myocardial volume (p = 0.08).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests an anti-inflammatory strategy to limit infarct size in primary PCI.

title: Guided versus standard antiplatelet therapy in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 randomised trials and 3 observational studies; 20 743 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Mixed randomised and observational data, heterogeneous guidance strategies and endpoint definitions.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis: guided antiplatelet therapy reduced MACE after PCI versus standard therapy, with escalation lowering ischaemic events and de-escalation lowering bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Guided selection reduced major adverse cardiovascular events (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.63-0.95, p=0.015) and bleeding, not significantly (RR 0.88, 0.77-1.01, p=0.069). All-cause death and major bleeding did not differ.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on guided de-escalation and escalation of P2Y12 therapy in PCI.

title: Diabetes-Related Factors and the Effects of Ticagrelor Plus Aspirin in the THEMIS and THEMIS-PCI Trials.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc analyses of the randomised THEMIS (n = 19,220) and THEMIS-PCI trials.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc subgroup analyses without multiplicity control.
appraisal.one_line: THEMIS and THEMIS-PCI: relative effects of ticagrelor plus aspirin were consistent across diabetes duration, HbA1c and antihyperglycaemic therapy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 3-point MACE reduction with ticagrelor plus aspirin (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.90; p = 0.04) was generally consistent across subgroups; major bleeding was increased (HR: 2.32; p < 0.001) similarly across subgroups.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs long-term ticagrelor plus aspirin in diabetes with coronary disease.

title: Kidney Transplant List Status and Outcomes in the ISCHEMIA-CKD Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc analysis of the randomised ISCHEMIA-CKD trial (n = 777); 194 patients (25%) listed for transplant; NCT01985360.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc subgroup; wide intervals.
appraisal.one_line: ISCHEMIA-CKD analysis: an invasive strategy did not improve outcomes in patients listed for kidney transplant.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Adjusted hazard ratios for the primary outcome with invasive versus conservative strategy were 0.91 (95% CI: 0.54-1.54) in listed and 1.03 (95% CI: 0.78-1.37) in not listed patients (pinteraction= 0.68).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses pre-transplant coronary evaluation in advanced CKD.

title: Multivessel PCI Guided by FFR or Angiography for Myocardial Infarction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised multicentre trial; 586 FFR-guided and 577 angiography-guided patients; NCT02943954.
appraisal.main_limitation: Wide confidence interval; the authors state the findings do not allow a conclusive interpretation.
appraisal.one_line: FLOWER-MI: FFR-guided complete revascularisation did not show benefit over angiography-guided in STEMI with multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary outcome event occurred in 32 of 586 patients (5.5%) vs 24 of 577 (4.2%) (hazard ratio, 1.32; 95% confidence interval, 0.78 to 2.23; P = 0.31).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly addresses physiology guidance for non-culprit lesions after STEMI.

title: Long-term follow-up after ultrathin vs. conventional 2nd-generation drug-eluting stents: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Random-effects meta-analysis of 16 randomised trials, 20 701 patients; mean follow-up 2.5 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Soft driver (revascularisation) and heterogeneous stent platforms.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of 16 trials: ultrathin-strut DES reduced target lesion failure versus conventional thin-strut DES.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Ultrathin-strut DES were associated with a reduction in long-term TLF (relative risk (RR) 0.85, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.76-0.96, P = 0.008) driven by CD-TLR (RR 0.75, 95% CI 0.62-0.92, P = 0.005).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Device-selection evidence for second-generation DES.

title: Cardiac mortality in patients randomised to elective coronary revascularisation plus medical therapy or medical therapy alone: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 25 randomised trials, 19 806 patients; PROSPERO CRD42021225598.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level meta-regression, heterogeneous eras and no all-cause mortality difference.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of 25 trials: elective revascularisation plus medical therapy lowered cardiac death and spontaneous MI versus medical therapy alone in stable CAD.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Revascularisation yielded a lower risk of cardiac death [RR 0.79 (0.67-0.93), P < 0.01] and spontaneous MI [RR 0.74 (0.64-0.86)]. All-cause mortality [0.94 (0.87-1.01), P = 0.11].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges the conclusion of ISCHEMIA for revascularisation in chronic coronary syndromes.

title: The European bifurcation club Left Main Coronary Stent study: a randomized comparison of stepwise provisional vs. systematic dual stenting strategies (EBC MAIN).

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial in 11 European countries; 230 patients stepwise provisional and 237 systematic dual stent.
appraisal.main_limitation: Sample size gives wide confidence intervals, so a clinically important difference cannot be excluded.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised comparison in true left main bifurcation lesions found no significant difference between stepwise provisional and systematic dual stenting, with provisional favoured as default.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 14.7% of the stepwise provisional group vs. 17.7% of the systematic dual stent group (hazard ratio 0.8, 95% confidence interval 0.5-1.3; P = 0.34).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Left main bifurcation technique is a common high-stakes decision, and this trial reaffirms provisional stenting as the default against an earlier trial favouring dual stenting.

title: Aspirin versus clopidogrel for chronic maintenance monotherapy after percutaneous coronary intervention (HOST-EXAM): an investigator-initiated, prospective, randomised, open-label, multicentre trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Investigator-initiated, open-label randomised trial in South Korea; 5438 randomised (clopidogrel 2710, aspirin 2728).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, single-country population, composite endpoint including readmission.
appraisal.one_line: HOST-EXAM: clopidogrel monotherapy reduced a composite of death, MI, stroke, ACS readmission and major bleeding versus aspirin monotherapy in chronic maintenance after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 152 (5.7%) patients in the clopidogrel group and 207 (7.7%) in the aspirin group (hazard ratio 0.73 [95% CI 0.59-0.90]; p=0.0035).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly addresses which single antiplatelet to use long term after PCI.

title: Ten-Year All-Cause Death According to Completeness of Revascularization in Patients With Three-Vessel Disease or Left Main Coronary Artery Disease: Insights From the SYNTAX Extended Survival Study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Substudy of the randomised SYNTAXES study (NCT00114972, NCT03417050); sample size not stated in the extracted abstract.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc, non-randomised comparison of completeness groups.
appraisal.one_line: SYNTAXES: 10-year mortality after PCI with incomplete revascularisation exceeded CABG with complete revascularisation, and rose with residual SYNTAX score.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Incomplete revascularisation after PCI versus complete CABG: 10-year all-cause death 33.5% versus 23.7% (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.48 [95% CI, 1.15-1.91]); residual SYNTAX score above 8 versus complete PCI: 50.1% versus 22.2% (adjusted hazard ratio, 3.40 [95% CI, 2.13-5.43]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports completeness of revascularisation as a driver in PCI versus CABG choice.

title: Long-term mortality in patients with ischaemic heart failure revascularized with coronary artery bypass grafting or percutaneous coronary intervention: insights from the Swedish Coronary Angiography and Angioplasty Registry (SCAAR).

appraisal.design_and_n: SCAAR registry cohort, 2509 patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and multivessel disease.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational, with selection of treatment by anatomy and frailty despite propensity and instrumental adjustment.
appraisal.one_line: Swedish registry analysis with instrumental variable adjustment associated CABG with lower long-term mortality than PCI in ischaemic heart failure.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Risk of death was lower after CABG than after PCI [odds ratio (OR) 0.62; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.41-0.96; P = 0.031].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Relevant to revascularisation choice in ischaemic cardiomyopathy alongside randomised evidence.

title: Prognostically relevant periprocedural myocardial injury and infarction associated with percutaneous coronary interventions: a Consensus Document of the ESC Working Group on Cellular Biology of the Heart and European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI).

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus document; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Thresholds rely on expert consensus and limited data, as the document states.
appraisal.one_line: ESC/EAPCI consensus document on prognostically relevant periprocedural myocardial injury and infarction after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Proposes a troponin threshold of more than 5 times the 99th percentile for major periprocedural injury.

title: 10-Year Follow-Up After Revascularization in Elderly Patients With Complex Coronary Artery Disease.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified age analysis of the randomised SYNTAXES study; 1,800 randomised, 575 elderly (31.9%); NCT03417050, NCT00114972.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis with small numbers in the elderly.
appraisal.one_line: SYNTAXES elderly analysis: 10-year mortality did not differ significantly between PCI and CABG in patients 75 years or older with complex disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Ten-year mortality was 44.1% vs 41.1% in elderly patients (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.08; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.84 to 1.40). Five-year MACCE was 39.4% vs 35.1% (HR: 1.18; 95% CI: 0.90 to 1.56).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs revascularisation mode in older patients.

title: Mechanical Complications of Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few high-quality studies guide practice, as the statement notes.
appraisal.one_line: AHA scientific statement on mechanical complications of acute MI, including papillary muscle rupture, ventricular septal defect and free wall rupture.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Reference position on a high-mortality complication group with considerable practice variation.

title: P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy or dual antiplatelet therapy after coronary revascularisation: individual patient level meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient level meta-analysis of 6 randomised trials, 24 096 patients; PROSPERO CRD42020176853.
appraisal.main_limitation: Sex interaction is exploratory; trial designs and loading strategies differed.
appraisal.one_line: IPD meta-analysis of six trials: P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy was non-inferior to DAPT for death, MI or stroke and lowered bleeding after revascularisation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 283 (2.95%) with monotherapy and 315 (3.27%) with DAPT in the per protocol population (hazard ratio 0.93, 95% confidence interval 0.79 to 1.09; P=0.005 for non-inferiority). BARC 3 or 5 bleeding: hazard ratio 0.49, 0.39 to 0.63; P<0.001.
appraisal.why_it_matters: IPD evidence on de-escalation of antiplatelet therapy, with a sex-specific signal.

title: Evidence-Based Practices in the Cardiac Catheterization Laboratory: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement (review); no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not describe the method of evidence selection.
appraisal.one_line: American Heart Association scientific statement reviewing which catheterisation laboratory practices are supported or discounted by evidence.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Consensus-style summary of evidence-based catheterisation laboratory practice that may inform guideline and quality-standard work.

title: Fractional flow reserve derived from computed tomography coronary angiography in the assessment and management of stable chest pain: the FORECAST randomized trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 1400 patients with stable chest pain at 11 centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: Only 38% of the experimental group underwent FFR-CT, and the primary endpoint was cost rather than clinical events.
appraisal.one_line: FORECAST randomised a CT coronary angiography strategy with selective FFR-CT against standard care pathways in stable chest pain and found no significant difference in cost or clinical outcomes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Mean total cardiac costs were higher by £114 (+8%) in the experimental group, 95% CI from -£112 (-8%) to +£337 (+23%), P = 0.10. MACCE were 10.2% vs. 10.6%; invasive angiography was 19% vs. 25% (P = 0.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows that an FFR-CT pathway reduces invasive angiography without saving cost, informing diagnostic pathways that feed revascularisation decisions.

title: Early invasive coronary angiography and acute ischaemic heart failure outcomes.

appraisal.design_and_n: Population-based cohort, 2994 patients with acute ischaemic HF among 7239 with acute HF; 1567 had early angiography.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational with confounding by indication and oversampling of angiography patients.
appraisal.one_line: Early coronary angiography in acute ischaemic heart failure was associated with lower mortality in an Ontario cohort.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Early angiography was associated with lower all-cause mortality [hazard ratio (HR) 0.74, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.61-0.90, P = 0.002], cardiovascular death (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.56-0.93, P = 0.012), and HF readmissions (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.71-0.99, P = 0.042) after IPTW.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Indications for angiography in acute HF are not established and no trial guides practice.

title: Antiplatelet therapy in patients with conservatively managed spontaneous coronary artery dissection from the multicentre DISCO registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: DISCO multicentre registry, 199 conservatively managed patients (NCT04415762).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small non-randomised sample with confounding by indication.
appraisal.one_line: In conservatively managed SCAD, DAPT was associated with more MACE at 1 year than single antiplatelet therapy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patients treated with DAPT had a significantly higher MACE rate than those with SAPT [18.9% vs. 6.0% hazard ratios (HR) 2.62; 95% confidence intervals (CI) 1.22-5.61; P = 0.013].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Antiplatelet strategy in SCAD is unsettled and the signal challenges routine DAPT.

title: Sex differences in outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting: a pooled analysis of individual patient data.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and pooled analysis of individual patient data from four trials, 13 193 patients (2714 females).
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial populations are selected and numbers of women are modest.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled IPD from four large CABG trials found higher MACCE but similar mortality in women at 5 years.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Women had a significantly higher risk of MACCE [adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 1.12, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.04-1.21; P = 0.004] but similar mortality (adjusted HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.94-1.14; P = 0.51) compared to men.
appraisal.why_it_matters: IPD evidence on sex differences relevant to PCI versus CABG decisions.

title: Reperfusion therapies and in-hospital outcomes for ST-elevation myocardial infarction in Europe: the ACVC-EAPCI EORP STEMI Registry of the European Society of Cardiology.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective EORP STEMI registry, 11 462 patients in 196 centres across 29 countries.
appraisal.main_limitation: Descriptive registry with centre selection and no adjusted comparison.
appraisal.one_line: European STEMI registry described reperfusion use and in-hospital mortality across 29 countries.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary PCI (total cohort frequency: 72.2%), fibrinolysis (18.8%), and no reperfusion therapy (9.0%) were performed. Corresponding in-hospital mortality rates from any cause were 3.1%, 4.4%, and 14.1%.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Benchmarks guideline adherence and geographic variation in STEMI reperfusion.

title: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy after PCI in Patients at High Bleeding Risk.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 4434 patients in the per-protocol population and 4579 in the intention-to-treat population.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, noninferiority margins for ischaemic outcomes, and results apply to one stent platform.
appraisal.one_line: MASTER DAPT showed that one month of DAPT after a biodegradable-polymer sirolimus-eluting stent was noninferior to a longer course in high bleeding risk patients, with less bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Net adverse clinical events occurred in 165 patients (7.5%) with abbreviated therapy and 172 (7.7%) with standard therapy (difference, -0.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.80 to 1.33; P<0.001 for noninferiority). Major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was 148 (6.5%) vs. 211 (9.4%) (difference, -2.82 percentage points; 95% CI, -4.40 to -1.24; P<0.001 for superiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large trial in a common high-risk group that supports shortening DAPT to one month after PCI and bears directly on guideline recommendations for high bleeding risk.

title: Percutaneous Myocardial Revascularization in Late-Presenting Patients With STEMI.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Three nationwide FAST-MI cohorts, 6,273 STEMI patients; 1,077 latecomers analysed.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational with confounding by indication for revascularisation.
appraisal.one_line: French registries associated revascularisation of late-presenting STEMI with lower mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Revascularization of latecomer STEMI patients was independently associated with a significant reduction of mortality occurrence during follow-up (HR: 0.65 [95% CI: 0.50-0.84]; P = 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Late-presenting STEMI beyond 12 hours has limited randomised evidence.

title: Five-year outcomes after state-of-the-art percutaneous coronary revascularization in patients with de novo three-vessel disease: final results of the SYNTAX II study.

appraisal.design_and_n: SYNTAX II multicentre single-arm open-label study compared with matched cohorts from SYNTAX I.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised comparison with historical controls.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year SYNTAX II results of a contemporary PCI strategy compared with matched SYNTAX I cohorts.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 5 years, MACCE rate in SYNTAX II was significantly lower than in the SYNTAX I PCI cohort (21.5% vs. 36.4%, P < 0.001). Outcomes among patients in SYNTAX II and predefined patients in the SYNTAX I CABG cohort were similar (21.5% vs. 24.6%, P = 0.35).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Relevant to the PCI versus CABG debate in three-vessel disease with modern PCI technique.

title: Unguided de-escalation from ticagrelor to clopidogrel in stabilised patients with acute myocardial infarction undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (TALOS-AMI): an investigator-initiated, open-label, multicentre, non-inferiority, randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised open-label noninferiority trial, 2697 patients (1349 de-escalation, 1348 control) in South Korea.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, single-country, and underpowered for ischaemic events alone.
appraisal.one_line: TALOS-AMI found that unguided de-escalation from ticagrelor to clopidogrel after the first month reduced net clinical events after myocardial infarction, mainly through less bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 59 (4·6%) vs 104 (8·2%) patients (pnon-inferiority<0·001; HR 0·55 [95% CI 0·40-0·76], psuperiority=0·0001). Cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or stroke was 2·1% vs 3·1% (HR 0·69; 95% CI 0·42-1·14, p=0·15).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds randomised evidence for uniform de-escalation in an Asian population, bearing on antiplatelet strategy after myocardial infarction.

title: Systems of Care for ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Policy Statement From the American Heart Association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Policy statement; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Policy statement without systematic quantification of evidence in the abstract.
appraisal.one_line: American Heart Association policy statement setting out recommendations for the design of STEMI systems of care.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Reference document for systems-of-care questions in STEMI.

title: Fractional Flow Reserve-Guided PCI as Compared with Coronary Bypass Surgery.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised noninferiority trial, 1500 patients at 48 centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: One-year follow-up only, with repeat revascularisation driving part of the composite.
appraisal.one_line: FAME 3 found that FFR-guided PCI did not meet noninferiority against CABG at 1 year in three-vessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 1-year composite primary end point was 10.6% with FFR-guided PCI and 6.9% with CABG (hazard ratio, 1.5; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.1 to 2.2; P = 0.35 for noninferiority). Death, myocardial infarction or stroke was 7.3% vs. 5.2% (hazard ratio, 1.4; 95% CI, 0.9 to 2.1).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Randomised test of contemporary physiology-guided PCI against CABG in three-vessel disease, central to the revascularisation choice.

title: Angiographic quantitative flow ratio-guided coronary intervention (FAVOR III China): a multicentre, randomised, sham-controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised sham-controlled trial, 3825 patients in the intention-to-treat population at 26 hospitals in China.
