appraisal.main_limitation: Single-country trial, and the benefit was driven by myocardial infarction and ischaemia-driven revascularisation rather than death.
appraisal.one_line: FAVOR III China found that QFR-guided lesion selection for PCI improved 1-year clinical outcomes compared with angiographic guidance.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 1-year primary endpoint occurred in 110 (Kaplan-Meier estimated rate 5·8%) participants in the QFR-guided group and 167 (8·8%) in the angiography-guided group (difference, -3·0% [95% CI -4·7 to -1·4]; hazard ratio 0·65 [95% CI 0·51 to 0·83]; p=0·0004).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large randomised evidence for angiography-derived physiology guidance without a pressure wire, with potential effect on guideline recommendations.

title: Percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stents versus coronary artery bypass grafting in left main coronary artery disease: an individual patient data meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: IPD meta-analysis of four RCTs (SYNTAX, PRECOMBAT, NOBLE, EXCEL), 4394 patients (2197 per group).
appraisal.main_limitation: Four trials with largely low or intermediate anatomical complexity, and a Bayesian result suggesting a possible small mortality difference.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis of four trials found no significant difference in 5-year mortality between PCI and CABG for left main disease, with more myocardial infarction and revascularisation after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Kaplan-Meier 5-year all-cause death was 11·2% (95% CI 9·9-12·6) with PCI and 10·2% (9·0-11·6) with CABG (hazard ratio 1·10, 95% CI 0·91-1·32; p=0·33). Spontaneous myocardial infarction was HR 2·35, 95% CI 1·71-3·23; repeat revascularisation HR 1·78, 1·51-2·10.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Resolves conflicting left main trials with patient-level data and informs the PCI versus CABG choice and guideline discordance.

title: Duration of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy for Patients at High Bleeding Risk Undergoing PCI.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: XIENCE Short DAPT programme of three single-arm studies, 3,652 enrolled; 1,392 on 1-month and 1,972 on 3-month DAPT.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised exploratory comparison across single-arm studies.
appraisal.one_line: Exploratory pooled analysis of HBR patients found 1-month DAPT had similar ischaemic outcomes and less bleeding than 3-month DAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint of all-cause mortality or myocardial infarction was similar between the 2 groups (7.3% vs 7.5%; difference -0.2%; 95% CI: -2.2% to 1.7%; P = 0.41). BARC type 2-5 bleeding was lower with 1-month DAPT (7.6% vs 10.0%; difference -2.5%; 95% CI: -4.6% to -0.3%; P = 0.012).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses optimal DAPT duration in high bleeding risk patients.

title: 2021 ACC/AHA/SCAI Guideline for Coronary Artery Revascularization: Executive Summary: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical practice guideline (executive summary), replacing the 2011 CABG and 2011 and 2015 PCI guidelines.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not list recommendation classes or levels.
appraisal.one_line: Executive summary of the 2021 ACC/AHA/SCAI coronary artery revascularisation guideline.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Defines the American position on revascularisation, against which ESC discordance and evidence gaps can be assessed.

title: 2021 ACC/AHA/SCAI Guideline for Coronary Artery Revascularization: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical practice guideline, replacing the 2011 CABG and 2011 and 2015 PCI guidelines.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not list recommendation classes or levels.
appraisal.one_line: Full 2021 ACC/AHA/SCAI guideline for coronary artery revascularisation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Source of class IIb and level C recommendations and evidence gaps in coronary revascularisation.

title: 2021 ACC/AHA/SCAI Guideline for Coronary Artery Revascularization: Executive Summary: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical practice guideline (executive summary).
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not list recommendation classes or levels; this is a parallel publication of an item already stored.
appraisal.one_line: Executive summary of the 2021 ACC/AHA/SCAI coronary artery revascularisation guideline (duplicate publication in a second journal).
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Parallel publication of the American revascularisation guideline summary.

title: Early Hospital Discharge Following PCI for Patients With STEMI.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective pathway cohort of 600 low-risk STEMI patients compared with a historical group of 700 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised comparison with a historical control group.
appraisal.one_line: Early discharge pathway after primary PCI for low-risk STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Median length of stay was 24.6 hours (interquartile range [IQR]: 22.7-30.0 hours), with 2 deaths (0.33%), both caused by coronavirus disease 2019, and MACE rates of 1.2%, compared with mortality 0.7% and MACE 1.9% in the >48-hour control group.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It supports shorter admission after primary PCI in selected patients, a systems-of-care question with resource implications.

title: Comparative effects of guided vs. potent P2Y12 inhibitor therapy in acute coronary syndrome: a network meta-analysis of 61 898 patients from 15 randomized trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis of 15 RCTs, 61 898 patients; PROSPERO CRD42021258603.
appraisal.main_limitation: Indirect comparisons across heterogeneous trials of guided strategies and fixed agents.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis found that guided selection of P2Y12 inhibitor therapy was the only strategy associated with fewer MACE without more bleeding in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A guided approach was associated with reduced MACE (IRR: 0.80, 95% CI: 0.65-0.98) without any significant trade-off in all bleeding (IRR: 1.22, 95% CI: 0.96-1.55).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on guided versus potent P2Y12 inhibitor therapy, with relevance to guideline recommendations.

title: Cost-Effectiveness of Coronary Artery Bypass Surgery Versus Medicine in Ischemic Cardiomyopathy: The STICH Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Decision-analytic patient-level simulation model using resource use and clinical data from the STICH randomised trial.
appraisal.main_limitation: Model-based estimate built on US cost weights and a single trial population.
appraisal.one_line: Lifetime cost-effectiveness of CABG versus medical therapy using STICH trial data.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio for CABG compared with MED was $63 989 per quality-adjusted life-year gained; CABG was economically favourable in 87% of microsimulations at a willingness-to-pay threshold of $100 000 per quality-adjusted life-year.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It adds an economic argument for surgical revascularisation in ischaemic cardiomyopathy.

title: Antithrombotic Therapy in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation After Acute Coronary Syndromes or Percutaneous Intervention.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified-style subgroup analysis of a 2 x 2 factorial randomised trial; 4,386 of 4,614 patients with calculable scores.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis, and the trial was not powered for ischaemic outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: AUGUSTUS secondary analysis found that apixaban without aspirin reduced bleeding irrespective of baseline bleeding or stroke risk scores in atrial fibrillation with ACS or PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Bleeding rates were lower with apixaban than VKA (HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.41-0.78 [HAS-BLED ≤2]; HR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.59-0.88 [HAS-BLED ≥3]; interaction P = 0.23). Aspirin increased bleeding (HR: 1.86; 95% CI: 1.36-2.56 [HAS-BLED ≤2]; HR: 1.81; 95% CI: 1.47-2.23 [HAS-BLED ≥3]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports omitting aspirin and using apixaban across risk strata in patients on oral anticoagulation after ACS or PCI.

title: High-Sensitivity Troponin I after Cardiac Surgery and 30-Day Mortality.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: International prospective cohort study (VISION Cardiac Surgery) of 13,862 patients undergoing cardiac surgery.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational association with mortality; thresholds have wide confidence intervals and the study does not test an intervention.
appraisal.one_line: International prospective cohort relating peak high-sensitivity troponin I after cardiac surgery to 30-day mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Among patients who underwent isolated coronary-artery bypass grafting or aortic-valve replacement or repair, the threshold troponin level, measured within 1 day after surgery, that was associated with an adjusted hazard ratio of more than 1.00 for death within 30 days was 5670 ng per liter (95% confidence interval [CI], 1045 to 8260), a level 218 times the upper reference limit. Among patients who underwent other cardiac surgery, the corresponding threshold was 12,981 ng per liter (95% CI, 2673 to 16,591), a level 499 times the upper reference limit.
appraisal.why_it_matters: The mortality-associated thresholds are far above those used to define periprocedural myocardial injury, which bears on definitions and on triggers for invasive investigation after surgical revascularisation.

title: 5-Year Outcomes of PCI Guided by Measurement of Instantaneous Wave-Free Ratio Versus Fractional Flow Reserve.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry-based randomised trial, 2,037 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label noninferiority design; mortality point estimate was numerically higher with iFR.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year follow-up of iFR-SWEDEHEART found no difference between iFR-guided and FFR-guided revascularisation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 5 years, the primary composite endpoint was 21.5% in the iFR group and 19.9% in the FFR group (HR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.90-1.33). All-cause death was 9.4% vs 7.9% (HR: 1.20; 95% CI: 0.89-1.62).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Long-term data on physiology index choice from a registry-based randomised trial.

title: Effect of Alirocumab Added to High-Intensity Statin Therapy on Coronary Atherosclerosis in Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction: The PACMAN-AMI Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised double-blind trial, 300 patients (alirocumab n = 148, placebo n = 152) at 9 European hospitals.
appraisal.main_limitation: Imaging surrogate endpoint with no clinical outcome data.
appraisal.one_line: PACMAN-AMI found that adding alirocumab to high-intensity statin therapy produced greater coronary plaque regression 52 weeks after myocardial infarction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Mean change in percent atheroma volume was -2.13% with alirocumab vs -0.92% with placebo (difference, -1.21% [95% CI, -1.78% to -0.65%], P < .001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports early PCSK9 inhibition after myocardial infarction through plaque effects, relevant to secondary prevention.

title: Variation in revascularisation use and outcomes of patients in hospital with acute myocardial infarction across six high income countries: cross sectional cohort study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective cross-sectional cohort study of administrative data; admissions ranged from 19 043 in Israel to 1 064 099 in the US.
appraisal.main_limitation: Administrative data in patients aged 66 years and older, with limited adjustment for case mix.
appraisal.one_line: Six-country comparison of revascularisation and outcomes for older patients with STEMI and NSTEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The proportion of patients with STEMI who received percutaneous coronary intervention in hospital during 2017 ranged from 36.9% (England) to 78.6% (Canada; 71.8% in the US); death within one year of admission for STEMI in 2017 ranged from 18.9% (Netherlands) to 27.8% (US) and 32.3% (Taiwan).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It documents marked international practice variation in invasive management of myocardial infarction.

title: Timing of invasive strategy in non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials; randomised trials including 10 209 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: All-comers pooling with heterogeneous timing definitions and risk profiles; patient-level effect modification not addressed.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of randomised trials found that early invasive strategy in NSTE-ACS did not reduce all-cause mortality but reduced recurrent ischaemia and length of stay.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: No significant difference in all-cause mortality (RR: 0.90, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.78-1.04); recurrent ischaemia was reduced (RR: 0.57, 95% CI: 0.40-0.81) with an early invasive strategy.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Timing of invasive strategy in NSTE-ACS remains contested, and the pooled evidence frames the guideline position for all-comers.

title: Association of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy With Ticagrelor With Vein Graft Failure After Coronary Artery Bypass Graft Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: IPD meta-analysis of randomised trials; 4 RCTs with 1316 patients and 1668 saphenous vein grafts.
appraisal.main_limitation: Graft patency is an imaging endpoint rather than a clinical event, and the trials were small and few.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis found ticagrelor DAPT was associated with less saphenous vein graft failure than aspirin after CABG, at the cost of more BARC 2, 3 or 5 bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Ticagrelor DAPT was associated with a significantly lower incidence of saphenous vein graft failure (11.2%) per graft than was aspirin (20%; difference, -8.7% [95% CI, -13.5% to -3.9%]; OR, 0.51 [95% CI, 0.35 to 0.74]; P < .001); BARC type 2, 3, or 5 bleeding was higher (OR, 2.98 [95% CI, 1.99 to 4.47]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs antithrombotic choice after CABG, a decision at the PCI versus CABG interface, though clinical-event benefit is not shown.

title: Routine Pressure Wire Assessment Versus Conventional Angiography in the Management of Patients With Coronary Artery Disease: The RIPCORD 2 Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label randomised trial in 17 UK centres; 1100 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, with coprimary outcomes of cost and quality of life rather than clinical events.
appraisal.one_line: RIPCORD 2 found that systematic pressure wire assessment at diagnostic angiography did not reduce costs or improve quality of life versus angiography alone.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Median hospital costs were similar: angiography, £4136 (interquartile range, £2613-£7015); and angiography+FFR, £4510 (£2721-£7415; P=0.137); median quality of life was 75 in both groups (P=0.88).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests routine physiology assessment of all vessels at diagnostic angiography and does not support systematic use.

title: Impact of Medication Nonadherence in a Clinical Trial of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a randomised trial; 4,579 high bleeding risk patients, using inverse probability-of-censoring weights.
appraisal.main_limitation: Adherence-corrected analysis is non-randomised in nature, and the reported confidence interval for MCB does not enclose its point estimate.
appraisal.one_line: MASTER DAPT adherence analysis in high bleeding risk patients found that abbreviated DAPT was associated with similar NACE and MACE and lower bleeding after correcting for nonadherence.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: NACE (HR: 1.01; 95% CI: 0.88-1.27) or MACE (HR: 1.07; 95% CI: 0.83-1.40) did not differ, and MCB was lower with abbreviated compared with standard treatment (HR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.60-0.73).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports the robustness of the abbreviated DAPT result in high bleeding risk patients (D8).

title: Percutaneous Revascularization for Ischemic Left Ventricular Dysfunction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 700 patients (347 PCI, 353 optimal medical therapy alone).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design; selected patients with demonstrable viability, and quality of life appeared to favour PCI early on.
appraisal.one_line: REVIVED-BCIS2 found that PCI added to optimal medical therapy did not reduce death or heart failure hospitalisation in ischaemic left ventricular systolic dysfunction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary-outcome event occurred in 129 patients (37.2%) in the PCI group and in 134 patients (38.0%) in the optimal-medical-therapy group (hazard ratio, 0.99; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78 to 1.27; P = 0.96).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly challenges routine PCI for ischaemic cardiomyopathy and bears on guideline recommendations for revascularisation in this group (D1).

title: A Multicenter, Phase 2, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blind, Parallel-Group, Dose-Finding Trial of the Oral Factor XIa Inhibitor Asundexian to Prevent Adverse Cardiovascular Outcomes After Acute Myocardial Infarction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Phase 2 randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; 1601 patients with recent acute MI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Dose-finding trial with few ischaemic events and 90% confidence intervals, not powered for efficacy.
appraisal.one_line: Phase 2 dose-ranging trial of the factor XIa inhibitor asundexian after acute MI showed near-complete FXIa inhibition without a significant increase in bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The main safety outcome occurred in 30 (7.6%), 32 (8.1%), 42 (10.5%), and 36 (9.0%) patients receiving asundexian 10 mg, 20 mg, or 50 mg, or placebo, respectively (pooled asundexian versus placebo: hazard ratio, 0.98 [90% CI, 0.71-1.35]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First factor XI inhibitor data on top of DAPT after MI, relevant to future antithrombotic strategies (D8).

title: Routine Functional Testing or Standard Care in High-Risk Patients after PCI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 1706 patients (849 functional testing, 857 standard care).
appraisal.main_limitation: Event rates were low at 2 years, limiting power to detect small differences.
appraisal.one_line: POST-PCI randomised high-risk patients after PCI to routine functional testing at 1 year or standard care and found no difference in clinical outcomes at 2 years.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary-outcome event had occurred in 46 of 849 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 5.5%) in the functional-testing group and in 51 of 857 (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 6.0%) in the standard-care group (hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.61 to 1.35; P = 0.62).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Argues against routine surveillance functional testing after complex PCI, a common practice.

title: Effects on Mortality and Major Bleeding of Radial Versus Femoral Artery Access for Coronary Angiography or Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Meta-Analysis of Individual Patient Data From 7 Multicenter Randomized Clinical Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: IPD meta-analysis of randomised trials; 21 600 patients (10 775 TRA, 10 825 TFA) from 7 trials.
appraisal.main_limitation: Mediation analysis is observational in nature, and the mortality effect was driven by patients with anaemia in subgroup analysis.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis of seven randomised trials found radial access was associated with lower all-cause mortality and major bleeding than femoral access.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause mortality (1.6% versus 2.1%; hazard ratio, 0.77 [95% CI, 0.63-0.95]; P=0.012) and major bleeding (1.5% versus 2.7%; odds ratio, 0.55 [95% CI, 0.45-0.67]; P<0.001) were lower with TRA.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Strengthens the case for radial access as default and identifies baseline haemoglobin as an effect modifier (D1, D6).

title: Empagliflozin in acute myocardial infarction: the EMMY trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Academic, multicentre, double-blind randomised trial; 476 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Biomarker and echocardiographic primary endpoint rather than clinical events; very few heart failure hospitalisations.
appraisal.one_line: EMMY randomised patients with acute MI to empagliflozin or placebo and found greater NT-proBNP reduction and echocardiographic improvement at 26 weeks.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: NT-proBNP reduction was significantly greater in the empagliflozin group, compared with placebo, being 15% lower [95% confidence interval (CI) -4.4% to -23.6%] after adjusting for baseline NT-proBNP, sex, and diabetes status (P = 0.026).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides mechanistic support for SGLT2 inhibitor use after MI (D6) pending hard-endpoint trials.

title: Fractional Flow Reserve or Intravascular Ultrasonography to Guide PCI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised noninferiority trial; 1682 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Industry-funded, with PCI performed in 44.4% of the FFR group and 65.3% of the IVUS group, so it compares strategies rather than modalities.
appraisal.one_line: FLAVOUR randomised intermediate stenoses to FFR-guided or IVUS-guided PCI and found FFR guidance noninferior for death, MI or revascularisation at 24 months.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 24 months, a primary-outcome event had occurred in 8.1% of the patients in the FFR group and in 8.5% of those in the IVUS group (absolute difference, -0.4 percentage points; upper boundary of the one-sided 97.5% confidence interval, 2.2 percentage points; P = 0.01 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the choice between physiology and imaging to guide PCI in intermediate lesions (D1).

title: Effect of Clinical Decision Support With Audit and Feedback on Prevention of Acute Kidney Injury in Patients Undergoing Coronary Angiography: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Stepped-wedge cluster randomised trial in Alberta; 7820 procedures among 7106 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Time-adjusted pre-post comparison without effect on major cardiovascular or kidney events.
appraisal.one_line: Stepped-wedge cluster trial of decision support with audit and feedback was associated with less contrast-associated AKI after coronary angiography.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The incidence of AKI was 7.2% (310 events after 4327 procedures) during the intervention period and 8.6% (299 events after 3493 procedures) during the control period (odds ratio [OR], 0.72 [95% CI, 0.56 to 0.93]; P = .01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: A system-level intervention for a common PCI complication (D1), though clinical-event benefit was not shown.

title: Everolimus-Eluting Stents or Bypass Surgery for Multivessel Coronary Artery Disease: Extended Follow-Up Outcomes of Multicenter Randomized Controlled BEST Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial terminated early for slow enrolment; 880 patients included (438 PCI, 442 CABG), median follow-up 11.8 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Early termination left the trial underpowered relative to its design target of 1776 patients.
appraisal.one_line: Extended follow-up of BEST found no significant difference between everolimus-eluting stent PCI and CABG in the primary composite, with more spontaneous MI and repeat revascularisation after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 151 patients (34.5%) in the PCI group and 134 patients (30.3%) in the CABG group (hazard ratio [HR], 1.18 [95% CI, 0.88-1.56]; P=0.26).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Long-term PCI versus CABG data in multivessel disease with contemporary stents (D1).

title: Abbreviated Antiplatelet Therapy After Coronary Stenting in Patients With Myocardial Infarction at High Bleeding Risk.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified subgroup analysis of a randomised trial; 4,579 patients at HBR, of whom 1,780 had acute or recent MI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis, with limited power for ischaemic events within the MI stratum.
appraisal.one_line: MASTER DAPT analysis by presence of recent MI found that 1-month DAPT in high bleeding risk patients gave similar NACE and MACCE and less bleeding irrespective of MI presentation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: NACE and MACCE did not differ with abbreviated vs nonabbreviated APT regimens in patients with an acute or recent myocardial infarction (n = 1,780; HR: 0.83; 95% CI: 0.61-1.12 and HR: 0.86; 95% CI: 0.62-1.19, respectively).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Extends abbreviated DAPT evidence to high bleeding risk patients with MI (D8, D6).

title: Coronary angiography after cardiac arrest without ST-elevation myocardial infarction: a network meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and network meta-analysis; 16 studies (six RCTs, ten non-randomised studies).
appraisal.main_limitation: DerSimonian-Laird pooling with high heterogeneity overall and mixed randomised and non-randomised designs; search ended July 2022.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis found that the apparent survival benefit of early coronary angiography after cardiac arrest without ST elevation was driven by non-randomised studies and was not seen in randomised trials.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Meta-analyses showed a statistically significant increase in survival after early CAG compared with selective CAG in the overall analysis [OR: 1.40, 95% confidence interval (CI): (1.12-1.76), P < 0.01, I2 = 68%]; this effect was lost in the subgroup analysis of RCTs [OR: 0.89, 95% CI: (0.73-1.10), P = 0.29, I2 = 0%].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on routine early angiography after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest without STEMI (D2), where guideline practice is still debated.

title: Treatment Time and In-Hospital Mortality Among Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction, 2018-2021.

appraisal.design_and_n: Cross-sectional study of 114 871 patients with STEMI treated at 648 hospitals in the Get With The Guidelines-Coronary Artery Disease registry.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational association subject to confounding and selection into timely treatment.
appraisal.one_line: Treatment times and in-hospital mortality for STEMI in a national US registry.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Adjusted in-hospital mortality was lower for first medical contact to device ≤90 minutes via emergency medical services (adjusted OR, 0.40 [95% CI, 0.36-0.44]); system goals were not met in most quarters, with 17% of transferred patients treated ≤120 minutes.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It shows persistent shortfalls against reperfusion time goals, especially after interhospital transfer.

title: Indobufen or Aspirin on Top of Clopidogrel After Coronary Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation (OPTION): A Randomized, Open-Label, End Point-Blinded, Noninferiority Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised, open-label, endpoint-blinded noninferiority trial in 103 Chinese centres; 4551 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, troponin-negative patients only, clopidogrel as P2Y12 inhibitor, and a Chinese population limiting generalisability.
appraisal.one_line: OPTION randomised patients after drug-eluting stents to indobufen or aspirin plus clopidogrel and found a lower net clinical composite driven by less bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 101 patients (4.47%) in the indobufen-based DAPT group and 140 patients (6.11%) in the conventional DAPT group (absolute difference, -1.63%; Pnoninferiority<0.001; hazard ratio, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.56-0.94]; P=0.015).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests an aspirin alternative within DAPT after PCI (D8) in a large randomised sample.

title: Survival After Invasive or Conservative Management of Stable Coronary Disease.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial extended follow-up; 5179 participants, 557 deaths over a median follow-up of 5.7 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Interim report, with undetermined deaths classified as cardiovascular by protocol and a selected population excluding unacceptable angina and recent ACS.
appraisal.one_line: Extended follow-up of ISCHEMIA found no difference in all-cause mortality between invasive and conservative strategies, with lower cardiovascular and higher non-cardiovascular mortality after an initial invasive strategy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause mortality was not different between randomized treatment groups (7-year rate, 12.7% in invasive strategy, 13.4% in conservative strategy; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.00 [95% CI, 0.85-1.18]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Long-term survival data for revascularisation in chronic coronary syndrome (D1).

title: Aspirin Versus Clopidogrel for Long-Term Maintenance Monotherapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: The HOST-EXAM Extended Study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Post-trial follow-up of a randomised trial; 5438 patients randomised, per-protocol analysis of 2431 clopidogrel and 2286 aspirin patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post-trial extension analysed per protocol, open to attrition and treatment crossover bias, in an East Asian population.
appraisal.one_line: HOST-EXAM extended follow-up found clopidogrel monotherapy was associated with a lower net clinical composite than aspirin monotherapy over more than 5 years after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: During a median follow-up of 5.8 years (interquartile range, 4.8-6.2 years), the primary end point occurred in 12.8% and 16.9% in the clopidogrel and aspirin groups, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.74 [95% CI, 0.63-0.86]; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the choice of long-term single antiplatelet agent after PCI (D8).

title: Surgical or percutaneous coronary revascularization for heart failure: an in silico model using routinely collected health data to emulate a clinical trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Target trial emulation in Hospital Episode Statistics matched to STICH data; target population 13 519 patients, emulated cohort 2046 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational instrumental variable design relying on regional variation as a valid instrument.
appraisal.one_line: Instrumental variable emulation using English administrative data associated CABG with fewer deaths or cardiovascular hospitalisations than complex PCI in heart failure.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: IVA of the emulated cohort showed that CABG was associated with a lower risk of the primary outcome (ATE 16.2, 95 CI 20.6 to 11.8), with comparable estimates in the unmatched target population (ATE 15.5, 95 CI 17.5 to 13.5).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses CABG versus PCI in ischaemic cardiomyopathy (D1), where randomised evidence is thin, and argues a pragmatic trial would be feasible.

title: Bivalirudin plus a high-dose infusion versus heparin monotherapy in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention: a randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Investigator-initiated, open-label randomised trial at 87 Chinese centres; 6016 patients (3009 bivalirudin, 3007 heparin).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, Chinese centres with predominantly radial access, and an industry research grant; 30-day follow-up only.
appraisal.one_line: BRIGHT-4 randomised STEMI patients to bivalirudin with a post-PCI high-dose infusion or heparin monotherapy; bivalirudin reduced 30-day death or major bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with heparin monotherapy, bivalirudin reduced the 30-day rate of the primary endpoint (132 events [4·39%] in the heparin group vs 92 events [3·06%] in the bivalirudin group; difference, 1·33%, 95% CI 0·38-2·29%; hazard ratio [HR] 0·69, 95% CI 0·53-0·91; p=0·0070).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large randomised evidence on anticoagulation in primary PCI (D8, D6) that bears on guideline recommendations for bivalirudin versus heparin.

title: 2-Year Outcomes of Angiographic Quantitative Flow Ratio-Guided Coronary Interventions.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre, randomised, sham-controlled trial; 3,825 participants (1,913 QFR-guided, 1,912 angiography-guided).
appraisal.main_limitation: Chinese centres only, with the benefit concentrated in patients whose strategy QFR changed.
appraisal.one_line: FAVOR III China 2-year follow-up found QFR-guided lesion selection was associated with fewer MACE than angiography guidance.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 2-year MACE occurred in 161 of 1,913 (8.5%) patients in the QFR-guided group and in 237 of 1,912 (12.5%) patients in the angiography-guided group (HR: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.54-0.81; P < 0.0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports angiography-derived physiology for PCI lesion selection (D1) with a hard composite endpoint.

title: Long-term mortality, cardiovascular events, and bleeding in stable patients 1 year after myocardial infarction: a Danish nationwide study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Danish nationwide registry cohort of 82 108 patients with first-time MI during 2000-17 who survived 1 year free from bleeding and cardiovascular events.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational temporal trends, with treatment changes only partly accounted for by standardisation.
appraisal.one_line: Two decades of long-term risk in event-free one-year survivors of myocardial infarction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The crude 5-year risk of mortality fell from 18.6% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 17.9-19.2) to 12.5% (CI: 11.9-13.1) and recurrent MI from 7.5% (CI: 7.1-8.0) to 5.5% (CI: 5.1-6.0).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Lower contemporary residual risk affects the expected benefit of extended secondary prevention after MI.

title: Dual antiplatelet therapy duration after percutaneous coronary intervention in high bleeding risk: a meta-analysis of randomized trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials; 11 trials including 9006 HBR patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level pooling across varying HBR definitions and DAPT strategies; patients with an indication for oral anticoagulation were excluded.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of randomised trials in high bleeding risk patients found 1-month or 3-month DAPT reduced bleeding and cardiovascular mortality without more ischaemic events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Abbreviated DAPT reduced major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding [risk ratio (RR): 0.76, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.61-0.94; I2 = 28%], major bleeding (RR: 0.80, 95% CI: 0.64-0.99, I2 = 0%), and cardiovascular mortality (RR: 0.79, 95% CI: 0.65-0.95, I2 = 0%) compared with standard DAPT.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Summarises the evidence for DAPT de-escalation in high bleeding risk PCI (D8).

title: Fractional flow reserve versus angiography-guided strategy in acute myocardial infarction with multivessel disease: a randomized trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 562 patients (284 FFR-guided, 278 angiography-guided), median follow-up 3.5 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Modest sample size, and the angiography arm had near-universal non-culprit PCI.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial in acute MI with multivessel disease found FFR-guided PCI of non-infarct arteries was associated with fewer deaths, MI or revascularisations than angiography-guided PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 18 patients of 284 patients in the FFR-guided PCI group and in 40 of 278 patients in the angiography-guided PCI group (7.4% vs. 19.7%; hazard ratio, 0.43; 95% confidence interval, 0.25-0.75; P = 0.003).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses how to select non-culprit lesions in complete revascularisation after STEMI or NSTEMI (D6, D1).

title: Exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation for coronary heart disease: a meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of 85 RCTs involving 23 430 participants with a median 12-month follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Searches ended in September 2020 and the trials are heterogeneous in intervention and era.
appraisal.one_line: Updated meta-analysis of exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation in coronary heart disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation was associated with reduced cardiovascular mortality (RR: 0.74, 95% CI: 0.64-0.86) and myocardial infarction (RR: 0.82, 95% CI: 0.70-0.96), with no significant impact on overall mortality (RR: 0.96, 95% CI: 0.89-1.04).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Confirms the contemporary benefit of rehabilitation after myocardial infarction and revascularisation, relevant to secondary prevention pathways.

title: P2Y12 Inhibitor Monotherapy or Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Complex Percutaneous Coronary Interventions.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled patient-level data from 5 randomised trials including 22,941 patients, of whom 4,685 (20.4%) had complex PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis by PCI complexity, with few events in the complex group and a short-DAPT lead-in that differs between trials.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis of P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy versus DAPT by complexity of PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary efficacy endpoint was similar between strategies in complex PCI (HR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.64-1.19) and noncomplex PCI (HR: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.76-1.09); BARC 3 or 5 bleeding was lower with monotherapy in complex PCI (HR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.31-0.84).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses whether shortened DAPT is safe in higher-risk anatomy, a common decision in antithrombotic de-escalation.

title: Sex Differences in 10-Year Outcomes After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention With Drug-Eluting Stents: Insights From the DECADE Cooperation.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled individual data from 5 randomised trials with 10-year follow-up; 9700 patients, of whom 2296 were women and 7404 were men.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc comparison by sex within trials not designed for it, with women under-represented.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data analysis of sex differences in 10-year outcomes after DES implantation in the DECADE cooperation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Cardiovascular death occurred in 407 of the 2296 female patients and 1012 of the 7404 male patients (adjusted HR [HRadj], 0.94 [95% CI, 0.80-1.11]); female sex was associated with an increased risk of myocardial infarction in the first 30 days (HRadj, 1.65 [95% CI, 1.24-2.19]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides long-term data on sex-specific risk after contemporary stenting, relevant to early post-PCI risk in women.

title: Coronary artery restenosis treatment with plain balloon, drug-coated balloon, or drug-eluting stent: 10-year outcomes of the ISAR-DESIRE 3 trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial extended to 10 years; 402 patients (500 lesions) assigned to plain balloon (134), drug-coated balloon (137) or drug-eluting stent (131).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample with non-proportional hazards and differences between PCB and PES that did not reach significance.
appraisal.one_line: Ten-year follow-up of a randomised trial of balloon, drug-coated balloon and drug-eluting stent for drug-eluting stent in-stent restenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 10 years the primary composite endpoint occurred in 90 patients (72.0%) assigned to PB, 70 patients (55.9%) assigned to PCB, and 72 patients (62.4%) assigned to PES (P < 0.001); PCB versus PES was non-significant (Cox: HR 1.10, 95% CI 0.79-1.52).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides the longest randomised follow-up for treatment of in-stent restenosis, informing the choice between DCB and DES.

title: On-Site Computed Tomography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve to Guide Management of Patients With Stable Coronary Artery Disease: The TARGET Randomized Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial in 6 Chinese centres; 1216 patients with stable coronary artery disease.
appraisal.main_limitation: Primary endpoint is a process measure and the trial was not powered for clinical outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of on-site machine-learning CT-FFR care pathway versus standard care in stable coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The proportion undergoing invasive angiography without obstructive disease or with disease not intervened on was 28.3% [119/421] versus 46.2% [223/483]; P<0.001, and MACE at 1 year did not differ (hazard ratio, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.59-1.30]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows a non-invasive physiology pathway can reduce unnecessary angiography, shaping referral to catheterisation.

title: Comparison of 3- to 6-Month Versus 12-Month Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Coronary Intervention Using the Contemporary Drug-Eluting Stents With Ultrathin Struts: The HOST-IDEA Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label randomised trial at 37 centres in South Korea; 2013 patients randomised to 3- to 6-month DAPT (n=1002) or 12-month DAPT (n=1011).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design in a single country with physician choice of antiplatelet agent and exclusion of STEMI.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised noninferiority trial of 3- to 6-month versus 12-month DAPT after ultrathin-strut DES.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 37 (3.7%) patients versus 41 (4.1%); noninferiority was met (absolute risk difference, -0.4% [1-sided 95% CI, -∞% to 1.1%]; P<0.001 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds to evidence supporting shortened DAPT after contemporary stents.

title: Intravascular Imaging-Guided or Angiography-Guided Complex PCI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 1639 patients, 1092 assigned to intravascular imaging-guided PCI and 547 to angiography-guided PCI, median follow-up 2.1 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not state blinding; the 2:1 allocation and composite endpoint driven by softer components limit inference on individual hard outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of intravascular imaging-guided versus angiography-guided PCI in complex lesions reduced a composite of cardiac events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary end-point event occurred in 76 patients (cumulative incidence, 7.7%) in the intravascular imaging group and in 60 patients (cumulative incidence, 12.3%) in the angiography group (hazard ratio, 0.64; 95% confidence interval, 0.45 to 0.89; P = 0.008).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds randomised evidence for imaging guidance in complex PCI, a decision that guidelines grade variably.

title: Dual antiplatelet therapy de-escalation in acute coronary syndrome: an individual patient meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data meta-analysis of four RCTs including 10 133 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooled trials differ in the de-escalation approach (guided versus unguided, and drug switching), and open-label designs may bias bleeding reports.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis of DAPT de-escalation versus standard DAPT after PCI for acute coronary syndrome.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The ischaemic endpoint was lower with de-escalation than standard strategy (2.3% vs. 3.0%, hazard ratio [HR] 0.761, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.597-0.972), and bleeding was lower (6.5% vs. 9.1%, HR 0.701, 95% CI 0.606-0.811).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports de-escalation of antiplatelet therapy after ACS, a common decision.

title: Immediate versus staged complete revascularisation in patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome and multivessel coronary disease (BIOVASC): a prospective, open-label, non-inferiority, randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label noninferiority randomised trial; 764 patients assigned to immediate and 761 to staged complete revascularisation.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design and a composite primary outcome.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of immediate versus staged complete revascularisation in acute coronary syndrome with multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome at 1 year occurred in 57 (7·6%) of 764 patients in the immediate group and in 71 (9·4%) of 761 patients in the staged group (HR 0·78, 95% CI 0·55-1·11, pnon-inferiority=0·0011).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the timing of non-culprit revascularisation in ACS.

title: Influence of Culprit Lesion Intervention on Outcomes in Infarct-Related Cardiogenic Shock With Cardiac Arrest.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry and randomised trial analysis of 1,015 patients, of whom 550 (54.2%) had cardiac arrest.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis with limited power for interaction testing.
appraisal.one_line: Analysis of cardiac arrest in infarct-related cardiogenic shock within the CULPRIT-SHOCK population.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: One-year death was 53.8% vs 50.4% (P = 0.29) in patients with and without cardiac arrest; cardiac arrest was an independent predictor of 1-year mortality (HR: 1.27; 95% CI: 1.01-1.59).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports culprit-lesion-only PCI in shock regardless of cardiac arrest.

title: Differences in Treatment Patterns and Outcomes of Acute Myocardial Infarction for Low- and High-Income Patients in 6 Countries.

appraisal.design_and_n: Serial cross-sectional cohort study of 289 376 patients hospitalized with STEMI and 843 046 with NSTEMI, aged 66 years or older, in the US, Canada, England, the Netherlands, Taiwan and Israel, 2013 through 2018.
appraisal.main_limitation: Administrative data with limited clinical detail and area-level or imputed income measures; observational associations only.
appraisal.one_line: Six-country administrative cohort comparing treatment patterns and mortality after acute myocardial infarction between high- and low-income older patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Adjusted 30-day mortality generally was 1 to 3 percentage points lower for high-income patients. For STEMI in the Netherlands, 30-day mortality was 10.2% for high income vs 13.1% for low income (difference, -2.8 percentage points [95% CI, -4.1 to -1.5]). For PCI in STEMI in England, 73.6% vs 67.4% (difference, 6.1 percentage points [95% CI, 1.2 to 11.0]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows income-related gaps in invasive treatment and survival persist under universal coverage, relevant to equity-focused systems-of-care questions.

title: 5-Year Outcomes After Bioresorbable Coronary Scaffolds Implanted With Improved Technique.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Large blinded randomised trial comparing BVS with CoCr-EES; target lesion failure assessed at 5 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not give a hazard ratio for the primary result.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year results of the Absorb IV randomised trial of bioresorbable scaffolds implanted with an improved technique.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Target lesion failure at 5 years occurred in 216 (17.5%) patients assigned to BVS and 180 (14.5%) patients assigned to CoCr-EES (P = 0.03).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows excess events with scaffolds persisted despite improved implantation, closing a device question.

title: Management strategies for heavily calcified coronary stenoses: an EAPCI clinical consensus statement in collaboration with the EURO4C-PCR group.

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical consensus statement prepared with the EURO4C-PCR group, updating the 2015 EAPCI consensus on rotational atherectomy.
appraisal.main_limitation: Expert consensus rather than trial evidence, with comparative data between calcium modification tools sparse.
appraisal.one_line: EAPCI clinical consensus statement on the management of heavily calcified coronary stenoses.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides guidance on imaging, tool selection and technique for calcified lesions, a growing share of PCI.

title: PCI or CABG for left main coronary artery disease: the SWEDEHEART registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: Observational nationwide all-comers registry study, 11 137 patients with LMCA disease underwent CABG (n = 9364) or PCI (n = 1773), 2005 to 2015.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised, pre-2016 PCI era with limited intravascular imaging and contemporary stents; residual confounding is possible despite the instrumental variable.
appraisal.one_line: Swedish registry comparison of PCI and CABG for unprotected left main disease using inverse probability weighting and an instrumental variable.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: PCI patients had higher mortality than CABG patients with IPW analysis (hazard ratio [HR] 2.0 [95% confidence interval (CI) 1.5-2.7]) and with IV analysis (HR 1.5 [95% CI 1.1-2.0]). MACCE was higher with PCI with IV analysis (HR 2.8 [95% CI 1.8-4.5]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds observational data to a contested PCI versus CABG decision in left main disease, including a diabetes interaction.

title: Defining Strategies of Modulation of Antiplatelet Therapy in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease: A Consensus Document from the Academic Research Consortium.

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus document from the Academic Research Consortium.
appraisal.main_limitation: Terminology and definitions rather than new outcome evidence.
appraisal.one_line: Academic Research Consortium consensus defining strategies of antiplatelet therapy modulation in coronary artery disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Standardises de-escalation and escalation terminology used across antithrombotic trials and guidelines.

title: Considerations on the Management of Acute Postoperative Ischemia After Cardiac Surgery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement from a multidisciplinary group.
appraisal.main_limitation: The statement notes that evidence on management is sparse and of low methodological quality.
appraisal.one_line: AHA scientific statement on acute postoperative myocardial ischaemia after cardiac surgery.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives guidance on diagnosis and choice between PCI and redo CABG in a rare but life-threatening complication.

title: P2Y12 Inhibitor or Aspirin Monotherapy for Secondary Prevention of Coronary Events.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data meta-analysis of 7 trials; 24,325 participants, 12,178 assigned to P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy and 12,147 to aspirin.
appraisal.main_limitation: Mostly clopidogrel and ticagrelor trials with differing populations and open-label designs.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis of P2Y12 inhibitor versus aspirin monotherapy for long-term secondary prevention in coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Risk of the primary outcome was lower with P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy compared with aspirin over 2 years (HR: 0.88; 95% CI: 0.79-0.97; P = 0.012), with similar major bleeding (HR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.70-1.09; P = 0.23).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges aspirin as default chronic antiplatelet agent and bears on guideline recommendations.

title: STREAM-2: Half-Dose Tenecteplase or Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Older Patients With ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Randomized, Open-Label Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label randomised trial; patients assigned to pharmaco-invasive treatment (n=401) or primary PCI (n=203).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, with a 2:1 allocation and small numbers for clinical events; six intracranial haemorrhages occurred in the pharmaco-invasive arm.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of half-dose tenecteplase pharmaco-invasive treatment versus primary PCI in older patients with STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The composite clinical end point occurred in 12.8% (51/400) of patients undergoing pharmaco-invasive treatment and 13.3% (27/203) of patients undergoing primary PCI (relative risk, 0.96 [95% CI, 0.62-1.48]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs reperfusion choice in older patients when primary PCI is delayed.

title: Race-Based Differences in ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Process Metrics and Mortality From 2015 Through 2021: An Analysis of 178 062 Patients From the American Heart Association Get With The Guidelines-Coronary Artery Disease Registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry analysis from 2015 through 2021.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry with residual confounding and hospital-level participation in the registry.
appraisal.one_line: Registry analysis of race-based differences in STEMI process metrics and mortality in the Get With The Guidelines-CAD registry.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with non-Hispanic White women, Hispanic White women had higher adjusted in-hospital mortality (odds ratio, 1.39 [95% CI, 1.12-1.72]), whereas Black women did not (odds ratio, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.74-1.03]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Documents persistent disparities in STEMI system performance by race and ethnicity.

title: Impact of Complete Revascularization in the ISCHEMIA Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Non-randomised analysis within a randomised trial; 1,824 INV patients assessed, with weighted comparison of 2,296 INV and 2,498 CON patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Completeness of revascularisation was not randomised, so the comparison is open to confounding.
appraisal.one_line: Analysis of the effect of complete revascularisation on outcomes in the invasive arm of ISCHEMIA.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Anatomic complete revascularisation in all INV patients compared with CON patients was associated with a lower 4-year rate of cardiovascular death or MI (difference -3.5; 95% CI: -7.2% to 0.0%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on whether complete revascularisation explains benefit in chronic coronary disease.

title: Intravascular imaging during percutaneous coronary intervention: temporal trends and clinical outcomes in the USA.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective cohort study of 1 189 470 Medicare beneficiaries undergoing PCI, 2013 through 2019.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective claims analysis with residual confounding, although falsification endpoints were null.
appraisal.one_line: Medicare cohort of intravascular imaging use in PCI, with trends and one-year outcomes against angiographic guidance.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: IVI was used in 10.5% of PCIs. IVI use was associated with lower adjusted rates of 1 year mortality [adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 0.96, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.94-0.98], MI (aHR 0.97, 95% CI 0.95-0.99), repeat PCI (aHR 0.74, 95% CI 0.73-0.75) and MACE (aHR 0.85, 95% CI 0.84-0.86).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Documents low uptake of imaging-guided PCI in the US and supports randomised findings in unselected practice.

title: Arrhythmia and Death Following Percutaneous Revascularization in Ischemic Left Ventricular Dysfunction: Prespecified Analyses From the REVIVED-BCIS2 Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a randomised trial; 700 patients, 347 assigned to PCI plus OMT and 353 to OMT alone.
appraisal.main_limitation: Secondary analysis of a trial with open-label allocation; arrhythmia ascertainment depends on device availability.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified REVIVED-BCIS2 analysis of arrhythmia and death after PCI in ischaemic left ventricular dysfunction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause death or aborted sudden death occurred in 144 patients (41.6%) in the PCI group and 142 patients (40.2%) in the OMT group (hazard ratio, 1.03 [95% CI, 0.82-1.30]; P=0.80).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows PCI did not reduce fatal arrhythmia in ischaemic cardiomyopathy, informing revascularisation in this population.

title: Fractional Flow Reserve-Guided PCI or Coronary Bypass Surgery for 3-Vessel Coronary Artery Disease: 3-Year Follow-Up of the FAME 3 Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 1500 patients randomised to FFR-guided PCI or CABG, follow-up above 96%.
appraisal.main_limitation: The trial did not show noninferiority at 3 years on the composite, and MI findings are secondary.
appraisal.one_line: Three-year follow-up of FFR-guided PCI versus CABG for three-vessel disease in FAME 3.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There was no difference in the incidence of the composite of death, MI, or stroke after FFR-guided PCI compared with CABG (12.0% versus 9.2%; hazard ratio [HR], 1.3 [95% CI, 0.98-1.83]; P=0.07); MI occurred more frequently after PCI (7.0% versus 4.2%; HR, 1.7 [95% CI, 1.1-2.7]; P=0.02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the PCI versus CABG decision in three-vessel disease.

title: Biodegradable-Polymer or Durable-Polymer Stents in Patients at High Bleeding Risk: A Randomized, Open-Label Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label randomised trial; 1948 patients at high bleeding risk, 969 to biodegradable-polymer stents and 979 to durable-polymer stents.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label with a 1-year horizon and a composite primary outcome.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised noninferiority trial of biodegradable-polymer sirolimus-eluting stents versus durable-polymer zotarolimus-eluting stents in high bleeding risk patients with 1 month of DAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, the primary outcome was observed in 33 of 969 patients (3.6%) versus 32 of 979 patients (3.4%) (risk difference, 0.2 percentage points; upper boundary of the 1-sided 95% CI, 1.8; P<0.0001 for noninferiority for both tests).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports stent choice with short DAPT in high bleeding risk patients.

title: 2022 Joint ESC/EACTS review of the 2018 guideline recommendations on the revascularization of left main coronary artery disease in patients at low surgical risk and anatomy suitable for PCI or CABG.

appraisal.design_and_n: Task force review of updated aggregated data from four randomized trials comparing PCI with DES versus CABG in left main disease.
appraisal.main_limitation: The summary abstract gives no recommendation classes or levels.
appraisal.one_line: Joint ESC/EACTS review of 2018 recommendations on left main revascularisation in low-risk patients with suitable anatomy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Revises European positions on PCI versus CABG for left main disease, ending a period of withdrawn support.

title: Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided or Intravascular Ultrasound-Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: The OCTIVUS Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 1005 patients in the OCT group and 1003 in the IVUS group.
appraisal.main_limitation: Selected population with lower-than-expected event rates, as the authors note.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised noninferiority trial of OCT-guided versus IVUS-guided PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, primary end point events occurred in 25 of 1005 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 2.5%) in the OCT group and in 31 of 1003 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 3.1%) in the IVUS group (absolute difference, -0.6 percentage points; upper boundary of one-sided 97.5% CI, 0.97 percentage points; P<0.001 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows equivalence of the two intravascular imaging modalities for guidance.

title: Instantaneous wave free ratio vs. fractional flow reserve and 5-year mortality: iFR SWEDEHEART and DEFINE FLAIR.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of two trials; iFR and FFR-guided revascularization was performed in 2254 and 2257 patients respectively.
appraisal.main_limitation: Mortality was a secondary outcome in the original trials and the pooled comparison was not prespecified as primary.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled analysis of iFR SWEDEHEART and DEFINE FLAIR on five-year mortality with iFR versus FFR guidance.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Hazard ratio [95% confidence interval (CI)] estimates were 1.18 [1.04; 1.34] for MACE and 1.34 [1.08; 1.67] for all-cause mortality with iFR compared with FFR.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Raises a mortality signal bearing on the choice of physiological index.

title: OCT or Angiography Guidance for PCI in Complex Bifurcation Lesions.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 1201 patients, 600 to OCT-guided PCI and 601 to angiography-guided PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: The confidence interval approaches 1 and the primary composite includes softer components.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of OCT-guided versus angiography-guided PCI in complex bifurcation lesions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 2 years, a primary end-point event had occurred in 59 patients (10.1%) in the OCT-guided PCI group and in 83 patients (14.1%) in the angiography-guided PCI group (hazard ratio, 0.70; 95% confidence interval, 0.50 to 0.98; P = 0.035).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports OCT guidance in bifurcation PCI.

title: Complete or Culprit-Only PCI in Older Patients with Myocardial Infarction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 1445 patients, 720 to complete revascularization and 725 to culprit-only revascularization, median age 80 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Composite primary outcome and open-label allocation.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of complete versus culprit-only PCI in older patients with myocardial infarction and multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary-outcome event occurred in 113 patients (15.7%) in the complete-revascularization group and in 152 patients (21.0%) in the culprit-only group (hazard ratio, 0.73; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.57 to 0.93; P = 0.01).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Extends complete revascularisation evidence to older patients, a population underrepresented in earlier trials.

title: Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided versus Angiography-Guided PCI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial at 80 sites in 18 countries; 2487 patients, 1233 to OCT-guided PCI and 1254 to angiography-guided PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Powered for stent area rather than clinical events, with no apparent difference in target-vessel failure.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of OCT-guided versus angiography-guided PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Target-vessel failure within 2 years occurred in 88 patients in the OCT group and in 99 patients in the angiography group (Kaplan-Meier estimates, 7.4% and 8.2%, respectively; hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.67-1.19; P = 0.45).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows larger stent area with OCT guidance without a demonstrated clinical benefit, in contrast to other imaging trials.

title: Timing of Complete Revascularization with Multivessel PCI for Myocardial Infarction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 418 patients to immediate multivessel PCI and 422 to staged multivessel PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Composite endpoint driven by non-fatal MI and unplanned revascularisation.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of immediate versus staged multivessel PCI in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary end-point event occurred in 35 patients (8.5%) in the immediate group as compared with 68 patients (16.3%) in the staged group (risk ratio, 0.52; 95% confidence interval, 0.38 to 0.72).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs timing of complete revascularisation in STEMI alongside BIOVASC.

title: Bivalirudin Versus Heparin During PCI in NSTEMI: Individual Patient Data Meta-Analysis of Large Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data meta-analysis; 12 155 patients randomised, 6040 to bivalirudin and 6115 to heparin.
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooled trials differ in heparin comparator use, including planned glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis of bivalirudin versus heparin during PCI for NSTEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Thirty-day mortality was 1.2% versus 1.1% (adjusted odds ratio, 1.24 [95% CI, 0.86-1.79]; P=0.25), and bivalirudin reduced serious bleeding (3.3% versus 5.5%; adjusted odds ratio, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.48-0.72).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs choice of procedural anticoagulant in NSTEMI.

title: Coronary Computed Tomographic Angiography With Fractional Flow Reserve in Patients With Type 2 Myocardial Infarction.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective single-study enrolment of 50 participants meeting Fourth Universal Definition criteria for type 2 MI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample without outcome data; no evidence on whether revascularisation or other therapy changes outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Prospective coronary CTA with FFRCT in adjudicated type 2 MI to describe the prevalence and haemodynamic significance of CAD.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Coronary CTA revealed coronary plaque in 46 participants (92%). A moderate or greater stenosis (≥50%) was identified in 42% of participants, and obstructive disease was present in 26%. A hemodynamically significant focal stenosis identified by FFRCT was present in 13 participants (26%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Describes coronary substrate in type 2 MI, a population lacking trials to inform invasive evaluation.

title: Invasive Endotyping in Patients With Angina and No Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 231 patients randomised after 250 underwent invasive endotyping.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trial in which the primary patient-reported outcome did not differ.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of invasive coronary endotyping in angina with no obstructive coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Intervention patients were more likely to be diagnosed with a coronary vasomotor disorder (odds ratio, 4.05 [95% CI, 2.32-7.24]; P<0.001), but the Seattle Angina Questionnaire summary score did not differ between groups (global P=0.36).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests whether physiology-guided diagnosis improves outcomes in INOCA.

title: Safety and Efficacy of Ticagrelor Monotherapy in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: An Individual Patient Data Meta-Analysis of TWILIGHT and TICO Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data meta-analysis of the TWILIGHT and TICO trials, n=7529.
appraisal.main_limitation: Only two trials pooled, and the analysis is limited to patients completing 3 months of DAPT.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis of ticagrelor monotherapy versus ticagrelor plus aspirin after PCI in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Between 3 and 12 months, ticagrelor monotherapy reduced BARC 3 or 5 bleeding (0.8% versus 2.1%; hazard ratio, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.24-0.56]; P<0.001) with all-cause death, myocardial infarction, or stroke not significantly different (2.4% versus 2.7%; hazard ratio, 0.91 [95% CI, 0.68-1.21]; P=0.515).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports aspirin-free strategies after ACS PCI.

title: Stopping Aspirin Within 1 Month After Stenting for Ticagrelor Monotherapy in Acute Coronary Syndrome: The T-PASS Randomized Noninferiority Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 2850 patients randomised, 2823 (99.0%) completed the trial.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trial in an East Asian population; the superiority finding needs replication.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised noninferiority trial of ticagrelor monotherapy after under 1 month of DAPT versus 12-month ticagrelor-based DAPT in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point occurred in 40 patients (2.8%) in the ticagrelor monotherapy group and in 73 patients (5.2%) in the 12-month DAPT group (hazard ratio, 0.54 [95% CI, 0.37-0.80]; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P=0.002 for superiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports very short DAPT with potent P2Y12 monotherapy after ACS PCI.

title: Clopidogrel vs Aspirin Monotherapy Beyond 1 Year After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 3,005 study patients, with 2,934 (97.6%) completing the 5-year follow-up.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design in a Korean population with the primary superiority comparison not met.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year randomised comparison of clopidogrel and aspirin monotherapy beyond one year after PCI in HOST-EXAM.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The clopidogrel group compared with the aspirin group was noninferior but not superior for the primary endpoint (11.75% and 13.57%, respectively; HR: 0.85; 95% CI: 0.70-1.05; Pnoninferiority < 0.001; Psuperiority = 0.13).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides long-term randomised evidence for clopidogrel as chronic monotherapy after PCI.

title: Long-term outcomes with biodegradable polymer sirolimus-eluting stents versus durable polymer everolimus-eluting stents in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: 5-year follow-up of the BIOSTEMI randomised superiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised superiority trial; 1300 patients with STEMI, 649 to biodegradable-polymer stents and 651 to durable-polymer stents.
appraisal.main_limitation: The difference was driven by ischaemia-driven target lesion revascularisation rather than harder endpoints.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year follow-up of BIOSTEMI comparing biodegradable-polymer sirolimus-eluting stents with durable-polymer everolimus-eluting stents in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 5 years, target lesion failure occurred in 50 (8%) patients treated with biodegradable polymer sirolimus-eluting stents and in 72 (11%) patients treated with durable polymer everolimus-eluting stents (RR 0·70, 95% Bayesian credible interval 0·51-0·95).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Suggests a device-specific benefit in primary PCI at long-term follow-up.

title: Intravascular imaging guided versus coronary angiography guided percutaneous coronary intervention: systematic review and meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of 20 randomized controlled trials (n=11 698).
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level data with heterogeneity in imaging modality and lesion types.
appraisal.one_line: Systematic review and meta-analysis of intravascular imaging-guided versus angiography-guided PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Intravascular imaging guided PCI was associated with a reduced risk of cardiac death (rate ratio 0.53, 95% confidence interval 0.39 to 0.72) and myocardial infarction (0.81, 0.68 to 0.97), but not all cause death (0.81, 0.64 to 1.02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Consolidates randomised evidence for imaging guidance across PCI.

title: Can Machine Learning Aid the Selection of Percutaneous vs Surgical Revascularization?
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Development in the SYNTAX trial (n = 1,800) with external validation in the CREDO-Kyoto registry (n = 7,362).
appraisal.main_limitation: Heterogeneity of treatment benefit derived from one trial and an observational registry rather than tested prospectively.
appraisal.one_line: Machine learning models to predict 5-year death and individual benefit of CABG versus PCI in left main or three-vessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The hybrid gradient boosting model performed best for predicting 5-year all-cause death with C-indexes of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.75-0.81) in cross-validation and 0.77 (95% CI: 0.76-0.79) in external validation.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Moves towards individualised heart team decisions beyond the SYNTAX score.

title: An Aspirin-Free Versus Dual Antiplatelet Strategy for Coronary Stenting: STOPDAPT-3 Randomized Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 5966 patients in the full analysis set (no-aspirin group, 2984 patients; DAPT group, 2982 patients).
appraisal.main_limitation: No bleeding reduction was shown, and there was an excess of unplanned coronary revascularisation.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of an aspirin-free versus dual antiplatelet strategy after coronary stenting (STOPDAPT-3).
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 month, the no-aspirin group was not superior to the DAPT group for the coprimary bleeding end point (4.47% and 4.71%; hazard ratio, 0.95 [95% CI, 0.75-1.20]) and was noninferior for the coprimary cardiovascular end point (4.12% and 3.69%; hazard ratio, 1.12 [95% CI, 0.87-1.45]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests omission of aspirin from the start of stenting, informing the limits of antiplatelet de-escalation.

title: Comparison of Intravascular Imaging, Functional, or Angiographically Guided Coronary Intervention.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis of 32 randomized controlled trials including 22,684 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Network comparison with indirect estimates and heterogeneous trials.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis comparing intravascular imaging, functional and angiographic guidance of PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with angiography-guided PCI, intravascular imaging-guided PCI was associated with reduced risk of MACE (relative risk [RR]: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.62-0.82) and cardiovascular death (RR: 0.56; 95% CI: 0.42-0.75).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Ranks guidance strategies and supports imaging guidance.

title: A Placebo-Controlled Trial of Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Stable Angina.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Placebo-controlled randomised trial; 301 patients, 151 to PCI and 150 to placebo.
appraisal.main_limitation: Symptom endpoint at 12 weeks only, in patients on little or no antianginal medication.
appraisal.one_line: Placebo-controlled trial of PCI for stable angina with objective ischaemia found a lower angina symptom score with PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At the 12-week follow-up, the mean angina symptom score was 2.9 in the PCI group and 5.6 in the placebo group (odds ratio, 2.21; 95% confidence interval, 1.41 to 3.47; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides blinded evidence of symptom benefit from PCI in stable angina with ischaemia.

title: Coronary Angiography, Intravascular Ultrasound, and Optical Coherence Tomography for Guiding of Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: 24 randomized trials (15 489 patients) in the network meta-analyses.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level data with limited power for hard outcomes and a stent thrombosis finding present only in the frequentist analysis.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis of 24 randomised trials finds intravascular imaging-guided PCI associated with less ischaemia-driven target lesion revascularisation than angiography, most clearly for IVUS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: IVUS was associated with reduced target lesion revascularization compared with ICA (odds ratio [OR], 0.69 [95% CI, 0.54-0.87]), whereas no significant differences were observed between OCT and ICA (OR, 0.83 [95% CI, 0.63-1.09]) and OCT and IVUS (OR, 1.21 [95% CI, 0.88-1.66]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the choice between IVUS and OCT guidance, where randomised comparisons have been mixed.

title: Intravascular imaging-guided coronary drug-eluting stent implantation: an updated network meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: 22 trials in which 15 964 patients were randomised, weighted mean follow-up 24·7 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Study-level pooling of trials with varying endpoints and follow-up, and the analysis was funded by a device manufacturer.
appraisal.one_line: Updated network meta-analysis of 22 randomised trials reports that intravascular imaging guidance reduced target lesion failure, cardiac death and all-cause death compared with angiography.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with angiography-guided PCI, intravascular imaging-guided PCI resulted in a decreased risk of target lesion failure (RR 0·71 [95% CI 0·63-0·80]; p<0·0001). Intravascular imaging guidance also reduced the risks of all-cause death (RR 0·75 [95% CI 0·60-0·93]; p=0·0091).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Suggests a mortality signal with imaging guidance that individual trials could not show, relevant to guideline recommendations.

title: Postprocedural Anticoagulation After Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: 2989 patients with STEMI randomised at 53 centres in China to low-dose postprocedural anticoagulation or placebo.
appraisal.main_limitation: Low event rate and 30-day follow-up in a Chinese population, with three different anticoagulant regimens chosen by centre.
appraisal.one_line: The RIGHT trial found that routine postprocedural anticoagulation after primary PCI did not reduce 30-day ischaemic events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary efficacy end point occurred in 37 patients (2.5%) in both the PPA and placebo groups (hazard ratio, 1.00 [95% CI, 0.63 to 1.57]). The incidence of Bleeding Academic Research Consortium 3 to 5 bleeding did not differ between the PPA and placebo groups (8 [0.5%] vs 11 [0.7%] patients; hazard ratio, 0.74 [95% CI, 0.30 to 1.83]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a common unproven practice and supports omitting routine anticoagulation after primary PCI.
