title: Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon vs Uncoated Balloon for Coronary In-Stent Restenosis: The AGENT IDE Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: 600 patients with in-stent restenosis at 40 US centres, randomised 2:1 to paclitaxel-coated (n = 406) or uncoated (n = 194) balloon.
appraisal.main_limitation: Comparator was an uncoated balloon rather than a drug-eluting stent, with one-year follow-up and a numerically higher cardiac death rate with the coated balloon.
appraisal.one_line: AGENT IDE showed a paclitaxel-coated balloon reduced one-year target lesion failure compared with an uncoated balloon in coronary in-stent restenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary end point at 1 year occurred in 17.9% in the paclitaxel-coated balloon group vs 28.6% in the uncoated balloon group, meeting the criteria for superiority (hazard ratio [HR], 0.59 [95% CI, 0.42-0.84]; 2-sided P = .003).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First US randomised evidence for a drug-coated balloon in the coronary circulation, supporting its approval for in-stent restenosis.

title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Versus Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Patients With Left Main Disease With and Without Diabetes: Findings From a Pooled Analysis of 4 Randomized Clinical Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data from 4 trials; 4393 patients, of whom 1104 (25.1%) had diabetes.
appraisal.main_limitation: Diabetes subgroups were not randomised strata, and the population largely had low to intermediate SYNTAX scores.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled individual patient data from four left main trials show PCI and CABG had similar mortality regardless of diabetes, with larger late absolute excesses of spontaneous MI and repeat revascularisation after PCI in diabetes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Rates of all-cause mortality did not differ after PCI versus CABG in those with (84/563 [15.3%] versus 74/541 [14.1%]; hazard ratio, 1.11 [95% CI, 0.82-1.52]) or without (155/1634 [9.7%] versus 142/1655 [8.9%]; hazard ratio, 1.08 [95% CI, 0.86-1.36; PintHR=0.87) diabetes.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs heart team decisions in left main disease with diabetes, a common and contested group.

title: Beta-Blockers after Myocardial Infarction and Preserved Ejection Fraction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: 5020 patients with acute myocardial infarction and LVEF of at least 50% randomised in an open-label trial at 45 centres, median follow-up 3.5 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, with 95.4% of patients from Sweden and a lower than expected event rate.
appraisal.one_line: REDUCE-AMI found no lower risk of death or new myocardial infarction with long-term beta-blockade after MI with preserved ejection fraction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary end-point event occurred in 199 of 2508 patients (7.9%) in the beta-blocker group and in 208 of 2512 patients (8.3%) in the no-beta-blocker group (hazard ratio, 0.96; 95% confidence interval, 0.79 to 1.16; P = 0.64).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges routine beta-blocker use after MI in a very common population and informs guideline recommendations.

title: FFR-Guided Complete or Culprit-Only PCI in Patients with Myocardial Infarction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: 1542 patients randomised (764 FFR-guided complete revascularization, 778 culprit-lesion-only PCI) in a registry-based trial, median follow-up 4.8 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: The trial stopped short of its planned enrolment and its confidence interval does not exclude a modest effect in either direction.
appraisal.one_line: FULL REVASC found no lower risk of death, MI or unplanned revascularisation with FFR-guided complete revascularisation versus culprit-only PCI in multivessel MI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary-outcome event had occurred in 145 patients (19.0%) in the complete-revascularization group and in 159 patients (20.4%) in the culprit-lesion-only group (hazard ratio, 0.93; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 1.17; P = 0.53).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds neutral evidence on physiology-guided complete revascularisation to a contested area where guidelines favour complete revascularisation.

title: Invasive vs. conservative management of older patients with non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome: individual patient data meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Six eligible studies including 1479 participants.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small pooled sample from heterogeneous trials, and the primary composite had wide confidence intervals.
appraisal.one_line: IPD meta-analysis of six trials in patients over 70 with NSTE-ACS found no clear reduction in death or MI at 1 year with routine invasive management, but lower MI and urgent revascularisation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 181 of 736 (24.5%) participants in the invasive management group compared with 215 of 743 (28.9%) participants in the conservative management group with a hazard ratio (HR) from random-effects model of 0.87 (95% CI 0.63-1.22; P = .43). The hazard for MI at 1 year was significantly lower in the invasive group compared with the conservative group (HR from random-effects model 0.62, 95% CI 0.44-0.87; P = .006).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses an older population with uncertain invasive benefit, where guideline recommendations are weak.

title: Ticagrelor alone versus ticagrelor plus aspirin from month 1 to month 12 after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with acute coronary syndromes (ULTIMATE-DAPT): a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: 3400 patients randomly assigned (1700 to ticagrelor plus aspirin and 1700 to ticagrelor plus placebo) after an event-free first month of dual antiplatelet therapy.
appraisal.main_limitation: Randomisation occurred only after one event-free month of dual therapy, and the sample was drawn from a single prior trial population.
appraisal.one_line: A double-blind trial found ticagrelor alone from month 1 to month 12 after PCI for ACS caused less clinically relevant bleeding than ticagrelor plus aspirin, with similar MACCE.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Between month 1 and month 12 after percutaneous coronary intervention, clinically relevant bleeding occurred in 35 patients (2·1%) in the ticagrelor plus placebo group and in 78 patients (4·6%) in the ticagrelor plus aspirin group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·45 [95% CI 0·30 to 0·66]; p<0·0001). MACCE occurred in 61 patients (3·6%) in the ticagrelor plus placebo group and in 63 patients (3·7%) in the ticagrelor plus aspirin group (absolute difference -0·1% [95% CI -1·4% to 1·2%]; HR 0·98 [95% CI 0·69 to 1·39]; pnon-inferiority<0·0001, psuperiority=0·89).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Strong placebo-controlled support for early aspirin withdrawal after ACS PCI, relevant to guideline DAPT recommendations.

title: Effectiveness of Clopidogrel vs Alternative P2Y12 Inhibitors Based on the ABCD-GENE Score.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Genotyped PCI cohort of 4,335 patients (3,200 with scores <10 and 1,135 with scores ≥10).
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational with residual confounding and small genotype-stratified subgroups.
appraisal.one_line: Observational analysis of clopidogrel versus prasugrel or ticagrelor after PCI stratified by ABCD-GENE score and CYP2C19 genotype.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Among patients with scores <10, MAE was not different with alternative therapy vs clopidogrel (weighted HR: 0.89; 95% CI: 0.65-1.22; P = 0.475). Among CYP2C19 LOF allele carriers with scores ≥10, MAE risk appeared lower with alternative therapy (weighted HR: 0.48; 95% CI: 0.29-0.80; P = 0.004).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs genotype-guided P2Y12 inhibitor selection, where randomised results are mixed.

title: Coronary sinus reducer for the treatment of refractory angina (ORBITA-COSMIC): a randomised, placebo-controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: 51 patients randomly assigned (CSR n=25, placebo n=26) in a blinded Bayesian trial at six UK hospitals.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample, six-month follow-up and symptom endpoints with two embolisation events in the device group.
appraisal.one_line: ORBITA-COSMIC found the coronary sinus reducer improved angina episodes but not myocardial blood flow compared with placebo.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Myocardial blood flow in ischaemic segments did not improve with CSR compared with placebo (difference 0·06 mL/min per g [95% CrI -0·09 to 0·20]; Pr(Benefit)=78·8%). The number of daily angina episodes was reduced with CSR compared with placebo (OR 1·40 [95% CrI 1·08 to 1·83]; Pr(Benefit)=99·4%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First blinded sham-controlled evidence for the coronary sinus reducer, relevant to refractory angina options.

title: Intravascular ultrasound-guided versus angiography-guided percutaneous coronary intervention in acute coronary syndromes (IVUS-ACS): a two-stage, multicentre, randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: 3505 patients with ACS randomised to IVUS-guided (n=1753) or angiography-guided PCI (n=1752).
appraisal.main_limitation: Benefit was driven by target vessel events rather than death or stent thrombosis, and staff in the catheterisation laboratory were not masked.
appraisal.one_line: IVUS-ACS found IVUS-guided PCI reduced one-year target vessel failure compared with angiography guidance in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 70 patients in the intravascular ultrasound group and 128 patients in the angiography group (Kaplan-Meier rate 4·0% vs 7·3%; hazard ratio 0·55 [95% CI 0·41-0·74]; p=0·0001), driven by reductions in target vessel myocardial infarction or target vessel revascularisation.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Extends imaging-guided PCI evidence to an ACS population.

title: Preventive percutaneous coronary intervention versus optimal medical therapy alone for the treatment of vulnerable atherosclerotic coronary plaques (PREVENT): a multicentre, open-label, randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: 1606 patients randomised to PCI (n=803) or optimal medical therapy alone (n=803), open-label, 2-year primary outcome.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design with a composite driven largely by softer components such as revascularisation and angina hospitalisation, and low event counts for death and MI.
appraisal.one_line: PREVENT found preventive PCI of non-flow-limiting vulnerable plaques reduced a two-year composite of cardiac death, target-vessel MI, revascularisation or unstable angina hospitalisation compared with medical therapy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 2 years, the primary outcome occurred in three (0·4%) patients in the percutaneous coronary intervention group and in 27 (3·4%) patients in the medical therapy group (absolute difference -3·0 percentage points [95% CI -4·4 to -1·8]; p=0·0003).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges the physiology-based paradigm for PCI and raises the possibility of treating imaging-defined vulnerable plaques.

title: Periprocedural myocardial infarction after percutaneous coronary intervention and long-term mortality: a meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: 19 studies and 109 568 patients included.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational pooled data using adjusted estimates with considerable heterogeneity for the SCAI definition.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of 19 studies reports that periprocedural MI under three definitions was associated with higher all-cause mortality after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All PMI definitions were independently associated with all-cause mortality [UDMI: hazard ratio (HR) 1.61, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.32-1.97; I2 34%; ARC-2: HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.40-3.08, I2 0%; SCAI: HR 3.24, 95% CI 2.36-4.44, I2 78%].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs which periprocedural MI definition should anchor trial endpoints and clinical decisions.

title: Ticagrelor monotherapy for acute coronary syndrome: an individual patient data meta-analysis of TICO and T-PASS trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data from two randomized clinical trials including 5906 ACS patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Only two trials contribute to the primary IPD analysis, both in East Asian populations, with open-label designs.
appraisal.one_line: IPD meta-analysis of two trials in ACS finds ticagrelor monotherapy after short DAPT associated with less BARC 3 or 5 bleeding without more ischaemic events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary ischaemic endpoint did not differ between the ticagrelor monotherapy and ticagrelor-based DAPT groups [1.9% vs. 2.5%; adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 0.79; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.56-1.13; P = .194]. The incidence of the primary bleeding endpoint was lower in the ticagrelor monotherapy group (2.4% vs. 4.5%; adjusted HR 0.54; 95% CI 0.40-0.72; P < .001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds to the evidence for P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy in ACS, a decision made frequently in practice.

title: N-of-1 Trial of Angina Verification Before Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Fifty-one patients undergoing single-vessel PCI for stable symptoms in a multicentre n-of-1 study.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample, a research-only procedure and no outcome beyond symptoms.
appraisal.one_line: ORBITA-STAR suggests a placebo-controlled balloon occlusion symptom similarity score predicts symptom relief from PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A patient with an upper quartile similarity score of 5.25 was significantly more likely to have lower angina frequency at follow-up (OR: 8.01; 95% credible interval: 2.39-15.86) than a patient with a lower quartile similarity score of 0.875 (OR: 1.31; 95% credible interval: 0.71-1.99), Pr(difference) >99.9%.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Proposes a way to select stable angina patients likely to benefit from PCI.

title: Non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndromes with previous coronary artery bypass grafting: a meta-analysis of invasive vs. conservative management.

appraisal.design_and_n: Summary data from 11 RCTs comprising 897 patients with previous CABG (477 routine invasive, 420 conservative/selective invasive).
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup data from trials not designed for this population, with small numbers and wide confidence intervals.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of 11 trials finds no benefit of a routine invasive strategy in NSTE-ACS patients with prior CABG, a group under-represented in trials.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A routine invasive strategy did not reduce all-cause mortality (RR 1.12, 95% CI 0.97-1.29), cardiac mortality (RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.70-1.58), myocardial infarction (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.65-1.23), or cardiac-related hospitalization (RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.78-1.40).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses an excluded population in which the guideline recommendation for an invasive strategy is uncertain.

title: Ventricular septal defect complicating acute myocardial infarction: diagnosis and management. A Clinical Consensus Statement of the Association for Acute CardioVascular Care (ACVC) of the ESC, the European Association of Percutaneous Cardiovascular Interventions (EAPCI) of the ESC and the ESC Working Group on Cardiovascular Surgery.

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus statement and state-of-the-art review; no sample size applicable.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus is built on observational evidence because no randomised trials are available.
appraisal.one_line: Clinical consensus statement on post-MI ventricular septal defect, a rare complication with very high mortality and no randomised evidence.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets out management options and research priorities for a high-mortality complication with no trial evidence.

title: 10-Year Mortality After ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Compared to the General Population.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort of 18,818 first-time STEMI patients matched to 94,090 individuals from the general population.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational, single-region registry.
appraisal.one_line: Danish registry comparison of long-term mortality after primary PCI for STEMI with an age- and sex-matched general population.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: STEMI was associated with a 5.9% excess mortality from 0 to 30 days (6.0% vs 0.2%; HR: 36.44; 95% CI: 30.86-43.04). In 90-day STEMI survivors, the absolute excess mortality was only 2.1 percentage points at 10-year follow-up (26.5% vs 24.5%; HR: 1.04; 95% CI: 1.01-1.08).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Locates remaining excess mortality in the first 90 days, directing research towards early care.

title: Timing of P2Y12 Inhibitor Administration in Patients With STEMI Undergoing Primary PCI.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicentre registry, 1,624 patients (1,033 pretreated; 591 treated in the cath lab).
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational and prone to confounding by indication, despite doubly robust weighting.
appraisal.one_line: Registry analysis of P2Y12 inhibitor pretreatment in STEMI patients transferred for primary PCI within a regional network.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Pretreatment with P2Y12 inhibitors predicted lower risk of MACE (adjusted HR: 0.53; 95% CI: 0.37-0.76), without increasing bleeding risk (adjusted HR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.36-1.05), with a net clinical benefit adjusted HR of 0.47 (95% CI: 0.26-0.86).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses P2Y12 timing in STEMI where randomised data are limited and guidelines differ.

title: CYP2C19 Genetic Testing for Oral P2Y12 Inhibitor Therapy: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Scientific statement; no sample size applicable.
appraisal.main_limitation: Statement based on trials and meta-analyses, with implementation requirements such as rapid results and health record integration unresolved.
appraisal.one_line: AHA scientific statement concludes that evidence supports CYP2C19 genetic testing before oral P2Y12 inhibitor prescribing in ACS or PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on P2Y12 inhibitor selection and de-escalation strategies in ACS and PCI.

title: Percutaneous Coronary Revascularization Strategies After Myocardial Infarction: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Twenty-four eligible trials randomized 16,371 patients (weighted mean follow-up: 26.4 months).
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level pooling in which the mortality effect is borderline and not significant in STEMI alone, and timing comparisons are indirect.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis of randomised trials reports that complete revascularisation after MI with multivessel disease reduced all-cause mortality compared with culprit-only treatment.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with culprit revascularization, complete revascularization reduced all-cause mortality in patients with any MI (RR: 0.85; 95% CI: 0.74-0.99; P = 0.04). In patients presenting with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, the point estimate for all-cause mortality with complete revascularization was RR: 0.91 (95% CI: 0.78-1.05; P = 0.18).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs timing and guidance of complete revascularisation, a frequently made decision with guideline implications.

title: Bleeding risk prediction after acute myocardial infarction-integrating cancer data: the updated PRECISE-DAPT cancer score.

appraisal.design_and_n: Nationally linked cohort of 216 709 STEMI patients (4569 with cancer) from MINAP and Hospital Episode Statistics.
appraisal.main_limitation: Model development in a single national dataset without external validation reported in the abstract.
appraisal.one_line: Updated PRECISE-DAPT score that adds cancer as a predictor of one-year major bleeding after STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The original score showed moderate accuracy (C-statistic .60), and the modified score showed modestly higher discrimination (C-statistics .64; hazard ratio 1.03, 95% confidence interval 1.03-1.04). According to the modified score, 94.0% of cancer patients were HBR.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Cancer is a common high-bleeding-risk feature; a better score could guide DAPT duration.

title: Antithrombotic Strategies in Atrial Fibrillation After ACS and/or PCI: A 4-Way Comparison From AUGUSTUS.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: 4,614 patients with AF and recent ACS and/or PCI, in a 2 x 2 factorial randomised trial.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc four-way comparison of a trial designed as two factorial comparisons, with an open-label VKA comparison and no estimate for the pairwise differences in the abstract.
appraisal.one_line: A four-way AUGUSTUS analysis finds apixaban without aspirin on top of a P2Y12 inhibitor had the lowest rate of death, bleeding or cardiovascular hospitalisation in AF after ACS or PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 21.9% of patients randomized to apixaban plus placebo, 27.3% randomized to apixaban plus aspirin, 28.0% randomized to VKA plus placebo, and 33.3% randomized to VKA plus aspirin.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports a P2Y12 inhibitor plus anticoagulant regimen without aspirin, a common decision in AF patients undergoing PCI.

title: Aspirin vs. clopidogrel monotherapy after percutaneous coronary intervention: 1-year follow-up of the STOPDAPT-3 trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: 5833 patients in the 30-day landmark analysis (aspirin group: N = 2920 and clopidogrel group: N = 2913).
appraisal.main_limitation: Landmark secondary analysis that breaks randomisation, since groups were defined by the initial dual therapy strategy.
appraisal.one_line: A STOPDAPT-3 secondary analysis found similar cardiovascular and bleeding outcomes with aspirin and clopidogrel monotherapy beyond 1 month after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The incidence rates beyond 30 days and up to 1 year were similar between the aspirin and clopidogrel groups for both cardiovascular endpoint [4.5 and 4.5 per 100 person-year, hazard ratio 1.00 (95% confidence interval .77-1.30), P = .97], and bleeding endpoint [2.0 and 1.9, hazard ratio 1.02 (95% confidence interval .69-1.52), P = .92].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Offers the first trial-based comparison of aspirin and P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy after short DAPT, relevant to choice of single antiplatelet agent.

title: PCI in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Implantation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: 455 patients randomised (227 PCI, 228 conservative treatment), median follow-up 2 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trial of modest size with a confidence interval near unity and the composite driven partly by revascularisation.
appraisal.one_line: NOTION-3 found PCI of significant coronary stenoses in patients undergoing TAVI reduced a composite of death, MI or urgent revascularisation, at the cost of more bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A major adverse cardiac event (primary end point) had occurred in 60 patients (26%) in the PCI group and in 81 (36%) in the conservative-treatment group (hazard ratio, 0.71; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.51 to 0.99; P = 0.04). A bleeding event occurred in 64 patients (28%) in the PCI group and in 45 (20%) in the conservative-treatment group (hazard ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.03 to 2.22).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives the first randomised evidence on managing coronary disease in TAVI candidates, a common clinical decision.

title: Complete vs Culprit-Only Revascularization in Older Patients With Myocardial Infarction With or Without ST-Segment Elevation.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: 1,445 older patients with MI randomised in FIRE; STEMI (n = 256 culprit-only vs n = 253 complete) and NSTEMI (n = 469 culprit-only vs n = 467 complete).
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis within a trial, with limited power in the STEMI stratum.
appraisal.one_line: A FIRE trial analysis finds the benefit of physiology-guided complete revascularisation in older patients was consistent across STEMI and NSTEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 54 (21.1%) STEMI patients randomized to culprit-only vs 41 (16.2%) STEMI patients of the complete group (HR: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.50-1.13) and in 98 (20.9%) NSTEMI patients randomized to culprit-only vs 72 (15.4%) NSTEMI patients of the complete group (HR: 0.71; 95% CI: 0.53-0.97), with negative interaction testing (P for interaction, 0.846).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports complete revascularisation in older patients with NSTEMI, where trial evidence has been thinner.

title: Aspirin Monotherapy vs No Antiplatelet Therapy in Stable Patients With Coronary Stents Undergoing Low-to-Intermediate Risk Noncardiac Surgery.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: 1,010 patients randomised; 926 in the modified intention-to-treat population (462 aspirin, 464 no antiplatelet).
appraisal.main_limitation: Lower than expected event rate, so the trial is underpowered to show equivalence for ischaemic events.
appraisal.one_line: ASSURE-DES found no significant difference in ischaemic or major bleeding outcomes between perioperative aspirin and no antiplatelet therapy in patients with a remote DES undergoing noncardiac surgery.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary composite outcome occurred in 3 patients (0.6%) in the aspirin monotherapy group and 4 patients (0.9%) in the no antiplatelet group (difference, -0.2 percentage points; 95% CI: -1.3 to 0.9; P > 0.99).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges guideline advice to continue aspirin in stable stented patients undergoing low-to-intermediate risk surgery.

title: Complete Versus Culprit-Only Revascularization in Older Patients With ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: An Individual Patient Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Data from 7 randomized clinical trials encompassing 1733 patients (917 randomized to culprit-only and 816 to complete revascularization).
appraisal.main_limitation: Modest pooled sample with variable follow-up, and the overall primary endpoint was not significantly reduced at longest follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: IPD meta-analysis of seven trials in patients aged 75 or over with STEMI finds complete revascularisation reduced the primary endpoint up to 4 years but not at longest follow-up.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Complete revascularization reduced the primary end point up to 4 years (hazard ratio, 0.78 [95% CI, 0.63-0.96]) but not at the longest available follow-up (hazard ratio, 0.83 [95% CI, 0.69-1.01]). Complete revascularization significantly reduced the occurrence of cardiovascular death or myocardial infarction at the longest available follow-up (hazard ratio, 0.76 [95% CI, 0.58-0.99]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports complete revascularisation in older STEMI patients beyond the one-year follow-up of single trials.

title: Fasting vs. no fasting prior to catheterization laboratory procedures: the SCOFF trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: 716 patients randomised 1:1 (358 per group) in Australia, open-label with blinded endpoint assessment.
appraisal.main_limitation: Composite is dominated by hypotension and glucose abnormalities rather than aspiration, which was rare, and the trial is Australian only.
appraisal.one_line: SCOFF found that no fasting was noninferior and superior to fasting for a composite of aspiration pneumonia, hypotension and glycaemic events before sedated catheterisation procedures.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary composite outcome occurred in 19.1% of patients in the fasting arm and 12.0% of patients in the no-fasting arm. The estimate of the mean posterior difference in proportions with credibility interval (CI) in the primary composite outcome was -5.2% (95% CI -9.6 to -.9), favouring no fasting.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges a routine pre-procedural fasting practice that is guideline-recommended without trial support.

title: Invasive Treatment Strategy for Older Patients with Myocardial Infarction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: 1518 patients aged 75 years or older randomised (753 invasive, 765 conservative) at 48 UK sites; 32% were frail.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trial with crossover and a broad population including frail patients, which may dilute subgroup signals.
appraisal.one_line: SENIOR-RITA found an invasive strategy did not significantly lower cardiovascular death or nonfatal MI compared with conservative care in older adults with NSTEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary-outcome event occurred in 193 patients (25.6%) in the invasive-strategy group and 201 patients (26.3%) in the conservative-strategy group (hazard ratio, 0.94; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.77 to 1.14; P = 0.53) over a median follow-up of 4.1 years.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Defines the evidence for routine invasive management in older and frail NSTEMI patients, directly affecting guideline recommendations.

title: De-escalation to ticagrelor monotherapy versus 12 months of dual antiplatelet therapy in patients with and without acute coronary syndromes: a systematic review and individual patient-level meta-analysis of randomised trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Six randomised trials; 23 256 patients in the per-protocol population and 24 407 patients in the intention-to-treat population.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trials were mostly open-label, excluded patients needing oral anticoagulation, and the mortality and sex findings come from interaction tests and are hypothesis-generating.
appraisal.one_line: Ticagrelor monotherapy after short DAPT was noninferior for MACCE and reduced BARC 3 or 5 bleeding and all-cause death in an IPD meta-analysis of six randomised trials.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Among 23 256 patients in the per-protocol population, MACCE occurred in 297 (Kaplan-Meier estimate 2·8%) with ticagrelor monotherapy and 332 (Kaplan-Meier estimate 3·2%) with DAPT (HR 0·91 [95% CI 0·78-1·07]; p=0·0039 for non-inferiority; τ2<0·0001). Among 24 407 patients in the intention-to-treat population, the risks of BARC 3 or 5 bleeding (Kaplan-Meier estimate 0·9% vs 2·1%; HR 0·43 [95% CI 0·34-0·54]; p<0·0001 for superiority; τ2=0·079) and all-cause death (Kaplan-Meier estimate 0·9% vs 1·2%; 0·76 [0·59-0·98]; p=0·034 for superiority; τ2<0·0001) were lower with ticagrelor monotherapy.
appraisal.why_it_matters: High-quality pooled evidence for DAPT de-escalation to a potent P2Y12 inhibitor, directly relevant to ESC and ACC/AHA duration recommendations.

title: Drug-coated balloon angioplasty with rescue stenting versus intended stenting for the treatment of patients with de novo coronary artery lesions (REC-CAGEFREE I): an open-label, randomised, non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: 2272 patients randomly assigned to the DCB group (1133) or the DES group (1139) at 43 sites in China.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trial in a Chinese population using a paclitaxel-coated balloon, so findings may not extend to other balloons or populations.
appraisal.one_line: REC-CAGEFREE I found drug-coated balloon angioplasty with rescue stenting did not meet noninferiority to intended drug-eluting stent implantation for de novo non-complex lesions at 24 months.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 24 months, the DoCE occurred in 72 (6·4%) of 1133 patients in the DCB group and 38 (3·4%) of 1139 in the DES group, with a risk difference of 3·04% in the cumulative event rate (upper boundary of the one-sided 95% CI 4·52; pnon-inferiority=0·65; two-sided 95% CI 1·27-4·81; p=0·0008); the criterion for non-inferiority was not met.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets limits on the use of drug-coated balloons in de novo coronary lesions, a growing practice.

title: Optical coherence tomography-guided versus angiography-guided percutaneous coronary intervention for patients with complex lesions (OCCUPI): an investigator-initiated, multicentre, randomised, open-label, superiority trial in South Korea.

appraisal.design_and_n: 1604 patients requiring PCI for complex lesions randomly assigned to OCT-guided (n=803) or angiography-guided PCI (n=801) at 20 hospitals in South Korea.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trial in one country with a one-year horizon, and the lower confidence limit approaches no effect.
appraisal.one_line: OCCUPI found OCT-guided PCI reduced one-year major adverse cardiac events compared with angiography guidance in complex lesions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 37 (5%) of 803 patients in the OCT-guided PCI group and 59 (7%) of 801 patients in the angiography-guided PCI group (absolute difference -2·8% [95% CI -5·1 to -0·4]; hazard ratio 0·62 [95% CI 0·41 to 0·93]; p=0·023).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds randomised evidence for OCT guidance in complex lesions alongside other imaging trials.

title: Bivalirudin vs Heparin Anticoagulation in STEMI: Confirmation of the BRIGHT-4 Results.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data meta-analysis; Six trials randomizing 15,254 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Older trials differed in bivalirudin regimen and glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitor use, and the mortality estimate for the BRIGHT-4 regimens crossed unity.
appraisal.one_line: IPD meta-analysis of six trials supports the BRIGHT-4 finding that bivalirudin with prolonged post-PCI infusion reduces cardiac mortality and major bleeding versus heparin in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Pooled across all regimens, bivalirudin reduced 30-day all-cause mortality (2.5% vs 2.9%; adjusted OR: 0.78; 95% CI: 0.62-0.99) but increased reinfarction (adjusted OR: 1.30; 95% CI: 1.02-1.65) and stent thrombosis (adjusted OR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.05-1.93). In the BRIGHT-4 regimens, 30-day all-cause mortality was 1.8% vs 2.9% (adjusted OR: 0.74; 95% CI: 0.48-1.12).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears directly on the choice of anticoagulant in primary PCI for STEMI and the regimen-specific effect on mortality, bleeding and stent thrombosis.

title: Fractional Flow Reserve and Instantaneous Wave-Free Ratio as Predictors of the Placebo-Controlled Response to Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Stable Coronary Artery Disease.

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a placebo-controlled randomized trial; invasive physiology available for 279 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc use of physiology as a continuous predictor in a trial of selected patients with low median FFR, and a symptom endpoint only.
appraisal.one_line: ORBITA-2 analysis shows that lower FFR and iFR predict greater placebo-controlled angina improvement after PCI, supporting physiology-guided symptom-driven PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: FFR 0.46 versus 0.73: odds ratio, 2.01; 95% credible interval, 1.79-2.26; probability of interaction, >99.9%. iFR 0.50 versus 0.86: odds ratio, 2.13; 95% credible interval, 1.87-2.45.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs how physiology should be used to select patients for PCI aimed at angina relief in stable disease.

title: Derivation and Validation of the PRECISE-HBR Score to Predict Bleeding After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled derivation cohort of 29 188 patients from 4 registries and one trial; external validation in 4578 patients from MASTER DAPT and 5970 from STOPDAPT-2.
appraisal.main_limitation: Discrimination was moderate and the gain over PRECISE-DAPT was small; impact on practice has not been tested.
appraisal.one_line: Derivation and external validation of a seven-item PRECISE-HBR bleeding risk score after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: AUC for 1-year BARC 3 or 5 bleeding of 0.73 (95% CI, 0.71-0.74) at apparent validation, 0.74 (95% CI, 0.68-0.80) in MASTER DAPT, and 0.73 (95% CI, 0.66-0.79) in STOPDAPT-2.
appraisal.why_it_matters: A simple score integrating ARC-HBR criteria could standardise high bleeding risk identification for antithrombotic de-escalation decisions.

title: Coronary artery bypass grafting vs. percutaneous coronary intervention in severe ischaemic cardiomyopathy: long-term survival.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort with inverse probability of treatment weighting; 2042 patients (1451 CABG, 591 PCI).
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational data with residual confounding, and the stroke estimate is very imprecise.
appraisal.one_line: Registry analysis in severe ischaemic cardiomyopathy associated CABG with lower long-term mortality than PCI after weighting.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Adjusted hazard ratio 0.59, 95% confidence interval 0.45-0.79, P = .001 for long-term mortality with CABG versus PCI; peri-procedural stroke aOR 19.6, 95% CI 4.21-91.6.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs revascularisation choice in low ejection fraction, where trial evidence is sparse.

title: Drug-Coated Balloon Angioplasty of the Side Branch During Provisional Stenting: The Multicenter Randomized DCB-BIF Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicenter randomized controlled trial; 784 patients (DCB n = 391, NCB n = 393).
appraisal.main_limitation: Benefit is driven by periprocedural myocardial infarction of unclear clinical significance, and follow-up is one year.
appraisal.one_line: DCB-BIF found a lower composite rate with a drug-coated balloon for the compromised side branch than with a non-coated balloon, driven by myocardial infarction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 28 patients in the DCB group and 49 patients in the NCB group (Kaplan-Meier rate: 7.2% vs 12.5%; HR: 0.56; 95% CI: 0.35-0.88; P = 0.013).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests a drug-coated balloon strategy for bifurcation side branches against plain balloon angioplasty.

title: Bioadaptor implant versus contemporary drug-eluting stent in percutaneous coronary interventions in Sweden (INFINITY-SWEDEHEART): a single-blind, non-inferiority, registry-based, randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry-based single-blind randomized non-inferiority trial in 20 hospitals; 1189 bioadaptor and 1192 DES assessable patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Short follow-up, and the later landmark differences are secondary analyses.
appraisal.one_line: INFINITY-SWEDEHEART showed non-inferiority of a bioadaptor to contemporary DES for target lesion failure at 12 months.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Risk difference of -0·41% (95% CI -1·94 to 1·11; pnon-inferiority<0·0001) for target lesion failure at 12 months.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides the first large randomized evidence for a bioadaptor against drug-eluting stents.

title: Quantitative flow ratio versus fractional flow reserve for coronary revascularisation guidance (FAVOR III Europe): a multicentre, randomised, non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomized open-label non-inferiority trial; QFR versus FFR strategy in 34 centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design and a one-year endpoint that includes revascularisation.
appraisal.one_line: FAVOR III Europe found QFR did not meet non-inferiority to FFR for guiding revascularisation of intermediate stenoses.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 12 months, a primary endpoint event had occurred in 67 (6·7%) patients in the QFR group, and in 41 (4·2%) patients in the FFR group (hazard ratio 1·63 [95% CI 1·11-2·41]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges guideline support for QFR as an alternative to wire-based FFR.

title: Definitions of clinical study outcome measures for cardiovascular diseases: the European Unified Registries for Heart Care Evaluation and Randomized Trials (EuroHeart).

appraisal.design_and_n: Modified Delphi consensus informed by systematic review, drawing on a consortium of 82 experts across five working groups.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus definitions depend on expert agreement and have not yet been tested for uptake across trials and registries.
appraisal.one_line: ESC EuroHeart international data standards defining outcome measures for ACS/PCI, AF, HF and TAVI studies.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 24 Level 1 (generic: 5, ACS/PCI: 8, AF: 2; HF: 5, TAVI: 4) and 48 Level 2 (generic: 18, ACS-PCI: 7, AF: 6, HF: 2, TAVI: 15) outcome measures were defined.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Harmonised outcome definitions would improve comparability of registries and trials and ease pooling in future syntheses.

title: Routine Spironolactone in Acute Myocardial Infarction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicenter 2-by-2 factorial placebo-controlled randomized trial; 7062 patients (3537 spironolactone, 3525 placebo).
appraisal.main_limitation: Fewer primary events than anticipated, so the trial may have limited power for modest effects.
appraisal.one_line: CLEAR SYNERGY found no reduction in cardiovascular death or heart failure with routine spironolactone after myocardial infarction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: First primary outcome: 183 events (1.7 per 100 patient-years) in the spironolactone group as compared with 220 events (2.1 per 100 patient-years) in the placebo group (hazard ratio adjusted for competing risk of death from noncardiovascular causes, 0.91; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.69 to 1.21; P = 0.51).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large neutral trial that bears on routine post-MI use of mineralocorticoid antagonists after PCI.

title: Colchicine in Acute Myocardial Infarction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicenter 2-by-2 factorial placebo-controlled randomized trial; 7062 patients (3528 colchicine, 3534 placebo).
appraisal.main_limitation: Vital status unknown in 45 patients (0.6%), and results may not apply to other timing or dosing.
appraisal.one_line: CLEAR SYNERGY found no reduction in the composite of cardiovascular death, recurrent MI, stroke or revascularisation with colchicine started soon after myocardial infarction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary-outcome event occurred in 322 of 3528 patients (9.1%) in the colchicine group and 327 of 3534 patients (9.3%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.99; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.85 to 1.16; P = 0.93).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large neutral trial that tempers guideline enthusiasm for routine colchicine after myocardial infarction.

title: Percutaneous vs. surgical revascularization of non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction with multivessel disease: the SWEDEHEART registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort of 57 097 revascularised patients, 42 190 (73.9%) PCI and 14 907 (26.1%) CABG, median follow-up of 7.1 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational comparison with residual confounding by indication, as PCI patients were older and CABG patients had more complex disease.
appraisal.one_line: SWEDEHEART registry comparison of PCI and CABG in NSTEMI with multivessel disease using instrumental variable adjustment.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: PCI was associated with higher risks of death (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 1.67; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.54-1.81) and MI (aOR 1.51; 95% CI 1.41-1.62) but there was no significant difference in stroke.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large-scale contemporary data on a decision where randomised evidence in NSTEMI with multivessel disease is limited.

title: Major Bleeding and Mortality After Revascularization of Left Main Disease.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc analysis of a randomized trial; 1,905 patients (PCI n = 948, CABG n = 957).
appraisal.main_limitation: Association from a secondary analysis, with confounding by illness severity.
appraisal.one_line: EXCEL bleeding analysis associated major bleeding with higher later mortality after left main PCI or CABG.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: MB events within 5 years were associated with a higher subsequent risk of all-cause mortality (adjusted HR: 2.71; 95% CI: 1.95-3.77; P < 0.0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Relevant to antithrombotic duration after left main PCI and to the bleeding profile of each strategy.

title: TransCatheter aortic valve implantation and fractional flow reserve-guided percutaneous coronary intervention versus conventional surgical aortic valve replacement and coronary bypass grafting for treatment of patients with aortic valve stenosis and complex or multivessel coronary disease (TCW): an international, multicentre, prospective, open-label, non-inferiority, randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label multicentre randomized non-inferiority trial; 172 patients (91 PCI plus TAVI, 81 SAVR plus CABG).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small trial that stopped enrolment below a large sample and evaluated 77 patients in the surgical group.
appraisal.one_line: TCW found FFR-guided PCI plus TAVI favourable versus SAVR plus CABG in severe aortic stenosis with complex coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary endpoint four [4%] of 91 patients versus 17 [23%] of 77 patients; risk difference -18·5 [90% CI -27·8 to -9·7]; hazard ratio 0·17 [95% CI 0·06-0·51].
appraisal.why_it_matters: First randomized comparison for combined aortic stenosis and complex coronary disease.

title: Optimal Strategy for Complete Revascularization in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction and Multivessel Disease: A Network Meta-Analysis.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis; 26 randomized trials enrolling 15,902 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: The immediate versus staged difference diminishes after excluding procedural MI.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis supports complete revascularisation in STEMI with multivessel disease, with immediate and staged strategies both beating culprit-only treatment.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: MACE was reduced with both immediate CR and staged CR compared with culprit-vessel-only treatment (RR: 0.48; 95% CI: 0.36-0.64 and RR: 0.65; 95% CI: 0.52-0.82, respectively). Immediate CR versus staged CR RR: 0.74; 95% CI: 0.56-0.97.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses timing of complete revascularisation in STEMI, a contested question.

title: Prevalence and Clinical Outcomes of Discordant Lesions Between Fractional Flow Reserve and Nonhyperemic Pressure Ratios in Clinical Practice: The J-PRIDE Registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicentre registry of 4304 lesions in 3200 patients from 20 Japanese centres; 1-year target vessel failure.
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised, with treatment choice by operators and small event counts in revascularised discordant subgroups.
appraisal.one_line: J-PRIDE registry describes prevalence and outcomes of FFR and non-hyperaemic pressure ratio discordance.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Discordance between FFR and NHPRs was observed in 20% of lesions (FFR+/NHPR-, 11.2%; FFR-/NHPRs+, 8.8%). In deferred vessels, the FFR+/NHPR- and FFR-/NHPR+ groups showed a higher 1-year incidence of target vessel failure compared with the FFR-/NHPR- group (7.9% versus 5.5% versus 1.7%; for FFR+/NHPR-, adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 4.89 [95% CI, 2.68-8.91]; P<0.001; for FFR-/NHPR+, aHR, 2.64 [95% CI, 1.49-4.69]; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs physiology-guided deferral where discordant lesions are common and guideline direction is unclear.

title: Stepwise Provisional Versus Systematic Dual-Stent Strategies for Treatment of True Left Main Coronary Bifurcation Lesions.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized open-label multicenter trial; 467 participants.
appraisal.main_limitation: Underpowered for the composite and subgroup interactions are exploratory.
appraisal.one_line: EBC MAIN found no difference in major adverse events between stepwise provisional and dual-stent strategies for left main bifurcation at 3 years, with less target lesion revascularisation with provisional stenting.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 3 years, the primary end point occurred in 54 of 230 (23.5%) stepwise provisional and 70 of 237 (29.5%) dual-stent patients (hazard ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.53-1.07]; P=0.11).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports provisional stenting as the default for non-complex left main bifurcations.

title: Antithrombotic Therapy to Minimize Total Events After ACS or PCI in Atrial Fibrillation: Insights From AUGUSTUS.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a 2x2 factorial randomized trial; 4,614 randomized participants.
appraisal.main_limitation: Secondary analysis of an open-label comparison with the aspirin comparison blinded.
appraisal.one_line: AUGUSTUS total-events analysis found apixaban reduced total bleeding versus VKA and aspirin roughly doubled bleeding without a clear ischaemic benefit.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Apixaban, compared with VKA, significantly reduced the risk of total bleeding (rate ratio [RR]: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.55-0.80). Aspirin, compared with placebo, significantly increased the risk of total bleeding (RR: 2.14; 95% CI: 1.75-2.60).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Reinforces antithrombotic regimens for patients with AF after ACS or PCI.

title: Prognostic Relevance of Type 4a Myocardial Infarction and Periprocedural Myocardial Injury in Patients With Non-ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Consecutive cohort of 1412 patients with NSTEMI undergoing PCI; internal validation cohort of 305 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-centre observational data with internal validation only.
appraisal.one_line: Single-centre cohort proposing a post-PCI troponin I threshold for prognostically relevant periprocedural injury in NSTEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A post-PCI ΔcTnI >20% but ≤40% showed similar outcomes to patients without PMI, whereas >40% was identified as the optimal threshold for prognostically relevant PMI. The abstract does not report an effect estimate with a confidence interval.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on the definition of type 4a MI and periprocedural injury in patients with elevated baseline troponin, where the Universal Definition is ambiguous.

title: Individual patient data meta-analysis of paclitaxel-coated balloons vs. drug-eluting stents for small-vessel coronary artery disease: the ANDROMEDA study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data meta-analysis of three randomized trials; 1154 patients and 1360 lesions.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few trials, with a mix of comparator stent generations.
appraisal.one_line: ANDROMEDA IPD meta-analysis associated paclitaxel-coated balloons with lower 3-year MACE than DES in small-vessel disease, without a significant difference in target lesion failure.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 3 years, PCB was associated with a lower risk of MACE compared with DES [hazard ratio (HR) 0.67, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.47-0.96], but did not reach statistical significance in the two-stage analysis (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.43-1.04).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs DCB use in small coronary vessels where trial evidence is limited.

title: Titanium-nitride-oxide-coated vs. drug-eluting stents in acute coronary syndromes: an individual patient data meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual patient data meta-analysis of three randomized trials; Patient-level data (n = 2743).
appraisal.main_limitation: Three trials, with secondary components not prespecified as primary.
appraisal.one_line: IPD meta-analysis in ACS found no significant difference in 5-year MACE between titanium-nitride-oxide-coated stents and DES, with lower cardiac death, MI and stent thrombosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: No significant difference in the primary endpoint between TiNOS and DES (12.6% vs. 16.2%; hazard ratio [HR] .82, 95% confidence interval [CI] .67-1.00, P = .051).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests whether a bioactive-coated stent offers hard-outcome advantages in ACS.

title: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical practice guideline based on a literature search from July 2023 to April 2024.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not describe individual recommendations, so classes and levels must be read from the full document.
appraisal.one_line: The 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI ACS guideline replaces prior NSTE-ACS, primary PCI and DAPT duration guidance.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets United States practice and creates ESC/ACC discordance questions across ACS management, antithrombotic therapy and revascularisation.

title: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical practice guideline based on a literature search from July 2023 to April 2024.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not describe individual recommendations, so classes and levels must be read from the full document.
appraisal.one_line: The 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI ACS guideline replaces prior NSTE-ACS, primary PCI and DAPT duration guidance (Circulation publication).
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sets United States practice and creates ESC/ACC discordance questions across ACS management, antithrombotic therapy and revascularisation.

title: Predictors of Outcomes of Reintervention After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: FRANCE 2 and FRANCE TAVI Registries.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort of 72,850 patients from FRANCE 2 and FRANCE TAVI, 2010 to 2022, with competing-risk analysis.
appraisal.main_limitation: Follow-up is too short to define reintervention risk in younger low-risk patients, and indications for reintervention were not adjudicated.
appraisal.one_line: French national registries quantify the incidence and predictors of reintervention after TAVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The cumulative incidence of overall reintervention at 8 years was 1.7% including 591 patients who had redo TAVR and 111 patients who required explant TAVR. Six-year mortality was high but was similar in patients who had early and late reintervention (76.2% vs 64.0%; P = 0.77).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives denominator-based reintervention rates relevant to lifetime management planning as TAVR extends to younger patients.

title: Medical therapy and outcomes in REVIVED-BCIS2 and STICHES: an individual patient data analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Pooled analysis of adjusted individual participant data from two randomized trials; 1912 participants.
appraisal.main_limitation: Cross-trial comparison of non-concurrent populations with different follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: Pooled IPD analysis suggests the better outcomes in REVIVED-BCIS2 than STICHES arise from medical therapy and population differences, not only revascularisation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Those receiving medical therapy alone in REVIVED-BCIS2 had fewer primary outcome events than those receiving medical therapy alone in STICHES (adjusted hazard ratio 0.60, 95% confidence interval 0.48-0.74, P < .001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Reframes interpretation of trials on revascularisation in ischaemic cardiomyopathy.

title: Invasive vs Conservative Management of Patients With Chronic Total Occlusion: Results From the ISCHEMIA Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a randomized trial; 3,113 CCTA-evaluable participants, 1,470 with at least 1 CTO.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup defined post randomization with an observational comparison for successful revascularisation.
appraisal.one_line: ISCHEMIA CTO analysis found similar risk-benefit of invasive versus conservative management with and without CTO, with improved angina and dyspnoea quality of life.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: INV did not reduce cardiovascular (CV) death or myocardial infarction (MI) (5-year difference -3.5%; 95% CI: -7.8% to 0.8%) and resulted in more procedural MIs (2.5%; 95% CI: 1.0%-4.0%) but fewer spontaneous MIs (-6.3%; 95% CI: -9.7% to -3.2%) than CON.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs CTO revascularisation in chronic coronary disease.

title: Stepwise dual antiplatelet therapy de-escalation in patients after drug coated balloon angioplasty (REC-CAGEFREE II): multicentre, randomised, open label, assessor blind, non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised open-label assessor-blind non-inferiority trial; 1948 adults with ACS.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trial in a Chinese population treated exclusively with paclitaxel-coated balloons.
appraisal.one_line: REC-CAGEFREE II found stepwise DAPT de-escalation non-inferior for ischaemic events with less major bleeding after drug-coated balloon treatment in ACS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 12 months, the primary endpoint occurred in 87 (8.9%) participants in the stepwise de-escalation group and 84 (8.6%) in the standard group (difference 0.36%; upper boundary of the one sided 95% CI 2.47%; Pnon-inferiority=0.013). BARC type 3 or 5 bleeding occurred in four versus 16 participants (0.4% v 1.6%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports shorter antiplatelet exposure after drug-coated balloon PCI in ACS.

title: Orbital atherectomy versus balloon angioplasty before drug-eluting stent implantation in severely calcified lesions eligible for both treatment strategies (ECLIPSE): a multicentre, open-label, randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre open-label randomised trial at 104 US centres; optical coherence tomography substudy of 276 and 279 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design, with results limited to lesions deemed treatable by either strategy.
appraisal.one_line: ECLIPSE found no benefit of routine orbital atherectomy before DES in severely calcified lesions for stent expansion or target vessel failure.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Mean minimal stent area 7·67 mm2 (SD 2·27) in the orbital atherectomy group and 7·42 mm2 (2·54) in the balloon angioplasty group (mean difference 0·26 [99% CI -0·31 to 0·82]; p=0·078); target vessel failure hazard ratio 1·16 [96% CI 0·87 to 1·54], p=0·28.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports a balloon-first approach to calcified lesions and tempers routine atherectomy.

title: Angiography-derived fractional flow reserve versus intravascular ultrasound to guide percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with coronary artery disease (FLAVOUR II): a multicentre, randomised, non-inferiority trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Investigator-initiated open-label randomised non-inferiority trial in 22 centres in China.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, single-country trial with one-year follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: Angiography-derived FFR-guided PCI was non-inferior to IUS guidance for 1-year clinical outcomes.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 56 patients in the angiography-derived FFR group and 54 patients in the intravascular ultrasound group (6·3% vs 6·0%, absolute difference 0·2 percentage points [upper boundary of one-sided 97·5% CI 2·4], pnon-inferiority=0·022; hazard ratio 1·04 [95% CI 0·71 to 1·51]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Compares imaging-free physiology guidance with intravascular imaging, relevant to guideline imaging recommendations.

title: Outcomes after fractional flow reserve-guided percutaneous coronary intervention versus coronary artery bypass grafting (FAME 3): 5-year follow-up of a multicentre, open-label, randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised trial in three-vessel disease; 757 assigned to PCI and 743 to CABG.
appraisal.main_limitation: Noninferiority of PCI was not shown at 1 year and the 5-year comparison is not powered for individual components.
appraisal.one_line: FAME 3 five-year results show no significant difference in death, stroke or MI between FFR-guided PCI and CABG, with more MI and repeat revascularisation with PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 5 years, there was no significant difference in the composite of death, stroke, or myocardial infarction between the two groups, with 119 (16%) events in the PCI group and 101 (14%) in the CABG group (hazard ratio 1·16 [95% CI 0·89-1·52]; p=0·27).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs shared decision-making between PCI and CABG in three-vessel disease.

title: Efficacy and safety of clopidogrel versus aspirin monotherapy in patients at high risk of subsequent cardiovascular event after percutaneous coronary intervention (SMART-CHOICE 3): a randomised, open-label, multicentre trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised open-label trial in patients at high risk of recurrent ischaemic events.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, industry-funded trial with a low event rate and a single-country population.
appraisal.one_line: Clopidogrel monotherapy reduced death, MI and stroke versus aspirin in high-risk patients after completing DAPT following PCI, without more bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Composite of death from any cause, myocardial infarction, and stroke at 3 years: 4·4% [95% CI 3·4-5·4] vs 6·6% [5·4-7·8]; hazard ratio 0·71 [95% CI 0·54-0·93]; p=0·013. Bleeding 0·97 [0·67-1·42].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on the choice of single antiplatelet agent in chronic therapy after PCI.

title: Implementation of a national AI technology program on cardiovascular outcomes and the health system.

appraisal.design_and_n: Observational cohort at 27 hospitals (CCTA n = 90,553 and FFR-CT n = 7,863).
appraisal.main_limitation: Non-randomised comparison with possible selection of patients and centres for FFR-CT.
appraisal.one_line: National NHS programme cohort assessing FFR-CT implementation against cardiovascular outcomes and downstream testing.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: FFR-CT was safe, with no difference in all-cause (n = 1,134 (3.2%) versus 1,612 (2.9%), adjusted-hazard ratio (aHR) 1.00 (0.93-1.08), P = 0.97) or cardiovascular mortality (n = 465 (1.3%) versus 617 (1.1%), aHR 0.96 (0.85-1.08), P = 0.48), while reducing invasive coronary angiograms (n = 5,720 (16%) versus 8,183 (14.9%), aHR 0.93 (0.90-0.97), P < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides system-level outcome data on an AI-based diagnostic pathway that influences referral for invasive angiography.

title: Definitions and standardized endpoints for the use of drug-coated balloon in coronary artery disease: consensus document of the Drug Coated Balloon Academic Research Consortium.

appraisal.design_and_n: International consensus document.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus rather than empirical evidence.
appraisal.one_line: DCB-ARC consensus document standardises definitions and endpoints for drug-coated balloon trials.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Harmonises endpoints across drug-coated balloon trials, improving comparability and pooling.

title: 10-Year Outcome of Complete or Infarct Artery-Only Revascularization in STEMI With Multivessel Disease: The DANAMI-3-PRIMULTI Study.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized trial long-term follow-up; 627 patients (313 infarct-related artery only, 314 complete revascularization).
appraisal.main_limitation: Benefit is driven by revascularisation, which is open-label and prone to ascertainment bias, with no reduction in death or MI.
appraisal.one_line: Ten-year DANAMI-3-PRIMULTI follow-up shows FFR-guided complete revascularisation reduced future events in STEMI with multivessel disease, driven by revascularisation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After 10 years, complete revascularization reduced the risk of the primary outcome (HR: 0.76; 95% CI: 0.60-0.94; P = 0.014). There was no difference in recurrent myocardial infarction (OR: 0.90; 95% CI: 0.60-1.35).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Long-term evidence for complete revascularisation strategy in STEMI.

title: Recurrent Events Analysis of MASTER DAPT: Total Ischemic and Bleeding Events After Abbreviated vs Prolonged DAPT in HBR Patients.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Recurrent events analysis of a randomized trial; abbreviated DAPT (n = 2,295) and prolonged DAPT (n = 2,284).
appraisal.main_limitation: Secondary analysis of an open-label trial with a one-month versus prolonged DAPT design.
appraisal.one_line: MASTER DAPT recurrent-events analysis shows abbreviated DAPT had similar total net adverse and ischaemic events and fewer total bleeding events in high bleeding risk patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 214 NACEs occurred in 172 patients, compared with 227 NACEs in 182 patients in the prolonged DAPT arm (HR: 0.95; 95% CI: 0.78-1.16; P = 0.64). Fewer total MCBs were observed in the abbreviated DAPT group (HR: 0.78; 95% CI: 0.64-0.94; P = 0.011).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports abbreviated DAPT in high bleeding risk patients with a total-event view.

title: P2Y12 inhibitor or aspirin after percutaneous coronary intervention: individual patient data meta-analysis of randomised clinical trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised trials; 16 117 patients in five trials.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trials with varying agents (ticagrelor or clopidogrel) and bleeding estimates with wide intervals.
appraisal.one_line: IPD meta-analysis of five trials found P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy associated with lower MACCE than aspirin monotherapy after PCI and DAPT completion, without more major bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy was associated with a lower risk of MACCE compared with aspirin monotherapy (one stage analysis: hazard ratio 0.77 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.67 to 0.89), P<0.001), with a number needed to treat to benefit of 45.5 (95% CI 31.4 to 93.6). Major bleeding one stage analysis: hazard ratio 1.26 (0.78 to 2.04), P=0.35.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the choice of long-term single antiplatelet agent after PCI, relevant to guideline recommendations.

title: Optical coherence tomography- vs angiography-guided coronary stent implantation in calcified lesions: the ILUMIEN IV trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified subgroup analysis of a randomized trial; overall population (n = 2114).
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis from a trial whose overall primary clinical endpoint was not met, so findings are hypothesis generating.
appraisal.one_line: ILUMIEN IV analysis shows OCT guidance reduced target vessel failure in moderately or severely calcified lesions but not in mild or no calcification.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: TVF within 2 years occurred in 35 patients with OCT guidance and in 51 patients with angiography guidance (6.8% vs 9.7%; adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.62; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.40-0.96), with Pinteraction = .01.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Suggests lesion calcification as a selector for intravascular imaging use.

title: Nonculprit Vulnerable Plaques and Prognosis in Myocardial Infarction With Versus Without ST-Segment Elevation: A PROSPECT II Substudy.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective natural history study of 898 patients, 199 (22.2%) with STEMI and 699 (77.8%) with NSTEMI, median follow-up 3.7 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc subgroup of a natural history study with few events and no randomised treatment.
appraisal.one_line: PROSPECT II substudy finds similar nonculprit vulnerable plaque prevalence and outcomes in STEMI and NSTEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The 4-year rates of nonculprit lesion-related major adverse cardiovascular events were similar in STEMI versus NSTEMI (8.6% versus 7.8%; hazard ratio, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.57-1.81]; P=0.95).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs whether nonculprit lesion strategy should differ between STEMI and NSTEMI, where guidelines differ.

title: Radial vs femoral access for percutaneous coronary intervention: temporal trends and outcomes in the USA.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort of 6 658 479 PCI procedures from 2013 to 2022; 2 420 805 PCIs in the comparative safety analysis.
appraisal.main_limitation: Instrumental variable estimates rest on untestable assumptions and cover in-hospital outcomes only.
appraisal.one_line: NCDR CathPCI analysis of radial versus femoral access using operator preference as an instrument.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In instrumental variable analyses, radial access site was associated with lower in-hospital mortality [absolute risk difference (ARD) -.15%, 95% confidence interval (CI) -.20 to -.10], major access site bleeding (ARD -.64%, 95% CI -.68 to -.60), and other major vascular complications (ARD -.21%, 95% CI -.23 to -.18) but a higher risk of ischaemic stroke (ARD .05%, 95% CI .03-.08).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Quantifies the contemporary US trend and comparative safety of radial access, including a signal for stroke that merits scrutiny.

title: Sex differences in dual antiplatelet therapy de-escalation strategies after percutaneous coronary intervention: a network meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Network meta-analysis of randomized trials; 71 272 patients from 20 trials, 23.3% female.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level sex subgroup data from trials not powered for sex interaction.
appraisal.one_line: Network meta-analysis suggests the effect of DAPT discontinuation differs by sex, with aspirin discontinuation ranking best in women.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: With DAPT discontinuation vs standard DAPT, a significant interaction between treatment effect and sex was found for both MACE (Pint = .028) and major bleeding (Pint = .015); MACE in females (HR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.75-0.98) and males (HR, 1.04; 95% CI 0.93-1.16).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses sex-specific tailoring of de-escalation, a population gap in DAPT trials.

title: Impact of the MISSION Act on Quality and Outcomes of Major Cardiovascular Procedures Among Veterans.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective cohort of veterans receiving PCI (n = 43 000), CABG (n = 23 301) or AVR (n = 14 682).
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational quasi-experimental design in a predominantly male veteran population with possible residual confounding.
appraisal.one_line: Difference-in-differences analysis of the VA MISSION Act on travel time and 30-day outcomes of PCI, CABG and AVR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After MISSION implementation, mean PCI MACE rates decreased by 0.5 percentage points for near patients and increased by 2.3 percentage points for far patients (difference in differences, 2.8 percentage points; P <.001). AVR MACE rates were not statistically different between the groups (P = .45).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Natural experiment on moving procedures to community hospitals, relevant to systems of care for coronary and valve procedures.

title: Heparin administration at first medical contact vs immediately before primary percutaneous coronary intervention: the HELP-PCI trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Investigator-initiated randomized trial at 36 centres in China; 999 patients (505 at FMC, 494 in Cath Lab).
appraisal.main_limitation: Surrogate angiographic primary endpoint and no clinical outcome difference.
appraisal.one_line: HELP-PCI found heparin at first medical contact improved spontaneous reperfusion without increasing bleeding in STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Pre-treated population at FMC showed a higher frequency of TFG-3 of IRA compared with the Cath Lab group (23.6% vs 17.6%; odds ratio, 1.44; 95% confidence interval, 1.06-1.97; P = .02). There were no significant differences in secondary endpoints, including 12-month MACCE.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses timing of anticoagulation in primary PCI.

title: Fractional flow reserve vs angiography to guide percutaneous coronary intervention: an individual patient data meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: IPD meta-analysis of 5 RCTs, 2493 patients (1241 angiography, 1252 FFR), PROSPERO CRD42024553676.
appraisal.main_limitation: Benefit was driven by peri-procedural MI, with no difference in mortality or MACE beyond 30 days, and the pooled sample is modest.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis of five randomised trials found fewer one-year major adverse cardiac events with FFR-guided than angiography-guided PCI, driven by peri-procedural MI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: One-year MACE occurred in 14.7% of patients in the angiography group and 12.1% in the FFR group (hazard ratio (HR) .80, 95% confidence interval (CI) .64-.99; P = .046).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Clarifies that the advantage of physiology guidance in chronic coronary syndrome and NSTE-ACS lies mainly in fewer procedural events, relevant to guideline weighting of FFR.

title: Long-Term Outcomes After Fractional Flow Reserve vs Intravascular Ultrasound to Guide PCI: The FLAVOUR Trial Extended Follow-Up.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised open-label trial, 1,682 patients (FFR 838, IVUS 844), median follow-up 6.3 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design and extended follow-up not powered for individual components; revascularisation is a softer endpoint.
appraisal.one_line: Extended follow-up of FLAVOUR found no difference in the primary composite between FFR- and IVUS-guided strategies at a median of 6.3 years, with more late revascularisation after FFR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary outcome occurred in 179 (23.1%) for FFR vs 160 (20.9%) for IVUS (HR: 1.15; 95% CI: 0.93-1.42; P = 0.208).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives long-term randomised evidence for choosing physiology or intravascular imaging to guide treatment of intermediate stenosis.

title: Computed Tomography Angiography or Standard Care After Left Main PCI?
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicentre open-label RCT, 606 patients, 303 per arm.
appraisal.main_limitation: Modest sample for rare events, and the spontaneous MI difference is a secondary finding.
appraisal.one_line: PULSE found routine CCTA six months after left main PCI did not reduce the clinical composite, with fewer spontaneous MIs but more imaging-triggered revascularisation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 36/303 experimental patients vs 38/303 control patients (11.9% vs 12.5%; HR: 0.97; 95% CI: 0.76-1.23; P = 0.80).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs whether routine surveillance imaging after left main stenting is justified.

title: Temporal modulation of antiplatelet therapy in high-risk patients undergoing complex percutaneous coronary intervention: the TAILORED-CHIP randomized clinical trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 2018 patients undergoing complex high-risk PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Strategy combined several changes at once, so the contribution of each component cannot be separated.
appraisal.one_line: TAILORED-CHIP found a tailored escalation and de-escalation antiplatelet strategy did not reduce net adverse events versus 12-month DAPT in complex high-risk PCI, with more bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary outcome event occurred in 105 patients (10.5%) assigned to tailored antiplatelet therapy and in 89 patients (8.8%) assigned to dual antiplatelet therapy [hazard ratio, 1.19; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.90-1.58; P = .21].
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests de-escalation to clopidogrel monotherapy in a high-risk complex PCI population, where trial evidence is scarce.

title: Fractional Flow Reserve-Guided Complete vs Culprit-Only Revascularization in Non-ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction and Multivessel Disease: The SLIM Randomized Clinical Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Investigator-initiated multicentre randomised trial, 478 patients (240 complete, 238 culprit-only).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small open-label trial whose composite includes any revascularisation, which drives much of the difference.
appraisal.one_line: SLIM reported fewer one-year events with FFR-guided complete revascularisation than culprit-only treatment in NSTEMI with multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 13 patients (5.5%) in the FFR-guided complete revascularization group vs 32 patients (13.6%) in the culprit-only group (hazard ratio [HR], 0.38 [95% CI, 0.20-0.72]; P = .003).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds randomised evidence for physiology-guided complete revascularisation in NSTEMI, where guideline support is weaker than in STEMI.

title: Early Withdrawal of Aspirin after PCI in Acute Coronary Syndromes.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre open-label randomised trial in Brazil, 3410 patients (1712 monotherapy, 1698 DAPT).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, with monotherapy started within 4 days of admission, and stent thrombosis numerically higher with monotherapy.
appraisal.one_line: Early aspirin withdrawal with potent P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy after PCI for ACS was not shown to be noninferior to DAPT for ischaemic events but reduced bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or urgent revascularization occurred in 119 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 7.0%) in the monotherapy group and in 93 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 5.5%) in the dual antiplatelet therapy group (absolute risk difference, 1.47 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.16 to 3.10; P = 0.11 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Suggests very early aspirin withdrawal in ACS trades bleeding for possible ischaemic cost, tempering the P2Y12 monotherapy strategy.

title: Aspirin in Patients with Chronic Coronary Syndrome Receiving Oral Anticoagulation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre double-blind placebo-controlled RCT in France, 872 patients (433 aspirin, 439 placebo), median follow-up 2.2 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Early termination and modest sample size, with a total death excess that is a secondary finding.
