appraisal.one_line: Adding aspirin to oral anticoagulation in high-risk chronic coronary syndrome increased deaths and bleeding, and the trial stopped early.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary efficacy outcome event occurred in 73 patients (16.9%) in the aspirin group and in 53 patients (12.1%) in the placebo group (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.53; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.07 to 2.18; P = 0.02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Directly addresses routine aspirin co-prescription with anticoagulation in stented patients beyond six months, where guidelines rely on weak evidence.

title: Early Discontinuation of Aspirin after PCI in Low-Risk Acute Myocardial Infarction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre open-label randomised trial at 40 European sites; 1942 randomised (961 monotherapy, 981 DAPT).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, restricted to low-risk selected patients, with few ischaemic events and a narrow noninferiority margin relative to event rates.
appraisal.one_line: In low-risk MI patients after complete revascularisation and one month of DAPT, P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy was noninferior for a net clinical composite and reduced clinically relevant bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary-outcome event occurred in 20 patients (2.1%) in the P2Y12-inhibitor monotherapy group and in 21 patients (2.2%) in the dual antiplatelet therapy group (difference, -0.09 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.39 to 1.20; P = 0.02 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports early step-down from DAPT to monotherapy after complete revascularisation in MI, a common decision.

title: Twice-Daily Clopidogrel vs Ticagrelor to Reduce Short-Term Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events After Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: The TADCLOT Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Double-blind randomised superiority trial at a single Karachi centre, 2,201 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-centre, one-month treatment period and few events.
appraisal.one_line: TADCLOT found no significant difference in one-month MACE between ticagrelor and twice-daily clopidogrel after primary PCI for STEMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: MACEs occurred in 24 (2.2%) ticagrelor patients vs 32 (2.9%) in twice-daily clopidogrel patients (HR: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.44-1.27; P = 0.28).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides head-to-head data for a lower-cost option in settings where potent P2Y12 inhibitors are less accessible.

title: Personalized or Standard Duration of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: The PARTHENOPE Randomized Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial of 2,107 patients undergoing PCI (personalized 1,055, standard 1,052).
appraisal.main_limitation: Strategy bundles variable durations of 3, 6 or 24 months, and the P value is close to the threshold.
appraisal.one_line: PARTHENOPE found a risk-score-based personalised DAPT duration lowered net adverse clinical events at 24 months compared with standard 12-month DAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: NACE occurred in 196 of 1,055 patients (18.6%) in the personalized DAPT group and in 232 of 1,052 patients (22.2%) in the standard DAPT group (difference, 3.54 percentage points; 95% CI: -6.99 to -0.99; P = 0.040).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests a risk-score-driven approach to DAPT duration rather than a fixed schedule.

title: Immediate versus staged complete revascularisation during index admission in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease (OPTION-STEMI): a multicentre, non-inferiority, open-label, randomised trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label randomised noninferiority trial at 14 hospitals in South Korea, 994 patients (498 immediate, 496 staged).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label with a wide noninferiority margin (HR 1·42) relative to observed event rates, so the result is inconclusive rather than showing equivalence.
appraisal.one_line: OPTION-STEMI did not show immediate complete revascularisation to be noninferior to staged complete revascularisation during the index admission in STEMI with multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred at 1 year in 65 patients (13%) in the immediate group and 53 patients (11%) in the staged group (HR 1·24 [95% CI 0·86-1·79]; pnon-inferiority=0·24).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses the timing of non-culprit PCI in STEMI, a question left open by existing complete revascularisation trials.

title: Clopidogrel versus aspirin for secondary prevention of coronary artery disease: a systematic review and individual patient data meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and one-stage IPD meta-analysis of 7 randomised trials, 28 982 patients (14 507 clopidogrel; 14 475 aspirin); PROSPERO CRD42025645594.
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooled trials differ in design, with a median follow-up of 2·3 years and an extrapolated 5·5-year estimate; most trials were open-label.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis found clopidogrel monotherapy associated with fewer MACCE than aspirin monotherapy in established coronary artery disease, with no difference in major bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 5·5 years, MACCE occurred in 929 events (2·61 per 100 patient-years) with clopidogrel vs 1062 events (2·99 per 100 patient-years) with aspirin; hazard ratio 0·86 [95% CI 0·77-0·96]; p=0·0082.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Challenges aspirin as the default long-term single antiplatelet agent in chronic coronary disease.

title: Indications for Use of Drug-Coated Balloons in Coronary Intervention: Academic Research Consortium Position Statement.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus position statement; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Consensus suggestions rest on a trial base that varies by device and setting, and the abstract gives no recommendation classes.
appraisal.one_line: Academic Research Consortium position statement classifying drug-coated balloon technologies and proposing indications for their use across lesion and clinical settings.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Offers a common framework for DCB use and trial design in coronary intervention, including in ACS and high bleeding risk.

title: Long-Term Continuous Monitoring of New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective two-centre German cohort of 198 patients with an insertable cardiac monitor implanted during CABG, followed for 1 year.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample, predominantly male, with no outcome comparison of anticoagulation strategies.
appraisal.one_line: Prospective insertable-monitor study shows high incidence but very low burden of new-onset AF after CABG, questioning anticoagulation guidance.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 95 patients developed new-onset AF within the first year after CABG (cumulative incidence, 48%; 95% CI, 41%-55%). The median AF burden during the first year was 0.07% (IQR, 0.02%-0.23%) or 370 minutes.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides rhythm-monitoring data bearing on the class 2a recommendation for 60 days of anticoagulation after post-CABG AF.

title: Part 11: Post-Cardiac Arrest Care: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Emergency Cardiovascular Care.

appraisal.design_and_n: Guideline; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Abstract does not state recommendation classes or levels, which must be taken from the full text.
appraisal.one_line: 2025 AHA guideline on post-cardiac arrest care, covering blood pressure, oxygen and temperature goals, PCI, mechanical circulatory support and neuroprognostication.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Updates US guidance on invasive coronary management and mechanical support after resuscitation, a common source of ESC and AHA discordance.

title: Immediate or Deferred Nonculprit-Lesion PCI in Myocardial Infarction.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: International open-label randomised trial, 1146 patients (558 iFR, 588 MRI).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, and the comparator strategy was itself an active imaging-guided approach rather than culprit-only management.
appraisal.one_line: iMODERN found immediate iFR-guided nonculprit PCI was not superior to deferred stress MRI-guided PCI in STEMI with multivessel disease at three years.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary-end-point event occurred in 50 patients (9.3%) in the iFR group and in 55 patients (9.8%) in the MRI group (hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% confidence interval, 0.65 to 1.40; P = 0.81).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs timing and guidance of complete revascularisation in STEMI, where practice and guidelines vary.

title: PCI of Native Coronary Artery vs Saphenous Vein Graft After Prior Bypass Surgery: A Multicenter, Randomized Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised trial across 14 European centres, 220 patients (native vessel PCI n = 108; SVG PCI n = 112).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample with a single-year follow-up, and the composite includes clinically driven revascularisation.
appraisal.one_line: PROCTOR found native vessel PCI led to more major adverse cardiac events than saphenous vein graft PCI at one year, contrary to the guideline preference.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, major adverse cardiac events occurred in 37 patients (34%) in the native vessel PCI group and 21 patients (19%) in the SVG PCI group (HR: 2.14; 95% CI: 1.25-3.65; P = 0.006).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Tests a guideline recommendation that rested solely on observational data.

title: Drug-Coated Balloon Angioplasty vs Up-Front Stenting for De Novo CAD: 3-Year Follow-Up of REC-CAGEFREE I Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label randomised noninferiority trial at 43 sites in China, 2,272 patients (1,133 DCB, 1,139 DES).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, single-country trial of a paclitaxel DCB strategy with rescue stenting, so results may not extend to other DCB devices.
appraisal.one_line: Three-year REC-CAGEFREE I follow-up shows a higher device-oriented composite with DCB angioplasty than with up-front DES in de novo coronary disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 3 years, the DOCE occurred in 92 patients (8.2%) in the DCB arm and 56 (5.0%) in the DES arm (difference: 3.21%; 95% CI: 1.17%-5.26%; P = 0.002).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Counters wider use of DCB as a stent-free default for de novo lesions.

title: Therapy for Atrial Fibrillation in Patients with Drug-Eluting Stents.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre open-label noninferiority RCT in South Korea, 960 patients (482 monotherapy, 478 combination).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, single-country trial, with the net composite driven largely by bleeding and not powered for stent thrombosis.
appraisal.one_line: ADAPT AF-DES found NOAC monotherapy noninferior and superior to NOAC plus clopidogrel for net adverse events in AF patients at least one year after drug-eluting stent implantation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A primary end-point event had occurred in 46 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 9.6%) in the monotherapy group and in 82 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 17.2%) in the combination-therapy group (absolute difference of -7.6 percentage points (95.2% confidence interval [CI], -11.9 to -3.3; P<0.001 for noninferiority) and a hazard ratio of 0.54 (95.2% CI, 0.37 to 0.77).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports stopping antiplatelet therapy beyond one year after stenting in patients on anticoagulation.

title: Complete versus culprit lesion-only revascularisation for acute myocardial infarction (Complete Revascularisation Trialists' Collaboration): an individual patient data meta-analysis of randomised trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: IPD meta-analysis of 6 randomised trials, 8836 patients (4259 complete revascularisation, 4577 culprit lesion-only); PROSPERO CRD420251124098.
appraisal.main_limitation: Pooled trials differ in lesion selection, timing and guidance, and are open-label.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data meta-analysis found complete revascularisation reduced cardiovascular death or new MI, and cardiovascular death alone, versus culprit-only PCI in acute MI with multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Cardiovascular death or new myocardial infarction occurred in 382 (9·0%) of 4259 patients in the complete revascularisation group compared with 528 (11·5%) of 4577 patients in the culprit lesion-only group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·76 [95% CI 0·67-0·87], p<0·0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Establishes a cardiovascular mortality benefit for complete revascularisation, strengthening guideline recommendations including in NSTEMI.

title: Women with chronic coronary artery disease: long-term outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention vs coronary artery bypass grafting.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective cohort of 2469 PCI and 3721 CABG patients, with 2033 matched pairs and median follow-up 5.1 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective propensity matching leaves residual confounding, and anatomical complexity was not fully captured in administrative data.
appraisal.one_line: Ontario propensity-matched comparison of PCI and CABG in women with chronic severe CAD.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: MACCE was higher with PCI compared with CABG (hazard ratio [HR] 1.81, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.63-2.01], P < .001). All-cause mortality was higher with PCI compared with CABG (HR 1.34 [95% CI: 1.16-1.54], P < .001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Sex-specific revascularisation data are scarce, and women are under-represented in the defining trials.

title: Potent P2Y12 Inhibitor Monotherapy vs DAPT After PCI in Patients With and Without STEMI: The NEO-MINDSET Substudy.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified analysis of a randomised trial, 3,410 participants (2,119 STEMI; 1,291 NSTE-ACS).
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis with a modest interaction P value, in an open-label trial.
appraisal.one_line: NEO-MINDSET substudy suggests early aspirin withdrawal increased ischaemic events in STEMI but not in NSTE-ACS, with less bleeding in both.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Among STEMI patients, an early aspirin-free strategy was associated with a higher rate of the co-primary ischemic composite outcome compared with DAPT at 1 year (8.2% vs 5.2%, respectively; HR: 1.60; 95% CI: 1.14-2.24); in NSTE-ACS 5.1% vs 6.0% (HR: 0.84; 95% CI: 0.53-1.35; P for interaction = 0.030).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Suggests presentation type should guide whether aspirin is withdrawn early after PCI for ACS.

title: Physiology vs angiography-guided percutaneous coronary intervention in transcatheter aortic valve implantation: the FAITAVI trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre open-label randomised superiority trial, 320 patients across 15 Italian centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: Small open-label trial with a borderline P value and a benefit driven mainly by all-cause mortality.
appraisal.one_line: FAITAVI found FFR-guided PCI was associated with lower 12-month MACCE than angiography-guided PCI in TAVI patients with intermediate coronary lesions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: FFR-guided PCI was associated with a significantly lower rate of MACCE at 12 months compared with angiography-guided PCI (8.5% vs 16.0%; hazard ratio .52; 95% confidence interval .27-.99; P = .047).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Randomised evidence on coronary revascularisation strategy in TAVI candidates, a question with little trial data.

title: Prognostic Implications of Evolving Universal Definitions of Periprocedural Myocardial Infarction in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome.

appraisal.design_and_n: Analysis of the MATRIX randomised trial cohort, 6724 patients undergoing PCI.
appraisal.main_limitation: Few events with wide intervals and borderline P values, in a non-randomised comparison of definitions.
appraisal.one_line: MATRIX analysis found only the fourth universal definition of PCI-related MI in NSTE-ACS was associated with later death among three definitions compared.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Only PCI-MI defined by the fourth UDMI in patients with non-ST-segment-elevation ACS was associated with increased risks of all-cause (hazard ratio, 2.08 [95% CI, 1.00-4.30]; P=0.048) and cardiovascular (hazard ratio, 2.62 [95% CI, 1.03-6.65]; P=0.043) death.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs how periprocedural MI is defined and used as an endpoint in coronary intervention trials.

title: Complete revascularization timing in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease with heart failure: the OPTION-STEMI trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified subgroup analysis of a randomised trial, 994 patients, of whom 329 (33.1%) had heart failure at admission.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis with a borderline interaction P value, in a trial that did not meet its noninferiority aim.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified OPTION-STEMI subgroup suggests immediate complete revascularisation was worse than staged in STEMI patients with heart failure at admission, but not in those without.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Immediate complete revascularization was associated with a higher incidence of the primary endpoint than staged in patients with heart failure (22.8% vs 13.3%; HR 1.79; 95% CI 1.05-3.04), but not in those without (8.0% vs 9.5%; HR 0.84; 95% CI .50-1.40); P = .043 for interaction.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Suggests Killip class should inform the timing of non-culprit PCI in STEMI.

title: Fractional flow reserve-guided percutaneous coronary intervention versus medical therapy for stable coronary artery disease: long-term results of the FAME 2 trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Long-term follow-up of a randomised trial, 748 patients from 16 hospitals (PCI n = 447; medical therapy n = 441 in original allocation).
appraisal.main_limitation: Benefit was driven by urgent revascularisation, with win ratio for all-cause death 0.88 (95% CI 0.66-1.17), and the trial was open-label.
appraisal.one_line: FAME 2 long-term follow-up to a median of 11.2 years shows FFR-guided PCI superior to medical therapy alone on a hierarchical win ratio composite in stable CAD.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint occurred in 150 of 447 patients (33.6%) in the PCI group versus 182 of 441 (41.3%) in the medical therapy group, with a win ratio of 1.25 in favor of PCI (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.01-1.56, P = 0.043).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Longest randomised follow-up on revascularisation versus medical therapy in physiology-selected chronic coronary disease.

title: Association Between Age and PCI Effectiveness in Stable CAD: Secondary Analysis of ORBITA-2.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc secondary analysis of all patients in the placebo-controlled ORBITA-2 trial; mean age 64 ± 9 years, range 40 to 82.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc interaction analysis that was not prespecified and not powered for age subgroups.
appraisal.one_line: Post hoc Bayesian analysis of ORBITA-2 shows PCI relieved angina at all ages but improved exercise time less in older patients.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In older patients, PCI was more effective for symptom relief (OR: 2.03; 95% CrI: 1.67-2.45; Pr > 0.99) than in younger patients (OR: 1.70; 95% CrI: 1.38-2.15; Pr > 0.99; Pr [interaction] = 0.99).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the use of treadmill time as an endpoint and shows consistency of PCI symptom benefit in older patients with stable angina.

title: Dual antiplatelet therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention according to bleeding risk (HOST-BR): an open-label, multicentre, randomised clinical trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label multicentre randomised trial at 50 centres in South Korea, 4897 patients (1598 high bleeding risk; 3299 non-HBR).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, single-country trial, and the abstract excerpt does not give the non-HBR stratum result.
appraisal.one_line: HOST-BR found one-month DAPT did not reach noninferiority to three-month DAPT for net adverse clinical events in high bleeding risk patients after DES.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In the HBR stratum, 1-month compared with 3-month DAPT did not reach non-inferiority for net adverse clinical events (144 [18·4%] of 798 vs 110 [14·0%] of 800 patients; hazard ratio [HR] 1·337 [95% CI 1·043-1·713]; p=0·82 for non-inferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Questions very short DAPT in high bleeding risk patients, a common guideline-supported strategy.

title: Immediate vs Delayed Coronary Angiography After Cardiac Arrest Without ST-Segment Elevation: 5-Year Outcomes From the COACT Randomized Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Long-term follow-up of an open-label randomised trial at 19 Dutch centres; 5-year data for 514 of 552 patients (261 immediate, 253 delayed).
appraisal.main_limitation: Follow-up by telephone interview, and the landmark analysis was nonprespecified and exploratory.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year COACT follow-up shows no survival difference between immediate and delayed coronary angiography after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest without ST elevation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Five years after the index hospitalization, 143 patients (54.8%) were alive in the immediate angiography group, and 131 patients (51.8%) were alive in the delayed angiography group (HR: 0.95; 95% CI: 0.74-1.23).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Confirms that urgent angiography is not needed for survival benefit in shockable arrest without ST elevation, relevant to invasive management after arrest.

title: Spontaneous Myocardial Infarction After Left Main Revascularization: The EXCEL Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc analysis of a randomised trial, 1882 patients with left main disease revascularised by PCI or CABG.
appraisal.main_limitation: Association of MI with mortality is observational within a trial and subject to confounding.
appraisal.one_line: EXCEL analysis found spontaneous MI after left main revascularisation was more frequent after PCI than CABG and strongly associated with later mortality after both.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Spontaneous MI during 5-year follow-up occurred in 60 (6.8%) patients after PCI and in 29 (3.4%) patients after CABG (adjusted hazard ratio [adjHR], 2.01; 95 CI, 1.29-3.15; P=0.002).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the long-term MI burden in the PCI versus CABG decision for left main disease.

title: Intravascular Imaging- vs Angiography-Guided Complex PCI: 5-Year Outcomes From a Randomized Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicentre open-label superiority trial in South Korea; 1,639 patients randomised 2:1 (1,092 imaging-guided, 547 angiography-guided).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design and a composite endpoint with a target-vessel focus.
appraisal.one_line: Five-year follow-up of a randomised trial in complex lesions: imaging-guided PCI was associated with fewer target-vessel events than angiography guidance.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary endpoint occurred in 109 of 1,092 patients (10.5%) vs 78 of 547 patients (14.9%) (HR: 0.68; 95% CI: 0.51-0.91; P = 0.009).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Durable long-term benefit strengthens the case for routine intravascular imaging in complex PCI.

title: Multimodality Imaging to Determine Underlying Causes of Myocardial Infarction With Nonobstructive Coronary Arteries in Women and Men.

appraisal.design_and_n: International prospective diagnostic study at 28 sites; 754 patients enrolled, 389 with MINOCA, 336 undergoing OCT and 284 CMR.
appraisal.main_limitation: Diagnostic study without treatment or outcome data, and not all participants completed both tests.
appraisal.one_line: Prospective multimodality imaging study with multivessel OCT and CMR defines causes of MINOCA in women and men.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: An OCT-defined culprit lesion was identified in 45% (116 of 270 women [43%] and 35 of 66 men [53%], P=0.18). CMR demonstrated an ischemic pattern in 114 of 284 (40%). The combination confirmed myocardial infarction in 59% and identified an alternate cause in 20%.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows that routine imaging identifies a cause in most MINOCA patients, supporting guideline recommendations for imaging.

title: Left Ventricular Unloading in High-Risk Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 300 patients (148 microaxial flow pump, 152 standard care).
appraisal.main_limitation: Modest sample size and open-label design; wide interval around mortality.
appraisal.one_line: Elective microaxial flow pump unloading did not improve a hierarchical composite in high-risk PCI with severe LV dysfunction.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: 36.6% of pairwise comparisons favored the microaxial flow pump, and 43.0% favored standard care (win ratio, 0.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.63 to 1.15; P = 0.30).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Argues against routine elective MCS in complex PCI and bears on a numerically higher death count (hazard ratio, 1.54; 95% CI, 0.99 to 2.41).

title: Angiography-Based Physiology to Guide Coronary Revascularization.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: International open-label randomised noninferiority trial at 37 sites in Europe; primary endpoint assessed in 1116 (vFFR) and 1095 (FFR) patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, industry-funded, with 1-year follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: Angiography-derived vessel FFR-guided revascularisation was noninferior to pressure-wire FFR at 1 year.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary end-point event in 80 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 7.5%) vs 79 patients (7.5%) (risk difference, -0.02 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -2.25 to 2.21; P = 0.004 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports wire-free physiology to widen use of physiological guidance.

title: Angiography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve to Guide PCI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: International randomised noninferiority trial; 1930 patients (965 FFRangio, 965 pressure-wire).
appraisal.main_limitation: Industry-funded with a 1-year horizon.
appraisal.one_line: FFRangio-guided strategy was noninferior to pressure-wire FFR for 1-year outcomes in intermediate stenoses.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary end-point event in 64 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 6.9%) vs 65 patients (7.1%) (hazard ratio, 0.98; 95% confidence interval, 0.70 to 1.39; P<0.001 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Second large noninferiority trial of angiography-derived physiology, together supporting guideline uptake.

title: Intravascular Ultrasound-Guided or Angiography-Guided Complex High-Risk PCI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Investigator-initiated international open-label randomised trial; 2020 randomised, 1010 IVUS-guided and 1009 angiography-guided analysed.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design and a median follow-up of 19.0 months.
appraisal.one_line: Routine IVUS guidance did not reduce target-vessel failure compared with angiography in complex high-risk PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Target-vessel failure in 140 patients (13.9%) vs 112 patients (11.1%) (hazard ratio, 1.25; 95% confidence interval, 0.97 to 1.60; P = 0.08).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Contrasts with other imaging trials and complicates guideline recommendations in Western practice.

title: IVUS-Guided versus Angiography-Guided PCI in Unprotected Left Main Coronary Disease.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: International multicentre open-label randomised trial; 806 patients (401 IVUS-guided, 405 angiography-guided).
appraisal.main_limitation: Patient-oriented composite at longest follow-up with a modest sample.
appraisal.one_line: IVUS guidance showed no additional benefit over angiography in unprotected left main PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary end-point event in 135 patients (33.7%) vs 125 patients (30.9%) (hazard ratio, 1.11; 95% confidence interval, 0.87 to 1.42; P = 0.40).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Neutral result in left main disease challenges universal imaging recommendations and informs future meta-analysis.

title: IVUS or Angiography Guidance for Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Complex Coronary Bifurcation Lesions: The DKCRUSH VIII Randomized Clinical Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial (DKCRUSH VIII); 555 patients (277 IVUS-guided, 278 angiography-guided).
appraisal.main_limitation: Single technique (2-stent DK crush) and 1-year follow-up; benefit linked to achieving optimisation targets.
appraisal.one_line: IVUS guidance was associated with fewer 1-year events than angiography guidance in complex bifurcation lesions treated with DK crush.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary endpoint event in 17 patients (6.1%) vs 41 (14.7%) (HR: 0.40; 95% CI: 0.23-0.71; P = 0.002).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds bifurcation-specific randomised evidence on imaging guidance, to be weighed against neutral left main and complex PCI trials.

title: Aspirin versus clopidogrel for chronic maintenance monotherapy after percutaneous coronary intervention: 10-year follow-up of the HOST-EXAM trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 5438 patients assigned to aspirin (n=2728) or clopidogrel (n=2710), median follow-up 10·5 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design in a Korean population, and all-cause mortality did not differ.
appraisal.one_line: Ten-year follow-up of HOST-EXAM: clopidogrel monotherapy was associated with fewer composite events than aspirin after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Kaplan-Meier estimate 25·4% for the clopidogrel group vs 28·5% for the aspirin group; hazard ratio 0·86 [95% CI 0·77-0·96]; log-rank p=0·0050.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Longest randomised follow-up supporting clopidogrel as the preferred chronic single antiplatelet agent.

title: Deferral of percutaneous coronary intervention in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (PRO-TAVI): an investigator-initiated, multicentre, open-label, non-inferiority, randomised controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Investigator-initiated multicentre randomised trial (PRO-TAVI); 466 patients (233 deferral, 233 PCI before TAVI).
appraisal.main_limitation: Modest sample with a wide interval for the rate difference.
appraisal.one_line: Deferring PCI until after TAVI was non-inferior to PCI before TAVI for a 1-year composite.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary endpoint in 56 (24%) of 233 patients vs 60 (26%) of 233 patients (rate difference -1·7% [95% CI -9·5 to 6·2]; hazard ratio 0·89 [95% CI 0·62-1·28]; p=0·0008 for non-inferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports a conservative approach to CAD in TAVI candidates, a common decision with discordant guidance.

title: Percutaneous coronary intervention versus coronary artery bypass grafting for unprotected left main stenosis: 10-year final results from the randomised, open-label, non-inferiority NOBLE trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 1201 patients assigned to PCI (n=598) or CABG (n=603), 592 per group in the ITT population.
appraisal.main_limitation: Restricted to left main disease without additional complex lesions, and an older stent platform.
appraisal.one_line: Ten-year final results show no difference in all-cause mortality between PCI and CABG for unprotected left main disease without additional complex lesions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: All-cause mortality at 10 years 136 [23%] of 592 in the PCI group and 145 [25%] of 592 in the CABG group; hazard ratio 0·93 [95% CI 0·74-1·18]; p=0·56.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Long-term mortality parity informs heart team decisions and guideline classes for left main PCI.

title: Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial of Chronic Total Occlusion Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Stable Angina: The ORBITA-CTO Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised placebo-controlled trial (ORBITA-CTO); 50 patients (25 CTO PCI, 25 placebo).
appraisal.main_limitation: Small sample, symptom endpoint only, selected single-vessel population.
appraisal.one_line: Placebo-controlled trial found CTO PCI improved angina beyond placebo in symptomatic single-vessel CTO.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: CTO PCI resulted in an immediate and sustained improvement in the angina symptom score (OR: 4.38; 95% credible interval [CrI]: 1.57-12.69; probability of benefit [Pr{Benefit}] = 0.996).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Blinded evidence for symptomatic benefit of CTO PCI.

title: Left Ventricular Unloading in Anterior ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Without Shock: The ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Door to Unload Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial (STEMI-DTU); 527 patients (262 treatment, 265 control).
appraisal.main_limitation: Surrogate infarct-size endpoint, with longer total ischemic time in the treatment arm.
appraisal.one_line: Microaxial pump unloading with delayed PCI did not reduce infarct size in anterior STEMI without shock and increased bleeding and vascular complications.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: IS/LVM was 30.8% ± 16.2% in the treatment group and 31.9% ± 16.9% in the control group (mean difference: -1.1%; 95% CI: -4.2 to 2.0; P = 0.50).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Does not support routine unloading before reperfusion in haemodynamically stable anterior STEMI.

title: Coronary microvascular dysfunction and cardiovascular outcomes (Multicenter FLOW-CMD Registry): a prospective, multicentre cohort study in South Korea.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicentre cohort at seven hospitals; 5764 patients screened and 1003 enrolled, median follow-up of 1·9 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational, with microvascular dysfunction defined by thresholds that may not generalise, and funded by device manufacturers.
appraisal.one_line: Prospective Korean multicentre registry links coronary microvascular dysfunction to worse outcomes in patients undergoing invasive angiography.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Coronary microvascular dysfunction was observed in 123 (21·5%) of 573 patients with obstructive epicardial coronary artery disease and in 40 (9·3%) of 430 patients without. The primary endpoint hazard ratio 1·91 [95% CI 1·22-2·99]; p=0·0047.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides prevalence and prognosis data for microvascular dysfunction in routine invasive practice, supporting physiology-guided management trials.

title: P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy after abbreviated dual antiplatelet therapy following percutaneous coronary intervention: a meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of eleven randomised trials including 37,443 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level pooling with heterogeneity in populations and regimens.
appraisal.one_line: Pairwise and network meta-analysis of P2Y12 monotherapy after abbreviated DAPT: less bleeding without a difference in MACE.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: No significant differences in the risk of MACE with aspirin discontinuation at either ≤1 month (risk ratio [RR] 1.01; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.85-1.20) or 3 months (RR 0.95; 95% CI 0.67-1.36); major bleeding RR 0.46; 95% CI 0.23-0.94 for ≤1-month discontinuation.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Synthesises the abbreviated DAPT question and allows indirect comparison of discontinuation timing.

title: Sirolimus-Eluting Balloon With Provisional Stenting Versus Systematic Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation to Treat De Novo Coronary Lesions: A Randomized, Open-Label, Noninferiority Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised noninferiority trial at 62 sites; 3323 participants randomised and treated.
appraisal.main_limitation: Per-protocol sensitivity analysis did not confirm noninferiority and bailout stenting occurred in 343 (20.7%).
appraisal.one_line: Sirolimus-eluting balloon with provisional stenting was noninferior to systematic DES for 1-year target vessel failure in the ITT analysis, but the per-protocol analysis did not confirm this.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Target vessel failure occurred over 365 days in 88 (5.3%) and 73 (4.4%) participants (risk difference, 0.91% [95% CI -0.55% to 2.38%]; 1-sided P=0.02 for noninferiority with a 2.44% noninferiority margin).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Largest trial of a DCB-first strategy in de novo lesions, relevant to leave-nothing-behind approaches.

title: Extended Dual Antiplatelet Therapy for Multivessel Coronary Artery Disease.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial (DAPT-MVD); 8250 patients (4125 extended DAPT, 4125 aspirin monotherapy), median follow-up 34.3 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Chinese population with a borderline P value and low bleeding event numbers.
appraisal.one_line: Extending DAPT by 12 months after DES in multivessel disease reduced cardiovascular death, MI or stroke compared with aspirin alone, without more bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary efficacy end-point event in 222 patients vs 266 patients (36-month Kaplan-Meier cumulative incidence, 5.8% vs. 6.8%; hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.69 to 0.98; P = 0.03).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large trial favouring extended DAPT in a defined high-risk group, contrasting with de-escalation trends.

title: 1-month versus 12-month dual antithrombotic therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with atrial fibrillation (OPTIMA-AF): a multicentre, open-label, hybrid non-inferiority and superiority, randomised, controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre randomised trial (OPTIMA-AF); 1088 randomised, 1079 analysed (542 vs 537).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label with few efficacy events and predominantly chronic coronary syndrome.
appraisal.one_line: In AF patients undergoing PCI, 1-month dual therapy followed by DOAC monotherapy was non-inferior to 12-month dual therapy for efficacy and reduced bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary efficacy endpoint (Kaplan-Meier estimate 5·4% vs 4·3%; absolute difference 1·1 percentage points [95% CI -1·5 to 3·6]; hazard ratio [HR] 1·25 [95% CI 0·73-2·17]); primary safety endpoint 4·5% vs 8·8% (HR 0·50 [95% CI 0·30-0·81]).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports short dual therapy duration in AF-PCI.

title: Antithrombotic therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with atrial fibrillation: an individual patient data network meta-analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: IPD network meta-analysis of six trials (10,634 patients).
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level heterogeneity in regimens and durations of triple therapy.
appraisal.one_line: Individual patient data network meta-analysis of antithrombotic regimens after PCI in AF found no efficacy difference but an early ischaemic signal with DOAC plus P2Y12 inhibitor.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, the risk of the primary efficacy outcome did not differ across the antithrombotic strategies (reference group: VKA plus DAPT; DOAC plus P2Y12 inhibitor: HR 1.16, 95%CI 0.97-1.41; VKA plus SAPT: 1.14, 0.85-1.54, DOAC plus DAPT: 0.99, 0.75-1.30).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Clarifies early-phase ischaemic risk with dual therapy and bleeding benefits, informing guideline wording in AF-PCI.

title: Aspirin Omission at the Time of Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in STEMI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised noninferiority trial (PREMIUM); 2216 patients in full analysis (1109 monotherapy, 1107 DAPT).
appraisal.main_limitation: Single P2Y12 agent in a population largely from Japan, with an industry sponsor.
appraisal.one_line: Low-dose prasugrel monotherapy started before primary PCI in STEMI was not noninferior to DAPT for death, stroke or MI, though it reduced major bleeding.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Death from any cause, stroke, or myocardial infarction at 12 months in 124 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 11.0%) vs 94 patients (8.5%) (hazard ratio, 1.34; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.02 to 1.75; P = 0.40 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Cautions against omitting aspirin from the outset of primary PCI in STEMI.

title: Prasugrel versus Ticagrelor in Acute Coronary Syndromes.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry-based randomised comparison of default policies (SWITCH-SWEDEHEART); 17,095 patients (9444 ticagrelor policy, 7651 prasugrel policy).
appraisal.main_limitation: Policy-level comparison with unequal group sizes and crossover in actual treatment.
appraisal.one_line: A default prasugrel policy did not lower ischaemic events compared with a default ticagrelor policy in ACS patients undergoing PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary end-point event in 11.8% vs 11.1% (adjusted odds ratio [prasugrel vs. ticagrelor], 0.90; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.77 to 1.06); major bleeding 4.4% and 4.2% (adjusted odds ratio, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.64 to 0.99).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Large pragmatic evidence on a common P2Y12 choice, relevant to ESC and ACC/AHA preference wording.

title: Complete Revascularization Guided by Functional Coronary Angiography in STEMI.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial (AIR-STEMI); 1823 patients (913 physiology-guided, 910 angiography-guided).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label trial with a composite including ischemia-driven revascularisation.
appraisal.one_line: Physiology-guided complete revascularisation reduced events compared with angiography-guided revascularisation in STEMI with multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary-outcome event in 81 patients (8.9%) vs 125 patients (13.7%) (hazard ratio, 0.62; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.47 to 0.83; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs the method of selecting non-culprit lesions for complete revascularisation in STEMI.

title: Timing of PCI in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic-Valve Implantation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised noninferiority trial (TAVI PCI); 986 patients (498 TAVI-first, 488 PCI-first).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label with a one-year horizon.
appraisal.one_line: In severe AS with coronary disease, TAVI before PCI was noninferior to PCI before TAVI at 1 year.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Primary end-point event in 105 patients (22.2%) vs 112 patients (24.2%) (risk difference, -2.0 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -7.4 to 3.4; P<0.001 for noninferiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs sequencing of PCI and TAVI, alongside the PRO-TAVI deferral trial.

title: Intracoronary Imaging-Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of 28 RCTs comprising 24,634 patients with a mean follow-up of 22 months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial-level pooling with heterogeneity linked to geography and lesion characteristics.
appraisal.one_line: Updated meta-analysis of 28 RCTs: intracoronary imaging-guided PCI reduced target lesion failure and mortality compared with angiography guidance.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: ICI-guided PCI reduced target lesion failure (relative risk [RR]: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.61-0.85; I2 = 61%) and all-cause mortality (RR: 0.82; 0.70-0.96; I2 = 0%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Updates the pooled evidence base on imaging guidance, overlapping with recent neutral Western trials.

title: Prognostic Value of Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve From a Large Nationwide Cohort.

appraisal.design_and_n: Nationwide cohort, 27 sites across England; 7836 patients aged 63 (56.0-71.0), 37.4% women, underwent FFR-CT analysis.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational design; associations only, with small incremental discrimination and no test of whether FFR-CT-guided management changes outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Large English nationwide cohort of FFR-CT in stable coronary disease linking stenosis-specific values to MI, death and revascularisation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Stenosis-specific FFR-CT was associated with future MI (hazard ratio [HR], 2.08-5.73; P<0.001), cardiovascular death (HR, 1.51-3.40; P<0.001), all-cause death (HR, 1.01-1.58; P=0.01), and revascularization (HR, 4.79-24.48; P<0.001). The addition of FFR-CT improved discrimination for MI or cardiovascular death compared with a risk factor and stenosis severity model (C index, 0.783; ∆C index, 0.012; P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It gives contemporary real-world prognostic data supporting FFR-CT thresholds for risk stratification before revascularisation decisions.

title: Oral Anticoagulant Monotherapy vs. Combination Therapy in Chronic Coronary Syndrome Requiring Long-Term Anticoagulation: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
journal: Clinical and applied thrombosis/hemostasis : official journal of the International Academy of Clinical and Applied Thrombosis/Hemostasis

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of RCTs comparing OAC monotherapy with OAC plus SAPT in chronic coronary syndrome; the abstract does not give the number of trials or patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not state the number of trials, and heterogeneity was moderate to substantial for some outcomes (I2 = 64% for NACE).
appraisal.one_line: A meta-analysis of randomised trials found less bleeding with oral anticoagulant monotherapy than with anticoagulant plus single antiplatelet therapy in chronic coronary syndrome.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: OAC monotherapy was associated with a significantly lower risk of major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding compared with dual antithrombotic therapy (DAT) (RR: 0.50; 95% CI: 0.38-0.65; p < 0.001; I2 = 42%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Antithrombotic de-escalation in anticoagulated patients with stable coronary disease is a common decision.

title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Facility Access and Clinical Outcomes Among Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Cohort study of 590 282 patients with AMI in California.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational quasi-experimental design with possible unmeasured confounding.
appraisal.one_line: A cohort study using facility openings in California found that new PCI capacity in underserved communities was associated with lower mortality after AMI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Openings in communities without baseline access were associated with a 30.0 percentage point (pp) increase (95% CI, 28.2 to 31.8 pp) in admission to PCI-capable hospitals and a 5.1 pp increase (95% CI, 3.3 to 7.0 pp) in PCI receipt, along with reductions in 30-day (-1.8 pp; 95% CI, -3.2 to -0.5 pp) and 1-year (-2.8 pp; 95% CI, -4.7 to -1.0 pp) mortality.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It addresses systems-of-care planning for AMI using a natural experiment.

title: Acute Coronary Occlusions in NSTEMI Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Insights From the CathPCI Registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort from the CathPCI Registry; 1,198,544 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: In-hospital outcomes only, and occlusion is defined from angiography after the event.
appraisal.one_line: A national registry analysis finds acute coronary occlusion in a sizeable share of NSTEMI patients undergoing PCI, with worse in-hospital outcomes than NSTEMI without occlusion.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patients with NSTEMI-ACO had a higher risk for the primary composite compared with those with NSTEMI-no-ACO (adjusted OR: 2.26; 95% CI: 2.18-2.34; P < 0.001) but a lower risk compared with those with STEMI (adjusted OR: 0.54; 95% CI: 0.52-0.56; P < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It quantifies the population targeted by occlusion-based triage proposals.

title: Occlusion-Focused Triage vs Very-High-Risk NSTEMI Criteria: A DIFOCCULT-3 Substudy.

appraisal.design_and_n: Substudy of the multicenter, cluster-randomized DIFOCCULT-3 trial; 4,398 patients without diagnostic ST-elevation.
appraisal.main_limitation: Outcomes are process measures (timing of invasive management and ACO identification) rather than clinical events.
appraisal.one_line: A substudy of a cluster-randomised trial comparing occlusion-focused triage with very-high-risk NSTEMI criteria for identifying acute coronary occlusion.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The OMI/NOMI approach selected more patients for early invasive management compared with the STEMI/NSTEMI framework (45.4% vs 13.6%; P < 0.001); adjudicated ACO was identified within 2 hours more frequently (35.1% vs 16.7%; P < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It informs the proposed shift from STEMI/NSTEMI to occlusion-based triage that would alter who receives immediate angiography.

title: Immediate Versus Staged Complete Revascularization in Multivessel Disease and STEMI: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Frequentist pairwise meta-analysis of RCTs; 4 randomized trials comprising 2,651 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: The authors note few deaths and statistical fragility, and the prediction interval includes no difference.
appraisal.one_line: A meta-analysis of four randomised trials suggests higher 1-year mortality with immediate than with staged complete revascularisation in STEMI with multivessel disease.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The risk of all-cause death at 1-year was higher with immediate complete revascularization (HR: 1.50; 95% CI: 1.02-2.21; P = 0.04; prediction interval [PI]: 0.80-2.81; I2 = 0%; t2 = 0).
appraisal.why_it_matters: The timing of non-culprit intervention is a common decision in STEMI and the signal runs against immediate treatment.

title: Intraprocedural Cardiac Arrest in Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Interventions in the United States: An Analysis of the NCDR CathPCI Registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort from the CathPCI Registry, 2018 to 2023; 36,755 intraprocedural cardiac arrests among 3,956,840 PCIs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Descriptive registry data with in-hospital outcomes only.
appraisal.one_line: A national registry describes the incidence and mortality of cardiac arrest during PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: A total of 36,755 IPCA occurred during 3,956,840 PCIs (0.93%); In-hospital death occurred in 40.5% of patients with IPCA.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It gives contemporary benchmarks for a catastrophic procedural complication that is rising in incidence.

title: Impact of Extent of Coronary Artery Disease in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A PRO-TAVI Substudy.

appraisal.design_and_n: Substudy of the PRO-TAVI trial; 466 patients with significant coronary artery disease undergoing TAVR.
appraisal.main_limitation: The findings are post hoc subgroup results that the authors say need confirmation in randomized trials.
appraisal.one_line: A post hoc substudy of a randomised trial examines coronary disease extent (SYNTAX score) and outcomes after deferred versus pre-TAVR PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In patients with SS >17, the ischemic composite outcome occurred more often in the deferral group (30.9% vs 14.8%; adjusted HR: 2.43; 95% CI: 1.04-5.64; P = 0.04), driven primarily by all-cause mortality and stroke.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It suggests that the safety of deferring PCI before TAVR may not extend to complex coronary disease.

title: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes After Physiology-Guided vs Angiography-Guided Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: From the FARGO Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Long-term follow-up of a randomised trial; median follow-up of 8.8 years; the abstract does not state the total sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Very small sample, and revascularisation was largely symptom-driven.
appraisal.one_line: A long-term follow-up of a randomised comparison of FFR-guided and angiography-guided CABG.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Patients in the FFR-guided group had significantly more MACCE compared to the angiography-guided group, (26 [52%] vs 16 [32%], log-rank test P = 0.03).
appraisal.why_it_matters: It adds long-term randomised data on physiology-guided surgical revascularisation, though the small size limits inference.

title: Extended Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Versus Aspirin Monotherapy After Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis With GRADE Evaluation and Trial Sequential Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of RCTs; six trials involving 28,601 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Trial sequential analysis did not cross the monitoring boundary; substantial bleeding heterogeneity (I2 = 87%) and low certainty.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of randomised trials comparing extended DAPT with aspirin monotherapy after about 12 months of uneventful DAPT following DES.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Extended DAPT significantly reduced MI compared with aspirin monotherapy (RR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.51-0.85; P = 0.001; I2 = 37%). Clinically relevant bleeding RR, 1.19; 95% CI, 0.66-2.15; P = 0.56.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on prolonged antithrombotic therapy decisions after stenting where the ischaemia-bleeding trade-off remains contested.

title: Intravascular Imaging-Guided Drug-Eluting Stenting for Complex Coronary Lesions: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of RCTs; 18 RCTs enrolling 18,975 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Geographic heterogeneity, with benefit concentrated in Asian trials, and subgroup comparison by stent optimisation is not randomised.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis of randomised trials found intravascular imaging guidance associated with fewer adverse events than angiography guidance in complex lesions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: MACE RR: 0.67; 95% CI: 0.55-0.83; cardiac death RR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.53-0.97. Significant geographic interaction for MACE (Pinteraction < 0.01), with benefit predominantly in Asian trial populations.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Updates the pooled evidence for imaging-guided PCI after recent large trials with divergent findings and flags possible transportability limits.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Combined TAVR-PCI Versus SAVR-CABG in Patients with Aortic Stenosis and Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

appraisal.design_and_n: Systematic review and meta-analysis; Fourteen studies (two randomized trials, nine cohorts, three administrative databases), 154,892 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Predominantly observational data with confounding; randomised data were too limited to confirm findings.
appraisal.one_line: Meta-analysis separating randomised and observational evidence for TAVR plus PCI versus SAVR plus CABG, excluding overlapping populations.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: TAVR+PCI was associated with lower early mortality (odds ratio (OR) 0.60, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.44-0.84), and with higher mortality over 12-72 months (hazard ratio (HR) 1.38, 1.28-1.49; nine observational studies).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses the common decision on revascularisation in patients with aortic stenosis and coronary disease, where randomised evidence is thin.

title: Comparison of Drug-Coated Versus Conventional Balloons for the Side Branches of Bifurcation Lesions: OCVC-BIF Study.

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre, randomised, open-label trial; 299 patients (151 DCB, 148 non-DCB).
appraisal.main_limitation: The primary endpoint is angiographic, and the trial was not powered for clinical events; open-label design.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre open-label randomised trial in Japan found that adding a drug-coated balloon to the side branch after main-vessel DES and kissing inflation lowered angiographic side-branch restenosis.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Restenosis rate was lower in the DCB group than in the non-DCB group (8.1% versus 18.3%, P=0.012); MACE at 12 months was similar (10.1% versus 12.4%, P=0.58).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bifurcation side-branch treatment is common and DCB use there lacks randomised evidence, so this informs a technique decision, though clinical benefit remains unshown.

title: Temporal trends and outcomes of intravascular imaging in chronic total occlusion interventions: insights from the PROGRESS-CTO registry.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry analysis (PROGRESS-CTO); 18,024 CTO PCIs at 76 centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry with operator-selected imaging and residual confounding; outcomes are procedural success rather than long-term events.
appraisal.one_line: Large multicentre CTO PCI registry analysis of intravascular imaging use, with higher technical and procedural success when IVUS was used to cross.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: After 1:1 propensity score matching, technical success (85.8% vs 78.8%; p < 0.001) and procedural success (83.6% vs 78.1%, p = 0.003) remained higher in the IVUS-to-cross group.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Describes uptake and practice variation of imaging in CTO PCI and supports a possible randomised evaluation of IVUS-guided crossing.

title: Impact of Stent Age on Antithrombotic Strategy for Atrial Fibrillation in Patients with Drug-eluting Stents.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prespecified analysis of the ADAPT AF-DES trial; remote PCI group (stent age > 2 years; n = 577) and intermediate PCI group (stent age 1-2 years; n = 383).
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis; the ischaemic outcome interaction was inconsistent across modelling approaches.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified analysis of ADAPT AF-DES testing whether stent age modifies the effect of NOAC monotherapy versus NOAC plus clopidogrel.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: No significant interaction between antithrombotic strategy and stent age was found for NACE. NOAC monotherapy was associated with less major bleeding or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding than combination therapy in both subgroups without interaction.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs antithrombotic de-escalation beyond 12 months in patients with atrial fibrillation and drug-eluting stents.

title: Dual antithrombic therapy with DOAC plus ticagrelor versus DOAC plus clopidogrel after PCI: results from the ReDUAL PCI real life registry-based randomized controlled trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label, multicentre, registry-based randomised controlled trial within the Southeast Netherlands Heart Registry; 109 patients randomized (53 ticagrelor, 56 clopidogrel).
appraisal.main_limitation: Stopped early for slow recruitment and underpowered, so no firm conclusion is possible.
appraisal.one_line: Prematurely terminated registry-based randomised trial of DOAC plus ticagrelor versus DOAC plus clopidogrel after PCI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Overall bleeding rates were similar between ticagrelor and clopidogrel (13.2% vs 14.3%). Major bleeding (9.4% vs 1.8%), MACCE (13.2% vs 5.4%), and NACE (20.8% vs 7.1%) occurred more frequently with ticagrelor, without statistical significance.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds randomised data to the unresolved choice of P2Y12 inhibitor alongside oral anticoagulation, and shows the feasibility limits of registry-based trials.

title: Adoption of intravascular imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention in the United States (2012-2022): temporal trends, disparities, and mortality association.

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective analysis of 5,220,590 PCI admissions from the National Inpatient Sample.
appraisal.main_limitation: Administrative coding captures imaging use imperfectly and confounding by indication cannot be excluded.
appraisal.one_line: US national inpatient analysis of intravascular imaging use in PCI from 2012 to 2022, with adjusted in-hospital mortality comparison.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: IVI-guided PCI increased from 7.1% (2012) to 21.3% (2022) (p trend < 0.001). IVI remained significantly associated with lower odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 0.783, 95% CI 0.742-0.827; P < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Quantifies slow uptake of a guideline-endorsed technique and hospital-level variation.

title: 2026 Focused Update of the Saudi Heart Association Guidelines on Best Practices in the Management of Chronic Coronary Syndromes.
journal: Journal of the Saudi Heart Association

appraisal.design_and_n: Consensus-based guideline update by a multidisciplinary expert panel; no sample size applies.
appraisal.main_limitation: Recommendations rest on expert consensus and are regional, so they add little to international evidence.
appraisal.one_line: National focused update of chronic coronary syndrome guidance from a Saudi expert panel, with new sections on ANOCA/INOCA and antiplatelet de-escalation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows how the shift to individualised DAPT duration and P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy is being adopted in national guidance.

title: Coronary artery disease management in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Meta-analysis of randomised trials: Five trials (N=1,644 patients) in the review, four in the primary quantitative synthesis (N=1,476).
appraisal.main_limitation: Few trials with a study-defined composite endpoint, and the network ranking rests on sparse direct comparisons.
appraisal.one_line: Systematic review with pairwise and network meta-analysis of randomised trials of routine PCI versus conservative management of coronary disease in patients undergoing TAVI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with conservative treatment, routine PCI was associated with lower risks of MACE (risk ratio [RR] 0.80, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.65-0.98) and unplanned revascularisation (RR 0.30, 95% CI: 0.11-0.83) and an increased risk of major bleeding (RR 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Pools the randomised evidence on revascularisation before TAVI, a contested decision in which guidelines remain cautious.

title: Quantitative Flow Ratio- vs Angiography-Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Secondary Analysis of the FAVOR III China Trial.

appraisal.design_and_n: Secondary analysis of a randomised trial (NCT03656848): 3825 patients in the intention-to-treat population, 2066 (54.0%) with MVD.
appraisal.main_limitation: Subgroup analysis in a trial not powered for the interaction, with Chinese centres only.
appraisal.one_line: Prespecified secondary analysis of FAVOR III China reporting 3-year outcomes of QFR-guided versus angiography-guided PCI by multivessel disease status.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: In the MVD cohort, MACE occurred in 124 of 1023 patients (12.1%) in the QFR-guided group and 188 of 1043 patients (18.1%) in the angiography-guided group (hazard ratio, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.52-0.81; P < .001). In the non-MVD cohort, the hazard ratio was 0.77; 95% CI, 0.57-1.04; P = .09, and P for interaction = .35.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds longer-term randomised evidence for angiography-derived physiology guidance of PCI across disease extent.
